# Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol (BACP)

> BACP is an open protocol that lets AI agents discover, negotiate, buy, pay for, and resolve issues with Indian commerce on behalf of people and businesses, natively on India's digital public infrastructure: ONDC/Beckn, UPI, Account Aggregator consent, and the DPDP Act.

BACP (Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol) is an open protocol for AI agents to transact in Indian commerce on ONDC/Beckn, UPI and other Indian payment rails, with mandate-bound authority, DPDP-compliant consent, signed requests and verifiable evidence.

# Specification

# Bharat Agentic Commerce Protocol (BACP) Specification

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. Each one links to the relevant entry in [Open Questions](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/index.md).

BACP is an open protocol that lets an AI agent run the full Indian commerce lifecycle on behalf of a person or a business: discover, negotiate, check out, pay, track fulfilment, return, get refunds and raise grievances. It does this on rails that already exist and are already regulated: ONDC/Beckn for commerce, UPI and the other Indian payment rails for money, Account Aggregator–style consent artefacts for authority, and the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act for personal data.

This page is the normative entry point. It defines the conventions that apply to every other page, the layering and actor model, the core artefacts, the lifecycle, and the rules for versioning and extensibility.

## Conventions

### Requirements language

The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **SHALL**, **SHALL NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, **RECOMMENDED**, **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** in this specification are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119.html) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174.html) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

### Data conventions

| Convention           | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Amounts              | Every amount is an `Amount` object: an integer `value` in **paise** (INR minor units) and `currency: "INR"`. ₹302 is `{"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}`. Every settlement amount MUST be in INR. A foreign-currency figure MAY appear only as a disclosure view ([`fx.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/fx.json)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Payable amounts      | A payable amount (a closed mandate's `amount`, a payment receipt's `amount`, a tender's `amount`) MUST be an integer number of paise greater than zero. Values that may legitimately be zero, such as a remaining budget or a free-goods line, MAY be zero.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Date and time        | Timestamps are [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339.html) `date-time` strings, for example `2026-10-12T10:15:00+05:30`. Where a rule depends on a calendar period (a budget month, an AFA period), the period is computed in IST (UTC+05:30). BACP-owned timestamps SHOULD carry the offset `+05:30`; Beckn `context` fields follow ONDC, which requires `Z`, and are relayed unchanged. Every comparison of times is a comparison of instants, so `…T10:00:05+05:30` and `…T04:30:05Z` are equal. The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 761(E)), Rule 7, require IST for any time reference from their commencement (notified, not in force as of 18-10-2026; about 24-02-2027, exact day not verified). Whether Rule 7 reaches machine timestamps is open ([Q-84](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-84)). |
| Durations            | ISO 8601 durations, for example `P30D` or `PT5M`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Signature timestamps | RFC 9421 `created` and `expires` parameters are integer seconds since the Unix epoch.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Canonical JSON       | Signed and hashed JSON is canonicalised with JCS ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Hashes               | Written as `alg:base64url`. `sha-256` is mandatory. `blake2b-512` is allowed only for Beckn digests.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Text shown to people | Multilingual maps keyed by BCP 47 tag, for example `{"hi-IN": "...", "en-IN": "..."}`. Hindi display text under `hi-IN` is written in Devanagari. Romanised Hindi (for example a voice transcript) is tagged `hi-Latn-IN`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Schemas              | JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Schemas are identified by their `$id` under `https://bacp.dev/schemas/`, and tools MUST resolve `$ref`s by `$id`, not by file path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

## The problem BACP solves

India already has interoperable commerce (ONDC/Beckn), instant interoperable payments with standing authorities (UPI Reserve Pay, UPI Circle, AutoPay), a consent-artefact model (Account Aggregator and DEPA), and a data-protection law (DPDP). None of them was designed for a software agent acting for a person. Each lacks the same four things:

- **Who** the agent is. Today only the platform is identified on the network, never the agent or the legal entity that operates it.
- **Under whose authority, and within what limits.** Nothing expresses "buy groceries for me, up to ₹3,000 a month, never more than ₹1,500 an order, and ask me above ₹1,200".
- **Whether a human was present.** Payment and consumer rules differ sharply between a person approving a payment and an agent acting alone.
- **What the person agreed to share,** with whom, for what purpose.

BACP adds these four things as a thin, namespaced agent layer, together with a hash-chained instruction log and rail-anchored receipts so that any dispute can be reconstructed from the person's instruction to the bank reference number. BACP does not fork ONDC/Beckn, UPI or any other rail.

## Design principles

1. **The model proposes, a deterministic engine decides.** An LLM interprets intent, searches, builds carts and drafts offers. It never verifies anything that matters. Every commitment (paying, accepting an offer, placing a bid, cancelling, returning) passes a deterministic, non-LLM check that fails closed. The agent is treated as untrusted: prompt injection cannot be prevented, so it is contained. See [the section below](#the-model-proposes-a-deterministic-engine-decides).
1. **The rail is authoritative.** Payment rails enforce their own limits. BACP limits MUST be at or below the rail's, and BACP re-checks them. BACP never relies on the rail to bound its own budgets.
1. **An agent is never an authentication factor.** The agent never sees or relays a UPI PIN, OTP or card credential, and never activates a mandate. Approval and authentication happen only on a non-agentic [Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/glossary/#trusted-surface).
1. **Consent is explicit and never inferred.** Purchase consent and DPDP consent come from an affirmative action by the person, never from silence.
1. **Minimum disclosure.** The payment leg is basket-blind. The seller never sees the payment instrument or the buyer's negotiation bounds. The bank never sees the basket.
1. **Evidence by default.** Every step is signed and logged so that liability can be decided from evidence. BACP makes no claim about how the law allocates liability for agent error ([Q-01](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-01)).
1. **Bharat-first.** Multilingual text, voice and IVR channels, voice-consent evidence, GST lines and cash on delivery are first-class.

Figure: BACP in one page. The principal and the agent operator (left) call the BACP gateway stack (centre), which reaches sellers and their Seller Apps on ONDC through Beckn (right). Payment rails, consent and identity (the "Shared base" group) are the base every call depends on. The "Capability discovery" group is the gateway's published profile, where a counterparty reads capabilities and payment handlers. Dashed boxes are Proposed or not yet usable, each tied to an [open question](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/index.md) or a [handler status](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md): a `reserved` handler backs no payment, and a `pilot` handler backs a mandate only when the gateway's conformance attestation lists it; `in.upi.circle` stays closed even then ([Q-77](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-77)).

## Layering

BACP is an agent layer **over** Beckn/ONDC, not a replacement for it. Each layer reuses an existing primitive.

```
flowchart TB
    subgraph T["Transport bindings"]
        REST["REST, RFC 9421 signed"]
        MCP["MCP tools"]
        A2A["A2A extension"]
    end
    subgraph F["BACP session facade (at the BACP gateway)"]
        SES["Checkout, negotiation and post-order sessions"]
        VER["Deterministic verifier and negotiation guard"]
        LOG["Instruction log, receipts, evidence bundle"]
    end
    subgraph N["Beckn / ONDC backbone"]
        BKN["search, select, init, confirm, status, cancel, update"]
        IGM["IGM 2.0 issue and on_issue"]
        CTX["context.bacp extension"]
    end
    subgraph P["Indian payment rails"]
        OPEN["Standing authorities for human-not-present use"]
        CLOSED["Per-transaction 2FA for human-present use"]
    end
    subgraph C["Consent (AA / DEPA style)"]
        MM["Mandate Manager and Trusted Surface"]
    end
    subgraph I["Identity"]
        REG["Registry, AgentCredential, status lists"]
    end
    T --> F
    F --> N
    F --> P
    N -.->|"payment terms and bank reference"| P
    C -.->|"mandates verified by"| F
    C -.->|"rail binding attestation"| P
    I -.->|"keys and credential status"| T
    I -.->|"subscriber keys"| N
```

Solid arrows are call paths. Dotted arrows are trust dependencies. Consent and identity are cross-cutting: every call depends on them. The facade talks to the payment rails through the payer PSP rather than through Beckn, because Beckn carries only payment *terms*: money moves off-network.

| Layer                   | What BACP reuses                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | What BACP adds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Transport bindings**  | REST (OpenAPI 3.1), MCP tools with `structuredContent`, A2A `DataPart` and the `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` task state. One operation set, bound three ways. UCP binds its own operations four ways (REST, MCP, A2A and an embedded binding), and BACP does not adopt the embedded one. | RFC 9421 agent signatures with separate tags for browsing, paying, post-order writes and negotiation. Step-up mapped to A2A `TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED` and MCP `insufficient_scope`. See [REST](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/index.md) and [MCP and A2A](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/mcp-a2a/index.md).                                                                             |
| **Session facade**      | UCP checkout lifecycle and status names; ACP full-state responses, flat errors, `messages[].resolution` and idempotency; AP2's Trusted Surface and fail-closed constraint evaluation.                                                                                                 | A synchronous session over asynchronous Beckn; the deterministic verifier; the instruction log; an in-doubt payment saga. See [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Beckn/ONDC backbone** | Beckn `{context, message}`, ACK plus `on_*` callbacks, Ed25519/BLAKE2b network signing, registry lookup, ONDC payment and settlement fields, IGM.                                                                                                                                     | The [`context.bacp`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/beckn-context-bacp.json) extension, mandatory idempotency and a replay cache, and an IGM `actors[]` entry of type `AI_AGENT` (Proposed: [Q-11](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-11)). Agent semantics stay in a namespace that network participants can ignore. See [Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/index.md). |
| **Payment rails**       | Live Indian rails: UPI Reserve Pay, UPI Circle, UPI AutoPay, card e-mandates, eNACH, PPIs, COD and others, with their own regulatory limits.                                                                                                                                          | Payment authority bound to a **live** rail primitive with a PSP-signed attestation; a basket-blind payment leg; rail-anchored receipts. See [Payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Consent**             | AA/DEPA consent-artefact semantics: immutable, purpose-coded, use-counted, revocable. AP2-style open and closed mandates.                                                                                                                                                             | Periodic budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds, post-order action scopes, a separate negotiation mandate, revocation within 60 seconds, DPDP consent receipts. See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Identity**            | ONDC registry onboarding and key lookup, W3C verifiable credentials and status lists, AP2 `cnf` key binding.                                                                                                                                                                          | The [`AgentCredential`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/agent-credential.json): the agent, its operator's legal entity, its BAP binding, AI disclosure and human handoff. See [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/index.md).                                                                                                                                                           |

### The layering decision

BACP makes four choices about how it sits on existing infrastructure:

1. **An agent layer over Beckn/ONDC.** Beckn already provides a signed asynchronous grammar, registry PKI, post-order writes (cancel, return), grievance handling (IGM), reconciliation and settlement (RSF), and a production network. BACP carries agent semantics in `context.bacp` and follows UCP checkout's lifecycle and status names (BACP spells `cancelled` and adds `human_handoff`). BACP is not wire-compatible with UCP: paths, totals and the sign of discounts, the `ucp` envelope, the `complete` payload and payment authority, and the MCP argument shape differ ([BACP and other protocols](https://bacp.dev/latest/documentation/other-protocols/#ucp)). BACP is neither a UCP profile only (UCP has no network discovery, post-order writes, Indian rails or DPDP) nor an ONDC domain specification only (that would lose global-agent interoperability and the AP2 mandate format).
1. **Mandates in AP2 style with AA/DEPA consent semantics.** A mandate has the structure of an AP2 open or closed Checkout Mandate or Payment Mandate, and the life of an Account Aggregator consent artefact: immutable once signed, tied to a purpose code, use-counted, and revocable at any time.
1. **Payment bound to live Indian rails.** An open (human-not-present) payment mandate MUST bind to a standing authority that a live rail already enforces, such as a UPI Reserve Pay block or a UPI Circle delegation. A closed (human-present) payment is authorised by a fresh per-transaction factor on the Trusted Surface. BACP does not wait for a future rail: as of 17-10-2026, NPCI has not published an agent-payment specification for UPI, so the handler `in.upi.uap` is reserved.
1. **RFC 9421 agent signatures.** Every agent request is signed with [RFC 9421](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9421.html) HTTP Message Signatures under the key bound in the AgentCredential, with a tag that limits what the request may do. The network leg keeps the network's own signing.

## Actor model

| Actor               | Role in BACP                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Trust                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Principal**       | The person or business on whose behalf the agent acts (the DPDP Data Principal and, for payments, the payer). Sets up, pauses and revokes mandates; answers step-ups; receives notices.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Trusted to authorise. Consent is always an explicit, affirmative action on the Trusted Surface, never inferred.                              |
| **Agent**           | The LLM runtime (voice or text) that interprets intent, discovers, builds carts, negotiates and closes open mandates with its `cnf` key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Untrusted.** It never verifies anything that matters, never holds a PIN or OTP, never signs consent and is never an authentication factor. |
| **Agent operator**  | The legal entity that runs the agent and holds its AgentCredential. Keeps the operator signing key out of the agent's reach, runs the instruction log, appoints a grievance officer, keeps an AI inventory, and provides AI disclosure and a human handoff.                                                                                                                                                                                           | Accountable and identified through registry onboarding.                                                                                      |
| **BACP gateway**    | The BACP endpoint that agents call. It is co-located with, or runs on behalf of, a registered **Buyer App (BAP)**, so the BAP subscriber is the network-visible party. It verifies agent signatures and credentials, runs the deterministic mandate verifier and negotiation guard, translates calls into signed Beckn actions, holds the replay cache, idempotency store and reservation ledger, and is the interfacing network participant for IGM. | Trusted to enforce policy deterministically, but audited by conformance tests and evidence rather than trusted on its word.                  |
| **Seller / BPP**    | The seller and its Seller App (BPP). Provides catalogue, signed quotes, fulfilment, cancel and return handling, GST invoices, and responds to IGM issues. A BACP-aware BPP verifies `context.bacp` and, in negotiation, the buyer's `within_bounds` attestation.                                                                                                                                                                                      | Honest but curious. Its content is **untrusted input** to the agent (dark patterns, prompt injection).                                       |
| **Mandate Manager** | Turns an approval on the Trusted Surface into signed, immutable mandates and consent receipts. Keeps status, usage and revocation, publishes a status list and notifies counterparties within 60 seconds. Acts as, or for, a DPDP Consent Manager.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Data-blind**: stores mandates and logs, never order or payment payloads.                                                                   |
| **Trusted Surface** | The non-agentic surface, typically the payer's UPI app, where the principal reads notices in their language, approves mandates and step-ups, and enters a PIN or biometric.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Non-agentic by requirement. Trusted for consent capture and authentication.                                                                  |
| **PSP / rail**      | The payer PSP and the rail behind it (for UPI, NPCI and the issuer bank). Creates the standing authority (block, delegation, mandate), issues the `rail_binding` attestation, executes debits and refunds, and signs receipts with the rail reference (RRN, UTR or equivalent).                                                                                                                                                                       | Authoritative for money movement and limits. Sees only payee, amount, mandate reference and checkout hash, never the basket.                 |
| **Registry**        | The ONDC registry or another accredited registry. Publishes subscriber keys for BAPs, BPPs, Mandate Managers and PSPs; issues AgentCredentials and their status lists; records conformance attestations and payment-aggregator authorisation.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Root of trust for keys. Which body anchors agent identity is open ([Q-02](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-02)).  |

Other parties appear in specific flows: the Beckn gateway (BG), which multicasts `search` and is routing-only; grievance redressal officers and ODR providers; payment aggregators; logistics providers; and, for trade profiles, roles such as consignee, paying authority, broker, financier and a neutral auctioneer (see [Trade Profiles](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/trade-profiles/index.md)).

Co-location

In BACP `2026-10-18` the Mandate Manager is operated by, or co-located with, the payer PSP that also provides the Trusted Surface, so that consent capture and PIN entry happen on one non-agentic surface. The roles stay logically separate so that an independent DPDP Consent Manager can take over. An MM that acts as a registered Consent Manager does not also act as credential provider; that role runs as a separate component ([Q-16](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-16)).

## Core artefacts

| Artefact                           | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Schema                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **AgentCredential**                | Identifies the agent, its operator and its BAP; binds the agent's signing key (`cnf`); lists the signature tags it may use; carries the AI disclosure and human-handoff link. An SD-JWT VC, `vct: in.bacp.agent.1`. | [`agent-credential.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/agent-credential.json)           |
| **Mandate**                        | The principal's signed authority, AP2-compatible: open or closed, Checkout or Payment, with budgets, allow-lists, step-up thresholds, action and data scopes, and a rail or auth binding.                           | [`mandate.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/mandate.json)                             |
| **Negotiation mandate**            | A separate mandate (`vct: in.bacp.mandate.negotiation.1`) holding negotiation bounds, including a reservation price that is never disclosed.                                                                        | [`mandate-negotiation.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/mandate-negotiation.json)     |
| **ConsentReceipt**                 | The DPDP record of what personal data goes to which recipient, for what purpose, in which language, with the withdrawal and grievance routes. One per recipient per mandate.                                        | [`consent-receipt.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/consent-receipt.json)             |
| **Receipt**                        | A PSP-signed payment or refund receipt anchored to the rail reference (RRN, UTR or other rail evidence). Budgets decrement only from these.                                                                         | [`receipt.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/receipt.json)                             |
| **InstructionLog entry**           | A signed, hash-chained record of prompt → intent → cart → mandate → payment reference, held by the operator.                                                                                                        | [`instruction-log-entry.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/instruction-log-entry.json) |
| **`context.bacp`**                 | The extension carried in the Beckn/ONDC `context` of every BACP-originated network message.                                                                                                                         | [`beckn-context-bacp.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/beckn-context-bacp.json)       |
| **TermSheet**                      | The multi-issue terms under negotiation: price, quantity, delivery, payment, returns, warranty and more.                                                                                                            | [`termsheet.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/termsheet.json)                         |
| **Offer and negotiation messages** | Signed, expiring offers, counter-offers, bids, ACCEPT, REJECT, WITHDRAW and related messages.                                                                                                                       | [`offer.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/offer.json)                                 |
| **NegotiationSession**             | The state of a negotiation, RFQ or auction, and the negotiation capability advert.                                                                                                                                  | [`negotiation-session.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/negotiation-session.json)     |
| **Handler descriptor**             | Data describing one Indian payment handler: binding class, presence rules, limits, AFA, refund route, settlement evidence.                                                                                          | [`handler-descriptor.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/handler-descriptor.json)       |
| **PaymentPlan**                    | A split-tender or multi-tranche payment plan.                                                                                                                                                                       | [`payment-plan.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/payment-plan.json)                   |
| **Credit ledger entry**            | A hash-chained B2B credit (khata) posting.                                                                                                                                                                          | [`credit-ledger-entry.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/credit-ledger-entry.json)     |
| **LoanOffer**                      | A regulated credit offer with its key fact statement reference and cooling-off period.                                                                                                                              | [`loan-offer.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/loan-offer.json)                       |
| **FX view**                        | A disclosure view of a foreign-currency amount; settlement stays in INR.                                                                                                                                            | [`fx.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/fx.json)                                       |
| **Common types**                   | `Amount`, `Hash`, `Jws`, `Jwk`, `Signature`, `Presence`, `LangText`, `HandlerRef` and others.                                                                                                                       | [`common.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/common.json)                               |

The **evidence bundle**, which packages mandates, the BPP-signed quote, receipts and the instruction-log chain for a dispute, is defined in the REST binding (`EvidenceBundle` in the OpenAPI document listed under [Reference](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/reference/index.md)) and described in [Evidence and Instruction Log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/index.md).

## Lifecycle

A BACP transaction moves through seven stages. Mandate setup happens once, before the first stage, on the Trusted Surface. Negotiation is optional: a fixed-price catalogue purchase goes straight from discovery to checkout.

```
flowchart LR
    M["Mandate setup<br/>on the Trusted Surface"] --> D
    D["Discover<br/>POST /discover<br/>Beckn search"] --> NG
    D --> C
    NG["Negotiate (optional)<br/>signed offers under<br/>a negotiation mandate"] --> C
    C["Checkout<br/>POST and PUT /sessions<br/>Beckn select and init"] --> P
    P["Pay<br/>POST complete<br/>verifier, rail debit,<br/>Beckn confirm"] --> F
    F["Fulfil<br/>GET /orders<br/>Beckn status"] --> R
    F --> G
    R["Return and refund<br/>POST returns<br/>Beckn update,<br/>refund to source"] --> G
    G["Grievance<br/>POST /issues<br/>ONDC IGM as AI_AGENT"]
```

| Stage             | Agent call                                                                                      | Signature tag                                                                                                       | Network or rail action                                                                                                                          | Defined in                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mandate setup     | `POST /mandates`                                                                                | `bacp-browse`                                                                                                       | None on the network. The Mandate Manager and PSP create the mandate and the rail authority after the principal approves on the Trusted Surface. | [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md)             |
| Discover          | `POST /discover`                                                                                | `bacp-browse`                                                                                                       | Beckn `search` → `on_search` through the Beckn gateway, with registry lookup                                                                    | [Discovery and Profiles](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/index.md)          |
| Negotiate         | `/negotiations`, `/negotiations/{id}/offers`, `/negotiations/{id}/accept`, `/rfqs`, `/auctions` | `bacp-browse` for non-binding messages; `bacp-negotiate` for firm offers, ACCEPT, auction creation, bids and awards | `select` / `on_select` rounds carrying negotiation tags                                                                                         | [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md)                   |
| Checkout          | `POST /sessions`, `PUT /sessions/{id}`                                                          | `bacp-browse`                                                                                                       | `select` → `on_select` (quote), then `init` → `on_init` (signed quote, payment terms)                                                           | [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md)            |
| Pay               | `POST /sessions/{id}/complete`                                                                  | `bacp-pay`                                                                                                          | Basket-blind debit through the payer PSP, then `confirm` → `on_confirm` with the rail reference                                                 | [Payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md)                         |
| Fulfil            | `GET /orders/{id}` and webhooks                                                                 | `bacp-browse`                                                                                                       | `status` and unsolicited `on_status` (`track` is proposed)                                                                                      | [Orders and Post-order](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/index.md) |
| Return and refund | `POST /orders/{id}/returns`, `POST /orders/{id}/cancel`                                         | `bacp-post-order`                                                                                                   | `update` (return) or `cancel`, then a refund to the original source                                                                             | [Orders and Post-order](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/index.md) |
| Grievance         | `POST /issues`, `POST /issues/{id}/actions`                                                     | `bacp-post-order`                                                                                                   | IGM 2.0 `issue` / `on_issue` with an `AI_AGENT` actor (Proposed) and an evidence bundle                                                         | [Evidence and Instruction Log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/index.md)     |

Revocation can happen at any point. A revoked mandate stops new commitments within 60 seconds. Protective actions on orders already placed under it (cancel, return, grievance) remain allowed with the principal present (`presence: HP`).

[Getting Started](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/getting-started/index.md) walks through one complete transaction.

## The model proposes, a deterministic engine decides

BACP separates proposing from deciding.

- The agent, and any LLM behind it, MAY propose anything: a search, a cart, a counter-offer, a return.
- A **deterministic, non-LLM engine** inside the gateway trust zone decides whether a proposal becomes a commitment. For checkout this is the mandate verifier, which runs authoritatively on every `complete` and as an advisory pre-check on every `PUT /sessions/{id}`. For negotiation it is the negotiation guard, which runs on every outgoing firm counter-offer, ACCEPT, bid and award, and on every incoming offer.
- The engine MUST fail closed: any failure, unknown constraint or unevaluable input rejects the commitment. The first failing check wins.
- The engine's outcome is limited to *pass*, *reject* or *escalate to the principal*. When the engine escalates, the decision moves to the principal on the Trusted Surface, never back to the LLM. In negotiation the LLM sees only the verdicts `acceptable`, `not_acceptable` or `needs_escalation`, never the principal's bounds.
- Free text from counterparties (product descriptions, seller chat) is untrusted input. It is returned to the agent only as data and can never widen a mandate.
- Budgets, usage counts and rail caps are evaluated against an atomic reservation ledger, so concurrent requests cannot together exceed a budget.

The detailed evaluation order is defined in [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md) and [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md).

## Protocol versioning

BACP versions are calendar dates in the form `YYYY-MM-DD`. A dated version is a snapshot of the whole protocol: the specification pages, the JSON Schemas, the OpenAPI document, the handler registry and the conformance manifest, published together.

- The current dated release is `2026-10-18`. The working version on `main` is `draft`, which has no date and may change without notice.
- A gateway publishes the versions it supports in its [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document) (`bacp.version` and `bacp.supported_versions`). An agent MUST use a version that the gateway lists.
- Schema `$id`s under `https://bacp.dev/schemas/` resolve to the latest release. Pinned copies live under `https://bacp.dev/YYYY-MM-DD/schemas/`.

The release process, URL scheme and breaking-change policy are defined on the [Versioning](https://bacp.dev/versioning/) page.

## Extensibility

BACP is designed to be extended without breaking existing participants, with one deliberate exception: authority is never extended silently.

1. **Unknown fields are ignored; a member of an unlisted capability is refused.** A receiver MUST ignore fields it does not understand in requests, responses, webhooks and network messages, unless the schema for that object forbids additional properties. A network participant that does not speak BACP ignores `context.bacp`. The exception is a request member that a capability owns, where the receiver's version defines the capability but the receiver does not list it: the receiver MUST refuse it with `400 capability_unsupported` at the member's path, MUST create or change nothing, and MUST NOT ignore it. An ignored `discounts` member would let an agent tell the principal that a coupon was applied when it was not. Fields from a version that the receiver does not implement are ignored as before. See [Capabilities](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#capabilities).
1. **Unknown mandate constraints fail closed.** A verifier that meets a constraint key it does not understand, in any mandate, MUST reject the mandate (`constraint_unknown`). An unknown constraint might be the very limit the principal relied on.
1. **New constraints go in new mandates.** Because existing AP2-compatible verifiers fail closed on unknown constraints, a new family of bounds is carried in a separate mandate type, as negotiation bounds are, rather than added to Checkout or Payment Mandates.
1. **Closed objects stay closed.** Objects whose schema forbids additional properties (for example the mandate `constraints` object, `context.bacp` and the term-sheet issue groups) MUST NOT carry extra fields. Extra negotiable issues go only under namespaced `extensions`, and the negotiation guard fails closed on any extension issue that is not agreed.
1. **Error codes are registered.** A new error code MUST be registered with its HTTP status and resolution before use. A client that meets an unregistered code MUST act on the HTTP status class and MUST NOT retry a 4xx with a new `Idempotency-Key`. See [Errors](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/index.md).
1. **Unknown handlers fail closed.** A payment handler reference that does not resolve in the [handler registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md) MUST be treated as not eligible. Resolving a handler does not make it eligible: reserved and deprecated handlers MUST NOT back a payment.
1. **Namespaces.** Indian rails and instruments use `in.<family>.<variant>` handler ids. BACP-native constructs use `bacp.<construct>`. Capabilities use `in.bacp.*`. The `in.*` ids are governed by the BACP registries and are **not bound to a DNS name**: nothing about a domain such as `bacp.in`, which an unrelated party holds (as of 18-10-2026), makes an `in.*` id or a schema URL under it trustworthy. BACP never declares an `in.*` id together with a `schema` in a profile that a UCP platform reads, and a BACP gateway MUST NOT accept or fetch a schema for an `in.*` id from any source.
1. **Extensions come from a digest-pinned registry and are never fetched.** A third-party extension is declared in `capability_declarations` by registry reference and schema digest ([Capability declarations](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#capability-declarations)), and its payload travels under `ext.<id>`. A gateway MUST NOT fetch an extension's schema at run time. An `ext` member that touches an amount, the payee, presence, a mandate or a disclosure is *critical*: it is refused unless its capability is listed and the amount also appears as a line of the base `totals`, and it is never a mandate constraint.

# Conformance

This page defines what it means to conform to BACP: the conformance levels a participant can claim, the requirements each role MUST meet, the invariants that must hold after every interaction, and how conformance is tested and attested.

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

Testing status

The levels and checklists on this page are normative for BACP `2026-10-18`. As of 17-10-2026, the automated conformance suite and the reference implementation are not yet published. Until they are, conformance is self-declared against these checklists.

## Principles

BACP treats conformance as **data**, not as code. A conformance rule that lives only inside a test tool cannot be read, compared between versions or signed on its own, and a validator that fails open, or checks only logs, proves little. So:

1. **Declarative cases.** Every conformance case MUST be data: a manifest entry naming its fixture, its steps as request templates, and its expected outcomes (HTTP status, error `code`, `resolution`, resulting state, and invariants). The test runner interprets the manifest; it is never the place where a rule is defined.
1. **Fail closed.** The runner MUST fail a case, and the level, on an unknown assertion kind, a missing expectation, a skipped case, an unregistered error code or an exception. A level is attested only if every required case passes. There is no "warn and continue" mode.
1. **Live and log.** Cases MUST drive the system under test live, with signed requests and mock counterparties, **and** check the resulting artefacts: the instruction-log chain, receipts, the Beckn message trace and webhooks. Checking logs alone is not sufficient.
1. **Invariants after every case.** The runner MUST evaluate the [global invariants](#global-invariants) after every case of a level, not only in dedicated cases.
1. **Stable ids and traceability.** Each case has a stable case id and an expected verdict. Requirement ids and specification sections are carried as data, so the traceability matrix is generated rather than hand-written.
1. **Versioned and signed.** The manifest is versioned with the specification (see [Versioning](https://bacp.dev/versioning/)). A run produces a published report, and a conformance authority on the [public list](#conformance-authority-list) may sign a [conformance attestation](#conformance-attestation) listing the levels passed.
1. **Portable.** Schemas are resolved by their `$id` from the published schema bundle, never from a local path.
1. **Every required code is tested.** Every registered error or message code that a level requires MUST have at least one conformance case before that level can be attested.
