### Profile maturity

Each [trade profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/trade-profiles/#profile-table) carries a **maturity** label (as of 18-10-2026). The label changes no case. It says whether a conformance attestation can cover the profile.

| Maturity         | Profiles                                                                                 | Conformance scope of this release                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **launch**       | `b2c.ecom` (marketplace and quick commerce), `kirana.khata`, `subscription`, `ticketing` | Stable. An attestation MAY cover the levels the profile needs.                                                                                                                                                               |
| **proposed**     | `fmcg.distribution`, `b2b.procurement`, `services`, `social`                             | In the release. An attestation MAY cover the levels the profile needs, and the rules MAY change in a later dated release.                                                                                                    |
| **experimental** | `gem`, `agri`, `crossborder`, `high_value`, `c2c.rental`, `assisted.rural`               | Outside the scope. No attestation covers the profile, and a verifier MUST NOT treat a claim of one of these profiles as conformance. A party MAY refuse it with `capabilities_incompatible`, reason `profile_not_supported`. |

### Claiming a level

- A participant declares the levels it claims in its [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document) and carries them in its conformance credential. An AgentCredential carries them in `conformance.levels[]`, using the level ids above, with the signed attestation in `conformance.attestation` (see [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#agentcredential)).
- A participant that claims a level MUST pass every case of that level **and** of every level it requires.
- A gateway MAY offer a payment handler whose registry status is `pilot` only if its [conformance attestation](#conformance-attestation) lists that pilot in `pilots[]` and has not expired.
- Counterparties MAY check a participant's attestation at registry lookup (see [Registry lookup](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#registry-lookup)).

### Conformance attestation

A conformance attestation is a compact JWS issued after a conformance run (see [Principles](#principles), item 6). A gateway publishes its attestation in its [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document) (`conformance.attestation`), and an AgentCredential carries the agent's in `conformance.attestation`.

The payload is defined by [`conformance-attestation.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/conformance-attestation.json). The JOSE header `typ` MUST be `bacp-conformance+jwt` (RFC 8725 section 3.11); an attestation with any other `typ` is refused. All fields below are REQUIRED, and no other claim is allowed.

| Field                              | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `iss`                              | The `ca_id` of the entry in the [conformance-authority list](#conformance-authority-list) whose key signed the attestation.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `sub`                              | The participant the attestation is about: the gateway's subscriber id, the agent id or the Mandate Manager's registry id. For a `trusted_surface`, the subscriber id of the Mandate Manager or payer PSP that operates the Trusted Surface.                                                              |
| `subject_role`                     | `gateway`, `agent`, `mm` or `trusted_surface`. `trusted_surface` is the Trusted Surface of a Mandate Manager or a payer PSP, attested at level `bacp.ts.1` (`system_under_test: trusted_surface`). Only a gateway may list pilot handlers: for `agent`, `mm` and `trusted_surface`, `pilots[]` is empty. |
| `scope`                            | The constant `bacp-protocol-conformance`. It states that the attestation covers BACP protocol conformance and nothing else.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `iat`, `exp`                       | Issue and expiry time, as NumericDates (seconds since the epoch; NumericDate is defined in RFC 7519 §2, `exp` in §4.1.4 and `iat` in §4.1.6). `exp` is at most 180 days after `iat`. After `exp`, no verifier may rely on the attestation.                                                               |
| `jti`                              | The attestation's unique id (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$`). A mandate's `rail_binding.conformance` records it, and a pause for a lapsed attestation logs it.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `bacp_version`, `registry_version` | The dated BACP release whose cases were run, and the dated release of the handler registry that the run used.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `levels[]`                         | The [level ids](#conformance-levels) passed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `pilots[]`                         | The canonical ids of the `pilot` payment handlers whose cases the gateway passed and that it may offer. Empty when there are none. A legacy alias is not a canonical id.                                                                                                                                 |
| `manifest_digest`                  | `sha-256:` digest of the conformance-case manifest that was run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `report_digest`                    | `sha-256:` digest of the published, reproducible run report behind the attestation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `status`                           | Where the attestation's revocation status is published: `{"status_list": {"uri": …, "idx": …}}`, the same shape as an AgentCredential's `status` ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#agentcredential)).                                      |

The attestation is a statement that the subject passed BACP protocol tests. It MUST NOT be offered or accepted in place of any rail onboarding, permission or certification, and MUST NOT be presented as approval by NPCI, RBI, ONDC or any public body. A gateway or agent that shows it to a principal says "passed BACP protocol tests" (and the same in `hi-IN`, in Devanagari) and MUST NOT use the words "certified", "approved", "verified" or "accredited", or their `hi-IN` equivalents, or any logo of NPCI, RBI or ONDC, and MUST NOT show `kind` to a principal.

### Conformance-authority list

The **conformance-authority list** is the only way to admit a signer of conformance attestations. It is a public, dated list that each dated BACP release publishes as `source/registry/conformance-authorities.json`, and whose digest the release manifest `source/handlers/release.json` records; its schema is [`conformance-authority-list.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/conformance-authority-list.json). The registry role `conformance_authority` ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#conformance-authority-keys)) names a key that signs attestations and nothing else, and only a key of a listed entry qualifies.

- **The list ships empty** in `2026-10-18`. No key qualifies until an entry is added, so a Mandate Manager still refuses open mandates on every `pilot` handler, as it did before this list existed. Adding an entry needs the further approval that [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#interim-maintainer) requires.
- **Who may be listed.** An independent test laboratory (`kind: lab`) or a rail-sponsor bank (`kind: rail_sponsor`). `kind` is for display and grants no extra power. A bank is listed only at its own request and is never the required signer. Every entry names its `operator` (legal name and id), its `funders[]`, its `keys[]`, the `report_uri_template` of its published run reports, its validity period and a `status` pointer.
- **Every entry is scoped.** `scope.levels[]` and `scope.pilots[]` (at least one handler) bound what the authority may attest. A pilot outside the entry's `scope.pilots` is refused.
- **A Mandate Manager may only narrow the list.** It MAY publish an exclusion list (`excluded_attesters[]` in its [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document)) and MUST NOT accept a signer that the public list does not contain.
- **A conformance authority only signs and revokes.** It never routes, holds or settles funds. The project's interim maintainer never holds, operates or funds an authority key (GOVERNANCE.md).
- **Separation is checked per mandate.** The Mandate Manager compares the entry's `operator` and `funders[]` with the operators of the attested subject, of the payer PSP and of itself ([Rules](#attestation-rules)).
- **Fees and reports.** Every entry carries `fee_model{basis: per_run | subscription, outcome_contingent: false, terms_uri}`, so that no fee depends on whether the subject passes, and `publishes_all_runs: true`, so that the report of every run, passes and failures, is published. No fee is payable to the project for a list entry ([GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#interim-maintainer)). A run report carries a `conflict_declaration{sponsor_of_subject, other}`, which `report_digest` covers: `sponsor_of_subject` is `true` when the authority, its operator or a funder sponsors the attested subject, and `other` states any other relationship, or `none`.

#### Rules

- **At issuance.** Before a Mandate Manager issues an open payment mandate on a handler whose registry status is `pilot`, it MUST verify the gateway's attestation, which the gateway forwards in the mandate request (`gateway_attestation`). The Mandate Manager MUST refuse issuance with `rail_binding_not_open_eligible` ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)) when any of these holds:
  - the JOSE `typ` is any value other than `bacp-conformance+jwt`;
  - the signing key, selected by the `kid` of the JOSE header, is not in the `keys[]` of an entry of the [conformance-authority list](#conformance-authority-list) of the latest publication of the registry files (the highest `registry_serial` of the release manifest); the time of the check is outside the entry's `valid_from` to `valid_until`; or the entry's status is revoked; while the list has no entry, no key qualifies, so a Mandate Manager refuses open mandates on every `pilot` handler, including `in.upi.circle` and `in.card.agentic`;
  - the entry is in the Mandate Manager's published exclusion list (`reasons: [attester_not_accepted]`);
  - a `pilots[]` member is outside the entry's `scope.pilots`, or the handler is not in `pilots[]`;
  - `exp` is passed, or `exp − iat` is over 180 days (JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so a conformance case tests it);
  - the status is revoked (`reasons: [binding_ineligible]`);
  - the copy of the status list is more than 24 hours old, or the list is unreachable (`reasons: [attestation_status_stale]`, `resolution: recoverable`);
  - the report at the entry's `report_uri_template` for this `jti` is absent, or does not hash to `report_digest`;
  - `registry_version` is older than the registry release in which the bound handler's `status`, `binding` or `mandate_primitives` last changed;
  - `sub` is not the subscriber that the signing key of the forwarded request resolves to in the registry (the Mandate Manager does not take `sub` from a body field);
  - the entry's operator, or any of its funders, is the same operator as `sub`, as the payer PSP in `rail_binding.psp_id` or as the issuing Mandate Manager, or any of those operators is unknown (`reasons: [attester_not_independent]`). A participant's operator is the `operator` of its [registry record](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#registry-lookup) with `assertion: registry`: a profile, a request body, the attestation or an `operator` whose `assertion` is `declared` never supplies it, and an absent or `declared` operator is unknown. Two operators are the same when they share a CIN, an LLPIN or a PAN, or a `group_id`; a GSTIN alone never decides it, because one entity can hold several. The entry's `operator.id` and the `id` of each of its `funders[]` are compared with the `entity_ids[]` of the other operators, and so is each of its `funder_ids[]`. When the entry names a `group_id`, a compared record that has none is unknown.
- **Binding.** The Mandate Manager MUST write `rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti}` on every open payment mandate bound to a `pilot` handler. The schema leaves the object optional, because a `live` handler needs none; this rule makes it REQUIRED for pilot bindings.
- **At `complete`.** On a pilot handler the gateway MUST refuse (`400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`) when `rail_binding.conformance` is absent or its `sub` is not itself. It MUST re-check, at every `complete`, the gateway's current attestation for the pilot: the bound `jti`, or after a lift the newer attestation from the same authority that lifted the pause, whose `sub` is itself and whose `pilots[]` lists the bound handler, under the same 24-hour rule. `rail_binding.conformance` records the attestation verified at issuance and is not rewritten; the InstructionLog entry for a lift records the new `jti`. It MUST also check, under the same 24-hour rule, that `rail_binding.conformance.iss` is still an entry of the list, within its validity and not revoked, that the attestation's key is still in its `keys[]`, and that the bound handler is still in its `scope.pilots`. An entry that is removed, lapsed or revoked, or a key that is removed, is a lapse of the attestation: the gateway adds `binding_ineligible` with cause `attestation`. While [Q-77](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-77) is open, it refuses every human-not-present `complete` under an open mandate on `in.upi.circle` with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`.
- **Freshness.** An attestation status list that is more than 24 hours old, or unreachable, is refused for issuance and for a human-not-present `complete` on a pilot handler, and the `complete` returns `reasons: [attestation_status_stale]` with `resolution: recoverable` and no pause. An agent that receives `attestation_status_stale` tells the principal that human-not-present payment on this handler is unavailable for now, and offers the human-present step. It never blocks a status check, a reversal, a refund or a post-order write. A revoked or expired attestation, at a re-check, pauses the mandate ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)).
- **Test fixtures.** The fixture `typ` `bacp-conformance-test+jwt` MUST be refused by every Mandate Manager outside a conformance harness.
- **No other use.** A conformance authority only signs and revokes; the attestation MUST NOT be offered or accepted in place of any rail onboarding, permission or certification, and MUST NOT be presented as approval by NPCI, RBI, ONDC or any public body.
- **Unchanged for `in.upi.circle`.** Listing Circle in an authority's scope and in an attestation does not open the human-not-present path on `in.upi.circle` ([UPI Circle](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/#upi-circle-delegate)).

No open question blocks a conformance level of `2026-10-18`; the remaining ones are listed on [Open Questions](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/index.md), each with a fail-safe default that the conformance cases test. Core is attested against stable vectors: the signature algorithms ES256 and EdDSA, both mandatory to verify ([Q-42](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-42)), the attached-JWS encoding used to close open mandates ([Q-41](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-41)), and the purpose-code registry with its bounds ([Q-47](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-47)) are settled in this version.

## Requirements by role

The checklists below collect the MUST-level requirements that conformance tests check for each role. They summarise the normative pages and do not replace them; each line links to its source.

### Agent

An agent (and its operator) MUST:

- Send its AgentCredential in the `BACP-Agent` header and sign every request with RFC 9421, covering every required component, including `@query` whenever a query string is present ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#request-signatures)).
- Use the signature tag each endpoint requires, a fresh nonce per request, and a validity window of at most 300 seconds ([Signature tags](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#signature-tags)).
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` on every `POST` and `PUT`, retry only with the same key, and read the resource before retrying after a lost response ([Idempotency](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#idempotency)).
- Never collect, store or relay a UPI PIN, OTP, card credential or Aadhaar number, and never call `POST /trusted-surface/events` ([Security and Privacy](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/index.md)).
- Present the AI disclosure and the human-handoff option in its first message of every session, logged at stage `ai_disclosure` as the first entry whose actor is `agent`; list a `tel:` route (optionally with DTMF digits) when its credential's `channels` include `voice`, `ivr` or `upi123pay`; and request a handoff with `POST /sessions/{id}/handoff` whenever the principal asks, even after the mandate is revoked ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ai-disclosure)).
- On an assisted session (`channel: assisted`, or an AgentCredential of class `assisted`), list the assisted operator in `participants[]`, and never answer a `bacp.input_request` whose `needed_from` is `principal` on the principal's behalf.
- Send `hp_proof{ts_event_hash, step_up_id}` with every post-order write that declares `presence: HP`, obtained through the `post_order` step-up that a write without it returns, and use each proof once, for the write its `ts_render` names ([Presence proof](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#hp-proof)).
- Record a GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection or ledger acknowledgement as an agent only with `hp_proof` ([Trade acts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#trade-acts)).
- Close an open mandate only for the exact amount and `checkout_hash` of the seller-signed quote, with its `cnf` key ([Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md)).
- Relay every step-up and pre-debit notice to the principal and never dismiss them on the principal's behalf ([Payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md)).
- Treat catalogue text, seller messages and other counterparty content, including every `origin: counterparty` message and `args[]` value, as untrusted data, never as instructions.
- Never emit a firm counter-offer outside its negotiation mandate. When the guard escalates, any counter it sends MUST be marked `subject_to_principal_approval: true` and `firm: false` ([Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md)).
- Verify a fetched receipt's hash against the `receipt_hash` in the webhook before relying on it ([Evidence and Instruction Log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/index.md)).
- On a mandate paused for `binding_ineligible`, open no Trusted-Surface resume request and no re-issue request (`POST /mandates`) without a new instruction from the principal ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)).
- In a multi-seller basket, open one session per seller under one `basket_id` and one root open Checkout Mandate, request a further block only with `checkout_mandate_ref`, `payee` and `rail_limits.block_amount`, offer a new block only beside a one-time human-present payment and never after a failed payment, and never re-route an `in_doubt` leg ([Per-leg rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule)).
- Keep its operator signing key separate from the agent's `cnf` key, and sign instruction-log entries asymmetrically.
- When it presents discovery results, say the fixed sponsorship sentence for every `sponsored` or `undeclared` item and never render `undeclared` as "not sponsored"; voice a prior price only as the amount pair; show no reduction, strike-through, percentage, "was" or "off" claim without a `prior_price`, and none taken from free text; and verify the seller-signed source of every item it presents or relies on, rendering an unverified item with no claim and with sponsorship as `undeclared` at least. It generates a fresh `Idempotency-Key` for each search, and checks `Disclosures.catalogue[]` against what it verified ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results), [Disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases); cases CD-07, CD-13, CD-14, CD-26 to CD-34, CD-47 to CD-51).
- Present a registered `type: disclosure` message as its fixed phrase, never as the message's `content`, and not hand over a step-up whose `catalogue_disclosure[]` does not match `Disclosures.catalogue[]` ([Message object](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/#message-object); cases CD-41, CD-R09, CD-R10).
- Submit no affiliate code of its operator when no human is present, and tell a present principal before it submits one ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts); case CD-50).
- Learn the `ts_event_hash` of a post-order approval only from `GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}` or `step_up.updated`, check the host of a `trusted_surface_url` against `StepUp.surface`, keep its voice channel off the Trusted Surface's call leg, and never send `afa_ref`, `ref_verification: verified` or `confirmation_floor` ([Presence proof](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#hp-proof); cases T6-14, T6-19, T6-38, T6-42, T6-47c).

### Gateway

A BACP gateway MUST:

- Publish a valid [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document) at `/.well-known/bacp`, including `message_id_namespace`.
- Decide a withdraw and accept crossing only by transcript positions inside the loser's own chain, return a `CounterSignaturePayload` in the synchronous response to every firm message within 5 seconds of the sender's dispatch on the sender's monotonic clock, return a byte-identical receipt on re-delivery, treat an unprovable order as `crossing_contested` and never as a breach, raise a contested crossing to its own principal without auto-confirming (a seller gateway too), keep one linearisable chain per `negotiation_id`, and fill `sender_log_seq`, `sender_log_prev` and `protocol_terms` itself ([Signed seller acceptance and clock skew](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#signed-seller-acceptance-and-clock-skew); cases T5-07 to T5-17, T5-19 to T5-24, T5-42, T5-45, T5-50).
- Raise a negotiation step-up only on an outgoing accept or firm-counter attempt, treat an absent `accept_confirmation` as `ask`, honour `autonomous` only with a usable `notice_route`, deliver the notice of an autonomous act through that route and not through the agent, accept a purchase-offer withdrawal, and accept a decline of an `AGREED` or `BOUND` deal only as the Trusted Surface event (cases T5-03, T5-29 to T5-40).
- Refuse request bodies over 256 KiB with `413`, then verify signatures on the raw bytes before parsing, in the specified order, with the replay cache and the 5-second skew ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#verification-order)).
- Verify each AgentCredential against the registry and its status list, and enforce that the tag is allowed for the endpoint and listed in the credential's `purposes`.
- Implement idempotency exactly as specified, including per-agent quotas, `Idempotent-Replayed`, never storing `5xx`, and failing closed with `503` when the store is unavailable ([Idempotency](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#idempotency)).
- Run the deterministic mandate verifier on every `complete`, fail closed, reject unknown constraints, and reject non-positive payable amounts ([Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md)).
- Re-check the open mandate's handler binding (status, conformance attestation and `rail_binding.primitive`) against the current registry on every `complete`, taken from the dated release; adopt a status downgrade within 24 hours of its `published_at`, refuse an HNP `complete` on a handler whose descriptor copy is more than 24 hours old (`reasons: [registry_copy_stale]`, `resolution: recoverable`, no pause), serve `GET /payment-handlers` with a `Cache-Control` `max-age` of at most 86400, and add the pause reason `binding_ineligible`, with the `registry_version` and `registry_serial` that caused it, to every affected mandate when a registry or attestation change makes its binding ineligible. Keep pause reasons as a set: keep a mandate `PAUSED` while any reason remains, remove only `binding_ineligible` and only on a strictly newer registry version in which the binding is eligible, pause a legacy mandate with `reissue_required` and never remove it, and write every addition and removal to the InstructionLog with the `registry_version` ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)).
- On a pilot handler, refuse a `complete` whose mandate has no `rail_binding.conformance` or names another gateway, re-check the bound attestation's `jti` (expiry, `pilots[]` and status) at every `complete`, pause the mandate with `binding_ineligible` (cause `attestation`, the `jti` logged) when it is revoked or expired, and for a status that is more than 24 hours old or unreachable refuse an HNP `complete` with `reasons: [attestation_status_stale]`, `resolution: recoverable` and no pause ([Conformance attestation](#attestation-rules); cases S-F1, S-F1-missing, S-F7, CA-04b, CA-07).
- Evaluate budgets, usage, rail caps and split-order detection inside one atomic section keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate against a reservation ledger, reserve every tender of a split-tender plan in that one section, decrement budgets only from PSP-signed receipts, and leave no reservation behind once every payment has resolved.
- Never rely on rail limits to bound BACP budgets.
- Count every Reserve Pay block as reserved spend at its full attested amount until its revocation is confirmed or it expires, also against any new root of the same principal; apply the activation of a sibling block inside the root's atomic section and refuse it (`403 mandate_exhausted`) when the block no longer fits the headroom of every budget window; hold the seller's BPP-signed payment terms (the raw `on_init` body and its Beckn `Authorization` header) for every Reserve Pay block before the request reaches the Trusted Surface, or refuse it (`400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`); where the payer PSP attests a block-debit feed, count an unmatched debit as settled spend and add the pause reason `unmatched_rail_debit`, which only the principal removes ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)).
- For a multi-seller basket: refuse a `basket_id` shared across principals, presence or root open Checkout Mandates (`400 invalid_request` at `$.basket_id`) and never send it to the network or the PSP; plan every leg under the per-leg rule, log chosen and skipped rungs in `comparison[]`, run the headroom check on every block and raise any `rail_fallback` step-up before the first debit; consume each `covers[]` entry once in the root-Checkout-Mandate atomic section; never let one payment span sellers; and never re-route an `in_doubt` leg ([Multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket)).
- Move a session to `requires_escalation` for every step-up, with a Trusted Surface link valid for at most 15 minutes (at least 5 for `ivr_callback` and `assisted`), and complete only after a signed approval from the Trusted Surface ([Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md)).
- Sign a `ts_render` once for every step-up, never change it, and serve it by `step_up_id` only to the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP ([Step-up signers](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-signers): for a session step-up, the PSP in `rail_binding.psp_id` of the open Payment Mandate under the session's mandate; for a `post_order` step-up, the PSP in `auth_binding.psp_id` of the order's closed Payment Mandates) (`404 not_found` to any other registry key, `429` above a rate limit counted per caller key before the lookup); refuse an approval from any other registry key (`404 not_found`), without `presentation`, without `presentation.checkout_hash` or with `user_action: decline` (`400 invalid_request`), with a `content_hash` that is not the hash of the `ts_render` (`403 ts_render_mismatch`), acted on after `expires_at` (`step_up_expired`), or, on an assisted session, without the principal's own factor or an `assisted_by` that is an assisted operator of the session (`403 presence_not_proven`); and skip evaluation step 8 only while the session's `checkout_hash` equals the approval's ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#presentation)).
- Accept a post-order write (cancel, return, raise issue, issue action) with `presence: HP` and a valid `hp_proof` on an order whose mandate is `REVOKED`, `PAUSED` (for every pause reason), `EXPIRED` or `EXHAUSTED`, and refuse it without HP with `403 presence_not_allowed`; let a status check, a reversal and a refund to the original source of a debit that is in the ledger proceed under a binding pause, and refuse a refund to any other destination (cases T2-OPS-01 to T2-OPS-03, S-F6b; [Post-order gate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#post-order-gate)).
- Refuse every post-order write with `presence: HP` that lacks a valid `hp_proof` (`403 presence_not_proven`, with a `post_order` step-up when the proof is missing) before any network message; accept a proof only for the action, order and issue its `ts_render` names (for an issue action, only while the issue's `resolution` still hashes to its `subject_hash`), and consume it once inside the atomic section keyed on the order's root Checkout Mandate; keep at most one pending `post_order` step-up per `(order_id, action, issue_id)`, return it again on a repeat, and rate-limit their creation (`429`) ([Post-order gate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#post-order-gate)).
- Accept `POST /sessions/{id}/handoff` in every state and after revocation; refuse the agent's `PUT` and `complete` in `human_handoff` with `409 session_state_conflict`, and hold every Trusted Surface approval until release; set `handoff.accepted_by` only from a support operator key under tag `bacp-handoff`; accept `action: release` only from that key, or from the agent while `accepted_by` is absent, and then return the session to `incomplete`; run `accept` and `release` as compare-and-set on `accepted_by` and `ended_at`, and refuse an `accept` after `ended_at` with `409 session_state_conflict`; and refuse `POST /sessions` for an assisted session with no `assisted_operator` participant ([Human handoff](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#handoff)).
- Never put counterparty text in a gateway-written message `content`; carry it in `args[]` with `origin: counterparty`, and label it visibly in every text rendering ([Messages](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#messages)).
- Over MCP, signal a step-up by URL-mode elicitation when the client declared it, and `insufficient_scope` otherwise; never treat an elicitation `accept` as an approval ([MCP and A2A](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/mcp-a2a/#mcp-results)).
- Apply every fail-safe default as stated in the release it claims, never a relaxed form ([Fail-safe defaults](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#fail-safe)).
- Debit at most once per closed payment mandate and per `checkout_hash`; handle `in_doubt` without a new debit and `debited_not_confirmed` with an immediate refund to source ([Payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md)).
- Send the PSP only payee, amount, rail reference, mandate reference and checkout hash: never the basket.
- Verify, before money moves, that the collecting party is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank.
- Remove pre-ticked add-ons, flag drip pricing, and refuse to reach `ready_for_complete` while a required disclosure is missing.
- Refuse to share personal data outside the mandate's `data_scopes` or not covered by a consent receipt.
- Add `context.bacp` to every BACP-originated network message, with `ai_disclosure: true`, `mandate_ref` on `init`, `confirm`, `update`, `cancel` and IGM `issue`, and the instruction-log head on every committing message, and mirror `ai_disclosure` into the `bacp` tag group ([Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/index.md)).
- Put every signed Trusted Surface event of a transaction, verbatim, in the evidence bundle's `trusted_surface_events[]`, and the `ts_render` of every step-up event, byte-identical, in `ts_renders[]` ([Evidence bundle](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#bundle)).
- Send `acting_for.gstin` and `acting_for.display_name` to a seller only when the mandate's `data_scopes` include `ACTING_FOR` ([Mirroring](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#mirroring)).
- Derive Beckn `message_id`s deterministically and bind each callback to its request ([Network leg signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#network-leg-signing)).
- On mandate revocation, cancel open sessions and refuse new commitments, while still allowing cancel, return and grievance on existing orders.
- Sign webhooks, embed only receipt references (never signed receipts), and never send personal data outside the agent's `data_scopes` or any negotiation bound.
- Accept `POST /trusted-surface/events` only from the registry key of the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP, signed under `bacp-ts` with no `BACP-Agent` header.
- Return errors through the two-channel model with registered codes, and document every status each operation can return ([Errors](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/index.md)).
- Run the negotiation guard on every outgoing firm counter-offer, ACCEPT, bid and award, and never reveal the reservation price or `total_max` (Negotiation level and above).
- Refuse a firm offer without `acceptance_revocation` and never insert a value; refuse `allowed_until_receipt` on every leg, incoming or in the principal's own draft (`capabilities_incompatible`); apply the value rules by leg and session, with the profile fixed at session open and the `acting_for` cross-check for consumer sessions; accept a `waived` offer without the principal only against a basis document obtained from the principal before the offer arrived; on a Beckn leg excuse no schema error other than a missing `waiver_basis`; release exposure once per reservation; refuse every `accept_revoke` with `accept_revoke_not_allowed`; apply the tag and presence rules for `accept_revoke`; and accept a negotiation approval only as `negotiation.step_up.approved` whose `presentation.offer_hash` equals the `ts_render`'s and the offer's (`403 ts_render_mismatch`) ([Acceptance revocation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation); cases T3-01 to T3-30 outside the Proposed (sunset) block).
- Return `sponsorship` on every discovery item with the monotone OR rule, relay the seller's `prior_price`, `mrp`, `tax_inclusive` and sponsorship unaltered, never create a `prior_price`, drop an invalid one with `prior_price_invalid`, state `ranking.sponsored` as the OR of the items, give every `results[]` entry the `source_digest` of one signed callback, keep and serve those callbacks, and sign the `POST /discover` response ([Catalogue disclosures](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures); cases CD-02 to CD-06, CD-09 to CD-12, CD-15, CD-20 to CD-22, CD-32).
- Report `discovery_price_changed` (escalating only for an item shown with a `prior_price`), fill `Disclosures.catalogue[]`, emit the registered `type: disclosure` messages, carry `catalogue_disclosure[]` on session step-ups, and refuse a `step_up.approved` whose `presentation.renders` lacks it ([Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#update), [Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-catalogue-disclosure); cases CD-16 to CD-19, CD-35, CD-40, CD-R11).
- Apply discounts only from the seller-signed quote, never submit a code the agent did not send, report each rejected code, rate-limit rejected codes, and refund from the seller-signed revised quote ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts); cases CD-42 to CD-46, CD-52, CD-R13 to CD-R18).
- Mint a `trusted_surface_url` only on an origin of the step-up's signer, push content-free through `ts_notify_url` or answer `503 trusted_surface_unavailable`; refuse `voice_confirm_plus_device` on `rail_auth` and on a debit-releasing `confirm`; bind a handoff to the session's agent operator's support operator key; serve `GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}` to the issuing credential only; match a `RETURN` or `CANCEL` field by field with an overlap rule; and apply the decline cool-off, the re-prompt cap and the declared limits ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#step-up-limits); cases T6-05 to T6-09, T6-15 to T6-30, T6-33b, T6-35 to T6-42, T6-44b, T6-46 to T6-49).
- Refuse an open mandate at a gateway that is not its `agent.bap_id`, take the principal section before the root section (K1 before K2), write a firm commitment into the root's ledger keyed by `offer_hash`, allow one debit per `checkout_hash` per root inside the root's section, send a signed `MandateEvent` to the `audit_uri` for each use, relinquishment and gateway-originated pause change, apply a receipt only when the PSP of the debit signed it, release a budget only on the refund evidence of the [usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger), hold human-not-present payment to a seller with an unresolved reversal, and state the `reversal_basis` and `refund_route` of a `debited_not_confirmed` payment (cases T7-01, T7-02, T7-07 to T7-14, T7-18 to T7-31, T7-36 to T7-38, T7-44).
- Pass the [binding cases](#binding-cases) for every one of `in.bacp.payment_plan`, `in.bacp.ledger`, `in.bacp.trade_document` and `in.bacp.ucp_checkout` that its profile lists, and, whatever it lists, the transport cases that bind every gateway (cases BND-TAG-01, BND-TAG-02, BND-MCP-STDIO-01, BND-MCP-ARGS-01, BND-MCP-IDEM-01).
- Refuse, and never ignore, a request member that a capability owns when its profile does not list that capability (`400 capability_unsupported` at the member's path, nothing created or changed), publish a closed MCP `inputSchema` generated from the capabilities it lists, and, on the UCP projection, refuse a buyer-consent, loyalty or `cart_id` member (cases T8-CAP-01, T8-CAP-03 to T8-CAP-05); require `BACP-Version` as a covered component when its profile lists more than one version, pin a session to its version, put the version in the idempotency fingerprint, run the protective checks of the newest version for `bacp-pay` and `bacp-post-order`, and never fetch an extension schema (cases T8-CAP-02, T8-VER-01 to T8-VER-06, T8-EXT-01 to T8-EXT-03, T8-FETCH-01 to T8-FETCH-04); refuse an off-increment quantity, an unoffered fulfilment option and a basket below `min_order`, refuse an upward weight adjustment that no band allows, accept no substitute without a new `checkout_hash`, assign `added_by` itself, and report every marketing purpose as not granted without a receipt (cases T8-QTY-01, T8-QTY-02, T8-ADJ-01 to T8-ADJ-03, T8-SUB-01, T8-FO-01, T8-MIN-01, T8-POL-01, T8-LINE-01 to T8-LINE-03, T8-GST-01, T8-GST-02, T8-MKT-01, T8-MKT-02, T8-LINK-01, T8-LOY-01).

### Seller (BPP)

A seller app that does not implement BACP needs no change: it ignores `context.bacp`. A **BACP-aware** BPP MUST:

- Reject a duplicate `message_id` within its `ttl` with a NACK.
- Refuse (NACK) an `init`, `confirm`, `update`, `cancel` or IGM `issue` that lacks `context.bacp.mandate_ref`, and verify the `kb_jwt` when one is present.
- Return a signed quote in `on_init`, with the required disclosures.
- Send `bacp.disclosure` tags only with values that are true: a `prior_price` only for a reduction it announced, as the lowest price in the 30 days before `announced_on`, and `sponsored` only as the fact of a paid placement ([Catalogue disclosure mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#disclosure-mapping)).
- In negotiation, sign every message with its registry key, give every firm offer an absolute expiry, verify only the buyer's `within_bounds` attestation, and never request the buyer's bounds.
- Respond to IGM issues whose complainant is an AI agent (an `actors[]` entry with `type = AI_AGENT`, Proposed: [Q-11](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-11)) as to any other complainant.

### Mandate Manager

A Mandate Manager MUST:

- Write `process.accept_confirmation` on every negotiation mandate it issues, present `ask` and `autonomous` with equal weight and preselect neither, capture `process.notice_route`, show the current-stage charge before the factor of a decline of an `AGREED` or `BOUND` deal, and show every time in IST (cases T5-30, T5-38, T5-47).
- Activate a mandate only after an explicit, affirmative approval by the principal on the Trusted Surface. An agent can never activate one.
- Run its Trusted Surface to TS-1 to TS-6 and send a `Presentation` with every `mandate.activated`, `step_up.approved`, `loan.accepted` and `payment.afa_completed` event ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements)).
- State each `catalogue_disclosure[]` entry of a step-up render before the total, in the fixed sentences and with the item name as labelled seller text, and report it in `Presentation.renders` ([Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-catalogue-disclosure); cases CD-37, CD-39).
- Reject, before anything reaches the Trusted Surface, a mandate request outside its purpose's bounds, and reject any mandate whose constraints exceed the limits of its rail binding.
- Refuse to issue an open payment mandate whose `rail_binding.primitive` is not in the handler descriptor's `binding.open_primitives`, whose handler is not open-eligible, or whose handler is `pilot` without a verified gateway [conformance attestation](#conformance-attestation) listing it. Take the registry from the dated release, never from a gateway endpoint, and record its version in `rail_binding.registry_version`.
- Verify the gateway's attestation under every rule of [Conformance attestation](#attestation-rules) (signer in the public list and not excluded, scope, `typ`, 180-day validity, 24-hour status freshness, `sub` equal to the signing gateway, separation of operators), write `rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti}` on every pilot binding, refuse any `in.upi.circle` open mandate request while [Q-77](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-77) is open, read the attestation's status list itself, and refuse the fixture `typ` outside a harness (cases T0-RT-11b, CA-01 to CA-15).
- For a Reserve Pay mandate, require `payee{vpa, bpp_id}` equal to the seller's BPP-signed payment terms and `rail_limits.block_amount`, and refuse a buyer-app payee for HNP; for a request with `checkout_mandate_ref`, build only a Payment Mandate under that `ACTIVE` root of the same principal; keep the block amounts under a root, the requested one included, within its smallest budget `max`; refuse an attested block larger than requested or expiring after the root's `valid_until`, and revoke at the rail any block created for a request it then refuses, reporting `rail_revocation`; key the parallel-root rule on the principal's account behind every pairwise `principal.ref` and refuse a new root while another is `ACTIVE` unless its notice states every other root's budgets and the combined total; show the requested block amount, each budget's remaining amount and, without an attested block-debit feed, the unseen-draw statement in the issuance notice; when a root ends in any way, revoke each block at the rail and send one `mandate.revoked` per sibling with `cascade_of` and `rail_revocation`; and be the only key that fetches and answers a summary step-up ([Sibling Payment Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#sibling-payment-mandates)).
- Copy `agent.bap_id` from the verified AgentCredential, accept `supersedes` only from the Trusted Surface and sign `carried_exposure` from its own use events, accept a `MandateEvent` only from the BAP of `agent.bap_id`, record `event_gap` on a missing `seq`, refuse an attested credit funding (an overdraft without a deposit attestation, or a missing funding) without `credit_funding_allowed`, refuse a gift PPI without principal-side custody, and compare operators only from the registry record's `operator` with `assertion: registry` (cases T7-03 to T7-06, T7-11, T7-12, T7-16, T7-17, T7-34).
- Sign mandates as immutable artefacts. Open mandates carry `cnf`, `data_scopes`, `audit_uri`, a data-retention period and at least one budget or `max_executions`.
- Issue a consent receipt per recipient, in the principal's language, with the withdrawal and grievance routes, and list `ACTING_FOR` in a per-seller receipt before the gateway tells that seller whom the agent acts for.
- Render a step-up only for a mandate of the principal who is logged in (TS-6), keep the principal's `confirmation_floor` and `device_jkt[]` under the principal's own control on the Trusted Surface, and read the floor in full in the activation notice (`bacp.ts.1`; cases T6-02, T6-46, T6-47).
- Publish mandate status in a status list and send signed status events (activation, pause, revocation) to the gateway within 60 seconds.
- Remain data-blind: store mandates and logs only, never order or payment payloads.
- Issue a `within_bounds` attestation only for an ACCEPT inside the negotiation mandate, or after the principal approves on the Trusted Surface (Negotiation level and above).

### PSP and rail

A payer PSP MUST:

- Run, or integrate with, a non-agentic Trusted Surface, and take the PIN or biometric only there, on its own app or on a call that the principal places to the PSP's published number, never on a web page and never on a call that the Trusted Surface places ([PIN rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-pin-rule)).
- Render a step-up only to the principal or payer that the render names (TS-6), draw its own voice challenge, accept a keypad answer as speech, refuse an unknown listed `render_required[]` name and a JWS without `typ: bacp-ts-render+jws`, and render no other language than the step-up's unless the principal chooses it (`bacp.ts.1`; cases T6-02, T6-03, T6-11 to T6-13, T6-32 to T6-34, T6-43 to T6-45).
- Render a step-up only from the `ts_render` fetched by `step_up_id` and its own templates, with counterparty text only in `counterparty_text`, decline no harder than approve, nothing preselected, no urgency text, the principal's language and modality, and audio read in full before the factor; record a `Presentation` whose `content_hash` is the hash of the `ts_render`; on an assisted session, take only the principal's own PIN or enrolled biometric and name the operator in `assisted_by`, taken from `ts_render.assisted_operators[]` ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements)).
- Create the standing authority (block, delegation or mandate) on a primitive listed in the handler's `binding.open_primitives`, and sign a `rail_binding` attestation of its reference, type, primitive, limits, expiry, payee and funding (`deposit` or `credit`); create no Reserve Pay block larger than the requested `rail_limits.block_amount`; never fetch or answer a summary step-up over a basket.
- Refuse a second debit for the same closed payment mandate or `checkout_hash`, refuse any payment request that carries a basket, and refuse a Reserve Pay debit to any payee other than the block's.
- Sign every payment and refund receipt with the rail evidence its handler requires (for UPI, a 12-digit RRN), name the original payment and the `refund_state` on refunds, and never include a PIN, OTP, card number, CVV, expiry or Aadhaar number.
- Refund to the original source.
- Send signed revocation, pre-debit notice and opt-out events to the gateway, and reject debits on a revoked authority.

### Verifier

A verifier of an evidence bundle (a grievance officer's tool, an ODR body, a PSP or a seller) MUST:

- Treat two receipts at one `log_seq` for different entries, a `received_at` that decreases along a chain without `clock_step_observed`, a `CounterSignaturePayload` with a missing member and a negotiation step-up event with no `ts_render` in `ts_renders[]` as `evidence_unverifiable`, and compare times as instants (cases T5-04, T5-06, T5-17, T5-45, T5-49).
- Run the six verification steps and the chain check, and report `evidence_unverifiable` on any failure, including a payment receipt whose payee VPA differs from `checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms` where the bundle carries them, a Reserve Pay payment whose bundle lacks those terms or whose terms' Beckn `Authorization` header does not verify over their `body`, a covered leg whose `covers[]` entry (or `ts_render_digests[]` entry, whose `render_hash` must equal the event's `content_hash`) differs from the leg's quote or payee, a step-up entry without a matching signed Trusted Surface event, an approval without a `Presentation`, a step-up event whose `ts_render` is missing from `ts_renders[]` or differs from the BPP-signed quote in `total`, payee or `checkout_hash`, or from the disclosures hash in `price_breakup_hash`, a step-up render whose `catalogue_disclosure[]` differs from the bundle's `Disclosures.catalogue[]`, omits a qualifying entry or names an item other than the quote's, a `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry whose `source_digest` the agent's `discover` log entry does not list or whose signed source fails (cases CD-36, CD-38, CD-R03, CD-R10), and a log whose first agent entry is not `ai_disclosure` ([Evidence bundle](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#ap2-verification)), a negotiation step-up whose `ts_render` or `presentation` carries an `offer_hash` or an `acceptance_revocation` that differs from the signed offer, and a negotiation transcript in which a later entry has an earlier `received_at` ([Clock skew](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#signed-seller-acceptance-and-clock-skew)).
- Accept a `step_up.*` or `negotiation.step_up.*` event only from a key that [Step-up signers](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-signers) derives from the bundle's mandates (case T6-01).
- Never accept a summary rendered under `in.bacp.evidence.summary.1` as evidence ([Evidence summary](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#evidence-summary)).

### Operator

These are duties of the operator of an agent, gateway or Mandate Manager as a Data Fiduciary under the DPDP Act and Rules. They sit outside the protocol, so the conformance runner does not test them: an operator that claims a level attests to them. Each applies from 13-05-2027 ([Commencement](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#commencement)).

An operator MUST:

- Engage a Data Processor, including a model or LLM host, only under a valid contract (Act s.8(2)) that requires reasonable security safeguards (DPDP Rule 6(1)(f)), and cause the processor to erase personal data whenever the operator must erase it (Act s.8(7)(b)) ([Retention](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#retention)).
- If it is, or belongs to a class notified as, a Significant Data Fiduciary: carry out a Data Protection Impact Assessment and an audit once in every twelve months and have the report of significant observations furnished to the Board (Rule 13(1)–(2)), and verify with due diligence that its algorithmic software, including the agent's models, is not likely to pose a risk to Data Principals' rights (Rule 13(3)). The AgentCredential's `model_family` and `build` feed this inventory ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/index.md)).
- If it is an e-commerce entity with at least two crore registered users in India: erase a Data Principal's personal data three years after she last approached it or exercised her rights (except what she needs to reach her user account or a stored virtual token), and tell her at least 48 hours before the erasure (Rules 8(1)–(2) and the Third Schedule, item 1). Data that another law requires to be kept is kept ([Retention](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#retention)).

## Global invariants

These invariants MUST hold after every conformance case:

| Invariant                          | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `INV-ONE-DEBIT-PER-CHECKOUT`       | At most one money-moving rail transaction per `checkout_hash`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `INV-NO-WRONG-AMOUNT`              | Every debit equals the amount of the session that owns its `checkout_hash`.                                                                                                                                        |
| `INV-EVIDENCE-5-OF-5`              | Every completed order's evidence bundle passes the five AP2 verification steps and step 6 (Trusted Surface events), with a valid instruction-log chain and bundle signature. The id is kept from earlier versions. |
| `INV-GUARDED-COMMITMENT`           | No firm counter-offer, ACCEPT or bid leaves the gateway without a guard pass or a signed step-up approval.                                                                                                         |
| `INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEAK`          | No reservation price or `total_max` value appears in any buyer-originated outgoing message, response, webhook or log. A number the counterparty sent first, and the buyer side merely echoes, is not a leak.       |
| `INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT`          | Once every payment has resolved, no budget reservation remains.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `INV-NO-SIGNED-RECEIPT-IN-WEBHOOK` | No webhook body contains a signed receipt.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `INV-CONTRACT`                     | Every recorded response validates against its documented schema, and no undocumented status is returned.                                                                                                           |

## How conformance is tested

1. **Select levels.** The participant names the levels it claims.
1. **Run the cases.** The runner loads the manifest for those levels (and the levels they require) and drives the system under test with signed requests from a test agent, against mock counterparties: a registry, a BPP, a Mandate Manager and Trusted Surface driver, and a PSP and rail with fault injection (timeouts, debit-then-silence, rejections).
1. **Check outcomes and invariants.** For each case the runner compares the responses, states, messages, rail counts, log entries and webhooks with the case's expectations, then evaluates every global invariant.
1. **Report.** The runner produces a report that anyone can reproduce. If every required case passed, a conformance authority on the [public list](#conformance-authority-list) may sign a [conformance attestation](#conformance-attestation) listing the levels, with the digest of the report.

Informative: suggested manifest layout. The layout is `levels.yaml` (the level table as data), `cases/<level>/*.yaml` (one file per case), `invariants.yaml` and `codes.yaml` (generated from the [error registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/index.md)). A case looks like this:

```
case_id: CORE-ATOM-001
title: Concurrent completes on one open mandate never exceed the budget
level: bacp.core.1
fixture:
  mandate: {purpose: P-GRO-01, rail: in.upi.reservepay, budgets: [{period: P1M, max: {value: 100000, currency: INR}}]}
  rail: {block_amount: 10000000, debit_latency_ms: 20}
  sessions: {count: 20, amount: 100000, state: ready_for_complete}
steps:
  - parallel: 20
    request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, idempotency_key: fresh}
expect:
  responses:
    - {status: 200, body.status: completed, count: 1}
    - {status: 403, code: mandate_exhausted, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 19}
  invariants: [INV-ONE-DEBIT-PER-CHECKOUT, INV-NO-WRONG-AMOUNT, INV-NO-RESERVATION-LEFT]
  rail:
    settled_debits: 1
    settled_amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}
  state:
    session: completed
```

The `expect` vocabulary is closed: status, code, resolution, `reasons`, state, message codes, rail counts, log entries, webhooks, invariants, `exactly_one_of`, `agent_requests`, `beckn`, `mcp` and `verdict`. Anything else fails the case. In detail:

- `webhooks` lists every webhook the case expects, in order, as objects with `type` and, for `mandate.status_changed`, `status`, `reason` and `pause_reasons`; a webhook not listed fails the case, so `webhooks: []` means none is sent.
- A `responses` entry MAY carry `path` (for example `accept` or `complete`) to say which of several parallel requests it answers.
- `exactly_one_of` lists alternative expectation sets; the case passes when exactly one of them holds.
- `agent_requests` counts the requests that an agent under test sends, by method and path or to the Trusted Surface.
- `beckn` lists what the network trace MUST show, for example the tags of the `bacp` tag group as the seller receives them.
- `mcp` gives the signal the MCP server sent for a step-up (`url_elicitation` or `insufficient_scope`).
- `verdict` is the result of a system under test that returns no HTTP response: a verifier's or validator's code (`evidence_unverifiable`, `schema_invalid`, `pass`), a Trusted Surface check (`ts_conformance_fail` with the rule, for example `TS-1`), or properties of a rendered output.
- `state` records the state of each state machine the case touches, keyed by machine. A case that changes the state of a machine MUST record the state it starts in as `fixture.<machine>.state` and the state it ends in as `expect.state.<machine>`, so that a checker can match the case to one transition. A case that is a refusal records the same state in both and shows that nothing changed. `<machine>` is the name of the machine in the specification: `session`, `mandate`, `mandate_request`, `negotiation` and the other machines that appear in `state` keys of the cases on this page. For the `session` machine the fixture key is the existing `sessions.state` (with `count`). A case that touches no state machine records no `state`. The rule applies to every case added from the release that introduces it; earlier cases are not rewritten.

A `POST /mandates` body in a case is an abbreviated fixture: a field that the schema REQUIRES but that the case does not exercise, such as `operator_compensation`, is present in the request under test with a valid value and is left out of the listing.

Fixture and step keys used by the cases on this page:

- `across_replicas: true` sends the parallel requests of a step to different gateway replicas (`gateway: {replicas: n}`).
- `library_level: true` means the case drives the gateway's verifier as a library, because the behaviour has no wire binding in this version.
- `create_session` is a step that opens a new checkout session under the fixture mandate.
- `registry_release.published` is the release time relative to the runner's clock (for example `-25h`).
- `registry_source` is the state of the mock registry source from which the gateway refreshes its descriptor copy: `reachable`, or `{unreachable_since: <time relative to the runner's clock>}`.
- `registry_update` is a step that publishes a newer registry version to the registry source; `sweep` is a step that lets the gateway (or named replicas) apply the registry it holds.
- `registry_by_replica` gives each gateway replica its own registry version and `serial`, to test replicas that lag within the 24-hour window.
- `trusted_surface_event` is a step in which the mock Mandate Manager sends a signed Trusted Surface event (for example `mandate.paused`) to the gateway.
- `system_under_test` may also be `verifier` (the runner hands over a bundle), `schema` (the runner validates a published vector), `trusted_surface` (the runner plays the gateway and inspects what a Mandate Manager or PSP surface renders and records) or `beckn_adapter` (the runner plays a seller behind a validator that strips `context.bacp`).
- The attestation cases use these fixture keys. `conformance_authorities` is the dated list that the Mandate Manager loads (entries with `ca_id`, `operator`, `scope` and, optionally, `kind`); the runner signs an attestation with the key of the entry named in `iss`. `operators` gives the declared operator of each subscriber and registry id, or `unknown`. `mandate_manager` gives its `id`, its `mode` (`harness`, which loads the fixture list and accepts the fixture `typ` `bacp-conformance-test+jwt`, or `production`) and its `excluded_attesters` and `private_accepted_attesters`. `gateway_attestation` gives the payload fields the case is about, the JOSE `typ`, and the `status` (`ok`, `revoked`, `unreachable` or `{last_good_fetch: <time relative to the runner's clock>}`); `iat_to_exp` replaces `exp` with a validity length. `attestation_status` gives the status of a `jti` as the gateway sees it, and as a step it changes that status. A step that names a fixture key (`operators`, `conformance_authorities`, `gateway_attestation`) replaces it. `clock: {advance_past: …}` moves the runner's clock past a time, and `psp_receipt_arrives` delivers a PSP-signed receipt to the gateway.
- `requirement: SHOULD` marks a case for a SHOULD-level rule: it is reported, and does not fail the level.
- `applies_from` is the date from which a case is required (for example `2027-05-13`); before it the case is reported only.
- `relies_on` names another rule or case set that the case depends on.
- The human-participant cases also use the steps `verify_bundle`, `validate`, `render`, `render_summary`, `requote`, `tool_call`, `elicitation_response`, `submit_each` and `wait_for`, each named for what the runner does, and the fixture keys `clock`, `transport`, `mcp_client`, `ts_render`, `bundle` and `acts`.
- A fixture key that names a BACP or Beckn object describes that object as the mock counterparties hold it, using the object's own field names: `mandate`, `checkout_mandate`, `child_mandate`, `order`, `orders`, `issue`, `termsheet`, `negotiation`, `bpp_quote`, `consent_receipts`, `agent_credential`, `payment_mandates`, `trusted_surface_events`, `ts_renders` and `vector` (a published example file). In `payment_mandates`, `of` says what a Payment Mandate belongs to: `session` (an open one under the session's mandate) or an order id (a closed one that paid that order). The other fixture keys are: `step_up_link` (the Trusted Surface link the agent receives), `llm_processor` (where the agent's model runs), `network_validator` (a validator between the gateway and the seller), `notice_template` (a Trusted Surface notice template) and `mandate_manager` (the state of the Mandate Manager under test).
- A request body lists the fields a case is about. The runner completes any other field that the operation's schema requires from the fixture (for example `reason_code` and `mandate_ref` on a return) and never adds `presence` or `hp_proof`. A value in braces is taken from the fixture or an earlier step: `{mandate_ref}` (the mandate the order was placed under), `{step_up_id}` (the step-up the previous refusal or fixture names), `{event_hash}` (the hash of its signed `step_up.approved` event) and `{event_hash_<step_up_id>}` (the hash of the event for that step-up).
- `parallel` sends the requests of a step at the same time: `parallel: n` sends `n` copies of the step's `request`, and `parallel: [ … ]` sends each listed request once.
- `step_up_limit` sets the per-agent creation limit for `post_order` step-ups for the case; the value in a case is only a test setting, and the spec does not fix the gateway's own limit.
- `on_issue` is a step in which the mock seller sends an unsolicited IGM `on_issue` with the given respondent action and `resolution`.
- `signer` on a request or a `trusted_surface_event` step names the key that signs it (for example `agent_key`, `support_operator_key_1` or a registry subscriber id such as `psp-b.example.in`); without it the step is signed with the key the endpoint expects.
- `system_under_test: agent` means the runner plays the gateway and the Trusted Surface and observes the agent. Its steps `webhook` and `request_from_gateway` deliver a webhook to the agent and answer the agent's next request with the given response; `principal_instruction: none_after_pause` means the runner gives the agent no new instruction from the principal after the pause.

Schema conformance is tested with published test vectors: every example whose file name ends in `.invalid.json` MUST fail validation against its schema, and every other example MUST pass. The vectors are listed on [Reference](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/reference/index.md).

- **The example map is normative.** [`examples/index.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/examples/index.json) lists, for each example file, whether it is valid and the schema or schemas that it is checked against (a path below `source/` with an optional JSON Pointer fragment, or an absolute URL, and an `instance` pointer where a schema applies to one member). A runner takes the mapping from that file and does not infer it from file names. `scripts/validate.py` derives the map and fails when the file is stale (`--write-index` regenerates it). Where an invalid example is accepted by every listed schema, the entry names the repository check that rejects it in `fails_by` (`protocol_terms_digest` or `alias_binding`).
- **`format` is asserted.** A validator MUST assert the JSON Schema `format` keyword (`date-time`, `date`, `uri`, `uuid` and the others that the schemas use), because some negative vectors fail on `format` alone (`catalog-item.prior-price-bad-date.invalid.json` and `catalog-offer.bad-until.invalid.json`). A validator also applies each `pattern` as an ECMA-262 regular expression.
- **No cryptographic vectors yet.** The signature values in the examples are placeholders and the hashes that are not stated as computed do not digest anything. The suite will carry cryptographic test vectors (JCS, JWS, RFC 9421, the chains and a golden evidence bundle) that implementations of the specification produce and offer back to it after release.

## Handler-binding and budget cases

The cases below cover the [handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding) of open mandates (including the registry source, 24-hour freshness and the set of pause reasons), the [conformance attestation](#conformance-attestation) and the [atomic reservation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#atomic-reservation) keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate. They are written in the manifest form above. A `mandate` fixture marked `preinstalled: true` is installed in the gateway as already signed and `ACTIVE`, so that the case can test `complete` without going through issuance. A step may carry its own `expect`, checked before the next step runs. `system_under_test: mandate_manager` means the runner drives a mock gateway that forwards the request, and checks the Mandate Manager. Amounts are integer paise.

```
- case_id: T0-RT-01
  title: A pilot handler that the gateway's attestation does not list backs no open mandate
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    registry: {in.erupi: {status: pilot}}
    gateway_attestation: {pilots: []}
    mandate: {rail: in.erupi, primitive: voucher, preinstalled: true}

  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: rail_binding_not_open_eligible, resolution: requires_buyer_input, count: 2}

    log: [{stage: mandate, reason: gateway_fault, count: 1}]

T0-RT-12 tests only the adoption of a downgrade, with the registry source reachable. The stale-copy branch (registry source unreachable for 25 hours, HNP refused with `registry_copy_stale` and no pause, HP not refused for staleness) is T0-RT-15. T0-RT-13b is the overspend variant of T0-RT-13. The ₹1,000 block counts as exposure at its full amount, so ₹1,000 of the budget is left. A debit on the block counts within its reservation, so only the gift-PPI amounts take headroom: each side fits on its own (₹600 for the plan's gift tender, ₹600 for the single `complete`), together they do not, so exactly one succeeds. T0-RT-19 tests only what an agent sends: it can show that the agent opens no re-issue or resume request, not what it says to the principal.

T0-RT-13 is tested at library level for a gateway that does not list `in.bacp.payment_plan` ([Q-44](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-44), settled with a capability binding), and on the wire for one that does. With the ₹1,000 block counted as exposure ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)), ₹1,000 is left: the plan's gift tender (₹1,200) does not fit, so the plan is refused whatever the order, and its block tender, which alone would fit, is not debited either. The single `complete` on the block (₹600) counts within the block's reservation and succeeds. T0-RT-07 races two gift-PPI legs for the ₹1,000 left beside a ₹1,000 block: without block exposure both would fit. T0-RT-10b uses the `bpp_payment_terms` fixture key of the [multi-seller cases](#multi-seller-cases). T0-RT-14 tests the outcome of a negotiated ACCEPT racing a `complete`, and asserts the order: the principal-keyed section (K1) is taken before the root-checkout-mandate section (K2), never the reverse, and the K1 reservation is visible in K2 keyed by `offer_hash` ([Atomic reservation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#atomic-reservation); case T7-07 repeats it across replicas).

Settled

T0-RT-04, T0-RT-05 and T0-RT-08 test that `in.store_credit`, `bacp.credit_ledger` and `in.loyalty` are not open-eligible in this release ([Q-59](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-59), settled as closed). If a later release opens them, these cases change to test the conditions in Q-59, which T7-40 already tests: a failure receipt signed by the payee keeps the reservation counted as spent; a third ₹1,500 sale under a ₹3,000 monthly budget gets `mandate_exhausted`; an acknowledgement signed by the agent's `cnf` key gets `ack_not_by_counterparty`; and a handler with no limits gets `mandate_scope_mismatch`.

T0-RT-11 cannot tell a correct Mandate Manager from one that refuses every pilot handler while the [conformance-authority list](#conformance-authority-list) is empty, because then no attestation verifies and every MM refuses. Its positive control, T0-RT-11b, runs with a fixture conformance authority and is in the block below.

The cases below test the [conformance attestation](#attestation-rules): T0-RT-11b and CA-01 to CA-19, including CA-05b, CA-07c, CA-12b, CA-15b and CA-16b (issuance, the pause on a lapsed attestation in CA-04b, CA-07, CA-16 and CA-16b, the lift only by the same authority in CA-07c, and the gateway-side Circle refusal in CA-15b), S-F1, S-F1-missing and S-F7 at `complete`, S-F4 on the reconciliation of a receipt, DISP-01 and DISP-02 on how an attestation is shown to a principal, and VER-CA-01 on a verifier's report of a debit sent under a lapsed attestation. T2-OPS-01, T2-OPS-02, T2-OPS-03a to T2-OPS-03c and S-F6b test what a binding pause, an expiry, an exhaustion and a revocation leave open for the principal. A Mandate Manager runs them in its conformance-harness mode, which loads the fixture list and accepts the fixture `typ`; CA-13 runs in production mode.

Proposed

T0-RT-09 needs a way for the Mandate Manager to check `rail_ref` against the bound primitive. The handler descriptor now has an optional `mandate_primitives[].ref_pattern`, but no descriptor sets one in this version, so T0-RT-09 is published as data for review and is not run against this version.

## Human-participant cases

The cases below cover the [Trusted Surface and human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/index.md): the AI disclosure, the render binding and `Presentation`, who may fetch a render and post an approval, presence proof through a `post_order` step-up, the assisted channel, the human handoff and its release, the slot rule for counterparty text and its text rendering, the `ts_render` in the evidence bundle, the evidence summary and the six fail-safe defaults. T1-04b, T1-04c, T1-04e, T1-04f and T1-05b each pair the refused signer with a positive control, so that a gateway that refuses every signer fails them. They use the manifest form above. A `trusted_surface_event` step sends the named signed event from the mock Mandate Manager or PSP; `presentation: omit` leaves the `Presentation` out, `presentation: {…}` overrides its fields, and a field set to `omit` (for example `checkout_hash: omit`) is left out. Amounts are integer paise.

T1-27 to T1-32 test that a fail-safe default is applied exactly as `2026-10-18` states it. Of the six, Q-12 and Q-52 escalate to the principal on the Trusted Surface, so their cases also expect a signed Trusted Surface event with a `Presentation` in the bundle; Q-15, Q-16 and Q-20 refuse or keep a feature off, with no escalation, and T1-31 now tests the fallback of the settled Q-44: a gateway that does not list `in.bacp.payment_plan` refuses `payment_plan`. T1-26 relies on the atomic section keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)).

    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP, body: {payment_plan: {tenders: 2}}}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: capability_unsupported, param: $.payment_plan, capability: in.bacp.payment_plan, count: 1}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: T1-32
  title: Q-52 default, a crossed withdraw and accept escalates to the Trusted Surface
  level: bacp.neg.1
  fixture:
    negotiation: {crossing: {withdraw_and_accept: true, outcome: accept_void_withdrawn}}
  steps:

      expect:

```

Proposed

T1-33 depends on `StepUp.delivery: ivr_callback`, which is Proposed until [Q-63](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-63) is answered. It is published as data for review and is not run against this version. T1-15 is in force: it rests on the registry field `ts_origins` and on `503 trusted_surface_unavailable` ([Origins and delivery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-origins)). Whether a registry other than the BACP schema can carry `ts_origins` is open with ONDC ([Q-87](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-87)).
