## Multi-seller basket cases

The cases below cover the [per-leg rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule) for a [multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket): sibling Payment Mandates under one root open Checkout Mandate, the payee binding of a Reserve Pay block, the sum-of-blocks rule and block exposure in the [usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger), the gateway-local `basket_id`, planning before the first debit, the summary step-up and its `covers[]`, the Trusted Surface rules for a basket, and the revocation cascade. They use the manifest form above. These cases also use:

- `basket` (fixture): the sessions of one basket, each with its seller, amount and planned handler; `basket_id` is shared;
- `bpp_payment_terms` (fixture): the seller's BPP-signed payment terms as the gateway holds them (`vpa`, `collected_by`);
- `psp_attestation.block_debit_feed` (fixture): whether the payer PSP attests a block-debit feed;
- `rail_event` (step): the mock PSP reports a debit on a block that the gateway did not send;
- `principal_preference` (fixture): the handler the principal designated;
- `summary_step_up` (fixture): a summary step-up (reason `rail_fallback`) over the named legs, with its `covers[]`;
- `fixture_override` (step): fixture values that apply to that step only;
- `plan_basket` (library call): the gateway's per-leg planning for a basket, without sending a request;
- `state` keys `payment_mandate_<name>`, `session_<id>` and `exposure` (the exposure of the root open Checkout Mandate in the window), and `rail` counts `calls`, `debit_requests`, `distinct_rrn`, `request_field_absent` and `revocations` (blocks revoked at the rail);
- `principal: {account, ref}` (fixture) and `as_principal` (request): the principal's account at the Mandate Manager and the pairwise `principal.ref` that one request carries, so that two refs of one account can be told apart;
- `bpp` (fixture): what the mock seller answers on the network, for example its `on_init` payment terms;
- `mandate_request` (fixture): the mandate request whose notice a Trusted Surface renders;
- `{transaction_id_<id>}` and `{render_hash_<step_up_id>}`: the transaction of a basket leg and the sha-256 of a step-up's `ts_render`, taken from the fixture.

T2-07 has two branches, chosen by `psp_attestation.block_debit_feed`: T2-07b, without an attested feed, is below; T2-07, with one, is Proposed because the feed has no wire form. T2-02b is the positive control of T2-02. T2-14b checks evidence verification for a covered leg that did not raise the summary. The cases T2-RT-11 to T2-RT-18 keep the ids of the red-team traces they close: the payee bound to BPP-signed terms on every block (T2-RT-11), headroom at issuance and the activation race (T2-RT-12, T2-RT-13), the requested block amount (T2-RT-14), the summary signer (T2-RT-15), the summary in a seller's bundle (T2-RT-16), block expiry and the cascade on every end of the root (T2-RT-17), the unseen-draw statement at issuance (T2-RT-18), a refused block with an unconfirmed rail revocation (T2-RT-19) and the first block of a new root (T2-RT-20). T2-24 is a regression case for the notice-gated repeat debit. T2-25 runs on two gateway replicas. Amounts are integer paise.

Proposed

T2-07 depends on a block-debit feed attested by the payer PSP, whose wire form `2026-10-18` does not define ([Q-10](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-10)); it can run only through the harness keys `psp_attestation.block_debit_feed` and `rail_event`. T2-16 depends on `StepUp.delivery: ivr_callback`, which is Proposed until [Q-63](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-63) is answered. Both are published as data for review and are not run against this version.

## Acceptance-revocation cases

The cases below cover [acceptance revocation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation): the REQUIRED `acceptance_revocation` term and its `waiver_basis`, the value rules by leg and session, the refusal of `allowed_until_receipt` on every leg, consumer sessions, the Beckn exception for a missing basis, exposure release, the tag rule for `accept_revoke`, the negotiation `ts_render` rows and their approval with `Presentation.offer_hash`, and the RFQ and auction rules. The cases that need a live or accepted offer with `allowed_until_receipt` test the [sunset text](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation-sunset) and are in the [Proposed (sunset) block](#acceptance-revocation-sunset-cases) below. They use the manifest form above. These cases also use:

- `leg` (fixture): the binding that carries negotiation messages between the parties, `rest` (the REST, MCP or A2A bindings) or `beckn`;
- `profile` (fixture): the session's `context.bacp.profile`, or `none` when it declares none;
- `acting_for` (fixture): the buyer side's `context.bacp.acting_for`, or `none` when it sends none; where a case does not set it, the buyer side sends `{kind: business}`;
- `offer` (fixture): the offer as the gateway under test holds it, with its `state`, `firm`, `acceptance_revocation`, `waiver_basis` and `offer_hash`, the guard `verdict` shown to the agent, `proposer: gateway_under_test` when the gateway under test made the offer, and `accepted_after: negotiation.step_up.approved` when the principal approved the acceptance on the Trusted Surface;
- `negotiations`, `rfq`, `auction` and `bids` (fixtures): several negotiations of one principal with their offers and revoke outcomes, an RFQ with its comparison set, and an auction with its bids;
- `held_documents` (fixture): the documents the acceptor's gateway obtained from its own principal, each with its `hash`, the counterparties it names (`names`, by `np_id` or GSTIN) and `waiver_basis: true` when the principal marked it as a waiver basis; `counterparty_documents` (fixture): documents the counterparty serves, by `uri`, with their hashes;
- `incoming` (step): the mock counterparty sends the given negotiation message to the gateway under test; `at` is the receipt time relative to the first `incoming` step, a field set to `omit` is left out, `repeat: n` delivers the same signed message n times, and `across_replicas: true` delivers the copies to different gateway replicas;
- `counterparty_receipt` (step): the mock counterparty returns its CounterSignature for the gateway's own message, with the given payload fields;
- `state` keys `offer`, `negotiation`, `live_offer`, `rfq`, `auction` and `exposure`; `exposure_releases` counts the releases of one reservation.

T3-06 and T3-18 run on a Beckn leg, and T3-29 on a Beckn leg too. T3-30 drives a verifier. Amounts are integer paise.

### Proposed (sunset) cases

Proposed (sunset)

These cases test the [sunset text](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation-sunset) for `allowed_until_receipt`. Each needs a live or accepted offer with that value, which no receiver creates in this version, so they carry no conformance level and are not run against `2026-10-18`. They are published as data, and passing them is sunset condition (f). The non-monotonic chain check that T3-16 exercises also applies in this version ([Clock skew](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#signed-seller-acceptance-and-clock-skew)). In these cases `log.entries[].counter_signature.returned: sync_response` means that the CounterSignature came back in the synchronous response to that message, and `before_step` names the step that it preceded; `replica` (step) names the gateway replica that receives the message; `outcome` (an `incoming` type) is the proposer's outcome message for a revoke.

```
- case_id: T3-08
  title: A revoke received before its matching accept within the hold is honoured, with receipts committed in each response
  fixture:
    leg: rest
    profile: b2b.procurement
    offer: {state: LIVE, firm: true, acceptance_revocation: allowed_until_receipt, proposer: gateway_under_test}
  steps:
    - incoming: {type: accept_revoke, accept_msg_hash: H_A, offer_hash: "{offer_hash}", dispatched_at: "-0.2s", at: "+0s"}
    - incoming: {type: accept, msg_hash: H_A, offer_hash: "{offer_hash}", dispatched_at: "-0.7s", at: "+1s"}
  expect:
    messages: [accept_revoke_honoured]
    state: {offer: ACCEPT_REVOKED, negotiation: NEGOTIATING}
    log:
      entries:
        - {seq: n, msg_type: accept_revoke, counter_signature: {log_entry_hash: present, returned: sync_response, before_step: 2}}
        - {seq: n+1, msg_type: accept, counter_signature: {log_entry_hash: present, returned: sync_response}}
        - {seq: n+2, msg_type: outcome, code: accept_revoke_honoured}

## Catalogue disclosure cases

The cases below cover the [catalogue disclosures](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures) of a discover response: the per-item `sponsorship`, the seller-asserted `prior_price`, `mrp` and `tax_inclusive`, the monotone OR rule, the rendering rules for an agent, the drift message `discovery_price_changed`, `Disclosures.catalogue[]`, the seller-signed sources and their [verification by the agent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results), the repeat on the Trusted Surface and as `type: disclosure` messages, and [discounts and published offers](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts). They use the manifest form above. The case ids run in three blocks: CD-01 to CD-25 test the disclosure fields and rules, CD-26 to CD-53 test source verification, the Trusted Surface repeat and discounts, and CD-R01 to CD-R27 close the traces of the red-team review of that design. Cases marked *harness* need a mock seller whose signed callbacks the test controls. CD-23 is blocked until `principal.minor_status` exists ([Q-17](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-17)); CD-25 is informative. These cases also use:

- `system_under_test` (case): `gateway` unless stated; `agent`, `trusted_surface`, `verifier` and `schema` as in the cases above;
- `bpp_on_search` (fixture): what the mock seller sends in its signed `on_search`: items, prices as decimal strings and `bacp.disclosure` tags; `signed: true` unless stated;
- `ranking_policy` (fixture): the gateway's own order (`main_parameters`) and any `placement_sold` (to which provider, by which party) or `upstream_signal` (an upstream ordering or promotion signal and whether its paid status is known);
- `discover_response` (fixture): a discover response as the gateway returned it, with the `sources` it serves; an `agent_render` step has the agent under test present it to a principal, and `output` expectations (`contains`, `contains_none_of`, `before`) apply to the transcript or the screen text;
- `session` (fixture): a session created from a discover response, with the `quote` the seller signed at `on_select` and `on_init`;
- `source_get` (step): the agent calls `GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}`;
- `log` (state): the InstructionLog entries the agent wrote.

Amounts are integer paise.

```

## Who-pays cases

The cases below cover [Fees on the payer's screen](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fee-lines), the [fee-bearer change](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#fee-bearer-change), [refunds](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#refunds), the fee read-out of the Trusted Surface, [operator compensation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#operator-compensation), the [ranking rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#ranking-by-payment-rungs), the convenience-fee mandate constraint and the seller confirmation profile. They use the manifest form above, and their ids use the prefix `WP-`. Amounts are integer paise. Until counsel answers [Q-81](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-81), no case passes a retained payment-related charge (`convenience`, `payment_handling`, `platform`), and none passes a retention on a return for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods (WP-14). WP-15 passes a delivery line only, subject to counsel's answer on rule 4(8).

```
- case_id: WP-01
  title: A fallback from UPI to COD with a COD fee changes the fee-bearer and raises a rail_fallback step-up
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  fixture:
    leg: {planned: in.upi.intent, replacement: in.cod}
    totals: [{type: cod_fee, applies_to_handlers: [in.cod], recipient: seller, amount: {value: 5000, currency: INR}}]
  steps:
    - fallback: {leg: L1}

    sessions: {count: 1, state: requires_escalation, step_up: {kind: confirm, reason: rail_fallback}}
    settled_debits: 0

    log: {"comparison[0].method_charge": 0, "comparison[1].method_charge": 0}

## Binding cases

The cases below cover the wire binding of payment plans, credit ledgers and trade documents ([Q-44](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-44)), the transport rules that go with them and the UCP projection. They use the manifest form above, and their ids use the prefix `BND-`. Amounts are integer paise. A case with `requires_capability` is required only of a gateway whose profile lists that capability: for any other gateway the runner records the case as not applicable, which is not a skipped case, and the gateway keeps the behaviour that case T1-31 checks. Cases without it bind every gateway.

```
- case_id: BND-PLAN-01
  title: A plan that matches an offered option is paid tender by tender, with one derived PSP key for each tender
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  requires_capability: in.bacp.payment_plan
  fixture:
    sessions: {count: 1, state: ready_for_complete, all_in_total: {value: 216000, currency: INR}}
    plan_options: [{plan_hash: H, tenders: [{handler: in.ppi.gift, amount: {value: 100000, currency: INR}, sequence: 1}, {handler: in.upi.circle, amount: {value: 116000, currency: INR}, sequence: 2}]}]
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP, body: {payment_plan: {tenders_hash: H}, closed_mandates: [{tender: {plan_hash: H, tender_id: tdr_gift001}}, {tender: {plan_hash: H, tender_id: tdr_upi001}}]}}
  expect:
    sessions: {count: 1, state: completed}
    receipts: {count: 2}
    rail: {settled_debits: 2, psp_keys_distinct: true}

- case_id: BND-PLAN-OFFER-01
  title: A plan that hashes to no offered or confirmed option is refused and nothing is debited
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  requires_capability: in.bacp.payment_plan
  fixture:
    sessions: {count: 1, state: ready_for_complete}
    plan_options: [{plan_hash: H1}, {plan_hash: H2}]
    ts_confirmed_plans: []
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HNP, body: {payment_plan: {tenders_hash: H3}}}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 400, code: plan_not_offered, param: $.payment_plan, count: 1}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: BND-PLAN-TS-01
  title: A plan_id that names an approved option while the tenders hash to another option gets mandate_scope_mismatch
  level: bacp.pay.all.1
  requires_capability: in.bacp.payment_plan
  fixture:
    step_up: {approved_for: {plan_id: P1, kind: card_only_2160}}
    plan_options: [{plan_id: P1}, {plan_id: P2}]
  steps:
    - request: {method: POST, path: "/sessions/{session_id}/complete", tag: bacp-pay, presence: HP, body: {payment_plan: {plan_id: P1, tenders_hash: H_P2}}}
  expect:
    responses:
      - {status: 403, code: mandate_scope_mismatch, count: 1}
    rail: {settled_debits: 0}

- case_id: BND-PLAN-P5-01

- case_id: BND-PLAN-NODEFAULT-01

## Negotiation timing cases

The cases below cover [Signed seller acceptance and clock skew](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#signed-seller-acceptance-and-clock-skew): the committed-order rule, the contested outcome, expiry, notice of an autonomous act, purchase-offer withdrawal, the decline of an `AGREED` or `BOUND` deal, the Dutch chain order and `tick_close`, and the clock-invariance property. They use the manifest form above, their ids use the prefix `T5-`, and they record state as `fixture.<machine>.state` and `expect.state.<machine>`. Case T5-28 is not used. Amounts are integer paise. They also use:

- `chain` (fixture): the positions in each party's own chain, as `{sender_log_seq, cs_log_seq}` for each message, with `n` names for the relative positions the case needs;
- `incoming` (step) and `counterparty_receipt` (step), as in the acceptance-revocation cases, with `cs_returned_after` giving how long after dispatch (on the sender's monotonic clock) the receipt came and `cs: omit` meaning none came;
- `harness_clock` (fixture): an offset applied to every participant's wall clock, and `rerun` (a step) that runs the named cases again under the given offsets.

Levels: gateway cases `bacp.neg.1`; auctioneer cases `bacp.auction.1`; verifier cases `bacp.neg.1` with `system_under_test: verifier`; Mandate Manager cases `bacp.neg.1` with `system_under_test: trusted_surface`.

**Clock-invariance property (T5-18).** Every ordering case (T5-07 to T5-13 and T5-24) runs three times: with every participant's wall clock offset by -3 s, 0 and +3 s (inside the existing 5-second band; fixture values, not limits). Outcome codes and offer states MUST be identical. Run again at +/-30 s, the only permitted difference is that a message is refused with `NEG_CLOCK_SKEW` before it enters ordering. No clock offset may ever change who wins: it may move an outcome only to a refusal or to contested.

## Trusted Surface and human-participant cases

The cases below cover [Requirement TS-6](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements), [Origins and delivery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-origins), [Voice confirmation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#voice), [Limits on step-ups](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#step-up-limits), the [typed `ts_render`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-render), the handoff operator binding, the registry record, the seller reasons and the [confirmation floor](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#confirmation-floor). They use the manifest form above, their ids use the prefix `T6-`, and amounts are integer paise. Levels: gateway, schema and verifier cases `bacp.core.1` (T6-37 and T6-49 `bacp.pay.upi.1`); Trusted Surface cases `bacp.ts.1` with `system_under_test: trusted_surface`. They also use:

- `registry` (fixture): the registry records the gateway reads, keyed by subscriber id, with the fields of [`registry-record.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/registry-record.json);
- `seeded_rng` (fixture): a seed for the random source of the Trusted Surface under test, so that a drawn challenge is predictable to the runner only;
- `logged_in_as` (fixture): the principal or payer whose session the Trusted Surface under test has open;
- `limits` (fixture): the declared `step_up_limits` of the gateway for the case, as test settings and not as limits the specification sets;
- `get_step_up` (step): `GET /step-ups/{step_up_id}` signed by the named credential (`credential: C1`);
- the expect keys `ts_renders` (what the gateway put in the renders it signed), `notify` (the content-free pushes it sent), `ts_prompts` (the prompts a Trusted Surface showed), `step_ups_created`, `agent_quota`, `log` and `messages`.

## Mandates, payments and registry cases

The cases below cover the [gateway binding and porting of an open mandate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#port), the [lock order](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#atomic-reservation), [mandate events](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#mandate-events), the [registry release manifest](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/#release-manifest), the [registry record](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#registry-lookup) and the separation of a [conformance authority](#conformance-authority-list), the receipts and [budget release](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger) after a seller-side reversal, the [reversal basis](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#debited-not-confirmed), funding and the [per-leg rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule), the split-order key, the post-order and presence rules, and the closing of [Q-59](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-59). They use the manifest form above, their ids use the prefix `T7-` (and the `T0-` ids that the registry serial changes), and amounts are integer paise. Levels: gateway cases `bacp.pay.all.1` unless stated; schema cases `bacp.core.1`. They also use:

- `registry` and `registry_by_replica` (fixture): besides `version`, each takes `serial` and `published_at`, the keys of the [release manifest](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/#release-manifest); a registry update names the `serial` that it publishes;
- `credentials` (fixture): further AgentCredentials of the agent, each with its `bap` and `cnf`, and `present_credential` (step), which makes the agent present one of them;
- `mandate_event` (step): the mock gateway sends a signed `MandateEvent` to the Mandate Manager under test, with `type`, `seq` and `signer` (a BAP subscriber id);
- `ts_confirm` (step): the principal answers a `confirm` step-up with reason `refund_received` on the Trusted Surface;
- `modification_request` (step): the agent asks the gateway to modify a block;
- the expect keys `mm` (what the Mandate Manager recorded: `events_recorded`, `event_gap`, `ts_view`, `rejected`, `refused_with`), `ledger` (the root's exposure and reservations, for example `reservations: [{key: offer_hash}]`), `comparison` (the `comparison[]` entries logged) and `message_text` (what a fixed message says and does not say).

The T0 cases that the registry serial and the new rules touch are changed in place: T0-RT-06 accepts a refusal at `create_session` or at `complete`, T0-RT-16 and T0-RT-17 read the registry `serial` where they read a version, and T2-OPS-03b gains a human-present `RAISE_ISSUE`. T0-RT-16b, T0-RT-17b, T0-RT-19b, T0-RT-19c and T0-RT-20 are added beside the other T0 cases.

## UCP capability parity cases

The cases below cover [refusing a member of an unlisted capability](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#capabilities), the closed per-gateway MCP [`inputSchema`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/mcp-a2a/#mcp-tools), the UCP projection's criterion UCPF-06, the [version of a request](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#request-version), [capability declarations and `ext`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#capability-declarations), [URL fetch hygiene](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#url-fetch-hygiene), [units and weighed goods](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#units), [fulfilment options](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fulfilment-options), [typed policies](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#typed-policies), [line provenance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#line-provenance), the business buyer, [marketing consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#marketing-consent) and the parked capabilities. They use the manifest form above, their ids use the prefix `T8-` and amounts are integer paise. Level: gateway cases `bacp.core.1` unless stated. They also use:

- `capabilities` (fixture): `{omits: [...]}` removes the named capability ids from the gateway's profile, and `{lists: [...]}` adds them;
- `tool_results` (expect), as in the binding cases, with `structuredContent.capability` and `content_key` (the disclosure-phrase key that the `content` text is taken from, in the principal's language);
- `sessions: {created: 0}` (expect): no session was created or changed by the step;
- `headers` (request): the request headers that the case sets, for example `BACP-Version`, with `covered: false` for a header that is sent and left out of `Signature-Input`, and `omit` for a header that is left out;
- `profile` (fixture): the gateway's profile, for example `{versions: [A, B]}`, `capabilities`, `capability_declarations` and `mcp_endpoints`;
- `fetch` (step): the runner makes the gateway or projection fetch a URL, and `fetch_target` (fixture) is the mock server's answer (a redirect, a resolved address, a body size); the expect key `fetches` counts the requests that the mock server saw;
- `ts_render`, `tool_call`, `psp_receipt_arrives`, `incoming` and `validate` as in the cases above, and `seller_callback` (step): the mock seller sends the named `on_*` callback.

Case T8-CAP-05 is [BND-UCPF-06](#binding-cases).

```
- case_id: T8-CAP-01
  title: A gateway that does not list in.bacp.discounts refuses a POST /sessions that carries discounts, and creates no session

- case_id: T8-VER-01

## R2 residual cases

The cases below cover the residual decisions of the second review round. They use the manifest form above, their ids use the prefix `R2-`, and amounts are integer paise.

```
- case_id: R2-AFA-01
  title: The NCMC top-up descriptor carries no Annexure-1 exemption, and the NETC top-up descriptor keeps row 4
  level: bacp.core.1
  system_under_test: registry
  steps:
    - read_descriptor: {handler: [in.ppi.ncmc_topup, in.ppi.netc_topup]}
  expect:
    verdict:
      in.ppi.ncmc_topup: {afa_model: per_txn_2fa, rbi_annex1_item: absent, pre_debit_notice: exempt}
      in.ppi.netc_topup: {afa_model: exempt, rbi_annex1_item: 4}

- case_id: R2-CREF-01
  title: A step-up approval names its render by a JSON Pointer fragment into the bundle, and a URL or a leading-zero index is rejected
  level: bacp.core.1
  system_under_test: schema
  steps:

    - validate: {schema: bacp.openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/TrustedSurfaceEvent, vector: trusted-surface-event.step-up-approved-content-ref-url.invalid.json}
    - validate: {schema: common.json#/$defs/Presentation, vector: common.presentation-content-ref-leading-zero.invalid.json}
  expect:
    verdict: {code: schema_invalid, count: 2, path: $.presentation.content_ref}

# Discovery and Profiles

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page defines how an agent learns what a BACP gateway supports, how the two sides agree on a protocol version, capabilities, negotiation features and payment handlers, how the gateway uses the network registry, and how network discovery (`POST /discover`) maps onto Beckn.

There are two kinds of discovery in BACP:

- **Gateway discovery.** The agent reads the gateway's **profile** at `/.well-known/bacp` to learn versions, transports, capabilities, payment handlers and keys. This is the UCP `/.well-known` pattern.
- **Network discovery.** The agent asks the gateway to search the ONDC/Beckn network for sellers and products. The gateway uses the network registry to find and verify sellers.

## Profile document

A BACP gateway MUST publish a profile document at the path `/.well-known/bacp` under its base URL, for example `https://gw.bap.example.in/bacp/.well-known/bacp`.

- The profile is fetched with an unsigned `GET`. It carries no `Idempotency-Key` and needs no AgentCredential.
- The response is `application/json` and MUST validate against the `Profile` schema of the [REST binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/index.md).
- Agents SHOULD cache the profile and SHOULD follow standard HTTP caching semantics, revalidating once the cached copy's `max-age` expires.
- An agent MUST NOT rely on a profile's `keys` until it has checked that they match the registry record of the `bap_id` the profile names (see [Registry lookup](#registry-lookup)).

### Fields

| Field                       | Required    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bacp.version`              | REQUIRED    | The protocol version this profile describes. See [Version negotiation](#version-negotiation).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `bacp.supported_versions`   | OPTIONAL    | Every protocol version the gateway accepts. When it lists more than one, a request names its version in the signed `BACP-Version` header ([Version negotiation](#version-negotiation)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `mcp_endpoints`             | OPTIONAL    | `{version: uri}`: the MCP endpoint of each listed version. REQUIRED when the gateway lists more than one version and offers `mcp`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `capability_declarations`   | OPTIONAL    | `{capability id: {version, extends, ...}}`: machine-readable declarations of capabilities, a sibling of `capabilities` ([Capability declarations](#capability-declarations)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `bap_id`                    | REQUIRED    | The Beckn/ONDC subscriber id of the BAP that hosts the gateway. Every AgentCredential the gateway accepts names this BAP.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `transports`                | REQUIRED    | Bindings offered: `rest`, `mcp`, `a2a`. See [Transports](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `capabilities`              | REQUIRED    | Capability ids the gateway supports (see [Capabilities](#capabilities)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `payment_handlers`          | REQUIRED    | Payment handlers the gateway can process, as handler references. See [Payment handlers in the profile](#payment-handlers-in-the-profile).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `reserved_handlers`         | OPTIONAL    | Handler ids or globs the gateway knows are reserved and will refuse, for example `in.upi.uap`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `keys`                      | REQUIRED    | A JWK Set (`{"keys": [...]}`) with the gateway's public keys. The gateway signs webhooks with these keys.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `message_id_namespace`      | REQUIRED    | The UUID namespace the gateway uses to derive Beckn `message_id`s (see [Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/index.md)). Agents need it to compute the `nonce` of a key-binding JWT for a seller.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `negotiation`               | OPTIONAL    | The gateway's negotiation capability advert (see [Negotiation capability](#negotiation-capability)). REQUIRED when the gateway supports negotiation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `step_up_limits`            | OPTIONAL    | The limits that the gateway applies to step-ups, each a `{count, window}` or, for the decline cool-off, a `{window}`: `post_order_per_principal`, `post_order_per_order`, `session_per_principal`, `reprompt_per_issue`, `decline_cooloff`, `render_fetch_per_key` and `render_fetch_per_step_up`. BACP sets no number. They are the gateway's own design values, never presented as external limits, and a gateway that declares none is tested against the conformance fixture's limit ([Limits on step-ups](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#step-up-limits)).                                                                                                            |
| `payment_handlers_registry` | OPTIONAL    | URI of the gateway's `GET /payment-handlers` endpoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `profiles`                  | OPTIONAL    | [Trade profiles](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/trade-profiles/index.md) the gateway supports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `limits.max_body_bytes`     | RECOMMENDED | The largest request body the gateway accepts. It MUST NOT exceed 256 KiB.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `conformance`               | RECOMMENDED | `{levels, attestation, excluded_attesters[]}`: the [conformance levels](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-levels) the participant claims, its signed [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation) (REQUIRED to offer a `pilot` handler) and, on a Mandate Manager's profile, `excluded_attesters[]`: the `ca_id`s of the [public conformance-authority list](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-authority-list) that it does not accept. A Mandate Manager only narrows the list and publishes the narrowing here, so that a refusal (`attester_not_accepted`) is testable. |

Receivers MUST ignore profile fields they do not understand.

Proposed

The field name `limits.max_body_bytes` is proposed and is not yet in the `Profile` schema.

### Example

```
{
  "bacp": {
    "version": "2026-10-18",
    "supported_versions": ["2026-10-18"]
  },
  "bap_id": "bap.vaani.example.in",
  "transports": ["rest", "mcp", "a2a"],
  "capabilities": [
    "in.bacp.discover",
    "in.bacp.checkout",
    "in.bacp.mandate",
    "in.bacp.order",
    "in.bacp.issue"
  ],
  "payment_handlers": [
    "in.upi.reservepay",
    "in.upi.circle",
    "in.upi.autopay",
    "in.upi.intent",
    "in.cod"
  ],
  "reserved_handlers": ["in.upi.uap"],
  "message_id_namespace": "55884fda-3b41-58be-87a9-2be7b3b43b7f",
  "payment_handlers_registry": "https://gw.bap.example.in/bacp/payment-handlers",
  "keys": {
    "keys": [
      {
        "kty": "OKP",
        "crv": "Ed25519",
        "x": "11qYAYKxCrfVS_7TyWQHOg7hcvPapiMlrwIaaPcHURo",
        "kid": "ukid-7"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Version negotiation

BACP versions are dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` form. The first dated release is `2026-10-18`; the unreleased working version on `main` is `draft` (see [Versioning](https://bacp.dev/versioning/)).

1. The agent fetches `/.well-known/bacp`.
1. The agent selects a version that appears in `bacp.version` or `bacp.supported_versions`. It SHOULD prefer the most recent version it implements.
1. If there is no common version, the agent MUST NOT call the gateway's other operations.
1. On the network leg, the gateway states the BACP version it is speaking in `context.bacp.version`.

A participant that implements `draft` MUST expect breaking changes at any time. A dated release such as `2026-10-18` changes only as the [Versioning](https://bacp.dev/versioning/) policy allows. Version strings are a release date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or `draft`, as defined by [`ProtocolVersion`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/common.json).

### The version of a request

An agent names the version of each request in the `BACP-Version` request header, whose value is a [`ProtocolVersion`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/common.json). A single header is enough because a profile that lists one version needs no choice.

1. **When it is required.** `BACP-Version` is REQUIRED on every agent request when the gateway's profile lists more than one version in `bacp.version` and `bacp.supported_versions`. A request without it gets `400 invalid_request` at `$.headers.BACP-Version`, on the pattern of `idempotency_key_required`. A gateway that lists one version accepts a request with no header as that version, and a request that names another version gets `400 version_unsupported`. A Trusted Surface request (`bacp-ts`) carries the version of the session it acts on and needs no header.
1. **It is signed.** `bacp-version` is a covered component of the request signature whenever the header is present ([Covered components](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#covered-components)). A header that is present and not covered gets `401 signature_invalid`, so that a party on the path cannot change the version of a signed request.
1. **An unlisted version** gets `400 version_unsupported` at `$.headers.BACP-Version`, with `supported_versions[]` listing the versions that the gateway lists.
1. **A session is pinned.** A session is pinned to the version that it was created under, on every transport. A later request for the session that names another version gets `409 version_mismatch`, and nothing changes. A new version needs a new session.
1. **The fingerprint.** The version is part of the idempotency *fingerprint* of a request, not of the key's scope: the same key with the same body and another version is refused as `422 idempotency_conflict` ([Idempotency](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#idempotency)).
1. **MCP.** A gateway that lists more than one version and offers `mcp` serves one MCP server for each version and publishes them in `mcp_endpoints{version: uri}`, because an MCP host may be unable to set a header. The version of a session on MCP is the version of the endpoint that created it.
1. **A2A.** The A2A extension URI carries the version, `https://bacp.dev/<version>/a2a`, and the Agent Card declares it with `required: true` ([Agent card](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/mcp-a2a/#a2a-card)).
1. **The protective floor.** A request that is `bacp-pay`, `bacp-post-order` or `bacp-negotiate` runs the protective checks of the newest version that the gateway lists, whichever version the request names, so that naming an older version cannot switch a protective check off. A protective check is any rule of that version that refuses, escalates or raises a step-up. A version that lacks a check never lowers the floor.
1. **Never from a fetched document.** A gateway and an agent MUST NOT take a version from a document that was fetched from a URL, such as a UCP profile or a seller's page. The version of a request is the signed header or the endpoint, and nothing else.

A gateway that lists one version is unaffected: the header is optional for it and the rules above change nothing.

## Capabilities

A capability is a named group of operations. A gateway MUST list every capability it supports in `capabilities`, and an agent SHOULD NOT call an operation whose capability the gateway does not list.

| Capability               | Operations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Defined in                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `in.bacp.discover`       | `POST /discover`, `GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}`                                                                                                                                                                         | [this page](#network-discovery)                                                                                                |
| `in.bacp.checkout`       | `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}`, `/sessions/{id}/complete`, `/sessions/{id}/cancel`                                                                                                                                                                  | [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md)                                           |
| `in.bacp.discounts`      | The `discounts` field of `POST /sessions` and `PUT /sessions/{id}`; extends `in.bacp.checkout`                                                                                                                                                     | [Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts)                                                     |
| `in.bacp.payment_plan`   | `payment.plan_options[]` on a session, `complete.payment_plan`, and `session_id` on `POST /payment-handlers/intersect`; extends `in.bacp.checkout`                                                                                                 | [Wire binding of plans](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#plan-wire)                 |
| `in.bacp.ledger`         | `GET /ledgers/{id}`, `GET /ledgers/{id}/entries`, `POST /ledgers/{id}/entries` (agent: `type: payment` only), and `ledger_ref` and `ledger_range` acts on `POST /trade-acts`                                                                       | [The khata credit ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#the-khata-credit-ledger) |
| `in.bacp.trade_document` | `POST /trade-acts` (GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection), `GET /orders/{id}/documents`                                                                                                                                                                      | [Seller-side and trade acts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#trade-acts)                         |
| `in.bacp.ucp_checkout`   | `/checkout-sessions`, `/checkout-sessions/{id}`, `/checkout-sessions/{id}/complete`, `/checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel`: the checkout in the shape of UCP checkout, pinned to UCP release `v2026-08-25`; listed only if every entry criterion passes | [UCP checkout projection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/ucp-checkout/index.md)                          |
| `in.bacp.mandate`        | `/mandates`, `/mandates/{id}`, `/mandates/{id}/relinquish`                                                                                                                                                                                         | [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md)                                            |
| `in.bacp.order`          | `/orders/{id}`, `/orders/{id}/cancel`, `/orders/{id}/returns`                                                                                                                                                                                      | [Orders and Post-order](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/index.md)                                |
| `in.bacp.issue`          | `/issues`, `/issues/{id}`, `/issues/{id}/actions`, `/evidence/{transaction_id}`                                                                                                                                                                    | [Evidence and Instruction Log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/index.md)                                    |

A gateway MUST support every operation of a capability it lists. `in.bacp.payment_plan` and `in.bacp.ucp_checkout` require `in.bacp.checkout` in the same list.

**Refuse, do not ignore.** A request member that a capability owns, where the gateway's version defines the capability but the gateway does not list it, MUST be refused with `400 capability_unsupported` at the member's JSON path, with `capability` set to the capability id, and nothing is created or changed. The gateway MUST NOT ignore the member. This covers:

- `discounts` on `POST /sessions` and `PUT /sessions/{session_id}` (`in.bacp.discounts`), at `$.discounts`;
- `payment_plan` on `complete` and `session_id` on `POST /payment-handlers/intersect` (`in.bacp.payment_plan`), at `$.payment_plan` and `$.session_id`;
- the members that a future capability owns.

A gateway that lists none of `in.bacp.payment_plan`, `in.bacp.ledger` and `in.bacp.trade_document` also exposes no tool or DataPart for them on MCP or A2A. A field that the gateway's version does not define is not capability-owned and keeps the rule of [Extensibility](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/overview/#extensibility) (it is ignored on REST). The refusal is not the `discount_code_unsupported` warning, which a gateway that lists `in.bacp.discounts` returns when the seller declines codes. In the OpenAPI document, `x-bacp-capability` names the capability that owns an operation or a property, so that `scripts/validate.py` can test the rule: a value is a capability id from the table above, or a list of ids when any one of them suffices.

### Capability declarations

The optional profile member `capability_declarations` is a map beside `capabilities`, which stays a list of ids. Every key MUST also appear in `capabilities`, and a gateway that lists a key in `capabilities` MAY omit its declaration.

- An `in.bacp.*` entry is `{version, extends}`: the capability's own date and the capability or capabilities that it extends (`in.bacp.discounts` extends `in.bacp.checkout`, as the table above says). The key MUST be a capability id of the table above; an id such as `in.bacp.emi` that BACP does not define is invalid.
- A third-party entry, for a capability that a bank or a distributor defines, is `{version, extends, registry_ref, schema_digest}`. `registry_ref` names the entry of the extension registry, and `schema_digest` is the digest of the schema that the registry pins for it. The entry has **no schema URL**: a gateway never fetches an extension's schema at run time, because a fetched schema is a way into the money path for whoever controls the URL. A third-party key is a reverse-DNS id under a domain that its operator controls, never an `in.*` id.
- **Gated.** A third-party entry activates only once a review process for the extension registry exists ([Q-94](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-94)). Until then only `in.bacp.*` entries are valid, a third-party entry is not activated, and any `ext` member of a request is refused with `capability_unsupported`.
- A third-party payload travels in the `ext` member of a session, under the capability's key. It is closed by the schema that the declaration pins, and it is present in an MCP `inputSchema` only while the capability is active. An `ext` member that touches an amount, the payee, presence, a mandate or a disclosure is *critical*: the gateway refuses it unless its capability is listed and the amount also appears as a line of the base `totals`, and it is never a mandate constraint ([Extensibility](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/overview/#extensibility)).

Negotiation, RFQs and auctions are advertised through the `negotiation` field rather than a capability id. Handler listing and intersection are advertised through `payment_handlers_registry`.

Conformance levels (see [Conformance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/index.md)) are the testable counterpart of capabilities: a gateway that claims a level MUST support every capability that level exercises.

## Negotiation capability

Negotiation features are agreed by intersecting two adverts, each shaped as [`negotiation-session.json#/$defs/Capability`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/negotiation-session.json):

- the **gateway** (BAP side) declares its advert in the profile's `negotiation` field;
- each **seller** (BPP) advertises `bacp.negotiation` as a provider tag in its Beckn `on_search` response.

| Advert field           | Meaning                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `negotiable_issues[]`  | JSON Pointers into the term sheet that may be negotiated, for example `/lines/*/unit_price` or `/payment/credit_days`. |
| `modes[]`              | Negotiation modes supported, for example `fixed`, `alternating`, `rfq_sealed`, `reverse_l1`.                           |
| `max_rounds`           | Maximum number of rounds.                                                                                              |
| `round_timeout`        | Maximum time for one round.                                                                                            |
| `min_offer_validity`   | Shortest validity an offer may have.                                                                                   |
| `sig_algs`             | Signature algorithms accepted for negotiation messages.                                                                |
| `firm_quote_supported` | Whether the participant issues firm (binding) quotes.                                                                  |
| `accepted_handlers[]`  | Payment handlers the seller accepts; feeds the [handler intersection](#payment-handlers-in-the-profile).               |
| `pricing_ai_vendor`    | Who supplies the participant's automated pricing, if anyone.                                                           |

Rules:

1. A negotiation session MUST use the **intersection** of the two adverts.
1. Any term-sheet issue that is not in the intersected `negotiable_issues` is **fixed**. A counter-offer that changes a fixed issue is refused with `NEG_ISSUE_NOT_NEGOTIABLE`.
1. If no `max_rounds` is agreed, the default is 10 for consumer sessions and 30 for business sessions.
1. `min_offer_validity` is at least `PT5M` in every profile. A counterparty's advert cannot lower this floor.
1. If the mode intersection is empty, `POST /negotiations` returns `201` with the message `capabilities_incompatible` (`requires_buyer_input`), and the agent falls back to mode `fixed`, an ordinary catalogue checkout.

See [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md).

## Payment handlers in the profile

`payment_handlers` lists the handlers the gateway can process. Each entry is a handler reference: a canonical id such as `in.upi.reservepay`, or an alias accepted during its deprecation window, such as `upi.reservepay.block`.

- A gateway MUST emit canonical ids in new profiles. Consumers MUST accept any handler reference and MUST compare handlers only after resolving them in the [handler registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).
- A reference that does not resolve MUST be treated as not supported.
- Listing a handler does not make it usable for every payment. Which handlers can pay for a given deal is decided by the **handler intersection**: the registry (live handlers, and pilot handlers only if the gateway's conformance attestation lists them), ∩ the gateway profile's `payment_handlers`, ∩ the seller's accepted handlers, ∩ the term sheet's payment options, ∩ the handlers the mandates allow, ∩ the handlers eligible at the session's presence, ∩ the amount limits, ∩ the instruments the Trusted Surface reports as available. The result is ordered by the principal's own preference, then the lowest all-in total, then the least authentication friction. It is never ordered by platform incentives.
- An empty intersection gives `200` with `handlers_incompatible` (`requires_buyer_input`).

`GET /payment-handlers` (public, unsigned, cacheable with `ETag`) returns the registry as handler descriptors. The response **MUST** carry a `Cache-Control` header with a `max-age` of at most 86400 (for example `Cache-Control: max-age=86400`), so that no cache holds a copy for more than 24 hours. Because the response is unsigned, a Mandate Manager or gateway **MUST NOT** use it as its registry source for open-mandate eligibility ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)). `POST /payment-handlers/intersect` computes an intersection. The intersect request carries a `negotiation_id` or, on a gateway that lists `in.bacp.payment_plan`, a `session_id` alone ([Q-45](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-45), settled); any other gateway requires the `negotiation_id`. Details are on [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).

## Registry lookup

The gateway relies on the network registry (the ONDC registry, or another accredited registry) for every key and status it trusts. It uses the registry to:

| Lookup                                                                             | Used for                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AgentCredential issuer keys and status list                                        | Verifying each agent's credential and that it is not revoked ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/index.md))                                                                                                      |
| BPP subscriber keys                                                                | Verifying the network signatures on `on_*` callbacks, quotes and negotiation messages                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| BPP subscriber keys (agent)                                                        | An agent verifying the `on_search` sources of presented discovery results ([Verifying discovery results](#verifying-results))                                                                                                                                               |
| Mandate Manager and PSP keys                                                       | Verifying mandates, rail-binding attestations, receipts and Trusted Surface events                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Trusted Surface origins, notify endpoint and languages of a Mandate Manager or PSP | Minting `trusted_surface_url` only on an origin of the step-up's signer, sending the content-free `app_push`, and refusing to offer a language the signer does not claim ([Origins and delivery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-origins)) |
| `support_operator` keys                                                            | Accepting a handoff only from a key whose record names its agent operator and one person ([Human handoff](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#handoff))                                                                                           |
| Regulatory status (`regulatory_status`)                                            | Checking, before money moves, that the party in `collected_by` has a `verified` `rbi_pa` or `bank` entry, so that it is an RBI-authorised payment aggregator or a bank                                                                                                      |
| Operator (`operator`)                                                              | Checking that two participants are not the same operator, for the separation rules of [conformance attestations](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules) and of discovery lookups                                                         |
| Conformance attestations                                                           | Checking which [conformance levels](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/index.md) a counterparty has passed                                                                                                                                               |

Rules:

1. The gateway MUST resolve keys by key id from the registry. Key ids are registry-resolvable, for example `bap.example.in|ukid-7|ed25519` (subscriber id, unique key id, algorithm) or a `did:web` URL with a fragment.
1. The gateway MAY cache a registry record until the record's own validity ends, and MUST NOT use it after that.
1. A key that the registry does not know, or a credential that its status list marks revoked, MUST be rejected (`agent_unregistered`, `agent_credential_revoked`).
1. A BACP-aware BPP resolves the BAP's keys, and the keys of the buyer's credential provider, through the same registry.
1. An agent that verifies a discovery source MUST resolve the BPP's key from the network registry's own endpoint, or through a lookup service whose operator is neither the gateway's operator nor shares an operator with the gateway's BAP. An agent operator that also operates, or shares an operator with, the gateway's BAP MUST use the network registry's own endpoint. Operators are compared as in [Conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules): by the `operator` of the registry record with `assertion: registry`, never by a profile or a response that the gateway supplies, and an operator that is not asserted by the registry is unknown, which means the agent uses the network registry's own endpoint. The agent MUST NOT use a key, a registry record or a lookup response that the gateway supplies. The agent records the lookup source in the `discover` InstructionLog entry.

**Registry record.** The part of a registry record that BACP reads is the schema [`registry-record.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/registry-record.json): `subscriber_id`, `bacp_role` (the `Signature.role` value), `keys[]`, `valid_from`, `valid_until` and `status`; for a Mandate Manager or a PSP, `ts_origins[]`, `ts_notify_url`, `ts_call_numbers[]`, `ts_languages[]` and `ts_modalities[]`; and for a `support_operator`, `operator_id` and `person_ref`, with exactly one key. Any record may also carry the legal `operator` (`legal_name`, `entity_ids[]`, `assertion` and an optional `group_id`), `regulatory_status[]` (each entry a dated, sourced statement with `regime`, `verified_on` and `status` of `verified` or `declared`) and a `data_residency` statement. `assertion: registry` means that the network registry's own lookup response carries the operator, which is the only form a separation check relies on; a `declared` or absent operator is unknown, and an unknown operator fails closed. A `declared` regulatory status is never treated as verified. A record whose `regulatory_status` has an `rbi_pa` or `rbi_ppi` entry has a company: its `entity_ids[]` contain a 21-character CIN. A registry may carry more fields, and a reader ignores any it does not know. Whether the ONDC network registry can carry `bacp_role`, `operator_id`, `person_ref` and the Trusted Surface fields is not settled (a question for ONDC). Where it cannot, BACP needs a side registry, which is a second trust root that this version does not define.

Which body anchors agent identity and issues AgentCredentials (an NPCI agent registry, the ONDC registry, or decentralised identifiers) is open ([Q-02](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-02)). BACP is issuer-agnostic: any accredited issuer whose keys the registry publishes can issue AgentCredentials.

## Network discovery

`POST /discover` searches the network on the agent's behalf. Capability `in.bacp.discover`; signature tag `bacp-browse`; `Idempotency-Key` REQUIRED.

Request fields:

| Field         | Meaning                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query`       | What to find, as a multilingual map, for example `{"hi-IN": "एक लीटर दूध"}`. REQUIRED. |
| `category`    | An ONDC domain or category code, for example `ONDC:RET10`.                            |
| `delivery`    | Delivery `pincode` or `gps`.                                                          |
| `mandate_ref` | An open Checkout Mandate. When present, each result is flagged `within_mandate`.      |
| `max_wait_ms` | How long to collect `on_search` callbacks.                                            |

What the gateway does on the network:

1. It verifies the agent's signature and credential.
1. It sends a Beckn `search` through the Beckn gateway with `context.bacp` (agent, presence, idempotency key, and the mandate reference when given). Network participants that do not speak BACP ignore `context.bacp`.
1. It collects `on_search` callbacks until `max_wait_ms`, verifies each seller's network signature against the registry, and drops callbacks it cannot verify. It keeps every callback it accepts, with its `Authorization` header, exactly as received ([Retention of the signed callbacks](#catalogue-retention)).
1. It returns the aggregated `results`: one entry per `on_search` callback, each with `bpp_id`, provider, items and a `source_digest` (the sha-256 of the raw BPP-signed `on_search` body that every item of the entry came from; a gateway that merges items from several callbacks of one provider returns one entry per callback), plus `within_mandate` when a mandate was given. Every item carries its own `sponsorship`, and `mrp`, `tax_inclusive` and `prior_price` where the seller sent them ([Catalogue disclosures](#catalogue-disclosures)). A result also carries the seller's published `offers[]`, where it sent any ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts)). `complete: false` means some sellers had not answered in time.
1. It returns `ranking`: the main parameters used to order results, in descending order of importance (for example distance, price and seller rating), an optional `description_url`, and `sponsored`, which is `true` if and only if at least one item is `sponsored`.

Catalogue text, including product names and descriptions, is untrusted input. Agents MUST treat it as data and never as instructions.

### Ranking by payment rungs

The gateway's default discovery ranking MUST NOT use any of these as a parameter:

- the handler rungs a seller offers, or whether it offers a human-not-present (HNP) rung;
- the seller's merchant discount rate, or its small-merchant (P2PM) category;
- Verified Merchant status;
- the level or acceptance of a finder fee.

The one exception is a finder fee that is paid to the operator for an item's prominence or selection: the agent then renders that item as `sponsored` with `by: agent` under [Declaring the status](#catalogue-disclosures), rule 7.

- A seller without an HNP rung is never dropped. Its result carries `needs_principal_factor: true`, which tells the agent that the principal must pay that seller herself, and keeps its rank.
- A principal's own filter ("only shops I can pay without a PIN") is allowed. The gateway logs it, and it never becomes a default for a later session.
- This is BACP policy. BACP does not cite the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 r.5(3)(f) as the source of a prohibition. The rule extends the [handler-order rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-intersection-and-preference). It also reflects NPCI OC 228, which enables Reserve Pay at first "only for online verified merchants with low ticket and high frequency transactions": a seller without that rung has done nothing wrong, and ranking would otherwise penalise the small shop first.

### Seller confirmation profile

A seller MAY declare `requires_principal_confirmation` on its discover result: `{reason, above_amount?}`, where `reason` is `made_to_order`, `age_restricted` or `high_value_cod`. `above_amount` (an `Amount`) is REQUIRED for `high_value_cod` and absent for the other reasons. On Beckn the declaration travels in the `bacp.confirmation` tag group of the signed `on_search` ([mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#disclosure-mapping)).

- For an order the declaration covers, the gateway raises a `confirm` step-up with reason `constraint_unresolved` ([Step-up](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#step-up)) before any money moves. It counts as a step-up like any other for any limit the specification sets on step-ups.
- The declaration MUST NOT change a price or a handler. It is a prompt to the human, not a pricing lever.
- A confirmation that the seller asks for at `on_init` without having declared it is treated like drip pricing: the same `confirm` step-up, reason `constraint_unresolved`. A seller that asks through the BPP-signed tag `seller_confirmation` in `on_select` or `on_init` gets a `confirm` step-up with reason `seller_confirmation` and a template sentence for the value ([Seller refusals and substitution](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#seller-reasons)).
- The gateway logs, for each seller, how often a declared or an undeclared confirmation is raised.

The response's `transaction_id` is the Beckn transaction id; the agent passes it to `POST /sessions`. The gateway MUST sign the response ([Response signature](#response-signature)). See [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md) and [Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/index.md).

### Verifying discovery results

A discover response is the gateway's own message. The seller's values in it (`unit_price`, `mrp`, `tax_inclusive`, `prior_price` and the seller's sponsorship) reach the agent through the gateway, so an agent that shows or relies on one of them checks it against the seller's signed callback, which the gateway serves by `source_digest`.

**Fetching a source.** `GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}` (capability `in.bacp.discover`; RFC 9421 request signature under tag `bacp-browse`; no `Idempotency-Key`, because it is a read) returns `200` with a `BecknSignedMessage`: the `on_search` body exactly as the gateway received it, and its Beckn `Authorization` header.

- The gateway serves a source only to the agent whose `POST /discover` produced the `transaction_id`. Every other caller, and an unknown digest, gets `404 not_found`.
- The gateway counts the rate limit per caller key before it looks up the `transaction_id` or the `source_digest`, so that a `429 quota_exceeded` never depends on whether the source exists.
- The gateway MUST serve a source for as long as it must keep it ([Retention](#catalogue-retention)).
- `source_digest` is sha-256 only, in the form `sha-256:<base64url>`, computed over the exact bytes of `body` as UTF-8 text. Every item of a `results[]` entry MUST come from the one callback that its `source_digest` names.

**What the agent MUST verify.** For each result whose items the agent *presents* (shows or reads to a principal) or *relies on* (selects, sorts or compares by `prior_price`, `mrp` or an offer figure), the agent MUST run the steps below. It runs them once for each distinct `source_digest`, and MAY cache the outcome by digest.

1. Fetch the source, or reuse a cached copy. The sha-256 of `body` MUST equal `source_digest`.
1. Parse `body` as JSON. A body with a duplicate member name, or one that exceeds the agent's size or nesting limits (measured on the decoded body), is unverified. RFC 8259 §4 says member names SHOULD be unique, and a duplicate lets two parsers read different values. BACP states no numeric limit.
1. Check the binding to this search:
   - `context.action` is `on_search`;
   - `context.bpp_id` equals the result's `bpp_id` and the subscriber id in the `keyId` of the `Authorization` header;
   - `context.bap_id` equals the `bap_id` of the gateway's profile;
   - `context.transaction_id` equals the response's `transaction_id`;
   - `context.message_id` equals `UUIDv5(message_id_namespace, agent_id | Idempotency-Key | "search")`, with the namespace from the gateway's profile ([Message ids](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#message-ids));
   - `created` in the `Authorization` header is not earlier than 300 seconds before the agent sent the `POST /discover`;
   - the agent SHOULD also compare `context.city` (or `context.location`), where the network carries it, with the delivery area it requested; a difference is a mismatch.

Because the agent chooses the `Idempotency-Key` of the search and never reuses it ([Idempotency](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#idempotency)), this binding stops a gateway from replaying a genuine signed callback from an earlier search. BACP adds no weaker freshness binding: a gateway that answers from a cached catalogue cannot meet it, and every claim in its results is unverified. A gateway that wants verified claims sends a targeted live `search` to the shortlisted sellers with the agent's `message_id`. 4. Resolve the BPP's key as the [registry lookup](#registry-lookup) rule 5 requires, never from the gateway. The key MUST be listed with registry role BPP and MUST be valid both at the `created` time of the signature and at the time of verification. An unknown, revoked, expired or wrong-role key leaves the source unverified. 5. Verify the Beckn signature over the body: Ed25519 over `(created)`, `(expires)` and the BLAKE2b-512 digest ([Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#signing)). The agent does not compare `expires` with the current time, because the callback is a stored artefact; freshness comes from step 3. 6. Locate the provider and item in `message.catalog` and derive the values by the [normative mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#disclosure-mapping). Compare them with the result.

Each item ends in one of three outcomes: **verified**; **mismatch** (steps 1 to 5 pass but a value differs); or **unverified** (any step fails, or the item is not in the body). A claim that the body carries and the result leaves out (for example a `prior_price` the gateway dropped and flagged `prior_price_invalid`) is not a mismatch: the agent makes no claim.
