| Outcome    | `prior_price`, `mrp`, offer figures                                                                                 | Sponsorship                                                                                                                       | `unit_price`                                                 | Record                                                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| verified   | Rendered per [Disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases) | As returned                                                                                                                       | As returned                                                  |                                                                                                    |
| unverified | MUST NOT be rendered or relied on: no claim                                                                         | `sponsored` (with the result's `by`) if the result says `sponsored`; otherwise rendered as `undeclared`, never as `not_sponsored` | MAY be shown as the price, never as half of a reduction pair | InstructionLog stage `discover`, reason `discovery_source_unverified`                              |
| mismatch   | MUST NOT render the result's value; MAY render the value derived from the verified body                             | The higher of the result's and the body's, by the precedence `sponsored`, `undeclared`, `not_sponsored`                           | The body's value                                             | Reason `discovery_source_mismatch`; the agent SHOULD report it to its operator's grievance contact |

The values that can make a principal pay are the reduction claim and the MRP anchor, so these fail closed. Sponsorship fails towards more disclosure, so a gateway gains nothing by breaking verification. An agent that presents nothing and relies on no claim, such as an agent in a human-not-present flow that buys by `unit_price` alone, has no duty to fetch a source. An agent that chooses between results by comparing `unit_price` MUST either verify those results by the steps above or, before `complete`, compare the chosen item's BPP-signed quote unit price with the discovered one. If the quote is higher, the choice no longer stands, and the agent re-ranks on quoted prices or escalates to the principal.

**At checkout.** When a session returns `Disclosures.catalogue[]`, an agent that verified or presented the items MUST check each entry against the values it presented for that item at discovery. The agent MUST also check that every line item it chose from a discover response has exactly one `catalogue[]` entry with that `item_id`. A missing entry is a mismatch. The entry's `source_digest` MUST be one the agent checked for that item, its `sponsorship.status` MUST NOT be weaker than the presented value (by the precedence `sponsored`, `undeclared`, `not_sponsored`) and its `sponsorship.by[]` MUST contain every party of the `sponsorship.by[]` the agent presented, and its `prior_price`, `mrp` and `discovered_unit_price` MUST equal the presented values. Otherwise the agent records `discovery_source_mismatch` and treats the session as `requires_buyer_review`. This closes the gap in which a gateway swaps in a different genuine callback at checkout.

The agent records, in the InstructionLog entry at stage `discover`, the digest of every source it checked, the outcome of each, the `Idempotency-Key` of the search and the host of the registry lookup it used ([Instruction log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#instruction-log)).

*Cost to agents (informative).* The work per distinct callback is one sha-256, one BLAKE2b-512 and one Ed25519 verification, which is small (analysis, not measured). An agent fetches one source for each distinct callback among the results it presents, in parallel. The size of an `on_search` body is not measured (not verified as of 18-10-2026), so an agent MAY cap the decoded size it accepts and treat a larger body as unverified. The real cost is registry access: ONDC's recommended lookup takes an `Authorization` header signed by a subscriber key, and the unsigned lookups are marked deprecated (reported by ONDC's developer documentation, not verified as of 18-10-2026), so an agent operator that is not an ONDC subscriber needs its own subscription or a lookup service it trusts that the gateway does not run ([Q-70](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-70)). If that is impractical, every presented item degrades to `undeclared` with no claim, which is safe.

#### Response signature

The gateway MUST sign the `POST /discover` response with RFC 9421, covering `@status` and `content-digest` ([Content-Digest](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#content-digest)), under a key published in its profile's `keys`, the key it uses for webhooks. The response MUST carry `Content-Digest`, `Signature-Input` and `Signature` headers. This makes the values that only the gateway asserts (`by: gateway`, `not_sponsored` for its own ranking, and `ranking`) non-repudiable, also for an item that was shown but not bought. An agent MAY verify the signature, and SHOULD keep the signed response with the InstructionLog entry of the search.

### Catalogue disclosures

Every item in a discover response carries the data that an e-commerce entity needs to tell a buyer whether a result is a sponsored listing, what the seller's lowest recent price was, and what the printed maximum retail price is. BACP carries that data. Whether an agent operator or a gateway is itself an "e-commerce entity" under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, as amended by the Amendment Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027), is a question for counsel, and it is open ([Q-66](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-66)). The rules below bind BACP participants whichever way it is answered.

| Item field      | Required                                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sponsorship`   | REQUIRED                                            | `{status, by[]}`. `status` is `sponsored`, `not_sponsored` or `undeclared`. `by[]` lists who sold the placement and is REQUIRED when `status` is `sponsored` and absent otherwise.                                                                              |
| `mrp`           | OPTIONAL                                            | The Legal Metrology retail sale price, inclusive of all taxes, as an `Amount` in integer paise. It maps from Beckn `price.maximum_value`.                                                                                                                       |
| `tax_inclusive` | REQUIRED whenever `mrp` or `prior_price` is present | Whether `unit_price` and `prior_price` include all taxes.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `prior_price`   | OPTIONAL                                            | `{amount, basis, announced_on}`: the lowest price of the item in the 30 days before `announced_on`, asserted by the seller (BPP). `basis` has one value, `lowest_30d`. Its presence is the claim that the seller announced a price reduction on `announced_on`. |
| `measure`       | RECOMMENDED                                         | The item's sale measure, a `QuantityUnit` ([Units](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#units)).                                                                                                                                                 |
| `policies[]`    | OPTIONAL                                            | Typed policies `{type, allowed, window, applies_to[], description, url}`, with `type` one of `in.bacp.policy.return`, `in.bacp.policy.cancel` and `in.bacp.policy.cod` ([Typed policies](#typed-policies)).                                                     |
| `min_order`     | RECOMMENDED                                         | `{value, item_qty}` on the item or its provider: the smallest basket total or item quantity that the seller accepts.                                                                                                                                            |

**Sponsored.** An item is *sponsored* when its position or selection was affected by payment, including through a ranking parameter that a party can buy. This is BACP policy. It is not a statutory definition.

**Declaring the status.**

1. A gateway MUST return `sponsorship` on every item. An agent that receives an item with no `sponsorship` (from an older or non-conforming gateway) MUST treat it as `undeclared`.
1. The party that orders the results MUST declare `sponsored` or `not_sponsored` for its own ranking. `undeclared` arises only when that order relays an upstream promotion or ordering signal whose paid status the ranking party does not know and did not price.
1. `by[]` is the party that sold the placement and asserts it: `bpp` (the seller app), `gateway` (the buyer app's gateway) or `agent` (the agent operator). It is an array because several parties can sell placement for one item. A reader MUST render an unknown `by` value as "sponsored, party unknown".
1. When a placement is sold for a provider (a "featured store"), every item of that provider in the response is `sponsored`, and `by[]` names the party that sold the placement.
1. **Monotone OR.** The precedence is `sponsored`, then `undeclared`, then `not_sponsored`. No party lowers a value that an upstream party set, and `by[]` is the union of the parties that sold placement. A seller that sends `bacp.disclosure` with `sponsored` set to `"true"` makes the item `sponsored` with `bpp` in `by[]`.
1. `ranking.sponsored` is `true` if and only if some item is `sponsored`. The schema enforces both directions.
1. An agent whose operator is paid for an item's prominence or selection MUST render that item as `sponsored` with `by: agent`, whatever the gateway returned.

**Prior price, MRP and the price figures.**

1. Only the BPP asserts `prior_price`. The gateway MUST relay `prior_price`, `mrp`, `tax_inclusive` and the BPP's sponsorship unaltered. It MUST NOT synthesise a `prior_price`, and MUST NOT derive one from Beckn `listed_value`, `offered_value` or `maximum_value`.
1. The gateway drops a `prior_price` whose `amount` is not above the item's `unit_price`, or is above `mrp` while `tax_inclusive` is `true`, and reports `prior_price_invalid` (`warning`, `recoverable`) at `$.results[n].items[m].prior_price`.
1. When `tax_inclusive` is `true` and `unit_price` is above `mrp`, the gateway reports `NEG_MRP_EXCEEDED` at `$.results[n].items[m].unit_price`. A comparison with `mrp` runs only when `tax_inclusive` is `true`.
1. A gateway MAY check a `prior_price` against prices it has itself seen for the same key: `bpp_id`, provider, item and the `area_code` of the search. If it saw a lower price in the 30 days before `announced_on`, it reports `prior_price_contradicted` (`warning`, advisory, `recoverable`) at `$.results[n].items[m].prior_price` and relays the value unaltered. The flag is advisory.
1. The gateway's default ranking MUST NOT use the size of a discount. When the principal asks to sort by discount, the gateway MAY use it, computed from `prior_price` only, and MUST list it in `ranking.main_parameters`.
1. A B2B profile is not exempt from these fields. An agent MUST NOT block a quote that carries a PTR-plus-scheme price for want of a `prior_price`. Schemes stay in TermSheet `scheme` mode ([Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md)).

**What an agent that presents results MUST do.** An agent *presents* a result when it shows or reads it to a principal.

1. It renders each item's sponsorship with the fixed phrases of [Disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases): the `sponsored` sentence with the party for `sponsored`, and the `undeclared` sentence for `undeclared`. It never renders `undeclared` as "not sponsored". For `not_sponsored` it says nothing. On audio, the label is spoken before the item. A paraphrase is non-conformant.
1. It shows or voices a reduction only as the amount pair of `prior_price` ("Now ₹549. The seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this offer: ₹599"), before any percentage, and never measured from `mrp`.
1. It MUST NOT show or voice a reduced price, a strike-through, a "was" or "off" claim or a percentage for an item that has no `prior_price`, whatever produced the reduction. It never shows `mrp` as a "was" price or strikes it through.
1. It MUST NOT show or voice a price figure, percentage, "was" or "off" claim taken from catalogue free text, such as an item name or description.
1. It SHOULD NOT voice the reduction claim of an item whose `prior_price` the gateway flagged `prior_price_contradicted`. This is a SHOULD because the rate of false flags has not been measured.
1. For a principal that is not present (HNP), it SHOULD NOT weight `sponsored` items in selection unless the principal asked for that. This is guidance, and not a mandate constraint, because an unknown constraint fails closed.

After a session is created for items from a discover response, the gateway copies each such item's discovered values into `Disclosures.catalogue[]` ([Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#update)).

#### Typed policies and minimum order

The typed policies are a projection of tags that ONDC sellers already send, so that an agent can read a return window without parsing prose. The binding text is still the disclosure.

1. **Projection.** The gateway projects `returnable` and `return_window` to `in.bacp.policy.return` (`allowed`, `window`), `cancellable` to `in.bacp.policy.cancel` and `available_on_cod` to `in.bacp.policy.cod`. It projects `time_to_ship` to the `tat` of the session's fulfilment option ([Fulfilment options](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fulfilment-options)), not to a policy. `description` and `url` are counterparty text.
1. **Hashed.** The session's typed policies are hashed into `disclosures.hash` with the rest of the disclosures, so that an approval covers them.
1. **Checked against the text.** The gateway compares each typed value with the binding `return_terms` and `cancellation_terms`. A typed value that contradicts the binding text raises the warning `policy_text_mismatch` (`requires_buyer_review`) and the session moves to `requires_escalation` with a `confirm` step-up, so that the session never reaches `ready_for_complete` on a typed value that the text denies.
1. **What the agent says.** The agent speaks the binding text, or a typed value only where the gateway has checked it against that text. A policy that the seller does not state is spoken as "not stated" (`policy_not_stated`, [Disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases)), never as "no returns".
1. **Minimum order.** A session whose basket is below the `min_order` of its provider or of one of its items is refused with `400 invalid_request` at `$.items`, never silently dropped or padded. `min_order` is a SHOULD for a seller that sets one.

#### Retention of the signed callbacks

The gateway MUST keep every `on_search` callback behind a `source_digest` it returned, as received, for as long as it keeps the session's evidence ([Retention](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#retention)). The evidence bundle carries the callbacks for every item in the session's `Disclosures.catalogue[]` ([Bundle contents](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#contents)).

# Errors

BACP reports problems on two channels, following the ACP error model. A request that the gateway could not accept fails with an HTTP error status and a flat `Error` object. A request that the gateway accepted, but whose business outcome the agent must act on, succeeds (200 or 201, or 202 where the operation is accepted asynchronously) with the full authoritative state and a `messages[]` array. This page defines both shapes, the resolution vocabulary that tells an agent what it may do next, and the registry of every code a conforming participant may emit.

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release. Codes are stable identifiers. A participant MUST NOT emit a code that is not registered on this page.

## Two channels

| Channel              | When                                                                                                                                    | HTTP status                                                                                             | Body                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Protocol failure** | The request was malformed, unauthenticated, unauthorised, refused by the deterministic mandate verifier, or could not reach the seller. | 4xx or 5xx                                                                                              | One flat [`Error`](#error-object) object                                                |
| **Business outcome** | The request was processed and the resource has a new authoritative state, but the agent must take note, ask the principal, or wait.     | 200 or 201; 202 for asynchronous operations (`POST /mandates`, return requests, Trusted Surface events) | The full resource (session, order, negotiation, …) with [`messages[]`](#message-object) |

Rules:

1. A gateway MUST return protocol failures as 4xx or 5xx with a flat `Error`. It MUST NOT wrap them in a 200.
1. A gateway MUST return business outcomes as 200, 201 or (for asynchronous operations) 202 with the full resource state and `messages[]`. The agent MUST treat the returned state as authoritative and MUST NOT reconstruct state from earlier responses.
1. **Step-up is never only an error.** When a human must approve, the resource moves to `status: requires_escalation`, carries a `step_up` object, and carries the message `step_up_required` with `resolution: requires_buyer_review`. See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md) and [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/index.md).
1. `param` is an RFC 9535 JSONPath into the request (for an `Error`) or into the returned resource (for a message), for example `$.mandate_ref` or `$.payment.scheduled_debit_at`. Header problems use `$.headers.<Name>`.

### Dual-channel codes

Some validator and guard codes can appear on either channel. The rule is:

- the code is a **200 message** when it describes an *incoming* counterparty object or a *computed* outcome (a handler intersection, a seller's offer);
- the code is a **403 error** when it blocks the caller's *own outgoing* commitment (a firm COUNTER, an ACCEPT, a bid, an award, a session update or `complete`).

For example, `handlers_incompatible` is a 200 message on `POST /payment-handlers/intersect` and a 403 error on an ACCEPT whose agreed payment option has no eligible handler. Registry rows marked "200 msg / 403" follow this rule.

A code that also appears as a 200 `error` message on a session cancelled by a mandate event (`mandate_expired`, `mandate_revoked`, `mandate_paused`, `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`) mirrors that code's error status: the message reports the same condition that `complete` would return as an error.

## The Error object

| Field                | Type                    | Required    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type`               | enum                    | yes         | Error class: `invalid_request`, `authentication_error`, `authorization_error`, `mandate_error`, `payment_error`, `upstream_error`, `service_unavailable`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `code`               | string                  | yes         | A code from the [registry](#registry)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `message`            | string                  | yes         | Human-readable explanation for logs and developers. Agents MUST NOT present it to the principal as a legal notice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `param`              | string                  | no          | RFC 9535 JSONPath to the offending field                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `resolution`         | enum                    | no          | How the agent should proceed; one of the [resolution values](#resolution). Gateways SHOULD send it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `reasons`            | array of string         | conditional | Every local and rail reason that applied. REQUIRED on rail-cap and step-up errors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `step_up_kind`       | enum                    | conditional | `confirm` or `rail_auth`. REQUIRED on step-up errors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `supported_versions` | array of string         | conditional | The versions that the gateway lists. REQUIRED on `version_unsupported` and absent on every other code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `capability`         | string                  | conditional | The capability id that owns the refused member. REQUIRED on `capability_unsupported` and absent on every other code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `reason`             | enum                    | conditional | `no_conforming_origin`, `language_unavailable` or `channel_not_allowed`. REQUIRED on `trusted_surface_unavailable` and absent on every other code. Not to be confused with `reasons`.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `seller_reason`      | object                  | conditional | On `bpp_nack` only: `{code, beckn_code}`, the reason the seller refused. `code` is `item_unavailable`, `quantity_reduced`, `price_changed`, `not_serviceable`, `store_closed`, `agent_orders_not_accepted`, `terms_mismatch` or `other`. The gateway sets it only from the BPP-signed NACK, and an unmapped Beckn code gives `other`. Which ONDC code maps to which value is for ONDC to answer. |
| `handoff_routes`     | array of `HandoffRoute` | conditional | On `trusted_surface_unavailable` with `reason` `language_unavailable` or `channel_not_allowed`: the session's `ai_disclosure.handoff_routes`, so that the agent can offer the principal a human. Absent when the session lists none.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `step_up`            | object                  | conditional | On `403 presence_not_proven` for a post-order write without `hp_proof`: a `StepUp` of kind `post_order` (reason `presence_proof`) that the principal confirms on the Trusted Surface to obtain the proof ([Presence proof](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#hp-proof)).                                                                                             |

Rail-cap and step-up errors MUST also carry `reasons[]` (every local and rail reason that applied) and `step_up_kind`. `idempotency_in_flight` and `quota_exceeded` MUST be sent with a `Retry-After` header.

```
{
  "type": "mandate_error",
  "code": "mandate_revoked",
  "message": "Mandate mdt_PAY7Q2W9X4K1M3 is REVOKED",
  "param": "$.mandate_ref"
}
```

## The Message object

| Field        | Type     | Required    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `type`       | enum     | yes         | `error`, `warning`, `info` or `disclosure`                                                                                                                                           |
| `code`       | string   | yes         | A code from the [registry](#registry)                                                                                                                                                |
| `origin`     | enum     | conditional | Who wrote `content`: `gateway` (the default when `args` is absent) or `counterparty`. REQUIRED whenever `args` is present.                                                           |
| `content`    | LangText | yes         | Multilingual text keyed by BCP 47 tag, for example `{"hi-IN": "…", "en-IN": "…"}`. A gateway-written `content` never contains counterparty text.                                     |
| `args`       | array    | no          | Values inserted at `{name}` placeholders in `content`, each `{name, origin, text}`. A counterparty value (an item name, a fee label) travels only here, with `origin: counterparty`. |
| `param`      | string   | no          | RFC 9535 JSONPath into the returned resource                                                                                                                                         |
| `resolution` | enum     | yes         | What the agent may do next (see [Resolution](#resolution))                                                                                                                           |

```
{
  "type": "warning",
  "code": "payment_in_doubt",
  "content": {
    "en-IN": "Debit status unknown. Reconciling with the PSP. Do not retry with a new key."
  },
  "param": "$.payment.status",
  "resolution": "recoverable"
}
```

The first message of every checkout session is the `ai_disclosure` message (`type: disclosure`), which carries the agent's AI notice in the principal's language and points (`param: $.ai_disclosure`) at the session's typed routes to a human.

For a message with `type: disclosure` and a code registered below with that type (`sponsored_listing`, `sponsorship_undeclared` and `prior_price_claim`), an agent that presents the session to a principal MUST present the fixed phrase for that code from [Disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases), in the principal's language, next to what `param` names, with the item's name, as labelled seller text, taken from the session line whose item is the `catalogue[]` entry's `item_id`, never from `args`. It fills the phrase's slots from the `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry that `param` names. It MUST NOT summarise, hide or drop the message, and it hands off to a human rather than present it in a reduced form. It never reads the message's `content` in place of the fixed phrase. A `type: disclosure` message with an unregistered code is treated as `info`: the agent records it and does not read it verbatim. `ai_disclosure` keeps its own rule.

## Resolution

Every `Error` code and every message has exactly one `resolution`. On a seller-side gateway a code whose registry resolution is `requires_buyer_review` is emitted with `requires_seller_review`, because the principal who reviews is the seller's. The one exception is `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`, whose registry row gives a resolution per cause; the `Error.resolution` field then carries the one that applies:

| Value                    | Meaning for the agent                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `recoverable`            | The agent may fix the request itself (re-select, wait, GET and retry with the same key) without involving the principal.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `requires_buyer_input`   | The agent must ask the principal for something new: set up or renew a mandate, choose another payment method, supply missing data.                                                                                                                                             |
| `requires_buyer_review`  | A human must review and approve on the Trusted Surface (step-up, disclosure review, out-of-scope action). The agent MUST NOT approve on the principal's behalf.                                                                                                                |
| `requires_seller_review` | The same, for the seller principal: a message that a seller-side gateway emits and that its principal reviews, in the seller application or on the seller's Trusted Surface. The agent MUST NOT approve on the seller principal's behalf. A buyer-side gateway never emits it. |
| `unrecoverable`          | The request cannot succeed as sent. The agent must not retry it; an operator may need to act.                                                                                                                                                                                  |

"Informational" is not a resolution value. Purely informational messages use `type: info` with `resolution: recoverable`.

## Client behaviour

- An agent that meets a code it does not know MUST act on the HTTP status class (and, for messages, on `resolution`). It MUST NOT retry a 4xx with a new `Idempotency-Key`: a new key is a new purchase intent and is evaluated against the mandate afresh.
- After a 5xx, a timeout or a lost response, the agent MUST first `GET` the resource and MAY then retry only with the **same** `Idempotency-Key` (see [REST binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/#idempotency)).
- On `payment_in_doubt` the agent MUST NOT re-key. The gateway reconciles with the PSP and reports the outcome.
- A new code MUST be registered here, with its HTTP status and resolution, before any participant emits it.
- A conformance run fails on any unregistered code (see [Conformance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/index.md)).

## Registry

"200 msg" means the code arrives in `messages[]` on a 200 or 201 response. "200 + `step_up`" means the resource moves to `requires_escalation` with a `step_up` object. A dash in the *Typical param* column means no single field applies.

**Why `rail_binding_not_open_eligible` is 400.** On `complete`, this code can be a refusal by the deterministic verifier of a well-formed, signed mandate (for example after a registry downgrade), which would normally be a 403 `mandate_error`. BACP keeps it on 400 `invalid_request` deliberately, so that one code keeps one status at `POST /mandates` and at `complete` and the registry entry stays unchanged. Moving the code to 403 was considered and not adopted. Both statuses are on the protocol-failure channel and carry the same resolution, so a client handles them the same way.

### Session and payment messages

These are always 200 or 201 messages. `prior_price_contradicted` and `prior_price_invalid` arrive in `messages[]` of a discover response; the others arrive on a session.

| `NEG_SCHEMA_INVALID`                     | 400                                     | The negotiation message or TermSheet fails its schema, or carries an extension issue the guard cannot evaluate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | the offending field                                                               | recoverable                                       |

| `NEG_STALE_OFFER`                        | 409                                     | The message cites an offer that is not the live offer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `$.in_reply_to`                                                                   | recoverable (GET, then respond to the live offer) |
| `NEG_OFFER_EXPIRED`                      | 200 msg / 403 (own, local)              | The cited offer is past `expires_at` on the offeror's receipt, or the acceptor's gateway refused locally to dispatch an accept within 5 s of `expires_at` on its own clock. ### Payment-handler and rail codes

These are raised by the handler and rail layer. When a gateway surfaces one over HTTP it MUST use the status given here. "200 msg" codes come back on `POST /payment-handlers/intersect` as `excluded[].reason` or as messages. See [Payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md) and [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).

| Code                            | HTTP when surfaced        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Typical `param`                | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `presence_handler_mismatch`     | 403                       | The handler needs a human-completed authentication but the request is human-not-present (or the handler needs an assisted session).                                                                                                                             | `$.presence`                   | requires_buyer_review                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `reservepay_block_wrong_payee`  | 403                       | A Reserve Pay debit for a seller other than the block's payee.                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `$.payment.handler`            | requires_buyer_input (pay this seller with another eligible handler under the per-leg rule, usually one human-present payment; a new block for this seller is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment, never after a failed payment) |
| `payee_mismatch`                | rail failure receipt      | Rail-level twin of the above: the rail refused a debit to a payee its authority does not cover.                                                                                                                                                                 | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `cod_not_allowed`               | 403                       | Cash on delivery is not allowed by the governing mandate.                                                                                                                                                                                                       | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `cod_open_orders_cap`           | 403 / 200 msg (intersect) | The mandate's cap on open COD orders is reached.                                                                                                                                                                                                                | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Rail and ledger refusals

These codes are returned by a rail or by the [khata credit ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#the-khata-credit-ledger) to the participant that called it. They follow the "rail refusal" rows of the table above: no money moves. A gateway that reports one to an agent MUST use the code unchanged and, over HTTP, the status given here.

| Code                               | Raised by      | HTTP when surfaced | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Typical `param`                | Resolution                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `afa_required`                     | rail refusal   | 403                | The debit needs an additional factor of authentication (for example a human-present wallet debit without 2FA). On a standing mandate the same condition is a `rail_auth` step-up instead (see [step-up reasons](#step-up-reasons)).                                                                                 | —                              | requires_buyer_review                                      |
| `insufficient_balance`             | rail refusal   | 403                | A wallet, UPI Lite, store-credit or loyalty balance is too low for the debit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                       |
| `ppi_not_reloadable`               | rail refusal   | 403                | A load into a gift PPI, which cannot be reloaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `pre_debit_notice_missing`         | rail refusal   | 403                | No matured 24-hour pre-debit notice covers this card e-mandate or NACH debit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `$.payment.scheduled_debit_at` | recoverable (send a notice and wait)                       |
| `consent_window_closed`            | rail refusal   | 409                | Cardholder consent for a refund was given after the refund left `pending_cardholder_consent` or after its 7-day window.                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `voucher_expired`                  | rail refusal   | 403                | An e-RUPI voucher is past its validity; unredeemed value returns to the sponsor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `voucher_purpose_mismatch`         | rail refusal   | 403                | An e-RUPI voucher redeemed at a merchant outside its purpose.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `bill_already_paid`                | rail refusal   | 409                | A BBPS bill that is already paid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `amount_mismatch`                  | rail refusal   | 422                | A BBPS payment that differs from the fetched bill amount when partial payment is not allowed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `$.amount`                     | recoverable                                                |
| `payee_name_mismatch`              | rail refusal   | 422                | The bank's beneficiary name look-up does not match the expected payee name for an account-to-account transfer.                                                                                                                                                                                                      | —                              | requires_buyer_review                                      |
| `maker_checker_required`           | rail refusal   | 403                | An account-to-account payment was approved by its maker, or without 2FA; a different human checker must approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | —                              | requires_buyer_review                                      |
| `invalid_state`                    | rail refusal   | 409                | An account-to-account payment is not in the state the operation needs (approve when not `pending_approval`, credit when not `sent`).                                                                                                                                                                                | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `illegal_cod_transition`           | rail refusal   | 409                | A cash-on-delivery order state change that the COD state machine does not allow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `loan_offer_not_lender_signed`     | rail refusal   | 422                | The loan offer presented for acceptance does not match the lender-signed KFS offer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `disbursal_not_to_end_beneficiary` | rail refusal   | 403                | A loan disbursal to an account other than the end beneficiary's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `cooling_off_over`                 | rail refusal   | 409                | A penalty-free exit from a loan after its cooling-off period ended.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `refund_not_allowed`               | rail refusal   | 400                | A refund that cites no successful debit with that RRN.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `poster_not_party`                 | ledger refusal | 403                | The poster of a ledger entry is not the ledger's creditor or debtor, or its signature does not verify under that party's registry key.                                                                                                                                                                              | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `ack_signature_required`           | ledger refusal | 400                | An acknowledgement without the counterparty's signature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                       |
| `ack_not_by_counterparty`          | ledger refusal | 403                | An acknowledgement by anyone other than the counterparty of the poster.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `ack_signature_invalid`            | ledger refusal | 400                | The acknowledgement signature does not verify under the counterparty's registry key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `grn_attestation_required`         | ledger refusal | 400                | An acceptance-dated credit sale without a buyer-signed GRN attestation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                       |
| `grn_attestation_invalid`          | ledger refusal | 400                | The GRN attestation is not signed by the ledger's debtor, or the GRN was already used.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `grn_date_invalid`                 | ledger refusal | 400                | The GRN date precedes the invoice or delivery date, is in the future, or differs from the sale's reference date.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | —                              | recoverable                                                |
| `receipt_required`                 | ledger refusal | 400                | A `payment` entry without a PSP-signed rail receipt.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | —                              | requires_buyer_input                                       |
| `receipt_reused`                   | ledger refusal | 409                | The rail receipt has already settled ledger entries, on this ledger or on any other ledger that the creditor's custodian holds (uniqueness is keyed on the rail and the RRN or UTR).                                                                                                                                | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `ledger_head_mismatch`             | ledger refusal | 409                | A posting or acknowledgement whose `prev_hash` or `head_hash` is not the ledger's current chain head (compare-and-swap). Nothing is appended.                                                                                                                                                                       | `$.prev_hash`                  | recoverable (GET the ledger, then act on the current head) |
| `settlement_payee_unmatched`       | ledger message | 201 msg            | A `payment` entry cites a receipt whose payee matches none of the creditor's `settlement_accounts[]` (or the `new_payee` after TReDS discounting), or whose `issued_at` is before the settled sale. The entry is accepted as `pending_ack` for the creditor and settles nothing until the creditor acknowledges it. | `$.settlement_evidence`        | requires_buyer_review                                      |
| `nothing_to_settle`                | ledger refusal | 409                | A `payment` entry when the ledger has no acknowledged open sale entries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | —                              | unrecoverable                                              |
| `credit_note_exceeds_open`         | ledger refusal | 400                | A credit note larger than the sale's open amount.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                              | recoverable                                                |

### Internal and nested reasons

These values are not registry codes. A participant MUST NOT put them in `Error.code` or `messages[].code`. Some reach the agent only inside a registered code, as shown.

| Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Where it arises                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | How it reaches the agent                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `local:per_txn`, `local:block_remaining`, `local:per_month`, `local:first_24h`, `local:binding_expired`                                                                                                                                           | The verifier's local rail-cap checks                                                                                                                                                                                                  | In `reasons[]` of `rail_limit_exceeded`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `rail:<reason>`: `block_expired`, `delegation_inactive`, `pin_auth_used`, `pin_auth_expired`, `unknown_rail_ref`, `unsupported_rail`, `payee_mismatch`, `amount_mismatch`, `pre_debit_notice_missing`, `pre_debit_opt_out`, `rail_limit_exceeded` | The payer PSP's pre-check of the bound rail                                                                                                                                                                                           | In `reasons[]` of `rail_limit_exceeded`. A pre-debit notice that has not matured is not a breach: the session gets the `pre_debit_notice` message instead, and `rail:pre_debit_opt_out` cancels the session with `pre_debit_opt_out`. The same reason is the `error` of a signed failure receipt, reported with `payment_failed`. |
| `unsupported_rail`, `block_exists`, `device_limit`                                                                                                                                                                                                | Rail set-up by the payer PSP on the Trusted Surface: attesting a rail type the PSP does not support, a second active Reserve Pay block for the same payee, too many Circle delegate devices                                           | Never to the agent; the mandate request is not activated                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `handler_mismatch`, `unsupported_handler`                                                                                                                                                                                                         | The gateway's payment-handler lookup                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The gateway first checks the handler against the mandate's rail binding (`mandate_scope_mismatch`, `$.payment.handler`); the handler intersection excludes an unknown handler with `not_in_registry`.
