| `refund_not_allowed`, `refund_exceeds_debit` on a post-order refund                                                                                                                                                                               | The rail refund call                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | As `status: FAILED:<code>` on the order's refund `adjustments[]` entry                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `auction_exists`, `not_sealed`, `no_award`                                                                                                                                                                                                        | The neutral auctioneer (create, commit, Dutch award without an accepted tick)                                                                                                                                                         | `invalid_request` (400); the auctioneer's text is in `message`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `auctioneer_not_neutral`, `not_eligible`                                                                                                                                                                                                          | The neutral auctioneer (seller-run auction, bidder outside the allowlist)                                                                                                                                                             | `mandate_scope_mismatch` (403)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `discovery_source_unverified`, `discovery_source_mismatch`                                                                                                                                                                                        | An agent's check of a discovery source ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results)): unverified when any step fails, mismatch when the signed body differs from the result | Never on the wire. The agent records it in the InstructionLog at stage `discover` and renders the item without the claim, as the table there says                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `discount_source_unknown`                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | An agent finds an `applied[]` entry with a `code` that it did not submit ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts))                                                                                 | Never on the wire. The agent records it in the InstructionLog and tells a present principal                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `NEG_ATTESTATION_INVALID`                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | A seller's Beckn error on `on_init` when the buyer's `within_bounds` attestation does not verify                                                                                                                                      | `bpp_no_on_init`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `NEG_BREACH`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `sub_category` of the IGM issue the gateway raises for a breach other than terms drift                                                                                                                                                | The IGM issue on the negotiation, not a code                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `capture_failed`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | A payment-plan tender capture that returned no success and no rail code                                                                                                                                                               | `error` of a failed payment-plan result, with `failed_tender`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `handler_non_paying`, `mandate_exceeds_rail_limit`                                                                                                                                                                                                | The handler binding check (class N handler; a mandate limit above the rail's limit)                                                                                                                                                   | Not surfaced; binding checks that reach the agent use `presence_handler_mismatch`, `cod_not_allowed`, `cod_open_orders_cap`, `credit_funding_not_allowed` or `reservepay_block_wrong_payee`                                                                                                                                       |

### Step-up reasons

`step_up.reason` (with `step_up.kind`) is one of:

| Reason                                    | Kind         | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `above_step_up_threshold`                 | confirm      | The amount is above the mandate's `step_up.above_amount`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `new_merchant`                            | confirm      | First order with this seller under the mandate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `outside_categories`                      | confirm      | The category is outside the mandate's step-up-free categories.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `first_order`                             | confirm      | First order under the mandate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `above_afa_limit`                         | rail_auth    | The debit is above the rail's AFA threshold (₹15,000; ₹1 lakh for listed categories).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `afa_threshold_card_emandate`             | rail_auth    | A card e-mandate debit above the AFA threshold.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `afa_crossborder_cnp`                     | rail_auth    | A non-recurring, cross-border, card-not-present payment whose acquirer requests AFA.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `split_tender_afa_on_total`               | rail_auth    | The total across tenders is above an AFA threshold.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `credit_acceptance`                       | confirm (HP) | Acceptance of a loan offer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `negotiation_out_of_mandate`              | confirm      | A negotiated term is outside the negotiation mandate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `negotiation_between_reservation_and_max` | confirm      | The price is between the reservation price and `total_max`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `accept_confirmation`                     | confirm      | The guard returned `acceptable`, the mandate's `accept_confirmation` is `ask` or absent, and the agent called accept. The `ts_render` carries `offer_hash`. Nothing seller-visible is sent before `negotiation.step_up.approved`.                                                                                                                                 |
| `rfq_prescribes_waiver`                   | confirm      | An agent-created RFQ sets `acceptance_revocation_required: waived`, which waives the principal's own ICA s.5 right.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `seller_confirmation`                     | confirm      | A BPP-signed `on_select` or `on_init` carries the `bacp` tag `seller_confirmation`: the seller asks for the buyer's own confirmation (a first cash-on-delivery order, an amount above the seller's threshold, a new credit line, a credit limit exceeded, or another reason). At most one per `checkout_hash`.                                                    |
| `refund_received`                         | confirm      | The gateway holds a refund receipt of the order's collector's PSP and not of the payer PSP, and asks the principal to confirm on the Trusted Surface that the credit arrived ("I have received ₹X"). Only that approval releases the spend of a `debited_not_confirmed` debit ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)). |
| `constraint_unresolved`                   | confirm      | Fallback when a constraint cannot be evaluated deterministically, and the reason for `discovery_price_changed` on an item shown with a `prior_price` and for `policy_text_mismatch`.                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Refund states

`Receipt.refund_state` is one of `pending_cardholder_consent`, `reversed_to_bank_account`, `released_block`, `credit_note_issued`, `refunded_to_source` (the default for a completed refund to source) and `adjusted_against_dues`. A card refund before the bill is paid MUST be `adjusted_against_dues` and MUST NOT pass through `pending_cardholder_consent`. See [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md).

# Evidence and Instruction Log

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

When an agent buys something on a principal's behalf, every party may later need to show what was authorised, what was instructed, what was offered and what was paid. BACP produces that evidence as a by-product of every transaction, using three artefacts:

| Artefact                   | Schema                                                                                     | Produced by                                          | Proves                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **InstructionLog** entries | [`instruction-log-entry.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/instruction-log-entry.json) | The agent operator's gateway                         | The ordered chain prompt → intent → cart → mandate → payment → order, tamper-evident |
| **Receipt**                | [`receipt.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/receipt.json)                             | The verifier that acted: PSP, BPP or Mandate Manager | That a payment, refund, checkout or mandate step happened, anchored to the rail      |
| **Evidence bundle**        | `EvidenceBundle` in the REST binding                                                       | The gateway, on request                              | Everything above for one transaction, verified and signed, for a dispute             |

## InstructionLog

The InstructionLog is a signed, append-only, hash-chained record kept **per checkout session**. It lets a reviewer reconstruct what the principal authorised and what they instructed, without the operator being able to rewrite history afterwards.

### Entry contents

| Field                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seq`                          | 0 for the first entry of the session, then +1 per entry, with no gaps.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `session_id`, `transaction_id` | The session and the Beckn transaction, end to end.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `stage`                        | What kind of step this is (see [Stages](#stages)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `actor`                        | Who performed the step: `user`, `agent`, `gateway`, `trusted_surface`, `bpp`, `psp`, or a session participant: `assisted_operator`, `seller_operator`, `sub_agent` ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#roles)).                    |
| `actor_ref`                    | The participant's `participant_id` (REQUIRED for `assisted_operator`, `seller_operator` and `sub_agent`), or on a handoff entry the key id of the support operator who accepted or released it.                                                                                    |
| `at`                           | When it happened.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `channel`, `language`          | For example `voice` and `hi-IN`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `content_hash`                 | `sha-256` of the raw content (a transcript, audio, a structured intent, a quote, a receipt).                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `content_ref`                  | Where the operator keeps the encrypted raw content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `summary`                      | A short multilingual summary.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `model`                        | The model `id`, `version` and, for voice or translated turns, `translation_model`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `refs`                         | Cross-references: `mandate_ref`, `checkout_hash`, `message_id`, `order_id`, `rrn`, `receipt_id`, `issue_id`; at stage `discover`, also `idempotency_key`, `source_digests[]`, `source_checks[]` and `registry_lookup`; at stage `cart`, `discount_codes[]` (`{code_mac, source}`). |
| `prev_hash`, `entry_hash`      | The chain links ([Hash chain](#hash-chain)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `signature`                    | The operator's signature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

**Only hashes and references leave the operator.** Raw content stays encrypted at the agent operator, and is released only inside an evidence bundle to a party entitled to it ([Access](#bundle-access)).

### Stages

| `stage`         | Recorded when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Typical `actor`                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `ai_disclosure` | The agent presents the AI disclosure and the routes to a human. It is the first entry whose actor is `agent`, before `intent` ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ai-disclosure))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `agent`                                    |
| `prompt`        | The principal instructs the agent (text or voice; voice records channel, language and translation model)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `user`                                     |
| `intent`        | The agent turns the instruction into a structured intent or mandate request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `agent`                                    |
| `discover`      | A search is sent and results arrive. The agent records the `Idempotency-Key` of the search, the `source_digest` of every discovery source it checked, the outcome of each (`verified`, `mismatch` or `unverified`, with the reason `discovery_source_mismatch` or `discovery_source_unverified`) and the host of the registry lookup it used ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results)). `content_hash` covers the discover response as returned | `agent`, `gateway`                         |
| `cart`          | Items are selected; the handler comparison is logged here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `agent`, `gateway`                         |
| `disclosure`    | The BPP's signed quote and disclosures arrive; records `checkout_hash` and the disclosures hash                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `bpp`                                      |
| `mandate`       | A mandate is activated, used or changes status, including each gateway pause reason (`binding_ineligible`, `reissue_required`) added or removed, with the `registry_version` ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)); records mandate hashes                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `gateway`, `trusted_surface`               |
| `step_up`       | A step-up is requested, approved, declined or expires                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `gateway`, `trusted_surface`               |
| `payment`       | A debit is initiated (basket-blind instruction), a receipt arrives, an in-doubt debit is reconciled, a refund is issued                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `gateway`, `psp`                           |
| `order`         | `on_confirm` creates the order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `bpp`                                      |
| `post_order`    | Cancels, returns, status changes and post-order refunds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `agent`, `assisted_operator`, `bpp`, `psp` |
| `grievance`     | An IGM issue is raised and every action on it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `agent`, `bpp`                             |
| `negotiation`   | Every negotiation message and counter-signature                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `agent`, `bpp`                             |
| `guard`         | Every negotiation guard verdict (constraint ids only)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `gateway`                                  |
| `ledger`        | Credit-ledger postings and acknowledgements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `gateway`, `seller_operator`               |
| `handoff`       | A handoff to a human is requested, accepted by a registered support operator, or released ([Human handoff](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#handoff))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `agent`, `gateway`                         |

The stage `disclosure` is the seller's quote; the AI disclosure is always `ai_disclosure`. The `negotiation`, `guard` and `ledger` stages are described in [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md) and [Credit and Split Tender](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/index.md).

### Signer roles

- Every entry is signed by the **agent operator** (the gateway's BAP registry key) with `signature.role: operator`, whatever its `actor`. The `actor` field records who acted; the signature records who attests to the record.
- The signature is asymmetric (ES256 or EdDSA), as a detached JWS over the JCS form of the entry minus `signature`. A shared-secret MAC **MUST NOT** be used, because it cannot give non-repudiation.
- The acts of other parties are proved by their own signatures on the artefacts the entry hashes and references: the BPP's signature on the quote, the PSP's on the Receipt, the principal's and MM's on the mandate, the Trusted Surface's on a step-up event. A human act is never proved by the operator's signature alone: the bundle carries the signed Trusted Surface events themselves ([Bundle contents](#bundle)).

### Hash chain

```
entry_hash = sha-256( JCS( entry minus {entry_hash, signature} ) )
prev_hash  = entry_hash of entry seq - 1
prev_hash of seq 0 (genesis) = sha-256( session_id as UTF-8 bytes )
```

Hashes are written `sha-256:<base64url>`. The **log head** is the `entry_hash` of the last entry, or the genesis hash when the log is empty.

**Anchoring.** The gateway **MUST** put the current `log_head` in `context.bacp.log_head` on every committing Beckn message it sends (`init`, `confirm`, `update`, `cancel`, `issue`). Those messages are signed on the network, so the BPP and the network hold independent copies of the head at each commitment. An operator that deletes or rewrites an entry produces a chain that no longer matches the heads recorded in the network trace.

```
{
  "seq": 0,
  "session_id": "ses_01HZXB",
  "transaction_id": "6f1c2a8e-0c7b-4f7e-9d0e-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "stage": "prompt",
  "actor": "user",
  "at": "2026-10-20T19:00:02+05:30",
  "channel": "voice",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "content_hash": "sha-256:YaIsf4NASd5cjPZvWWkQKmbj9SW9F-zJzj-1G6_KAi4",
  "content_ref": "https://logs.vaani.example.in/blobs/ses_01HZXB/0",
  "summary": {
    "hi-IN": "दो किलो आटा, एक लीटर दूध और पाँच सौ ग्राम दाल मँगवा दो",
    "en-IN": "Order 2 kg atta, 1 L milk and 500 g dal"
  },
  "model": {"id": "example-llm-2", "version": "2026.10.1", "translation_model": "bhashini-asr-hi-v3"},
  "refs": {},
  "prev_hash": "sha-256:QP09K6-qS2n7bF4INQ0RefqmkL9onuRPPhV0nYVtfWo",
  "entry_hash": "sha-256:nbwyd-n-VkI8y5myMA_yKrU7bG6Dh9OkbXcZO3R-lXI",
  "signature": {
    "role": "operator",
    "kid": "bap.vaani.example.in|ukid-7|ed25519",
    "alg": "EdDSA",
    "value": "eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSJ9.eyJsIjowfQ.c2ln"
  }
}
```

### Chain verification

A verifier **MUST** check a log as follows, and **MUST** reject it at the first failure:

1. The log is not empty.
1. Every entry validates against `instruction-log-entry.json`.
1. For entry *i* (counting from 0): `seq` = *i*, and `session_id` equals the first entry's.
1. `prev_hash` equals the genesis hash for *i* = 0, and the previous entry's `entry_hash` otherwise.
1. Recomputing `entry_hash` gives the stored value.
1. `signature` verifies against the registry key named by its `kid`.
1. If an expected head is known (for example from `context.bacp.log_head` in a network message, or from the gateway's current state), the last `entry_hash` equals it.

The gateway **MUST** run this check on the session's log before `complete`. A broken chain returns `403 log_chain_invalid` (`unrecoverable`) and no money moves ([Deterministic evaluation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#evaluation)).

## Receipts

A **Receipt** is the signed statement of the party that acted: the payer PSP for a payment or refund, the BPP for a checkout, the Mandate Manager for a mandate. It follows AP2's mandate, checkout and payment receipts and adds the Indian rail references.

| Field                              | Rule                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `receipt_type`                     | `mandate`, `checkout`, `payment` or `refund`.                                                                                                       |
| `iss`                              | The verifier that acted. A payment or refund receipt **MUST** be signed with a registry key of role PSP; a checkout receipt with a key of role BPP. |
| `result`                           | `success`, `failure` or `in_doubt`.                                                                                                                 |
| `reference`                        | The hash of the **closed mandate that was presented**: `sha-256` over the JCS form of the mandate minus `status`, `usage` and `signatures`.         |
| `mandate_ref`, `open_mandate_ref`  | The closed mandate id and its open parent.                                                                                                          |
| `transaction_id`, `order_id`       | The Beckn transaction, end to end, and the order.                                                                                                   |
| `checkout_hash`, `amount`, `payee` | Required on a successful payment or refund receipt. `amount` **MUST** be greater than zero.                                                         |
| `rail`                             | The rail evidence (below).                                                                                                                          |
| `refund_state`                     | Refund receipts only (below).                                                                                                                       |
| `fx`                               | Optional foreign-currency view; settlement stays in INR.                                                                                            |
| `signature`                        | The issuer's signature.                                                                                                                             |

### Rail evidence

- `rail.type` is a handler reference; producers **SHOULD** emit the canonical id. `rail.type`, `rail.rail_ref` and `rail.status` are always present.
- **UPI family** (`upi.*`, `in.upi.*`, `in.cod.upi`, `in.pos.tap`, `in.pos.dynamic_qr`): a successful payment or refund receipt **MUST** carry the 12-digit `rrn`, and **MUST** carry `utr` whenever the handler descriptor's `settlement.evidence_refs` lists it.
- **Other handlers**: the receipt **MUST** carry at least one of `rrn`, `utr` or `rail.evidence`. `rail.evidence` is a string map whose keys come from the descriptor's `settlement.evidence_refs` (for example `arn` and `auth_code` for cards, `umrn` for NACH, `voucher_id` for e-RUPI, `ledger_entry_id` for store credit and `bacp.credit_ledger`, `awb` for a COD record).
- `rail.evidence` **MUST NOT** contain anything the descriptor lists under `data_minimisation.never_collect` (PIN, OTP, card number, CVV, expiry, Aadhaar number).
- Cash on delivery moves no money through a rail and has no payment Receipt; the order records the collection against the shipment `awb`.

Rail references let receipts be joined with the rail's own dispute channel (UDIR for UPI). See [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).

### Refund receipts

A refund receipt **MUST** be signed by a registered PSP, and the gateway applies it only to a payment of the same `checkout_hash` and payee. A payment success or failure receipt is applied only when it is signed by the PSP of the closed Payment Mandate's `auth_binding.psp_id` (HNP: the open Payment Mandate's `rail_binding.psp_id`), and each `receipt_id` and rail reference is applied once; otherwise the gateway answers `400 receipt_invalid` and the reservation stays ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)). A refund receipt **MUST** identify the original payment (`original_rrn`, `original_utr`, or an `original_*` key in `rail.evidence`), proving the refund went back to the original method, and **MUST** carry `refund_state`: `refunded_to_source` (the default for a completed refund to source), `released_block`, `pending_cardholder_consent`, `reversed_to_bank_account`, `credit_note_issued` or `adjusted_against_dues`. A card refund before the bill is paid **MUST** be `adjusted_against_dues` and **MUST NOT** pass through `pending_cardholder_consent`.

### `budget_after` is never signed

The PSP holds no mandate budgets. A Receipt **MUST NOT** contain `budget_after`, and the schema rejects one that does. The gateway computes the remaining budget from its own ledger after applying the receipt and returns it unsigned in `session.payment.budget_after` ([Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)). A verifier **MUST** ignore any budget figure that claims to come from a receipt.

### How receipts are used

- The gateway applies a payment receipt to the mandate ledger only after verifying its signature against a registry key of role PSP and checking that it belongs to the mandate. A forged or mismatched receipt is refused with `400 receipt_invalid`.
- A webhook **MUST NOT** embed a signed Receipt. It carries a `ReceiptRef`: `receipt_id`, `receipt_hash` (`sha-256` over the JCS form of the full signed receipt), `receipt_type`, `result`, and where present `amount`, `refund_state` and `rail {type, rrn, status, original_rrn}`.
- The full signed receipt is available to the party of record by authenticated GET on its owning resource (`/sessions/{id}`, `/orders/{id}`, `/orders/{id}/returns/{rid}`). An agent that relies on it **MUST** check that its hash equals the `receipt_hash` it was sent.

```
{
  "receipt_id": "rcpt_PAY0000000001",
  "receipt_type": "payment",
  "iss": "psp.example.in",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-20T19:02:11+05:30",
  "result": "success",
  "reference": "sha-256:56zHckmGabR5RoD_aAjAlsFMjuSAjmXgymcJL4c7arY",
  "mandate_ref": "mdt_PAYC0000000001",
  "open_mandate_ref": "mdt_PAY7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "transaction_id": "6f1c2a8e-0c7b-4f7e-9d0e-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "order_id": "ORD-KIR-88231",
  "checkout_hash": "sha-256:vRBpqmLq4AipYw1ZNnIL3trdLVrcHQAQ0g5RurJB4CQ",
  "amount": {"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"},
  "payee": {"vpa": "ganeshkirana@examplebank", "name": "Shree Ganesh Kirana"},
  "rail": {
    "type": "in.upi.reservepay",
    "rail_ref": "SBMD-HDFX-000123456",
    "rrn": "629318004417",
    "utr": "629318004417",
    "npci_txn_id": "NPCIEX0000000001",
    "psp_confirmation_id": "PSPCONF-77812",
```

## Evidence bundle

`GET /evidence/{transaction_id}` returns the **evidence bundle** for a transaction: everything a grievance officer, an ODR body, a regulator or the principal needs to verify the purchase, without trusting the agent or its operator.

### Contents

| Field                      | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `transaction_id`           | The Beckn transaction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `agent_credential_hash`    | Hash of the AgentCredential the agent used.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `mandates[]`               | The open Checkout and Payment Mandates, each wrapped in a JWS by the operator (the payload keeps the principal and MM signatures), and the closed mandates exactly as presented (agent-signed or principal-signed attached JWS).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `checkout`                 | The BPP-signed quote (`bpp_signed_quote`), `checkout_hash`, `disclosures_hash` and the `disclosures` they hash (including `catalogue[]`), and `bpp_signed_payment_terms`: the seller's payment terms from `on_init` (Beckn `payments[]`, with `collected_by` and the payee VPA in `params.virtual_payment_address`) as the gateway received them, kept as `{body, authorization}`: the raw `on_init` body and its Beckn `Authorization` header, which verifies against the BPP's registry key ([Beckn signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#signing)). REQUIRED for every Reserve Pay leg ([Sibling Payment Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#sibling-payment-mandates)).                                                            |
| `receipts[]`               | The full signed receipts: the BPP's checkout receipt, the PSP's payment receipt, and any refund receipts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `consent_receipts[]`       | The ConsentReceipts under which data was shared.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `instruction_log[]`        | The session's full InstructionLog.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `discovery_response`       | The signed `POST /discover` response as `{status, body, content_digest, signature_input, signature}`, where `body` is the response content exactly as sent, with no content coding, and its sha-256 is the `content_hash` of the session's agent-written `discover` InstructionLog entry. REQUIRED when `Disclosures.catalogue[]` is present and that entry exists. The verifier rebuilds the signature base from `status` (`@status`) and the stored `content_digest`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `discovery_sources[]`      | For a session whose items came from `POST /discover`: the BPP-signed `on_search` callback behind every `source_digest` in `checkout.disclosures.catalogue[]`, each as `{body, authorization}` exactly as the gateway received it ([Retention of the signed callbacks](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-retention)). A verifier checks that the sha-256 of each `body` equals the `source_digest` and that the `authorization` verifies against the BPP's registry key, and compares the item values in the body with `checkout.disclosures.catalogue[]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `trusted_surface_events[]` | Every signed Trusted Surface event of the transaction, verbatim as received at `/trusted-surface/events` (step-up results, mandate activation, credit acceptance, AFA completion), each with its [`Presentation`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#presentation).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ts_renders[]`             | The gateway-signed [`ts_render`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-render) (compact JWS) of every step-up that a `step_up.approved`, `step_up.declined`, `negotiation.step_up.approved` or `negotiation.step_up.declined` event in `trusted_surface_events[]` names, byte-identical to what the Trusted Surface fetched. The `content_ref` of such an event's `presentation` is the fragment `#/ts_renders/<index>`, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the render's position in this array; an index outside the array, or a `content_hash` that differs from the sha-256 of the render found there, is `evidence_unverifiable`. In a bundle released to a seller or a payer PSP, a summary step-up's render is left out and `ts_render_digests[]` carries it instead. |
| `notice_renders[]`         | For every autonomous negotiation act of the transaction: the gateway-signed notice (`agreed_by_agent` or `purchase_offered_by_agent`) and the receipt of its delivery to the principal by the mandate's `notice_route`, as `{code, render, content_hash, delivery}`. A notice is not a step-up and has no event. A reviewer answers "I never agreed" from its `content_hash`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ts_render_digests[]`      | Only in a bundle released to a seller or a payer PSP: for each summary step-up over a [multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket), `{step_up_id, render_hash, cover}`, where `render_hash` is the sha-256 of its `ts_render` and `cover` is the `covers[]` entry of this transaction's leg. The other sellers' lines stay out of the bundle.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `verification`             | The gateway's own result: `steps_passed` (0 to 6), `chain_valid`, and for step 6 `catalogue_result` and `catalogue_unchecked[]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `bundle_signature`         | The operator's signature over the whole bundle minus `bundle_signature`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

A human-readable rendering of a bundle, the informative summary profile `in.bacp.evidence.summary.1`, is described in [Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#evidence-summary). It is built only from the signed artefacts in the bundle and is never itself evidence.

For a negotiated purchase the bundle also carries the negotiation transcript, the accepted offer, the `within_bounds` attestation and the bound `on_init`, so that a reviewer can check what was offered and agreed without seeing the principal's reservation price ([Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md)).

### AP2 five-step verification

A bundle verifies only if all six steps pass (the five AP2 steps and step 6), the InstructionLog chain is valid, and the bundle signature verifies:

1. **Closed Checkout Mandate.** It is signed by the open Checkout Mandate's `cnf` key (HNP) or by the principal who signed the parent (HP); its `parent_mandate_id` is the open mandate; and the open mandate's principal and MM signatures verify.
1. **Checkout hash.** The BPP signature on the quote verifies against a registry key of role BPP; `sha-256(JCS(quote))` equals `checkout_hash`; and the closed Checkout Mandate carries that `checkout_hash` and the quote total.
1. **Checkout receipt.** The BPP-signed checkout receipt is a success and its `reference` equals the hash of the closed Checkout Mandate.
1. **Closed Payment Mandate.** It is signed by the open Payment Mandate's `cnf` key (or the principal); its parent is the open Payment Mandate, whose signatures verify; its `checkout_hash` and `amount` match; and its `checkout_mandate_ref` is the closed Checkout Mandate.
1. **Payment receipt.** The PSP-signed payment receipt is a success; its `reference` equals the hash of the closed Payment Mandate; its `checkout_hash` and `amount` match; and it carries the rail evidence required for its handler ([Rail evidence](#rail-evidence)).
1. **Trusted Surface events.** Every `trusted_surface_events[]` entry verifies against a registry key of role Mandate Manager or PSP. The signer of every `step_up.*` and `negotiation.step_up.*` event MUST also be one of the keys that [Step-up signers](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-signers) derives from the mandates in the bundle: the issuer of the mandate that the render's `mandate_id` names, or the PSP that the table names for that step-up from the bundle's Payment Mandates. A registry Mandate Manager or PSP key that is not one of them is `evidence_unverifiable`. Every InstructionLog entry at stage `step_up` that records an approval or a decline has a matching event, whose hash the entry's `content_hash` carries. Every `step_up.approved`, `mandate.activated`, `loan.accepted` and `payment.afa_completed` event carries a `Presentation`, and for a step-up its `content_hash` is the hash of the step-up's `ts_render` and its `checkout_hash` is the bundle's `checkout_hash`. A contested crossing records `late_receipt_party` in its transcript entry; two receipts at one `log_seq` that name different entries, or a decrease of `received_at` along a chain without `clock_step_observed`, is `evidence_unverifiable`. A `negotiation.step_up.approved` event carries a `Presentation` with `offer_hash` instead of `checkout_hash`: the verifier **MUST** check that it equals the `offer_hash` of the step-up's `ts_render` and of the signed offer in the bundle's negotiation transcript, and that the `ts_render`'s `acceptance_revocation`, where present, equals that offer's value; the quote comparisons below do not apply to such an event. `negotiation.step_up.approved` and `negotiation.step_up.declined` are step-up events for the next rule: their `ts_render` MUST be in `ts_renders[]`, with its hash and signature checked, and a missing one is `evidence_unverifiable`; the quote comparisons below never apply to them. A `negotiation.agreed.declined` or `negotiation.purchase_offer.withdrawn` event carries a `Presentation` with `offer_hash`, which the verifier checks against the offer in the negotiation transcript. For every other step-up event, `ts_renders[]` **MUST** hold a `ts_render` whose sha-256 is that `content_hash` (where the event carries one) and whose signature verifies against the gateway's registry key, and the verifier **MUST** compare its `total`, its payee (`seller_name`) and its `checkout_hash` with the BPP-signed quote in `checkout`, and its `price_breakup_hash` with `checkout.disclosures_hash`; a missing render or any mismatch fails the step. Where the step-up's `ts_render` carries `covers[]` (a summary step-up over a basket), the verifier instead finds the `covers[]` entry whose `session_id` is the bundle's session and compares its `checkout_hash` and `amount` with the BPP-signed quote and its `payee.vpa` with the payee VPA of the PSP payment receipt; the summary's `total`, `seller_name` and `checkout_hash`, and the `Presentation.checkout_hash` equality above, are not checked against this leg's quote. In a bundle that carries the summary only as a `ts_render_digests[]` entry, the event's `content_hash` **MUST** equal its `render_hash` and the same comparison is made with its `cover`; that the `cover` is an entry of the render is checked by a reviewer that holds the full render (the principal, the grievance officer or the ODR body). The InstructionLog's first entry whose actor is `agent` is at stage `ai_disclosure`. Where the bundle carries `checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms`, its `authorization` **MUST** verify over its `body` against the registry key of the BPP that the body's `context.bpp_id` names, as of the signature's `created` time, and the payee VPA of the PSP payment receipt **MUST** equal the payee VPA in those terms; for a Reserve Pay payment the terms **MUST** be present and the open Payment Mandate's `payee.vpa` and `payee.bpp_id` **MUST** equal the VPA and the `bpp_id` in them ([Sibling Payment Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#sibling-payment-mandates)). For a session step-up of kind `confirm` or `rail_auth` the verifier also checks the catalogue disclosure: every `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry of `checkout.disclosures` that is `sponsored` or `undeclared`, or has a `prior_price`, MUST have an entry in the `ts_render`'s `catalogue_disclosure[]`, so that an omission fails; where the session's agent-written `discover` InstructionLog entry exists for the bundle's `transaction_id`, `checkout.disclosures.catalogue[]` MUST hold exactly one entry for each line item of the BPP-signed quote whose item appears in a source named in that entry's `refs.source_digests`; each entry's `sponsorship`, `prior_price` and `unit_price` MUST equal (JCS) those of the `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry that its `index` names (`unit_price` against `discovered_unit_price`; on a summary step-up, of the leg that `covers[cover_index]` names, which only a verifier that holds that leg's bundle can check); and `counterparty_text[name_ref].text` MUST equal a language value of the item's name in the BPP-signed quote for that item. For each `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry whose `source_digest` appears in `refs.source_digests` of the session's `discover` InstructionLog entry written by the agent, the signed source in `discovery_sources[]` whose sha-256 is that digest MUST verify against the BPP's registry key as of the signature's `created` time; its `context.message_id` MUST equal the derivation from the `idempotency_key` in that log entry; and its item values MUST match those of the `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry, derived by the [normative mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#disclosure-mapping). An entry whose digest is not there was not checked by the agent; the verifier records it as unchecked, and it does not fail the step. Where the session's agent-written `discover` InstructionLog entry exists, `discovery_response` MUST be present, its signature MUST verify against the gateway's profile key, and the sha-256 of its `body` MUST equal that entry's `content_hash`; each entry's `sponsorship.status` MUST then be no weaker than, and its `sponsorship.by[]` a superset of, those of the same item in `discovery_response`. Where there is no such entry, the sponsorship comparison is recorded as unchecked and does not fail the step. This makes the verifier, not the gateway, the judge of whether the sponsorship and prior price shown at checkout are those the seller sent. Any other failure of step 6 is `evidence_unverifiable`; a catalogue check that fails or is unchecked is recorded in `verification.catalogue_result` and `catalogue_unchecked[]` and does not stop the issue (see [Attaching evidence to an IGM issue](#igm-attachment)). Step 6 proves what the principal was shown and, through [`EvidenceBundle.checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms`](#contents), whom the seller asked to be paid; neither the quote nor `ts_render` carries the payee's VPA or settlement account.

The gateway runs this verification when it builds the bundle and records the result in `verification`. A reviewer **SHOULD** re-run it independently rather than trust `verification`.

### Attaching evidence to an IGM issue

- Before raising an issue the gateway **MUST** assemble the bundle and verify it fully. If it does not pass all six verification steps with a valid chain, `POST /issues` returns `422 evidence_unverifiable` and nothing is sent ([Orders and Post-order](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#igm)). The one exception is the catalogue checks of step 6: a catalogue entry that fails or is unchecked does not stop the issue; the gateway records it in `verification` (`catalogue_result`, `catalogue_unchecked[]`) and sends the issue. A gateway **MUST NOT** refuse to raise an issue because of a catalogue check.
- The Beckn `issue` carries the bundle by reference: `evidence_bundle_ref` (the `/evidence/{transaction_id}` URI) and `evidence_bundle_hash` (`sha-256` over the JCS form of the bundle). The bundle itself is also returned on the `Issue` to the agent.
- When the issue is escalated to `GRIEVANCE`, the same bundle, identified by the same hash, goes to the GRO. ODR bodies receive it the same way, out of protocol.
- For a payment issue, the RRN or UTR in the bundle and on the issue is the join key with the rail's dispute channel.

### Access

The bundle contains personal data and the principal's instructions. The gateway **MUST** release it only to:

- the principal, or the agent acting under the principal's mandate for that transaction;
- the counterparties of record (the seller and the payer PSP of that transaction);
- the grievance redressal officer or ODR body handling an issue on it;
- a regulator, on lawful request.

Anyone else gets `403 evidence_forbidden`. Selective disclosure keeps the basket away from the PSP and the instrument away from the seller where the format allows it. A summary step-up's full `ts_render`, which lists every seller of a basket, goes only to the principal (or the agent acting for the principal), the grievance officer, the ODR body and a regulator; a seller or a payer PSP gets its `ts_render_digests[]` entry instead.

## Retention

| Record                                                             | Kept by                          | Retention                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mandates, notices, consent and sharing records                     | Mandate Manager                  | At least 7 years, exportable in machine-readable form                                                                                                               |
| Personal data received by a seller                                 | Each recipient Data Fiduciary    | `dpdp.data_retention` of the mandate and `retention.recipient_max` of the ConsentReceipt, never below the one-year minimum of DPDP Rule 8(3), and erased afterwards |
| Idempotency keys and stored responses                              | Gateway                          | At least 24 hours (48 hours recommended)                                                                                                                            |
| Replay-cache nonces                                                | Gateway                          | Until the signature's `expires` (at most 300 seconds)                                                                                                               |
| InstructionLog, receipts and evidence bundles                      | Agent operator (gateway) and PSP | Long enough to serve grievances, disputes and regulatory review; see below                                                                                          |
| BPP-signed `on_search` callbacks behind a returned `source_digest` | Gateway                          | As long as the evidence bundle of any session that used an item from them, and in any case as long as the InstructionLog                                            |
| Negotiation transcripts                                            | Agent operator                   | Proposed: 2 years for B2C, longer for B2B and public procurement ([Q-56](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-56))                           |

Where these records contain payment data, RBI's directive on Storage of Payment System Data (RBI/2017-18/153, 06-04-2018) already requires RBI-authorised payment system providers to store that data only in India (the foreign leg of a cross-border transaction may also be stored abroad).

Until [Q-15](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-15) is settled, a gateway, Mandate Manager or PSP adapter MUST store InstructionLogs, receipts and evidence bundles that contain payment data only in India, and MUST NOT send that payment data to any processor outside India (see [Data localisation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#data-localisation)).

Proposed

A single retention table for InstructionLogs, receipts and evidence bundles, with downstream erasure on a deadline, is open ([Q-17](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-17)).

See [Security and Privacy](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/index.md) for encryption and access control of operator records.

# Getting Started

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page walks through one complete BACP transaction, from mandate setup to a refund. It is a guided tour of the normative pages, not a replacement for them: each step links to the page that defines the rules.

## The scenario

- **Who.** Meera lives in Bengaluru (PIN code 560034). She uses *Sakhi*, a Hindi voice agent run by Vaani Voice Commerce Pvt Ltd. Sakhi's BACP gateway runs at Vaani's Buyer App, `bap.vaani.example.in`.
- **What.** Sakhi orders chakki atta 2 kg (₹110), milk 1 L (₹68) and toor dal 500 g (₹89) from Meera's regular ONDC kirana, `bpp.kirana.example.in`.
- **How Meera pays.** Through an open mandate bound to a **UPI Reserve Pay** block of ₹3,000 for 30 days, payable to the kirana. The mandate caps each order at ₹1,500 and asks Meera to confirm anything above ₹1,200. A [UPI Circle](#alternative-upi-circle) binding works the same way and is described at the end.
- **Then.** One milk packet arrives damaged, and Sakhi returns it. The ₹68 goes back to Meera's UPI account.

All amounts on the wire are integer paise: ₹302 is `{"value": 30200, "currency": "INR"}`.

Example values

Identifiers such as `mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3`, `ses_…` and `ORD-KIR-88231`, and the RRN shown below, are illustrative. They match the examples in the OpenAPI document.

## What every call carries

Every agent call in this walkthrough is an HTTPS request to the gateway with:

- an RFC 9421 `Signature-Input` and `Signature` made with Sakhi's `cnf` key, with a `tag` parameter that limits what the request may do;
- a `Content-Digest` header (RFC 9530) over the raw body;
- the AgentCredential in the `BACP-Agent` header;
- on every `POST` and `PUT`, an `Idempotency-Key` of 22–64 characters.

The rules are in [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/index.md). The gateway verifies the signature on the raw bytes before it parses the body, and rejects a tag that the endpoint does not accept or that Sakhi's credential does not list in `purposes`.

## Overview

```
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Meera
    participant A as Sakhi (agent)
    participant G as BACP gateway (BAP)
    participant TS as UPI app (Trusted Surface) and Mandate Manager
    participant P as Payer PSP and NPCI
    participant S as Kirana (BPP)
    A->>G: GET /.well-known/bacp
    A->>G: POST /mandates (bacp-browse)
    G-->>A: 202 PENDING with Trusted Surface link
    U->>TS: Approve with UPI PIN
    TS->>P: Create Reserve Pay block payable to the kirana
    TS->>G: Signed mandate.activated (bacp-ts)
    G-->>A: Webhook mandate.status_changed ACTIVE
    A->>G: POST /discover (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn search and on_search
    A->>G: POST /sessions (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn select and on_select
    A->>G: PUT /sessions/id (bacp-browse)
    G->>S: Beckn init and on_init
    A->>G: POST /sessions/id/complete (bacp-pay)
    G->>P: Basket-blind debit of ₹302
    P-->>G: Signed receipt with RRN
    G->>S: Beckn confirm and on_confirm
    G-->>A: completed with order
    A->>G: POST /orders/id/returns (bacp-post-order)
    G->>S: Beckn update and on_update
    G->>P: Refund ₹68 to source
    G-->>A: Webhook return.updated
```

## Step 0: Read the gateway profile

`GET /.well-known/bacp` — unsigned, no tag.

Sakhi fetches the gateway's [profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#profile-document) and checks that the gateway supports a protocol version Sakhi speaks, the REST transport, the capabilities `in.bacp.mandate`, `in.bacp.discover`, `in.bacp.checkout` and `in.bacp.order`, and the handler `in.upi.reservepay`. It also reads `message_id_namespace`, which it needs in step 7.

**On Beckn:** nothing.

## Step 1: Disclose and capture the instruction

Sakhi's first message in every session discloses that Meera is talking to an AI and offers a human: *"Aap ek AI sahayak se baat kar rahe hain…"* ("You are talking to an AI assistant…"). The text and the routes to a human come from Sakhi's AgentCredential (`disclosure.ai_notice`, `disclosure.handoff_routes`). Because Sakhi is a voice agent, one route is a phone number with "press 0", not only a web link. The operator logs the disclosure at stage `ai_disclosure`, the first entry whose actor is the agent. See [Human Participants and the Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/index.md).

Meera says: *"Har mahine ka kirana tum mangwa dena, teen hazaar tak."* ("Order the groceries every month, up to three thousand.") Sakhi's operator records the turn as the first [instruction log](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/index.md) entry (stage `prompt`, channel `voice`, spoken language `hi-IN`, with the Roman-script transcript tagged `hi-Latn-IN`), with hashes of the audio and transcript and the translation model used. Sakhi turns it into structured constraints and logs that as stage `intent`.

**On Beckn:** nothing.

## Step 2: Request the mandate

`POST /mandates` — tag `bacp-browse`.

```
{
  "purpose_code": "P-GRO-01",
  "rail": "in.upi.reservepay",
  "presence_allowed": ["HNP", "HP"],
  "proposed_constraints": {
    "amount_per_txn": {"value": 150000, "currency": "INR"},
    "budgets": [{"period": "P1M", "max": {"value": 300000, "currency": "INR"}}],
    "categories_allow": ["ONDC:RET10"],
    "delivery_pincodes": ["560034"],
    "step_up": {
      "above_amount": {"value": 120000, "currency": "INR"},
      "outside_categories": true
    },
    "reject_preticked_addons": true
  },
  "data_scopes": ["NAME", "PHONE", "DELIVERY_ADDRESS"],
  "action_scope": ["DISCOVER", "QUOTE", "ORDER", "PAY", "CANCEL", "RETURN", "RAISE_ISSUE", "SHARE_DATA"],
  "validity": "P30D",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "webhook_url": "https://agents.vaani.example.in/bacp/hooks"
}
```

`rail` carries the canonical handler id `in.upi.reservepay`. The legacy alias `upi.reservepay.block` still resolves to it during its deprecation window, but new artefacts emit the canonical id ([Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/#alias-resolution)). `action_scope` lists the actions used later in this walkthrough, including `RETURN` and `RAISE_ISSUE`. `webhook_url` is where the gateway sends `mandate.status_changed`, which arrives before any session exists.

**What the gateway does.** It verifies the signature and credential, then checks the request against the bounds of purpose `P-GRO-01` (grocery replenishment): the per-transaction cap, a periodic budget, categories inside `ONDC:RET10`, and a validity of no more than 90 days. A request outside the purpose bounds is refused with 403 `mandate_scope_mismatch` before anything reaches Meera's phone. It then forwards the request, with Sakhi's `cnf` key, to the Mandate Manager.

**Response.** `202` with `status: PENDING` and a `trusted_surface_url` that expires after at most 15 minutes. Sakhi never signs or activates the mandate.

**On Beckn:** nothing. Mandates are off-network. See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md).

## Step 3: Meera approves on her UPI app

Sakhi says *"Kripya apne UPI app mein manzoori dein"* ("Please give your approval in your UPI app") and Meera opens the link in her UPI app, which is the [Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/glossary/#trusted-surface).
