| `subject_ref`                    | REQUIRED for a trade act: `{kind, id, through_seq?, payee?}`. `kind` is `order` or `document` for a `GRN`, `CRAC` or `MSMED_OBJECTION` (with `order_id`), and `ledger_entry` (`id` is the entry id; `payee` REQUIRED for a `payment` entry in `pending_ack` with `settlement_payee_unmatched`) or `ledger_statement` (`id` is the ledger id, `through_seq` REQUIRED) for a `LEDGER_ACK`, which has no `order_id`. For a GRN the Trusted Surface shows the delivery date and the accepted and rejected quantities with their enum reasons; for an MSMED objection, the objection text labelled as counterparty text; for a ledger entry, its amount, type and due date and, for a `payment` entry in `pending_ack` with `settlement_payee_unmatched`, the payee of the cited receipt, labelled as not one of the creditor's settlement accounts; for a statement, the count, the closing balance, the oldest unpaid date and every entry above `itemise_above`, counting only the entries the other party posted.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `language`                       | The principal's language, as a BCP 47 tag (`LanguageTag`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `checkout_hash`                  | The `checkout_hash` of the quote the step-up is about. For `post_order` it is the `checkout_hash` of the order's closed Checkout Mandate (the hash of the BPP-signed quote the order was placed under, also on the order's `Receipt`); an `Order` carries no `checkout_hash` of its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `total`                          | The total the principal pays, as a single figure (`Amount`, integer paise): the quote total plus the sum of the session's `operator_charges[]`. On a summary step-up, the sum of `basket[].amount`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `charge_lines[]`                 | Optional. On a step-up that pays for an order, one entry `{code, amount, recipient?}` for each fee line, then one `remainder` entry for everything else. The amounts add up to `total`. Absent when the order has no fee line. The Trusted Surface reads them by [TS-3](#ts-requirements) from its own templates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `price_breakup_hash`             | The hash of the BPP-signed price breakup and disclosures (`disclosures.hash`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `seller_name`                    | The payee seller, from the BPP-signed quote. Absent on a summary step-up, whose sellers are in `basket[]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `assisted_operators[]`           | On an assisted session only: the `participant_id` and `ref` of each `assisted_operator` in the session's `participants[]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `summary`                        | Gateway-written text (`LangText`) from the gateway's own templates, with no counterparty text in it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `counterparty_text[]`            | Optional. Each entry is `{label, text}`: a seller-supplied string (an item name, a fee label), labelled by the gateway.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `basket[]`                       | On a summary step-up over a [multi-seller basket](#multi-seller) only: one line per seller, `{bpp_id, payee_name, amount, handler, needs_pin, funds_locked, expires_at, funding}`. `payee_name` is the name the payer's bank returns for the payee VPA. `funds_locked` and `expires_at` are the amount a block reserves and when it is released. `funding` is `deposit` (the principal's own money) or `credit`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `covers[]`                       | On a summary step-up only: the legs the approval covers, each `{session_id, checkout_hash, payee, amount}` ([Step-up](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#step-up)). A summary's `session_id` and `checkout_hash` are those of the session whose `complete` raised it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `catalogue_disclosure[]`         | Optional. On a session step-up (`confirm` or `rail_auth`, including a summary step-up) only: one entry for each line item whose `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry is `sponsored` or `undeclared`, or carries a `prior_price`. Each entry is `{index, sponsorship, name_ref}` and, for a prior price, `prior_price` and `unit_price` (the discovered unit price shown with it). `index` is the position of the entry in that session's `Disclosures.catalogue[]`; on a summary step-up each entry also carries `cover_index`, the position in `covers[]` of the leg whose session it is. A `cover_index` that is not a position in `covers[]`, or an `index` that is not a position in that leg's `Disclosures.catalogue[]`, makes the render invalid (`evidence_unverifiable`). `name_ref` is the position of the item's name in `counterparty_text[]`. An entry for an item that is `not_sponsored` and has no `prior_price` is invalid. Never present on a `post_order` step-up or a negotiation `confirm`. It is hashed into `Presentation.content_hash` with the rest of the render ([Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface](#ts-catalogue-disclosure)). |
| `unrequested_lines[]`            | On a session step-up (`confirm` or `rail_auth`) only: one entry `{index, added_by, name_ref}` for each line of the session whose `added_by` is `seller` or `assisted_operator`, and for each line whose `added_by` is `agent` that the agent has not marked `principal_requested`. `index` is the position of the line in the session's `line_items[]`, and `name_ref` is the position of its name in `counterparty_text[]`. It is present only when it has an entry, and then it is also named in `render_required[]`, so that a Trusted Surface that does not understand it renders nothing. The Trusted Surface reads every entry in full, before the total ([Line provenance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#line-provenance)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `requested_line_count`           | Optional, on a session step-up. The number of lines that the agent marked `principal_requested` and that are not in `unrequested_lines[]`. The Trusted Surface counts them aloud ("and 11 items you asked for") and does not read them one by one unless the principal asks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `plan`                           | On a session step-up (`confirm` or `rail_auth`) over a [payment plan](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#plan-wire) only: `{plan_hash, tenders[]}`, each tender `{tender_id, handler, amount, sequence}`. The Trusted Surface shows the whole plan, every tender and its amount, never one tender alone, and reads the plan's total as one figure with its tenders beside it. When the session has operator charges, the render reads the plan total and then each operator charge, and `total` is their sum. Requires `checkout_hash`. It is hashed into `Presentation.content_hash` with the rest of the render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `offer_hash`                     | On a negotiation `kind: confirm` step-up only: the `offer_hash` of the offer the principal is asked to approve ([Step-up to the Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#step-up-to-the-trusted-surface)). Never present with `checkout_hash`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `acceptance_revocation`          | On a negotiation `kind: confirm` step-up about a firm offer only: the offer's [`acceptance_revocation`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation) value, copied unchanged; in this version only `waived` occurs, because receivers refuse `allowed_until_receipt`. Present only with `offer_hash`. It is hashed into `Presentation.content_hash` with the rest of the render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `revoke_route`                   | Where the principal revokes the mandate or cancels, as a URI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `grievance_contact`              | The agent operator's grievance officer contact.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `expires_at`                     | As in the `step_up` object.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

**Match code (`ts_match_code`).** A Trusted Surface and an agent MAY show a 4-digit code that both derive from the `content_hash` of the render: the first 4 bytes of the digest, as an unsigned big-endian integer, modulo 10000, written as 4 digits. The code is a derived display value, not a field of the render and not transmitted, and it is subject to these rules:

- It is shown on an app or web delivery only. On IVR and `upi123pay` it is not read, so that the principal hears one number only, the voice challenge ([Voice confirmation](#voice)).
- It is never a voice challenge, never a control and never evidence. No gateway or verifier relies on it.
- The text beside it says "A matching code does not make a link safe; only your bank's own app is safe" (`hi-IN`: "कोड मेल खाने से लिंक सुरक्षित नहीं हो जाता; सिर्फ़ आपके बैंक का अपना ऐप सुरक्षित है।", which says the same in English). The wording is a draft, under review.
- It is a MAY and not a SHOULD. A phishing page shows no code, so comparing two displays does not stop a phisher, and "the codes match, so it is safe" is a compromised agent's best phishing line. It helps against a look-alike page that an honest agent relays and against a mix-up between concurrent step-ups, and it adds nothing to the wire.

Content rules for `ts_render` and every Trusted Surface template:

1. The total is one figure, with the breakup reachable through its hash. Its fee lines are read separately ([TS-3](#ts-requirements)), and their amounts, with the `remainder`, add up to it.
1. A revoke or cancel route and a grievance contact are always present. BACP requires the grievance contact in every case. From 13-05-2027 the DPDP Act, 2023, s.6(3) requires a request for consent to give the contact details of the Data Protection Officer or another person authorised to answer the Data Principal, and the DPDP Rules, 2025, r.3(c) and r.9 require the notice to describe how to exercise rights and complain, and the business contact information of that person to be published and given in every response ([Legal time bands](#time-bands)).
1. No add-on is preselected, and no text creates urgency.
1. Seller free text appears only in `counterparty_text[]`.
1. On a negotiation step-up that carries `acceptance_revocation`, the Trusted Surface shows the value only as the fixed consequence sentence below, in the principal's language, followed by the offer's cancellation terms, which the gateway states in `summary`. It never shows the token, and it never says or implies that the order cannot be cancelled: cancelling after the contract is formed follows the cancellation terms.
1. On a step-up whose render carries `catalogue_disclosure[]`, the Trusted Surface repeats what discovery showed, before the total, as [below](#ts-catalogue-disclosure). On a step-up whose render carries `unrequested_lines[]`, the Trusted Surface first reads, with the `added_not_by_you` sentence of [Disclosure phrases](#disclosure-phrases), each line that the principal did not add, in the order of the list and with the item name as a labelled seller value from `counterparty_text[]`, then counts the lines the principal asked for (`requested_line_count`), and only then reads the total. A zero-price line that a seller scheme adds is read out and does not block. A paid line that a seller added needs a new quote. `unrequested_lines[]` is a list in the render, not a style, so that a screen reader announces it as a list with a count.
1. On an assisted session (`assisted_operators[]` present), before the factor, the Trusted Surface states from its own templates that an assisted operator is present and that only the principal enters the factor (`hi-IN`: "आपकी मदद के लिए एक व्यक्ति आपके साथ है। PIN सिर्फ़ आप डालें, किसी को न बताएँ।", in English: "Someone is helping you. Only you enter the PIN; tell it to no one."). The Trusted Surface does not read "unverified" aloud: the [evidence summary](#evidence-summary) and the evidence bundle flag an operator reference as asserted, never verified ([Assisted channel](#assisted)).

| Value                                 | `en-IN`                                                                                               | `hi-IN`                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `waived`                              | "Final once sent; it cannot be taken back. Cancelling afterwards follows the terms below."            | "भेजते ही सौदा पक्का, वापस नहीं होगा; रद्द करना नीचे की शर्तों से होगा।"                                         |
| `allowed_until_receipt` (sunset only) | "Final once the other party receives it; cancelling afterwards follows the cancellation terms below." | "सामने वाले पक्ष तक पहुँचते ही सौदा पक्का; उसके बाद रद्द करना नीचे की शर्तों से होगा।" (draft wording, under review) |

The `hi-IN` sentences say, in English: "The deal is final as soon as it is sent and will not be reversed; cancelling follows the terms below" (`waived`), and "The deal is final as soon as it reaches the other party; after that, cancelling follows the terms below" (`allowed_until_receipt`). A Trusted Surface in another language uses a fixed translation of the same sentence from its own templates.

ts-render.negotiation-confirm.json (payload of a negotiation confirm step-up)

```
{
  "step_up_id": "stp_01HZYNq8W3nK5vRt7YcLm2",
  "kind": "confirm",
  "reason": "negotiation_between_reservation_and_max",
  "mandate_id": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "offer_hash": "sha-256:WKKmq8K0e3cRnS6iOO5kEBXsGKuGOw9FdzlnlmLsPgA",
  "acceptance_revocation": "waived",
  "total": {
    "value": 216000,
    "currency": "INR"
  },
  "seller_name": "Bunkar Handlooms",
  "summary": {
    "hi-IN": "बनारसी साड़ी, कुल ₹2,160। भेजते ही सौदा पक्का, वापस नहीं होगा; रद्द करना नीचे की शर्तों से होगा। रद्द करने की शर्तें: पैक होने से पहले कोई शुल्क नहीं; पैक होने के बाद ₹216।",
    "en-IN": "Banarasi saree, ₹2,160 in all. Final once sent; it cannot be taken back. Cancelling afterwards follows the terms below. Cancellation terms: no charge before packing; ₹216 after packing."
  },
  "revoke_route": "https://mm.example.in/mandates/mdt_NEG7Q2W9X4K1M3/revoke",
  "grievance_contact": "grievance@vaani.example.in",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-13T11:17:00+05:30"
}
```

### Negotiation on the Trusted Surface

These rules apply to the negotiation renders and notices of [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md).

- **The acceptance choice.** At mandate set-up the Trusted Surface presents the two values of `process.accept_confirmation`, `ask` and `autonomous`, with equal weight, and preselects neither (TS-2). A mandate-setup `Presentation` that shows either value preselected is refused with `403 ts_render_mismatch`. The set-up also captures `process.notice_route`, the route by which the gateway tells the principal about each autonomous act through a channel the agent does not control. In a consumer session this is the explicit and affirmative action that Rule 4(9) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 asks for.
- **Notice of an autonomous act (a notice render: a gateway-signed compact JWS, not a `TsRender` and not a step-up; its payload schema is open, [Q-105](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-105)).** The gateway builds the notice of `agreed_by_agent` and `purchase_offered_by_agent` from its own templates, in the principal's language, and signs it as a render. It is not a step-up: the principal approves nothing. It states the seller or buyer name, `offeror_kind`, the all-in total (₹ with Indian digit grouping, spoken in words on a voice surface), the quantity and unit, the current-stage cancellation charge, the stop route available in that state, `revoke_route`, `grievance_contact` and its `content_hash`. It carries no URI other than those routes and no urgency text (TS-4), and never reaches the principal through the agent's output, where counterparty text could imitate it. The render and the receipt of its delivery go into the bundle as `notice_renders[]`.
- **Decline of an `AGREED` or `BOUND` deal.** The render shows the current-stage charge under the agreed `cancellation.terms` before the factor is taken, and the principal's confirmation is posted as the distinct event `negotiation.agreed.declined`, never `negotiation.step_up.declined`: one verb with two consequences cannot be told apart on a voice channel. The signed event with its `Presentation` is the proof of presence for the decline; no agent carries an `hp_proof` for it ([Presence proof](#hp-proof)).
- **Offer that ran out.** When an offer lapses during approval, or the acceptor's gateway refuses to dispatch within 5 seconds of `expires_at`, the Trusted Surface says that the offer ran out while the principal was approving, never that the principal declined. The `hi-IN` sentence says, in English, "The offer ran out while you were approving": "आपकी मंज़ूरी पूरी होने से पहले ही ऑफ़र का समय ख़त्म हो गया।" (`offer_expired_during_approval`).
- **IST.** Every time that the Trusted Surface shows or tells a person is in IST, in the person's language. This is a MUST. It is separate from the machine values in signed bytes, which SHOULD carry `+05:30`.
- **Contested crossing.** Each principal is asked on their own surface in one plain question, whether to proceed with the deal, with the same weight for each answer and neither preselected. Declining and silence have the same effect.

### Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface

An agent tells the principal about sponsored results and prior prices when it presents them ([Disclosure phrases](#disclosure-phrases)). The Trusted Surface says it again before the principal confirms, in words the agent does not control. For each entry of `catalogue_disclosure[]`, in order, the Trusted Surface:

1. shows or speaks the item's name as labelled seller text, taken from `counterparty_text[name_ref]` (TS-1);
1. gives the sponsorship sentence for the entry: `ts_sponsored` for `sponsored`, `ts_undeclared` for `undeclared`, and no sentence for `not_sponsored`;
1. if `prior_price` is present, gives the `ts_prior_price` sentence.

All of this comes **before the total**, and under TS-3 audio is read in full before the principal enters the factor. When more than three entries are `undeclared` and carry no `prior_price`, the Trusted Surface MAY give one `ts_undeclared_n` sentence for them instead of their per-item sentences. It never paraphrases. A Trusted Surface in another language uses a fixed translation of the same sentence from its own templates. The wording is a draft, under review with the [disclosure phrases](#disclosure-phrases), and its vocabulary is theirs, so that the principal hears the same words twice.

| Key               | `en-IN`                                                                               | `hi-IN`                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ts_sponsored`    | "Sponsored: {party} was paid to show this item."                                      | "प्रायोजित: इस सामान को दिखाने के लिए {party} को पैसे मिले थे।"                 |
| `ts_undeclared`   | "It was not stated whether this item was sponsored."                                  | "यह सामान प्रायोजित था या नहीं, यह नहीं बताया गया।"                         |
| `ts_undeclared_n` | "For {n} items in this order, it was not stated whether they were sponsored."         | "इस ऑर्डर के {n} सामानों के बारे में नहीं बताया गया कि वे प्रायोजित थे या नहीं।"     |
| `ts_prior_price`  | "Now ₹{price}. The seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this offer: ₹{prior}." | "अब ₹{price}। इस छूट से पहले के 30 दिनों में विक्रेता की सबसे कम कीमत: ₹{prior}।" |

`{party}` uses the party phrases of [Disclosure phrases](#disclosure-phrases), joined by the Trusted Surface's fixed "and" or "और". The `hi-IN` sentences say, in English: "Sponsored: {party} was paid to show this item"; "Whether this item was sponsored was not stated"; "For {n} items of this order it was not stated whether they were sponsored"; and the price pair as in the agent's phrase. Amounts use Indian digit grouping.

Rules:

- The gateway MUST include `catalogue_disclosure[]` on every session step-up of kind `confirm` or `rail_auth`, and on a summary step-up (with entries for every leg), whenever any qualifying item exists. It MUST NOT include it on a `post_order` step-up or on a negotiation `confirm`, which carries `offer_hash` and not `checkout_hash`.
- The `ts_render` stays gateway-signed with the BAP registry key. The gateway MUST copy `sponsorship`, `prior_price` and `unit_price` unaltered from the session's `Disclosures.catalogue[]` entry (`unit_price` is its `discovered_unit_price`).
- The Trusted Surface takes `catalogue_disclosure[]` only from the render, never from the agent. It does not verify seller signatures, so the repeat is only as trustworthy as the gateway's signature on it; a rogue gateway is caught on dispute ([Evidence](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#ap2-verification), step 6), and the agent checks it at run time (rule below).
- An agent that receives a session `step_up` carrying a `ts_render` SHOULD check, before it hands the principal the `trusted_surface_url`, that `catalogue_disclosure[]` matches the session's `Disclosures.catalogue[]` by the evidence step 6 rule. On a mismatch it MUST NOT hand the link over, and it records `discovery_source_mismatch`.
- A Trusted Surface on an earlier version ignores a field it does not know and would ask for the factor without the repeat. The gateway therefore MUST refuse a `step_up.approved` for a render that carries `catalogue_disclosure[]` when `presentation.renders` does not contain `catalogue_disclosure` (`400 invalid_request`, nothing changes).
- A step-up exists only when a threshold, a new seller or another trigger applies. A session that never needs one never reaches a Trusted Surface, so the repeat is absent from it by construction, and the agent's own sentences and the `type: disclosure` messages ([Message object](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/#message-object)) are then the only disclosure.
- The item names and positions in `catalogue_disclosure[]` tell a payer PSP, on a `rail_auth` render, what was bought, beyond the base render. Whether the names of items should reach the payer PSP at all is open ([Q-73](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-73)).

### Presentation record

`Presentation` ([`common.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/common.json) `$defs/Presentation`) records what the Trusted Surface showed, how, and what the principal did:

| Field                  | Required                                                                                                                                                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `surface`              | yes                                                                                                                                                            | The subscriber id of the PSP or Mandate Manager whose surface presented it, equal to the subscriber id of the registry key that signed the event. Never the agent. The gateway refuses an event whose `surface` is not the signer's subscriber id with `404 not_found`, and nothing changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `channel`              | yes                                                                                                                                                            | `Channel` (`app`, `ivr`, `upi123pay`, `assisted`, …).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `language`             | yes                                                                                                                                                            | `LanguageTag`, for example `hi-IN`. A language name such as `"Hindi"` is invalid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `modality`             | yes                                                                                                                                                            | `visual`, `audio` or `both`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `content_hash`         | yes                                                                                                                                                            | For a step-up, the sha-256 of the compact JWS `ts_render`. Otherwise the hash of the content the Trusted Surface rendered from its templates (for a mandate approval, the notice whose hash the ConsentReceipt carries in `notice.hash`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `content_ref`          | yes                                                                                                                                                            | Where a party entitled to the evidence fetches that content to recompute the hash. For a step-up, it is an RFC 3986 fragment that holds an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the evidence bundle, `#/ts_renders/<index>`, where `<index>` is the zero-based position of the render in the bundle's `ts_renders[]`, written without leading zeros. The bundle is signed and immutable, so the index is stable. It never points at the Mandate Manager and PSP only `GET /trusted-surface/step-ups/{step_up_id}`. For any other content it is an absolute URI.                                                                                                                                              |
| `user_action`          | yes                                                                                                                                                            | `tap_confirm`, `upi_pin`, `biometric`, `passkey`, `voice_confirm_plus_device` or `decline`. `biometric` is the principal's own biometric enrolled for the principal on the Trusted Surface device, never an operator's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `shown_at`, `acted_at` | yes                                                                                                                                                            | When it was shown and when the principal acted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `template_id`          | no                                                                                                                                                             | The Trusted Surface template and its version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `renders`              | on `step_up.approved` when the render carries `catalogue_disclosure[]` or `plan`, and on any step-up approval whose render lists a name in `render_required[]` | The render fields beyond this version's base set that the Trusted Surface presented: `catalogue_disclosure`, `plan`, `items`, `unrequested_lines` or `acceptance_revocation`, for example `["catalogue_disclosure", "plan"]`. It is the only extension point of `Presentation`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `checkout_hash`        | on `step_up.approved`                                                                                                                                          | The quote the content showed: the session's quote, or for a `post_order` step-up the `checkout_hash` of the order's closed Checkout Mandate. Never present with `offer_hash`. A `post_order` step-up for an order-less ledger act has no quote, and its approval carries none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `offer_hash`           | on `negotiation.step_up.approved`                                                                                                                              | The offer a negotiation `confirm` step-up showed. Never present with `checkout_hash`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `plan_hash`            | on `step_up.approved` when the render carries `plan`                                                                                                           | The `plan.plan_hash` of the payment plan the content showed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `device_signature`     | no                                                                                                                                                             | A JWS by a device key of the Trusted Surface over the JCS form of `{step_up_id, content_hash, acted_at}` (for a step-up) or `{content_hash, acted_at}`; its protected header carries the public key as `jwk`. Where the mandate lists `principal.device_jkt[]`, it MUST verify against a key whose RFC 7638 thumbprint is listed, or the gateway answers `403 presence_not_proven`. Where the mandate lists none, no verifier relies on it. It is never called an electronic signature under the Information Technology Act, 2000: whether it is an authentication technique under s.3A is not verified as of 18-10-2026 ([Q-86](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-86)). |
| `voice_evidence`       | no                                                                                                                                                             | Audio and transcript hashes and the translation model, for a voice confirmation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `assisted_by`          | on `assisted`                                                                                                                                                  | The `participant_id` of the assisted operator, taken by the Trusted Surface from `ts_render.assisted_operators[]`, never from the agent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

A `TrustedSurfaceEvent` of type `step_up.approved`, `negotiation.step_up.approved`, `mandate.activated`, `loan.accepted` or `payment.afa_completed` **MUST** carry `presentation`. Without it the gateway refuses the event with `400 invalid_request` and nothing changes. On `step_up.approved` the `presentation` **MUST** carry `checkout_hash`, except on the approval of a `post_order` step-up for an order-less ledger act (`LEDGER_ACK` with no `order_id`), which carries none; on `negotiation.step_up.approved`, the approval of a negotiation `confirm` step-up, it **MUST** carry `offer_hash`; it never carries both. On either approval its `user_action` **MUST NOT** be `decline`. The gateway refuses an event that breaks one of these rules with `400 invalid_request` and nothing changes; this includes a `step_up.approved` posted for a negotiation step-up. A decline is posted only as `step_up.declined`, which **SHOULD** carry a `Presentation` with `user_action: decline`. A ConsentReceipt **MAY** carry the same record in `captured_via.presentation`.

When the gateway receives a `step_up.approved` or `negotiation.step_up.approved` event it **MUST** check, before any state change:

- that the event is signed by the step-up's Mandate Manager or payer PSP ([Step-up signers](#ts-signers)); any other registry key gets `404 not_found`, never `403`, and nothing changes;
- that `presentation.surface` is the subscriber id of the signing key, or refuse the event with `404 not_found` (nothing changes);
- that `presentation.content_hash` is the sha-256 of that step-up's `ts_render`, or refuse the event with `403 ts_render_mismatch`;
- on `step_up.approved`, that `presentation.checkout_hash` equals the session's current `checkout_hash` (for a `post_order` step-up, the `checkout_hash` of the order's closed Checkout Mandate; none for an order-less ledger act); an approval for an earlier quote approves nothing ([Deterministic evaluation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#evaluation), step 8);
- on `negotiation.step_up.approved`, that `presentation.offer_hash` equals the `ts_render`'s `offer_hash` and the hash of the offer the step-up names, and, for a firm offer, that the `ts_render`'s `acceptance_revocation` equals that offer's value; otherwise it refuses the event with `403 ts_render_mismatch`, and nothing is sent;
- on `step_up.approved` for a `ts_render` that carries `catalogue_disclosure[]`, that `presentation.renders` contains `catalogue_disclosure`; otherwise it refuses the event with `400 invalid_request` and nothing changes;
- on a step-up approval for a `ts_render` that carries `render_required[]`, that `presentation.renders` contains every name listed there; otherwise it refuses the event with `400 invalid_request` and nothing changes;
- on `step_up.approved` for a `ts_render` that carries `plan`, that `presentation.renders` contains `plan` (otherwise `400 invalid_request`, nothing changes) and that `presentation.plan_hash` equals the render's `plan.plan_hash` (otherwise `403 ts_render_mismatch`);
- where the mandate carries a [`confirmation_floor`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#confirmation-floor), that `presentation.user_action` is not below its `min_user_action` and `presentation.channel` is in its `channels_allow`; otherwise it refuses the event with `403 presence_not_proven` at `$.presentation.user_action` or `$.presentation.channel` and nothing changes;
- where the mandate lists `principal.device_jkt[]`, that `presentation.device_signature` verifies against a key whose thumbprint is listed; otherwise it refuses the event with `403 presence_not_proven` and nothing changes;
- that `presentation.acted_at` is not after the step-up's `expires_at`, or treat the step-up as expired (`step_up_expired`, no money moves);
- on an assisted session, the [assisted channel](#assisted) rules.

While the session is in `human_handoff` the gateway holds a `step_up.approved` event that passes these checks and does not apply it. After the handoff is released it applies a held approval only if the step-up has not expired and its `checkout_hash` still equals the session's ([Human handoff](#handoff)). For a summary step-up the re-check is per leg: a held approval applies to a released session only if that session's `covers[]` entry still equals its current `checkout_hash`, payee and amount.

### Voice confirmation

`user_action: voice_confirm_plus_device` is a confirmation by voice or keypad on a call. Here "device" means the number or call leg that the Trusted Surface holds for the principal or payer, not a device key. The rules:

- **The Trusted Surface draws the challenge.** It draws a challenge of at least 4 digits from its own random source, on its own call leg, single-use, for one step-up. The challenge is never in `ts_render`, `StepUp`, `StepUpStatus` or anything else that an agent sees, because an agent that bridges the call would know it. No field of the render derives it.
- **The answer is bound in the event.** `voice_evidence.challenge_hash` is the sha-256 over the JCS form of `{step_up_id, content_hash, challenge}`, and is REQUIRED with this `user_action`. The gateway cannot recompute it: it is evidence, and the Trusted Surface's draw of an unpredictable value is a Trusted Surface conformance case, not a gateway check. A challenge that is guessed after the call from the hash is harmless, because it is single-use and ends with the call.
- **Keypad equals speech.** The principal may answer by DTMF or by speech, with the same steps and the same weight, so that a feature phone keeps its path. No rule depends on speech recognition of the challenge.
- **Which calls count.** Voice counts only on a call that the Trusted Surface placed to the number it holds for the principal or payer. It also counts when the principal dialled the Trusted Surface's published number from that number, but only together with the Trusted Surface's own challenge, because caller identity can be spoofed. The number is held by the Trusted Surface and is never in the mandate or the render.
- **Never money.** The gateway refuses `voice_confirm_plus_device` on a `rail_auth` step-up, and on any `confirm` step-up whose approval releases a debit, with `403 presence_not_proven` at `$.presentation.user_action`. Voice confirms only what moves no money (a cancel, an issue acceptance). RBI/2025-26/79 paras 5(a) and 6(b) and UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 para 19.2.2 settle this for money ([Q-13](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-13)). In human-not-present (HNP) the debit rests on the mandate's authentication model, so the refusal there is BACP policy implementing Q-13, not an RBI requirement. A PIN entered over a UPI 123PAY IVR stays `upi_pin`.
- **No PIN on a Trusted Surface call.** A call that the Trusted Surface places never takes a UPI PIN ([PIN rule](#ts-pin-rule)).
- **Agent side.** An agent's own voice channel MUST NOT stay on, conference or bridge the call leg of the Trusted Surface. This is an agent conformance disclosure check and cannot be observed on the wire.

## Multi-seller basket on the Trusted Surface

A [multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket) reaches the principal as one summary step-up (reason `rail_fallback`) whose `ts_render` lists every seller in `basket[]`. The Trusted Surface:

- states the **number of sellers first**, and for a human-present plan the number of payments and of PINs needed (for example "3 sellers, 3 payments, 3 UPI PINs"), before any line;
- then shows or reads each `basket[]` line: the bank-returned payee name, the amount, whether a PIN is needed, for a block the amount locked and until when, and whether the money is the principal's own (`deposit`) or `credit`; under TS-3, audio is read in full before the principal enters any factor;
- for a block whose debits the gateway cannot see, gives the unseen-draw statement that the `ts_render` carries in `summary`: that this seller can draw up to the stated amount unseen by BACP and can change the block's amount or validity ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger)). The same statement is in the notice when such a block is set up ([Issuance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#issuance), step 4);
- for a block whose mandate is paused for `unmatched_rail_debit`, shows the route to revoke the block in the UPI app (NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 16.10), because the pause stops BACP payments but not draws at the rail;
- shows the summary as approval of a **plan**, never as a payment: each human-present leg is then a separate step-up with its own `ts_render`, its own `content_hash` and the principal's own factor, and a summary `Presentation` alone authorises no debit.

A new per-seller block (3b in the [per-leg rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule)) is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment to the same seller, with equal weight: the same number of steps, neither option preselected, and declining the block no harder than paying once (TS-2). It is never offered after a failed payment, and never on a step-up with `delivery: ivr_callback`. On `ivr_callback` and UPI 123PAY every leg is a human-present call of its own, read in full before its PIN.

## Assisted channel

The following is **BACP policy**. No law found requires it; it exists so that an assisted operator is visible in the evidence and cannot approve for the principal.

- A session is **assisted** when its `channel` is `assisted` **or** the agent's AgentCredential has `agent.class: assisted`. An assisted agent that declares `channel: app` is still bound by every rule below.
- An assisted session **MUST** list an `assisted_operator` in `participants[]`. Otherwise `POST /sessions` returns `400 invalid_request` at `$.participants`.
- Every Trusted Surface approval on an assisted session **MUST** name the operator in `presentation.assisted_by`. The Trusted Surface takes it from `ts_render.assisted_operators[]`, which the gateway builds from the session's `participants[]`, never from the agent. The gateway refuses an `assisted_by` that is not an `assisted_operator` of the session with `403 presence_not_proven`.
- The principal approves with the principal's own factor: `user_action` is `upi_pin` or `biometric`, never a tap. `biometric` means the principal's own biometric enrolled for the principal on the Trusted Surface device. The gateway refuses any other approval with `403 presence_not_proven` (for example a schema-valid `presentation.channel: app` approval on an assisted session), and the session stays `requires_escalation`.
- A `Presentation` that fails its schema (for example `channel: assisted` with `user_action: tap_confirm`) is refused with `400 invalid_request`, as for every schema failure, and nothing changes.
- The operator may read the content aloud (`modality: audio` or `both`); the factor is the principal's.
- An assisted operator who reads discovery results aloud uses the same fixed sentences as an agent ([Disclosure phrases](#disclosure-phrases)).

`assisted_by` and `Participant.ref` are attribution, never authentication. A `ref` is namespaced `scheme:id`, where `scheme` is `csc_vle`, `bank_bc`, `ondc_np_agent` or `other`, and the gateway sets `Participant.ref_verification` to `asserted` or `verified`. The gateway writes `verified` only when it can name the verifying registry, and none exists today ([Q-62](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-62)), so `asserted` is the only value in practice. An agent that supplies `verified` gets `400 invalid_request`. The Trusted Surface does not read "unverified" aloud ([content rule 7](#ts-render)); the evidence summary and the bundle flag the reference as asserted.

The Information Technology Act, 2000, s.11(b) attributes an electronic record to the originator when it is sent "by a person who had the authority to act on behalf of the originator in respect of that electronic record", and s.11(c) when it is sent "by an information system programmed by or on behalf of the originator to operate automatically" ([India Code text](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/13116/1/it_act_2000_updated.pdf)). Whether an operator's tap could be attributed to the principal under either is a question for counsel ([Q-86](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-86)), and whether voice, tap or operator-relayed confirmation is valid consent is open ([Q-13](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-13)). Who certifies assisted operators is open ([Q-62](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-62)).

`StepUp.delivery: assisted` gives the step-up at least 5 minutes before `expires_at` (and at most 15). The 5-minute floor is a BACP design value, not an external requirement.

## Disclosure phrases

For a buyer on a feature phone, an IVR call or a screen reader, the agent is the display. The sentences below are how an agent tells the principal about sponsored results and prior prices ([Catalogue disclosures](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures)), about a refused capability, a line the principal did not add, a provisional loyalty benefit and a policy that a seller does not state. They are fixed: they bind agents and the scripts of assisted operators, and a paraphrase is non-conformant, because a paraphrase by a language model is itself a way to change what the principal understands. Counterparty text never appears inside them, except as a labelled value.

Draft wording

The wording in this table is a draft. It is under review by the human-experience review seat and the owner, and it changes only through that review before a dated release.

| Key                       | `en-IN`                                                                               | `hi-IN`                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sponsored`               | "Sponsored: {party} was paid to show this."                                           | "प्रायोजित: इसे दिखाने के लिए {party} को पैसे मिले हैं।"                          |
| `undeclared`              | "Not stated whether this is sponsored."                                               | "यह प्रायोजित है या नहीं, यह नहीं बताया गया है।"                              |
| `prior_price`             | "Now ₹{price}. The seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this offer: ₹{prior}." | "अब ₹{price}। इस छूट से पहले के 30 दिनों में विक्रेता की सबसे कम कीमत: ₹{prior}।" |
| `mrp`                     | "MRP ₹{mrp}."                                                                         | "एमआरपी (अधिकतम खुदरा मूल्य) ₹{mrp}।"                                      |
| `discount_applied`        | "Discount{ with code {code}}: ₹{amount} off."                                         | "छूट{ (कोड {code})}: ₹{amount} कम।"                                      |
| `discount_rejected`       | "Code {code} was not accepted."                                                       | "कोड {code} स्वीकार नहीं हुआ।"                                              |
| `discount_affiliate`      | "Your assistant's provider earns if this code is used."                               | "यह कोड इस्तेमाल होने पर आपके सहायक की कंपनी को कमाई होती है।"                |
| `added_not_by_you`        | "This item was not added by you: it was added by {party}."                            | "यह सामान आपने नहीं जोड़ा; इसे {party} ने जोड़ा है।"                           |
| `cart_estimate`           | "This is an estimate, not a price you will pay."                                      | "यह एक अनुमान है, आपसे लिया जाने वाला दाम नहीं।"                             |
| `loyalty_provisional`     | "A loyalty benefit may apply later. It is not in this total."                         | "लॉयल्टी का लाभ बाद में लागू हो सकता है। वह इस कुल राशि में शामिल नहीं है।"        |
| `policy_not_stated`       | "The {policy} policy is not stated."                                                  | "{policy} नीति नहीं बताई गई है।"                                          |
| `capability_absent`       | "This shopping service does not offer that feature, so your request was not applied." | "यह शॉपिंग सेवा यह सुविधा नहीं देती, इसलिए आपका अनुरोध लागू नहीं हुआ।"           |
| party `bpp`               | "the seller's app"                                                                    | "विक्रेता का ऐप"                                                          |
| party `gateway`           | "the shopping service"                                                                | "शॉपिंग सेवा"                                                             |
| party `agent`             | "your assistant's provider"                                                           | "आपके सहायक की कंपनी"                                                     |
| party `assisted_operator` | "the assistant helping you"                                                           | "आपकी मदद कर रहा सहायक"                                                 |
| party unknown             | "a party in the chain"                                                                | "बीच का कोई पक्ष"                                                        |

The `hi-IN` sentences say, in English: "Sponsored: {party} has been paid to show this"; "Whether this is sponsored has not been stated"; "Now ₹{price}. Seller's lowest price in the 30 days before this discount: ₹{prior}"; and "MRP (maximum retail price) ₹{mrp}". The party phrases say, in English: "the seller's app", "the shopping service", "your assistant's company" and "some party in the chain". The discount phrases say, in English: "Discount (code {code}): ₹{amount} less"; "Code {code} was not accepted"; "If this code is used, your assistant's company earns"; and "This shopping service does not offer that feature, so your request was not applied" (`capability_absent`, which has no slot). The new keys say, in English: "This item was not added by you: it was added by {party}" (`added_not_by_you`; the party is the one that the line's `added_by` names: `seller` is spoken as the seller's app); "This is an estimate, not a price you will pay" (`cart_estimate`, used only if a cart capability is ever added, [Q-95](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-95)); "A loyalty benefit may apply later; it is not in this total" (`loyalty_provisional`); and "The {policy} policy is not stated" (`policy_not_stated`, where `{policy}` is one of three fixed words: return (`वापसी की`), cancellation (`रद्द करने की`) or cash on delivery (`कैश ऑन डिलीवरी की`)). The part in braces and brackets of `discount_applied` is left out for an automatic discount, which has no code.

Rules:

1. The agent says the sentence for each item whose `sponsorship.status` is `sponsored` or `undeclared`, with `{party}` taken from `by[]` (several parties are joined with a fixed "and" or "और"; an unknown value uses the unknown-party phrase). There is no sentence for `not_sponsored`: the agent says nothing.
1. On audio the sentence is spoken **before** the item it labels, in the principal's session language.
1. Amounts are rendered with Indian digit grouping. The `prior_price` sentence is the only way to voice a prior price. The `mrp` sentence is the only way to voice an MRP, and it is never voiced as a "was" price.
1. A principal whose language is not `en-IN` or `hi-IN` hears the operator's own fixed and reviewed translation of the same sentence, as for the [acceptance-revocation sentences](#ts-render): a Trusted Surface or an agent in another language uses a fixed translation of the same sentence from its own templates, and never a free translation made at run time. Whether a reviewed translation route exists for fixed legal labels in the Eighth Schedule languages is open ([Q-68](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-68)).
1. `{party}`, `{price}`, `{prior}`, `{mrp}`, `{code}`, `{amount}` and `{policy}` are the only slots. `{code}` is filled from the code the agent itself submitted, never from `applied[].code`, which a seller could fill with text. The `title` of a discount is seller text, shown only as labelled counterparty text. An item name, if it is spoken, is a separate, labelled seller value and never part of a sentence.
1. On a step-up, the Trusted Surface repeats the sentences in its own fixed wording ([Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface](#ts-catalogue-disclosure)).

## AI disclosure

The agent's first message in every session is the AI disclosure, with typed routes to a human ([Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#ai-disclosure)):

- Every session carries `ai_disclosure{notice, handoff_routes[]}`, taken from the AgentCredential's `disclosure.ai_notice` and `disclosure.handoff_routes`. `ai_disclosure` is always present; `handoff_routes` is absent when the credential lists none. The disclosure message points at it with `param: $.ai_disclosure`.
- An AgentCredential whose `agent.channels` includes `voice`, `ivr` or `upi123pay` **MUST** list a `tel:` route ([RFC 3966](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3966)), optionally with DTMF digits (for example "press 0"), because a feature-phone caller cannot open a web link. A route with DTMF digits is always a `tel:` route. The schema rejects a credential that lists only `https:` routes, and a route that pairs DTMF digits with an `https:` URI.
- An agent **SHOULD NOT** split one intended order into several payments to change the fee that a seller bears. The gateway's suspected-split-order check enforces it ([Split-order detection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#step-up)); BACP adds no new trigger for it.
- The gateway writes an InstructionLog entry at stage **`ai_disclosure`**, `actor: agent`. It is the first entry whose actor is `agent`, before `intent`. The stage `disclosure` is the seller's quote, not the AI disclosure.
- On the network, `context.bacp.ai_disclosure: true` is REQUIRED, and the gateway **MUST** mirror it into the `bacp` tag group, so that a seller learns that an AI agent is ordering even when a validator strips `context.bacp` ([Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#mirroring)). The gateway **MAY** also send `acting_for`, `operator_name` and `operator_grievance_contact`. It sends `acting_for.gstin` and `acting_for.display_name` only when the mandate's `data_scopes` include `ACTING_FOR`, and otherwise omits them.

Example disclosure in Hindi ("You are talking to an AI assistant. Press 0 to talk to a human."): `"hi-IN": "आप एक AI सहायक से बात कर रहे हैं। किसी इंसान से बात करने के लिए 0 दबाएँ।"`

## Human handoff

A principal can ask for a human at any time, including after the mandate is revoked.

1. The agent calls `POST /sessions/{session_id}/handoff` (tag `bacp-browse`) with `action: request` and one of the session's `ai_disclosure.handoff_routes` (no route when the session lists none). The agent picks a route whose `languages` include the session's language, where one exists, and otherwise says so to the principal. The gateway **MUST** accept it in every session state and whatever the mandate's status, and returns `201`.
1. An open session moves to status **`human_handoff`**. While it is there, the gateway refuses `PUT` and `complete` from the agent with `409 session_state_conflict` at `$.status`, and holds any `step_up.approved` event without applying it ([Presentation record](#presentation)). A session in any other state keeps its status and records `handoff`.
1. A human support operator accepts with `action: accept`, signed with a registry key of role `support_operator` under tag `bacp-handoff`. Only then does the gateway set `handoff.accepted_by` (that key's id) and `handoff.accepted_at`. The gateway reads the key's [registry record](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#registry-lookup), which names the agent operator (`operator_id`) and the one person who holds the key, and answers an acceptance as follows, each time without changing the handoff:
   - a key whose registry role is not `support_operator`, or a signature under any other tag: `401 signature_invalid`;
   - a `support_operator` key of another agent operator than the session's: `404 not_found`, so that the key has no standing and the answer is no oracle for which sessions exist;
   - an `accept` while `accepted_by` is already set: `409 session_state_conflict` at `$.handoff.accepted_by`.
1. The handoff ends with `action: release`.
