Amounts are integer paise: `150000` is ₹1,500 per order, `300000` is ₹3,000 per calendar month, and step-up applies above ₹1,200.

## Issuance

An agent never signs or activates an open mandate. It **requests** one. The principal approves it on a **Trusted Surface** (the payer PSP's app, or a Mandate Manager app), and the **Mandate Manager** (MM) issues it.

1. The agent calls `POST /mandates` (tag `bacp-browse`) with a `MandateRequest`: `purpose_code`, `rail`, `presence_allowed`, `proposed_constraints`, `data_scopes`, `action_scope`, `validity` (an ISO 8601 duration), `language`, `channel` (the channel on which the principal will approve) and `webhook_url`, and REQUIRED `operator_compensation` ([Operator compensation](#operator-compensation)). The gateway **MUST** accept `webhook_url`, so that `mandate.status_changed` can reach the agent before any session exists. To add a seller to an existing root open Checkout Mandate, the request also carries `checkout_mandate_ref` (pattern `^mdt_[A-Za-z0-9]{12,40}$`). A request for a payee-bound primitive carries `payee{vpa, bpp_id}`, and a request for a Reserve Pay block also carries the block amount it asks for in `rail_limits.block_amount` ([Sibling Payment Mandates](#sibling-payment-mandates)). A request that the principal originates on the Trusted Surface to move a mandate to another gateway carries `supersedes{mandate_id}` ([Porting a mandate](#port)); an agent never sends it. Proposed: when `action_scope` is omitted, all eight actions (`DISCOVER`, `QUOTE`, `ORDER`, `PAY`, `CANCEL`, `RETURN`, `RAISE_ISSUE`, `SHARE_DATA`) are requested, and the Trusted Surface shows that full scope to the principal before approval.
1. Before anything reaches the Trusted Surface, the gateway or the MM **MUST** reject the request:
   - with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` if `rail` resolves to a handler that cannot back an open mandate at this gateway: one that is not open-eligible or has no `binding.open_primitives`, a `reserved` or `deprecated` descriptor, or a `pilot` descriptor that the gateway's conformance attestation does not list ([Handler binding](#handler-binding));
   - with `403 constraint_unknown` if `proposed_constraints` has a key this page does not define (see [Fail-closed handling](#unknown-constraints));
   - with `400 invalid_request` at `$.operator_compensation` if the request has no `operator_compensation`, or one that is not consistent with the `disclosure.compensation_model` of the signing AgentCredential ([Operator compensation](#operator-compensation));
   - with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` if it has no `amount_per_txn`; has no periodic budget; has no `categories_allow`, or one outside the purpose's categories; asks for a longer validity than the purpose allows; exceeds any per-transaction or per-period bound of the purpose ([Purpose bounds](#purpose-bounds)); asks for a data scope the purpose does not allow; names a `purpose_code` that is not in the [purpose-code registry](#purpose-bounds); or exceeds the static limits of the requested rail, including a `rail_limits.block_amount` above the handler's per-block limit in the [handler registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md) (at `$.rail_limits.block_amount`);
   - if `rail` resolves to `in.upi.reservepay` (primitive `sbmd_block`): with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.payee` if the request has no `payee`, and at `$.rail_limits.block_amount` if it has no `rail_limits.block_amount`; with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` if the gateway holds no BPP-signed payment terms of the seller `payee.bpp_id` and does not obtain them first (a Beckn `init` to that seller, never followed by `confirm`), if that `payee` is the buyer app (a block collected by the BAP) and `presence_allowed` includes `HNP`, or if `payee.vpa` is not the VPA in those terms; and, for every Reserve Pay request, with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` if the requested `rail_limits.block_amount` breaks the [sum-of-blocks rule](#sibling-payment-mandates), or `403 mandate_exhausted` if it does not fit the root's headroom, at `$.checkout_mandate_ref` for a request with `checkout_mandate_ref` and at `$.rail_limits.block_amount` for a request without it, whose root is the one it proposes. These checks run before anything reaches the rail, so the principal's PSP is never asked to create a block that the MM would then refuse.
1. Otherwise the gateway returns `202` with a `MandateHandle` in `PENDING`, carrying a `trusted_surface_url` deep link, which is an `https` URL on an origin of the issuing Mandate Manager or a rail deep link that opens the payer PSP's own app ([Origins and delivery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-origins)). The link expires after at most 15 minutes.
1. The principal opens the link. The Trusted Surface shows the notice in the principal's language (English or a language of the Eighth Schedule): limits, categories, data items, recipient class, withdrawal route and grievance route, and the [operator compensation](#operator-compensation): what the principal pays the operator, and what sellers pay the operator or the buyer app. The notice, with the compensation, is hashed into the ConsentReceipt `notice`. For a payee-bound primitive the notice also shows the payee name the bank returns for `payee.vpa` and the seller's `bpp_id`. For a Reserve Pay block it shows the requested block amount and, unless the payer PSP attests a block-debit feed, the unseen-draw statement ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)). For a block whose attested funding is credit, the notice says "credit" in the principal's language and, for an interest-bearing credit line, that interest may run from each debit (NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 26.1.2). For a sibling Payment Mandate it shows the other Payment Mandates under the same root, their combined total, and the amount each budget of the root has left (its `max` less the root's exposure). The principal approves with an explicit action and the rail's own authentication (for UPI, the UPI PIN).
1. The payer PSP creates or links the rail primitive (for example a Reserve Pay block, a UPI Circle delegation or an AutoPay mandate). It **MUST** use a primitive listed in the handler descriptor's `binding.open_primitives`, and signs a rail **attestation**: a JWS over `{rail_ref, type, primitive, limits, expiry, payee, funding}` (and, for a gift PPI, `custody`). It **MUST NOT** create a Reserve Pay block larger than the requested `rail_limits.block_amount`.
1. The MM checks [handler eligibility](#handler-binding) against the current registry, taken from the dated BACP release and never from a gateway endpoint, records that registry's version in `rail_binding.registry_version` (and, where it reads the release manifest, the `registry_serial` and the digest of the registry file in `rail_binding.registry_serial` and `rail_binding.registry_digest`), and **MUST** refuse issuance (`rail_binding_not_open_eligible`) if the attested `primitive` is not in the descriptor's `binding.open_primitives`, the descriptor is not open-eligible, or its `status` is neither `live` nor an attested `pilot`. For a `pilot` handler the MM **MUST** first verify the gateway's [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules), forwarded in the request's `gateway_attestation`, find the handler in its `pilots[]`, and write `rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti}` into the mandate. The MM then copies `agent.bap_id` from the verified AgentCredential's `bap.subscriber_id` into the mandate, never from the request, and checks that every BACP constraint is at or below the attested rail limits, and, for a Reserve Pay block, that the attested `block_amount` is at most the requested one and that the attested expiry is no later than the root open Checkout Mandate's `valid_until`. It refuses an attested `funding` of credit (or a missing one, or an overdraft account without a deposit attestation) when the root lacks `credit_funding_allowed: true`, with `403 credit_funding_not_allowed` ([Handler binding](#handler-binding)), and refuses a gift PPI whose attestation does not state `custody: principal_side`. It builds the open Checkout and open Payment Mandates, or, for a request with `checkout_mandate_ref`, only the open Payment Mandate ([Sibling Payment Mandates](#sibling-payment-mandates)). If the MM refuses issuance at this step after the rail primitive exists, it **MUST** revoke the primitive at the rail and report the outcome in `rail_revocation{status}` on the `mandate.rejected` event it sends to the gateway. A refused block whose revocation is `unconfirmed` is exposure at its attested `block_amount` until the revocation is confirmed or the block expires, although it never became `ACTIVE` ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)). The **principal** signs both (`signatures[].role: principal`) and the **MM countersigns** both (`role: mandate_manager`). The MM allocates a status-list entry per mandate and issues the ConsentReceipt.
1. The MM sends a signed `mandate.activated` event to the gateway's `/trusted-surface/events` (tag `bacp-ts`, registry key of role MM or PSP). The event **MUST** carry the [`Presentation`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#presentation) of the approval: surface, channel, language, modality, the hash of the notice shown and the principal's action. The gateway records an InstructionLog entry at stage `mandate` and sends the webhook `mandate.status_changed` (`ACTIVE`) to the agent. For a sibling Reserve Pay block the gateway applies the activation inside the atomic section keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)), so that an activation and a `complete` never both take the same headroom: if the block at its full attested amount no longer fits every budget window that contains the activation, the gateway refuses the event with `403 mandate_exhausted` and never treats the mandate as `ACTIVE`; the MM then revokes the mandate and its block at the rail and sends `mandate.revoked` with `rail_revocation{status}`. If that status is `unconfirmed`, the block is exposure at its attested `block_amount` until the revocation is confirmed or the block expires.

A verifier **MUST** accept an open mandate only if a principal signature and an MM signature both verify against registry-resolvable keys of those roles, and the rail attestation verifies against a key of role PSP and matches `rail_binding.rail_ref`, `rail_binding.type` and `rail_binding.primitive`.

```
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Principal
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway
    participant MM as Mandate Manager
    participant TS as Trusted Surface (payer PSP app)
    participant N as NPCI and issuer
    U->>A: Order my groceries every month, up to ₹3,000
    A->>G: POST /mandates with purpose, rail, constraints, data scopes, webhook_url
    G->>G: Check unknown constraints, schema, purpose bounds, rail static caps
    G->>MM: Mandate request with the agent cnf key
    MM-->>G: PENDING request id and Trusted Surface link (15 min)
    G-->>A: 202 PENDING with trusted_surface_url
    A->>U: Please approve in your UPI app
    U->>TS: Open link, read notice, approve with UPI PIN
    TS->>N: Create rail primitive (block, delegation or mandate)
    N-->>TS: rail_ref
    TS->>MM: Approval with device signature and PSP rail attestation
    MM->>MM: Check constraints are within rail limits
    MM->>MM: Principal and MM sign open Checkout and Payment Mandates
    MM->>MM: Issue ConsentReceipt and status-list entries
    MM->>G: Signed event mandate.activated
    G->>G: InstructionLog entry at stage mandate
    G-->>A: Webhook mandate.status_changed ACTIVE
```

### Operator compensation

A principal who knows how the operator behind her agent is paid can discount its advice. The mandate request therefore carries `operator_compensation`, and the Trusted Surface shows it in the notice before the principal approves.

```
{
  "from_principal": [{"basis": "per_order", "amount": {"value": 2000, "currency": "INR"}}],
  "from_sellers": "finder_fee"
}
```

| Field              | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `from_principal[]` | What the principal pays: one or more `{basis, amount?}`. `basis` is `per_order` (a fee on each order), `period` (a fee for a period named in the operator's terms) or `none`. `amount` is REQUIRED for `per_order` and `period`, and absent for `none`. A `none` entry stands alone. |
| `from_sellers`     | What sellers pay the operator or the buyer app for orders it brings: `finder_fee` (an ONDC buyer finder fee), `channel_margin`, `none` or `other`.                                                                                                                                   |

- The Mandate Manager **MUST NOT** activate a mandate whose request has no `operator_compensation` (`400 invalid_request` at `$.operator_compensation`; the mandate never becomes `ACTIVE`), and **MUST** show the value in the notice and hash it into the ConsentReceipt `notice` (`notice.operator_compensation` is REQUIRED).
- The source of the declaration is the operator. When the AgentCredential carries `disclosure.compensation_model`, the request **MUST** be consistent with it: `none` means every `from_principal` basis is `none` and `from_sellers` is `none`; `seller_paid` means `from_principal` is `none` and `from_sellers` is not `none`; `principal_paid` means a `from_principal` entry is not `none` and `from_sellers` is `none`; `mixed` means both. Otherwise the request is refused with `400 invalid_request` at `$.operator_compensation`.
- This is BACP policy, not a statutory duty. No Indian rule found requires an agent operator to disclose a seller-paid commission (not verified as of 18-10-2026), and BACP cites no law for it ([Q-79](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-79)).
- When a session's `intermediary_compensation[]` has an entry with `source: seller` while the mandate's notice says `from_sellers: none`, the gateway adds the warning `operator_compensation_mismatch` (`requires_buyer_review`) and logs it at stage `disclosure`. It tells the principal once per mandate on the Trusted Surface and reports the mismatch to the Mandate Manager. The Mandate Manager then asks the operator for a corrected notice, which takes effect only on the principal's re-approval.
- When the AgentCredential has no `compensation_model`, the notice says that the operator has not declared its compensation model to its credential issuer.
- Per-order amounts are shown again at the time of the order as an [operator charge](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fee-lines). What sellers pay is carried per order in `intermediary_compensation[]` and is never read out per order.

### Sibling Payment Mandates

A Reserve Pay block pays one seller, so a principal who shops hands-free across several sellers holds one open Payment Mandate per payee-bound instrument, all under **one** root open Checkout Mandate whose budgets cap the total ([Multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket)).

- **Requesting a sibling.** A `MandateRequest` with `checkout_mandate_ref` asks for one more open Payment Mandate under an existing root. `checkout_mandate_ref` **MUST** name an `ACTIVE` root open Checkout Mandate of the same principal; otherwise the MM refuses it with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.checkout_mandate_ref`. The MM builds **only** an open Payment Mandate, whose `checkout_mandate_ref` is that root and whose constraints narrow the root's ([Immutability and delegation](#immutability-and-delegation)). It never builds a second Checkout Mandate or a second budget for the same basket. `parent_mandate_id` stays reserved for sub-agent delegation.
- **Payee.** An open Payment Mandate whose `rail_binding.primitive` is `sbmd_block` **MUST** carry `payee{vpa, bpp_id}` and, when the seller's BPP-signed terms name a provider, `payee.provider_id`, which **MUST** equal `message.order.provider.id` of those terms at every leg. A leg whose provider differs is refused with `403 reservepay_block_wrong_payee` and nothing is debited (a BACP rule whose basis is RBI Master Direction on Payment Aggregators 2025 para 13(f), under which a PA ensures that a marketplace takes no payment for a seller not onboarded on it, and para 13(e), a merchant ID per merchant; the block-payee match itself is BACP policy); one seller app can serve several shops from one collection VPA, which is why the VPA alone is not enough (whether ONDC seller apps share one VPA is not verified as of 18-10-2026). A request without it is refused with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.payee`. `payee.vpa` **MUST** equal the VPA in the seller's BPP-signed payment terms (Beckn `payments[].params.virtual_payment_address` of `on_init`), and the attested payee **MUST** equal `payee.vpa`; otherwise issuance is refused with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` and nothing is sent to the rail ([Handler binding](#handler-binding)).
- **The payee is bound to BPP-signed terms, always.** The gateway **MUST** hold the BPP-signed payment terms of the seller `payee.bpp_id` before a Reserve Pay request goes to the Trusted Surface, including for a set-up outside any checkout. If it holds none, it obtains them first by a Beckn `init` to that seller that it never follows with `confirm`, or refuses the request with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`. The terms are the raw `on_init` body as received together with its Beckn `Authorization` header, verified against the registry key of the BPP named in `context.bpp_id`, which **MUST** be `payee.bpp_id`. No per-object JWS is needed ([Q-43](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-43); [Beckn signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#signing)). The gateway keeps them as `bpp_signed_payment_terms` for every Reserve Pay leg ([Evidence bundle](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#contents)).
- **Requested block amount.** A Reserve Pay request carries `rail_limits.block_amount`, the block the principal is asked to set up. The gateway and the MM check it at step 2 of [Issuance](#issuance), the notice shows it, and the payer PSP creates no larger block. It **MUST NOT** exceed the handler's per-block limit in the [handler registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md); otherwise the request is refused at step 2 with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.rail_limits.block_amount`. If the attested `block_amount` is larger than the requested one, the MM refuses issuance at step 6 and revokes the block at the rail.
- **Every Reserve Pay request is checked against a root.** The per-block limit, the sum-of-blocks rule and the headroom check below apply to every Reserve Pay request, with or without `checkout_mandate_ref`. A request without it proposes a new root: the checks then use the request's own `proposed_constraints.budgets` as the root's budgets, the exposure that already counts against a new root of the same principal (unconfirmed blocks) as the root's exposure, and `$.rail_limits.block_amount` instead of `$.checkout_mandate_ref` as the error location.
- **Sum of blocks.** The `block_amount`s of all Reserve Pay mandates under one root, including the one requested (its requested amount at step 2, its attested amount at step 6), **MUST NOT** exceed the smallest `budgets[].max` of the root; and, with the requested block at its full amount, the root's exposure ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)) **MUST** fit every budget window that contains the activation. A request that breaks the first rule is refused with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.checkout_mandate_ref`, and one that breaks the second (no headroom) with `403 mandate_exhausted` at `$.checkout_mandate_ref`; the first rule is checked before the second. The gateway checks the headroom at step 2 and again, authoritatively, when it applies the activation inside the root's atomic section (step 7), so that an issuance never races a `complete` for the same headroom.
- **Block expiry within the root.** The attested expiry of a block **MUST NOT** be later than the root open Checkout Mandate's `valid_until`; otherwise the MM refuses issuance at step 6 and revokes the block.
- **One root per principal.** The parallel-root key is the principal's **account at the Mandate Manager**: the one account behind every pairwise `principal.ref` that the MM issues for that person, whichever agent or operator asked. The MM **MUST** refuse a new root open Checkout Mandate for a principal who already holds one or more `ACTIVE` roots at that MM, with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.checkout_mandate_ref` (use `checkout_mandate_ref` to add a seller to an existing root), unless the notice the principal approves for it states the budgets of every other `ACTIVE` root and the combined total of all of them. A root at another Mandate Manager is outside this rule: each open mandate belongs to one gateway (`agent.bap_id`), and a move to another gateway is a successor root ([Porting a mandate](#port)).
- **Unconfirmed blocks outlive their root.** A block whose rail revocation is still `unconfirmed` when its root ends counts as exposure against every new root of the same principal (by the key above) until the MM reports it `confirmed` or the block expires. A PSP that never confirms can therefore hold at most the block's amount for at most the block's validity (at most 90 days, [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md)). The Trusted Surface shows the principal the route to revoke the block in the UPI app (NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 16.10).
- **Set-up outside a checkout.** A principal may set up a block for a seller in advance, outside any checkout, through this request. The rule that a new block is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment ([Per-leg rule](#per-leg-rule), 3b) does not apply to such a set-up.

### Porting a mandate to another gateway

A principal who changes buyer app or gateway does not move an open mandate: the mandate is bound to one gateway (`agent.bap_id`), and a **successor root** replaces it.

- **Principal-initiated, on the Trusted Surface only.** The principal approves the successor on the Trusted Surface, on the same terms as any issuance ([Issuance](#issuance)). The successor carries `supersedes{mandate_id}`, and the MM revokes the superseded root, with its siblings and their blocks as in [Revocation](#revocation), before the successor becomes `ACTIVE`. A `MandateRequest` that an agent or a gateway submits with `supersedes` is refused with `403 trusted_surface_only`. A support operator or an assisted operator never ports a mandate for a principal.
- **No prompt and no cap.** A gateway **MUST NOT** prompt or induce a port, for example by lowering a limit, adding a friction or offering a reward for it. BACP sets no numeric cap on ports: the UPI AutoPay rule that a port can be done three times in a rolling 90-day period binds UPI members, not BACP (NPCI UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 14.24.4).
- **The carried spend.** The MM signs the spend that the principal has already made into the successor as `carried_exposure[]{period, window_start, amount, source}`, derived from its own `use` events ([Mandate events](#mandate-events)). The successor's windows start at that spend, so a port never restores budget. No statement of the gateway that is being left is needed, so that gateway cannot hold the principal back by staying silent. For a window in which the MM's record has a gap, `source` is `incomplete`: the Trusted Surface says so in the principal's language and pre-fills that window at the superseded root's `max`. The principal may change any pre-filled figure before approving, because the cap is the principal's own, and the change is accepted only with the principal's own factor. On revocation of the superseded root its gateway **MUST** send, within 60 seconds, a `MandateEvent` of type `closed` with `last_seq`. Until the Mandate Manager holds every event up to `last_seq`, every window that contains the time since the last event received is `incomplete`. A `use` of the superseded root that the Mandate Manager receives after it has signed the successor counts against the successor: the Mandate Manager sends the successor's gateway a signed carried-exposure increment, which that gateway applies inside the root's atomic section ([Q-104](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-104) records that the wire form of the increment is not yet defined). Until it is defined, the Mandate Manager does not sign the successor before it holds a `closed` event and every event up to its `last_seq`, or 60 seconds have passed without one. In that second case every window is `incomplete` and is pre-filled at `max`, so the carried exposure is treated as at the old `max`. A `use` that arrives after signing makes the Mandate Manager revoke the successor and ask the principal to port again.
- **Reserve Pay blocks.** A successor MAY re-bind a block of its predecessor when the payer PSP signs a fresh attestation for the same block. A re-bound block is not revoked with the predecessor, its exposure moves to the successor inside the root's atomic section, and it never counts on both roots. Where the payer PSP does not re-attest, the old block is revoked and a new one is created, which asks the principal for the UPI PIN once for each seller, and both blocks count as exposure while a revocation is `unconfirmed`. Whether payer PSPs re-attest is open with NPCI.
- **Revocation parity.** No BACP route to revoke or move a mandate needs more steps or factors than the rail's own withdrawal ([Revocation](#revocation)).

### Purpose bounds

`purpose.code` comes from a purpose-code registry. Each purpose carries bounds that the gateway or MM enforces at `POST /mandates`. The table below is the normative purpose-code registry of BACP `2026-10-18`. The BACP working group governs it: a new code or a changed bound is a normative change and ships only in a dated release, and lowering a bound or removing a code is a breaking change (settled in [Q-47](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-47)). A `purpose_code` that is not in the table **MUST** be refused with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`. Amounts are in rupees (₹).

| Purpose    | Text                            | Per txn     | P1D         | P7D         | P1M         | FIRST_24H   | LIFETIME     | Categories                               | Max validity | Data scopes                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `P-GRO-01` | Household grocery replenishment | 20,000      | 20,000      | 25,000      | 25,000      | 20,000      | 1,00,000     | `ONDC:RET10`                             | 90 days      | NAME, PHONE, DELIVERY_ADDRESS, EMAIL        |
| `P-FAS-01` | Clothing and handloom           | 50,000      | 50,000      | 50,000      | 1,00,000    | 50,000      | 5,00,000     | `ONDC:RET12`                             | 90 days      | NAME, PHONE, DELIVERY_ADDRESS, EMAIL        |
| `P-PRC-01` | Business and public procurement | 1,00,00,000 | 1,00,00,000 | 2,00,00,000 | 5,00,00,000 | 1,00,00,000 | 50,00,00,000 | `ONDC:RET10`, `ONDC:RET12`, `ONDC:RET14` | 180 days     | NAME, PHONE, DELIVERY_ADDRESS, EMAIL, GSTIN |

Rail limits apply on top of purpose bounds. A Circle binding caps `amount_per_txn` at ₹5,000 and P1M at ₹15,000. An AutoPay binding caps `amount_per_txn` at the ₹15,000 AFA limit. See [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md).

## Constraints

`constraints` is a closed object. Every key below is a **known constraint key**. Amounts are `Amount` objects in integer paise. All checks run in the gateway against the BPP-signed quote, never against agent claims.

| Key                       | Type                                                        | Semantics                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Failure                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `amount_per_txn`          | Amount                                                      | The payable amount of one order **MUST NOT** exceed it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`                                                                                                                     |
| `budgets[]`               | `{period, max}`                                             | Exposure in the window plus this amount **MUST NOT** exceed `max` ([Budgets](#budgets)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `403 mandate_exhausted`                                                                                                                          |
| `max_executions`          | integer ≥ 1                                                 | Settled plus in-flight payments under the mandate **MUST** stay below it. When settled payments reach it, the mandate becomes `EXHAUSTED`.                                                                                                                                                                          | `403 mandate_exhausted`                                                                                                                          |
| `categories_allow`        | string[]                                                    | ONDC domain or category codes (e.g. `ONDC:RET10`, `RET10-Staples`). Every category in the order **MUST** be listed, unless `step_up.outside_categories` is `true`; then an order outside the list escalates instead of failing.                                                                                     | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`, or step-up                                                                                                         |
| `categories_deny`         | string[]                                                    | No category in the order may be listed. Deny wins over allow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`                                                                                                                     |
| `merchants_allow[]`       | `{bpp_id, provider_id?}`                                    | The seller's `bpp_id` **MUST** match an entry, and so must its `provider_id` when the entry names one.                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`                                                                                                                     |
| `delivery_pincodes`       | string[] (6-digit PIN code)                                 | The fulfilment PIN code **MUST** be listed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`                                                                                                                     |
| `line_items[]`            | `{item_id, qty_max}`                                        | Every ordered item **MUST** be listed, with quantity ≤ `qty_max`. This bounds basket changes injected through catalogue text.                                                                                                                                                                                       | `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`                                                                                                                     |
| `step_up`                 | object                                                      | Thresholds that force a human confirmation ([Step-up](#step-up)). Its keys are `above_amount`, `new_merchant`, `outside_categories` and `first_order`.                                                                                                                                                              | step-up                                                                                                                                          |
| `reject_preticked_addons` | `true`                                                      | The gateway declines every pre-ticked add-on the seller offers and re-quotes without it, reporting `preticked_addon_removed`.                                                                                                                                                                                       | message                                                                                                                                          |
| `cod_allowed`             | boolean                                                     | Cash-on-delivery orders are allowed HNP only when `true`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `403 cod_not_allowed`                                                                                                                            |
| `cod_max_open_orders`     | integer ≥ 0                                                 | Maximum open COD orders the agent may hold HNP. Where a negotiation mandate also sets a cap, the stricter wins.                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `403 cod_open_orders_cap`                                                                                                                        |
| `credit_funding_allowed`  | boolean                                                     | A credit-funded handler (BNPL, cardless EMI, a credit line) is refused unless this is `true`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `403 credit_funding_not_allowed`                                                                                                                 |
| `convenience_fees`        | `{allowed, max_per_order?}`                                 | In a human-not-present checkout, the agent may pay a convenience fee only when `allowed` is `true` and the total of the order's `convenience` and `other_charge` lines that apply to the handler being paid is at or below `max_per_order` (when it is set). With `allowed: false`, `max_per_order` MUST be absent. | `confirm` step-up, reason `constraint_unresolved`, before any money moves                                                                        |
| `confirmation_floor`      | `{min_user_action?, channels_allow?}` (at least one member) | The principal's standing floor on how an approval is given on the Trusted Surface ([Confirmation floor](#confirmation-floor)).                                                                                                                                                                                      | `403 presence_not_proven` at `$.presentation.user_action` or `$.presentation.channel`; `503 trusted_surface_unavailable` (`channel_not_allowed`) |

COD and credit funding are described in [Credit and Split Tender](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/index.md).

**Convenience fees in a human-not-present checkout.** NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 asks the Payee PSP to disclose a convenience fee "upfront to the User on the merchant payment page(s) prior to the selection of the payment mode". When the agent selects the mode and no human sees a payment page, the mandate is where the principal's consent to such a fee is recorded. In HNP, if the order has a `convenience_fee` line (a `convenience` charge) or an `other_charge` line that `convenience_fees` does not cover, because the field is absent, `allowed` is `false` or the total of those lines is above `max_per_order`, the gateway raises a `confirm` step-up with reason `constraint_unresolved` and moves no money. This is a mandate constraint, so a verifier that does not know the key fails closed ([Fail-closed handling](#unknown-constraints)). Whether disclosure through the Trusted Surface meets para 7.5 is open ([Q-78](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-78)). The check runs at `complete` against the handler actually debited, including after a `rail_fallback`. The existing split-order trigger applies when an order is split to stay under `max_per_order`.

### Confirmation floor

`confirmation_floor` records how the principal wants approvals to be given, as one object with two optional members and at least one present. It is a constraint, because only `constraints` fails closed: a gateway that does not know it refuses the mandate ([Fail-closed handling](#unknown-constraints)), so a principal who sets a floor cannot use a gateway that has not upgraded.

- `min_user_action` is the weakest `user_action` that the principal accepts. The ladder is `tap_confirm`, then `voice_confirm_plus_device`, then `upi_pin`, `biometric` and `passkey`, which are equal. Voice never releases money ([Voice confirmation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#voice)), so the ladder bites on non-money `confirm` and `post_order` approvals.
- `channels_allow` lists the channels on which the principal accepts an approval (at least one, no repeats). A request such as "always call me, never a tap" can be read aloud in the principal's language.
- **Set only by the principal.** The floor is set or changed only by the principal on the Trusted Surface at issuance, never through `MandateRequest` (a request that carries it is refused), so that an agent, including a grandson's agent acting for a grandmother, cannot lower it. The activation notice reads it in full in the principal's language.
- **Absent means any.** A mandate without it accepts any user action on any channel, so that a feature-phone principal on IVR keeps working.
- **Enforcement.** The gateway refuses an approval below the floor, or outside the channels, with `403 presence_not_proven` at `$.presentation.user_action` or `$.presentation.channel`, and it never offers a `delivery` outside the channels. If the only allowed channel is unavailable it answers `503 trusted_surface_unavailable` with `reason: channel_not_allowed` and the session's handoff routes.
- It is the principal's standing preference, which [TS-3](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements) alone does not record. It is not a security closure.

### Budgets

Each `budgets[]` entry names a `period` and a `max`. A mandate MAY carry several, and every one applies.

| Period      | Window at evaluation time *t*                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `P1D`       | Rolling: payments at times in (*t* − 24 h, *t*\].                                                                 |
| `P7D`       | Rolling: payments at times in (*t* − 7 days, *t*\].                                                               |
| `P1M`       | The **calendar month in IST** (Asia/Kolkata) that contains *t*. It resets at 00:00 IST on the first of the month. |
| `FIRST_24H` | \[`valid_from`, `valid_from` + 24 h). After this window the budget no longer applies.                             |
| `LIFETIME`  | Every payment over the life of the mandate.                                                                       |

Rail-side "per month" caps, such as the Circle monthly cap and the AFA period, are also evaluated per calendar month in IST.

The check is `exposure(window) + amount ≤ max`, where **exposure** is settled spend plus in-flight reservations in that window ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)). A breach returns `403 mandate_exhausted` with `resolution: requires_buyer_input` and moves no money.

### Fail-closed handling of unknown constraints

The set of constraint keys in the table above, and the set of `step_up` keys, is closed.

- A gateway, MM or verifier that meets a constraint key or `step_up` key it does not know **MUST** refuse the mandate with `403 constraint_unknown` (`unrecoverable`). It **MUST NOT** ignore the key, and **MUST NOT** evaluate the remaining keys and proceed.
- This applies at `POST /mandates` (to `proposed_constraints`) and at every evaluation.
- This is the one exception to BACP's rule that readers ignore unknown fields. New constraint types arrive as new mandate types (as the negotiation mandate does), never as new keys that an older verifier would skip.
- Any other malformed mandate fails closed: `400 mandate_schema_invalid` for a schema failure, `403 mandate_invalid` for unparseable or inconsistent content.

## Presence (HP and HNP)

`presence` is `HP` (human present) or `HNP` (human not present). It is declared on every session and every post-order write, and travels on the network in `context.bacp.presence`.

- The presence of a request **MUST** be in the open mandate's `presence_allowed`. Otherwise the gateway returns `403 presence_not_allowed` (`requires_buyer_review`).
- **HNP.** The agent closes the open mandates itself with its `cnf` key ([Closing](#closing)). The closed Payment Mandate's `auth_binding.type` is `parent_rail_binding`: the debit runs under the open mandate's rail binding. Only class-O handlers may back an HNP payment ([Handler binding](#handler-binding)).
- **HP.** The principal signs the closed mandates on the Trusted Surface and authorises the payment with a fresh per-transaction factor (`auth_binding.type` is `upi.pin`, `upi.biometric`, `card.3ds` or `instrument`). A one-off UPI payment authorised by PIN is identified as handler `in.upi.intent` with `auth_binding.type: upi.pin`. An HP payment does not draw on the open mandate's rail binding.
- An HP step-up payment counts toward `usage.count` but not toward the open mandate's budgets.
- **The basis of a debit that takes no new factor.** A closed Payment Mandate that executes under the parent's rail binding (HNP) carries, in the record that the gateway stores, `auth_binding.afa_ref{handler, primitive, registry_version}`: a reference to the registry descriptor at that version, not a copy. Only the gateway sets it, and an agent that supplies it gets `400 invalid_request`. The principal's post-debit notice and the [evidence summary](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#evidence-summary) render the basis from the descriptor through a fixed template, so that support staff need no registry lookup. For the `hi-IN` notice of a recurring AutoPay debit the sentence is "यह पैसा उस ऑटो-पे से कटा है जिसे आपने पहले मंज़ूरी दी थी, इसलिए PIN नहीं माँगा गया।", which says in English "This debit is under the AutoPay you approved earlier, so no PIN was asked." The basis records which rule the debit relies on. It does not make the debit lawful: the issuer remains liable under RBI/2025-26/79 para 9(b) for a non-compliant debit. The descriptor's `afa.rbi_annex1_item` names the Annexure-1 row where the handler relies on an RBI exemption, and a handler that relies on authentication at block creation or registration (Reserve Pay, OTM, UPI Circle) has none: it is never presented as an RBI exemption ([Handler registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md)). UPI Circle is not open-eligible while [Q-77](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-77) is open, so no HNP debit runs through it.
- **Voice never releases money.** The gateway refuses `voice_confirm_plus_device` on a `rail_auth` step-up and on any `confirm` step-up whose approval releases a debit, with `403 presence_not_proven` at `$.presentation.user_action` ([Voice confirmation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#voice)).
- Accepting a credit offer (a loan, BNPL) is always HP. An agent attempt returns `403 credit_acceptance_requires_hp`.
- Returns, and accepting or rejecting an IGM resolution, are HP ([Post-order gate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#post-order-gate)).
- **HP is proven, not declared.** Every post-order write with `presence: HP` (cancel, return, raise issue, issue action, and an agent's trade act: GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection, ledger acknowledgement) **MUST** carry `hp_proof{ts_event_hash, step_up_id}`, both REQUIRED: the id of a step-up of kind `post_order` whose gateway-signed `ts_render` names this write (`action`, `order_id` and, for an issue action, `issue_id` and, for `RESOLUTION_ACCEPTED` or `RESOLUTION_REJECTED`, the `subject_hash` of the resolution shown), and the sha-256 over the JCS form of the signed `step_up.approved` event that the gateway received for it at `/trusted-surface/events`. A write without `hp_proof` gets `403 presence_not_proven` (`requires_buyer_review`) carrying `step_up` (kind `post_order`, reason `presence_proof`) for the principal to confirm, the same pending step-up on a repeat; a proof issued for another action, order or issue, or for an issue whose `resolution` has changed since, gets the same code. A proof is single-use: the gateway consumes it inside the atomic section keyed on the order's root Checkout Mandate ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)). Nothing is sent to the network until the proof passes ([Presence proof](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#hp-proof)). An HP `complete` is proven by the principal's signatures on the closed mandates and needs no `hp_proof`.

## Closing an open mandate

To pay HNP, the agent turns the open Checkout and Payment Mandates into closed ones bound to the exact quote that the gateway returned in `ready_for_complete`.

The agent **MUST** produce:

| Field                  | Closed Checkout Mandate                | Closed Payment Mandate                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vct`                  | `in.bacp.mandate.checkout.1`           | `in.bacp.mandate.payment.1`                                   |
| `parent_mandate_id`    | the open Checkout Mandate              | the open Payment Mandate                                      |
| `checkout_hash`        | `session.quote.checkout_hash`          | the same                                                      |
| `amount`               | exactly the quote total                | the same                                                      |
| `checkout_mandate_ref` | n/a                                    | the closed Checkout Mandate's `mandate_id`                    |
| `payee`                | n/a                                    | the collecting party's VPA                                    |
| `auth_binding`         | n/a                                    | `{type: parent_rail_binding, handler, ref: rail_ref, psp_id}` |
| Validity               | within the parent's, typically minutes | the same                                                      |

**Key binding.** Each closed mandate **MUST** carry an inner signature with `role: agent` made by the open mandate's `cnf` key. It **MUST** be sent as an attached compact JWS whose payload is the mandate JSON (including that inner signature) and whose header `kid` is the `cnf` key id. The same key signs the agent's RFC 9421 requests, so a mandate closed under one agent's key cannot be presented by another ([Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/index.md)). An HP closed mandate is instead signed, inside and outside, by the principal key that signed the parent.

The agent **MAY** also send a key-binding JWT (`kb_jwt`) on `complete`. If present it **MUST** be signed by the `cnf` key with `aud` set to the seller's `bpp_id` and `nonce` set to the Beckn `message_id` of the `confirm` that the gateway will send. The gateway derives that `message_id` as `UUIDv5(message_id_namespace, agent_id | idempotency_key | "confirm")` and publishes `message_id_namespace` in `/.well-known/bacp`. The gateway forwards the `kb_jwt` to the BPP in `context.bacp.mandate_ref.kb_jwt`.

Encoding

The attached-JWS closing above is the only interoperable encoding of a closed mandate in BACP `2026-10-18`, and the conformance suite will carry test vectors for it. An SD-JWT / KB-JWT selective-disclosure encoding is not part of this version; a later release may add one as a new mandate `vct` (settled in [Q-41](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-41)). Verifiers **MUST** support both ES256 and EdDSA (Ed25519) signatures (settled in [Q-42](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-42); see [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#signature-algorithms)).

A closed Payment Mandate is single use. The gateway and the PSP adapter **MUST** allow at most one debit per closed Payment Mandate `mandate_id` and at most one per `checkout_hash`, except that under a payment plan each tender has its own closed Payment Mandate and is debited at most once, and the debits of all the tenders of one live plan together never exceed `all_in_total`. Presenting a used one returns `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`. A closed Payment Mandate that carries `tender` is for one tender of one plan and **MUST NOT** pay a `complete` that has no `payment_plan`.

## Handler binding of open mandates

An open Payment Mandate's `rail_binding.type` names the payment handler that backs it, and `rail_binding.primitive` names the mandate primitive of that handler that carries the standing authority (one of its `mandate_primitives[].type`). Handlers are grouped into binding classes in the [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).

- `rail_binding.type` **MUST** validate against the class-O id pattern (`RailTypeV1`) or a legacy alias of one. Ids of class C, A, D or N handlers fail schema validation and are refused.
- **Rail- or issuer-enforced primitives only.** An open Payment Mandate **MAY** bind to any class-O handler, but only through a mandate primitive whose limits the rail or the issuer enforces (`limits_enforced_by` is `rail` or `issuer`). The descriptor lists those primitives in `binding.open_primitives`. `rail_binding.primitive` **MUST** be one of them, and the PSP attestation **MUST** cover it. For example, `in.ppi.wallet` lists only `ppi_emandate`, so a wallet balance (`balance_cap`) never backs an open mandate.
- **Funding.** The PSP attestation states `funding` as `deposit` or `credit`. A savings or current account is deposit; a RuPay credit card or a pre-sanctioned credit line is credit; an overdraft account is credit unless the PSP attests deposit; and a missing `funding` is treated as credit. An attested `credit` without `credit_funding_allowed: true` on the root gets `403 credit_funding_not_allowed` at issuance, where the MM sends `mandate.rejected` with `rail_revocation`, and at `complete` on an existing mandate. A block that is refused after the rail call counts as exposure until its revocation is confirmed ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)).
- **Gift PPI custody.** `in.ppi.gift` is open-eligible only when the PSP attestation states `custody: principal_side`, that is, that the vault of the gift code is on the principal's side (the Trusted Surface or the payer PSP). With `custody: gateway_side`, or none, the MM refuses issuance with `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`, because the agent's side would hold the code. A gift PPI then remains usable human-present.
- Schema validity is not eligibility. After alias resolution the handler's descriptor **MUST** have `open_eligible: true`, **MUST** list `rail_binding.primitive` in `binding.open_primitives`, and **MUST** have `status: live`, or `status: pilot` only where the gateway's [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation) lists that pilot in `pilots[]` and has not expired. A `reserved` or `deprecated` descriptor (for example the reserved `in.upi.uap.*`) **MUST NOT** back a mandate. A binding that fails any of these checks gets `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`.
- **Checked at issuance.** The MM **MUST** refuse to issue an open Payment Mandate whose binding fails these checks, and **MUST** verify the gateway's conformance attestation before it issues one on a `pilot` handler ([Issuance](#issuance), step 6). While the [conformance-authority list](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-authority-list) has no entry, no attestation verifies, so an MM refuses open mandates on every `pilot` handler, including `in.upi.circle` and `in.card.agentic`.
- **Registry source.** The MM and the gateway **MUST** take the registry from the dated BACP release (its `source/handlers/registry.json`), and **MUST NOT** take it from a gateway endpoint such as `GET /payment-handlers`, which is unsigned ([Discovery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/index.md)). There is no registry-signed snapshot, because no party holds a registry signing key. Each publication of the registry files, including a backport that amends a dated release in place, is described by the release manifest `source/handlers/release.json` ([`registry-release.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/registry-release.json)): `registry_version`, a strictly increasing `registry_serial` (at least 1), `published_at` (IST, `+05:30`) and `files[]` with the `sha-256` digest of each file over its JCS form. A reader that wants to prove which copy it used compares that digest. The MM records the version it checked against in `rail_binding.registry_version`, and MAY also record `rail_binding.registry_serial` and `rail_binding.registry_digest`.
- **The attestation is bound into the mandate.** On a pilot handler the open Payment Mandate carries `rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti}`: the conformance authority, the gateway and the attestation's `jti`. The schema leaves it optional, and a conformance rule makes it REQUIRED for every pilot binding ([Conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules)). At `complete` the gateway refuses the mandate when it is absent or its `sub` is not the gateway itself, and re-checks the gateway's current attestation (the bound `jti`, or after a lift the newer attestation that lifted the pause).
- **Re-checked at every `complete`.** Eligibility (status, attestation and primitive) is not fixed at issuance. The gateway **MUST** re-check it at step 1 of [Deterministic evaluation](#evaluation) on every `complete`, against the current registry, never against a copy taken when the mandate was issued.
- **24-hour freshness.** A gateway **MUST** adopt a status downgrade within 24 hours of the `published_at` of the publication that makes it. It **MUST** refuse an HNP `complete` on a handler whose descriptor copy it last refreshed from the registry source more than 24 hours earlier, or whose copy carries a lower `registry_serial` than a publication whose `published_at` is more than 24 hours past, with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`, `reasons: [registry_copy_stale]` and `resolution: recoverable`. A stale copy is a gateway condition, not a fault of the binding: the gateway does not pause the mandate, the agent retries later without involving the principal, and an HP `complete` is not refused for staleness.
- **A downgrade pauses the mandate.** When a registry change, or a change to the gateway's conformance attestation, makes the binding of a mandate ineligible (for example a handler moved from `live` to `pilot` without an attested pilot, or to `reserved` or `deprecated`), the gateway **MUST** add the pause reason `binding_ineligible` to every affected mandate, recording the `registry_version` and `registry_serial` of the publication that made the binding ineligible. If the mandate was `ACTIVE`, it becomes `PAUSED` and the gateway sends `mandate.status_changed` (`PAUSED`, `reason: binding_ineligible`, with `pause_reasons` and `affected_sessions`) to the agent and cancels every open session under the mandate with the message `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`. Every later `complete` under it gets `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` with `reasons: [binding_ineligible]` while the binding stays ineligible.
- **A lapsed attestation pauses the mandate.** When the bound attestation is revoked, or its `exp` passes, or its authority's entry is removed, lapsed or revoked, or its key is removed from the entry, at a re-check, the gateway adds `binding_ineligible` with the cause `attestation`, and writes the attestation's `jti` into the InstructionLog entry for the addition. A status list that is stale or unreachable is not a revocation: the `complete` gets `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` with `reasons: [attestation_status_stale]` and `resolution: recoverable`, and the mandate is not paused ([Conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules)). A debit under an open Payment Mandate on a pilot handler is not authorised by the mandate if, when the gateway sent it, the bound attestation was revoked or expired, its entry was not on the list, or the gateway was not `rail_binding.conformance.sub`. A verifier reports such a debit as outside the mandate from the InstructionLog `payment` entry of the debit, the list version and the status list. A Mandate Manager that finds the bound attestation revoked or expired tells the principal on the Trusted Surface and offers revocation.
- **A binding pause gates new `complete` only.** It never blocks a status check, a reversal, or a refund to the original source of a debit whose `rrn` or `utr` is already in the ledger; these MUST proceed. A refund to any other destination MUST be refused (`credits_to_other_party: 0`). Cancel, return and issue on orders already placed under the mandate stay allowed with `presence: HP` ([Post-order gate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#post-order-gate)).
- **Pause reasons form a set.** A paused mandate carries the set of reasons for which it is paused: `principal_paused` (a pause by the principal on the Trusted Surface), `binding_ineligible`, `reissue_required` (below), `unmatched_rail_debit` (a debit on a Reserve Pay block that matches no BACP payment) and `block_modified` (a reported increase of a block that breaks the sum of blocks or the root's headroom), the last two in the [Usage ledger](#usage-ledger). The mandate stays `PAUSED` while any reason remains. A principal pause that arrives while a binding pause is in force is added to the set, never dropped, and a binding pause that arrives while the principal has paused the mandate is added in the same way. Only the principal, on the Trusted Surface, removes `principal_paused`, `unmatched_rail_debit` and `block_modified`. The gateway removes only `binding_ineligible`, and only on a `registry_serial` strictly greater than the one recorded for the pause, at which the binding is eligible again (a later publication of the same `registry_version`, such as a backport, has a greater serial and lifts the pause) or, for a pause caused by the gateway's conformance attestation, a newer attestation from the same authority (`iss` equal to `rail_binding.conformance.iss`), whose `sub` is the gateway itself, that lists the bound handler and passes every check in [At `complete`](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#attestation-rules); an attestation from another authority does not lift the pause, and the principal's Mandate Manager issues a new mandate instead, under every issuance rule. A replica that still holds the recorded or a lower serial **MUST NOT** remove it. When the last reason is removed the mandate returns to `ACTIVE` and the gateway sends `mandate.status_changed` (`ACTIVE`) to the agent; a change to the set of a mandate that stays `PAUSED` is sent as `mandate.status_changed` (`PAUSED`) with the new `pause_reasons`. While a binding reason is in the set, `complete` gets `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` at step 1 of [evaluation](#evaluation); when only `principal_paused`, `unmatched_rail_debit` or `block_modified` remain, it gets `403 mandate_paused`.
- **The gateway tells the Mandate Manager.** Every use of the mandate, every relinquishment at the gateway and every addition or removal of a gateway-originated pause reason (`binding_ineligible`, `reissue_required`) is reported as a [`MandateEvent`](#mandate-events) to the mandate's `audit_uri`, so that the Trusted Surface can show the principal why the agent cannot pay and can offer re-issue ([Q-61](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-61), settled). The Mandate Manager derives two causes itself: a change of registry status (it reads the same registry) and a pause that follows its own issuance record. It learns the others only from the event: an attestation swap (a binding pause caused by the gateway's own attestation) and `unmatched_rail_debit`, which also needs a block-debit feed ([Q-10](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-10)). For a pilot binding the MM **MUST** read the attestation's status list itself and does not rely on the gateway's report. The gateway **MUST** also record every addition and removal of `binding_ineligible` or `reissue_required` as an InstructionLog entry at stage `mandate` (actor `gateway`) whose content carries the reason, the `registry_version`, the `registry_serial`, the `registry_digest` of the registry file checked and, for a lapsed attestation, its `jti`, in the chain of every session the change cancels, and otherwise in the `mandate` entry of the next session opened under the mandate ([Evidence](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/evidence/#stages)).
- **Reasons are ordered.** When several apply, `reasons[]` of a `rail_binding_not_open_eligible` error lists them with `reissue_required` first, then `binding_ineligible`, then `registry_copy_stale`, then `attestation_status_stale`, and the `resolution` is that of the first.
- **The agent cross-checks the claim.** The agent checks `reissue_required` and `binding_ineligible` against the mandate that it holds. A mandate that carries `rail_binding.primitive` and `rail_binding.registry_version` is not one that needs a re-issue, so a gateway's `reissue_required` for it is a claim that the agent can disprove. A claim that the agent can disprove is a gateway fault: the agent sends no `POST /mandates`, records `gateway_fault` as the reason in the `mandate` entry of its InstructionLog and tells the principal that the gateway refused the payment. The same holds for every other non-recoverable `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`: the agent never turns it into a re-issue or resume request without a new instruction from the principal.
- **The agent does not turn a binding pause into a request.** This binding pause is not a principal pause: the principal does not resume it. On `binding_ineligible` the agent **MUST NOT** open a Trusted-Surface resume request or a re-issue request (`POST /mandates`) unless the principal gives a new instruction. It **MAY** tell the principal that payments under the mandate are paused and offer another payment method or an HP checkout ([Revocation, pause and expiry](#revocation)).
- **Mandates issued before these rules are re-issued.** An open Payment Mandate issued without `rail_binding.primitive` or `rail_binding.registry_version` cannot be amended, because the principal and MM signatures cover its content. The gateway **MUST** pause it with the reason `reissue_required`, and every `complete` under it gets `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible` with `reasons: [reissue_required]` (not `mandate_schema_invalid`), so that the agent is told to have it re-issued. The gateway never removes `reissue_required`; the mandate **MUST** be re-issued through [Issuance](#issuance) with an eligible `primitive` and `registry_version`.
- BACP constraints **MUST** be at or below the descriptor's rail limits. The MM rejects a mandate that exceeds its binding. The rail is authoritative for its own limits, but **MUST NOT** be relied on to enforce BACP budgets ([Usage ledger](#usage-ledger)).
- A Reserve Pay block is payable to one seller. Its open Payment Mandate **MUST** name the block's payee seller in `payee{vpa, bpp_id}`, and `payee.vpa` **MUST** equal the VPA in that seller's BPP-signed payment terms. A block whose payee is the buyer app (a BAP-collected block) **MUST NOT** back an HNP payment: the MM refuses it, and the gateway refuses such a binding, with `400 rail_binding_not_open_eligible`. So is a block whose seller's BPP-signed payment terms the gateway does not hold and cannot obtain ([Sibling Payment Mandates](#sibling-payment-mandates)).

Settled

Binding open mandates to class-O handlers through rail- or issuer-enforced primitives is settled in `2026-10-18` ([design choice (a)](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#proposed-a)). Agentic card tokens stay pilot-gated ([Q-39](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-39)), and `in.erupi` is `pilot` until [Q-38](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-38) is answered.

Settled

`in.store_credit` and `in.loyalty` (limits enforced by the merchant) and `bacp.credit_ledger` (limits enforced by BACP) are class O but have `open_eligible: false` and `hnp: none`. Letting them back open mandates is closed in this release ([Q-59](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-59) and [Q-46](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-46), settled); the conditions for opening them later are Proposed text in Q-59.

### Per-leg payment rule for a multi-seller basket

In a [multi-seller basket](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket) each seller is one **leg** with its own session, closed mandates and debit. No payment ever spans sellers. For each leg the gateway plans the payment in this order, and takes the first that is eligible for that seller at that presence ([handler intersection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-intersection-and-preference)):

1. **The principal's preference.** The handler the principal designated, ranked by rule 1 of the handler intersection. No other rung ranks above it.
1. **The seller's existing payee-bound instrument (3a).** An `ACTIVE` sibling open Payment Mandate under the basket's root whose `payee` is this seller, for example a Reserve Pay block the principal already holds for it. A block backs a leg only if the leg's fresh BPP-signed `on_init` names the VPA that equals `payee.vpa`; otherwise the rung is skipped with `comparison[].reason: payee_terms_changed`. Held terms are usable only until the `expires` of their Beckn `Authorization`. A terms-only `init` that obtains terms carries no personal data of the principal beyond what the network requires (whether the network lets billing details be omitted is open with ONDC).
1. **A gift PPI the principal designated.** An `ACTIVE` sibling open Payment Mandate bound to `in.ppi.gift` under the root.
1. **One planned human-present step.** If any leg is left without an HNP handler, the gateway raises **one** step-up (`confirm`, reason `rail_fallback`) for the whole basket **before any debit** ([Step-up](#step-up)). Each human-present leg is then paid with its own closed mandates and its own per-payee factor.

Rules on the order:

- Any-merchant primitives that are `pilot` (`in.upi.circle`, `in.card.agentic`) back no open mandate until a listed [conformance authority](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-authority-list) attests the gateway for them (`in.upi.circle` also waits for [Q-77](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-77)), and a rung never ranks above the principal's preference. A seller that lacks only a block keeps its place and is offered the human-present step; it is not dropped from the basket.
- The gateway **MUST** record, for every leg, the rung chosen and every rung skipped with its reason, as `comparison[]` entries in the InstructionLog ([handler intersection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-intersection-and-preference)).
- **A new block in a checkout (3b).** A new per-seller block **MAY** be offered during a checkout only beside a one-time human-present payment to the same payee, with equal weight (the same number of steps, neither preselected; TS-2 in [Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements)). It **MUST NOT** be offered after a failed payment, and **MUST NOT** be offered on a step-up whose `delivery` is `ivr_callback`. A block set up outside a checkout is exempt ([Sibling Payment Mandates](#sibling-payment-mandates)).
- **Fallback is a step-up.** When a leg cannot be paid with the handler first planned for it (the principal's preference, or the rung the principal last approved), and the replacement changes the leg's funding class, [fee-bearer](#fee-bearer-change), payee or collector, the gateway raises a `rail_fallback` step-up and moves no money. The funding class is read from the **attested** funding and is one of `own_deposit` (deposit-funded: `debit`, and `cbdc`), `prepaid` (`prepaid` and `voucher`) and `borrowed` (`credit`, `loan` and `trade_credit`). Prepaid is a class of its own because the principal's recourse differs: a failed on-us PPI payment is reversed by T+1 and a failed UPI merchant payment by T+5 (RBI/2019-20/67, Annex rows 8(b) and 4(b)), a refund goes back to the PPI (PPI Master Direction para 14.3(a)), and the complaint goes to the issuer within 48 hours to 30 days (para 16.2(e)). The payee is compared by the VPA **and** by the pair `(bpp_id, provider_id)`, and the collector stays in the trigger, because a different payee or collector changes who the principal pays and who must refund, which no budget or rail cap shows. A change in a charge shown to the payer is already covered by the fee-bearer. A change of rail alone, with none of those changing, is logged in `comparison[]` with `reason: rail_only_change` and raises no step-up.
- **No re-route of an in-doubt leg.** A leg whose payment is `in_doubt` **MUST NOT** be re-routed to another handler, and no new debit is attempted for it, until reconciliation resolves it ([Failed payments](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#failed-payments-tat-and-auto-reversal)).

Settled

The per-leg rule settles [design choice (d)](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#proposed-d) in `2026-10-18`. Whether an agent-initiated draw on a Reserve Pay block counts as a customer action on the merchant's platform is open ([Q-65](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-65)).

### Fee-bearer change

The payer-borne lines that apply to a handler are the session's `totals[]` lines of type `convenience_fee` or `cod_fee` whose `applies_to_handlers` lists the handler or is absent, and every line of the session's `operator_charges[]`. A replacement **changes the leg's fee-bearer** when the payer-borne lines that apply to the replacement handler differ from those that apply to the planned handler in `code` (the line type), `amount` or `recipient`. A line with no handler scope applies to every handler, so on its own it never changes the fee-bearer. The merchant discount rate, the payment aggregator's commission, the finder fee and every other cost the seller bears are never in the comparison. The trigger therefore fires mainly on a fallback to or from COD, on a change of operator fee and on a quote that charges one debit mode more than another.

## Step-up

A step-up hands the decision back to the human. It is never only an error: the session moves to `requires_escalation`, carries a `step_up` object, and its `messages[]` includes `step_up_required` with `resolution: requires_buyer_review`. The exception is a `post_order` step-up, which has no session: it comes in `Error.step_up` of the `403 presence_not_proven` that asks for it, and its approval yields the `hp_proof` for one write ([Presence](#presence)).

There are three kinds.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `confirm`    | The principal confirms this checkout on the Trusted Surface. split order. `new_merchant`: `step_up.new_merchant` is set and the seller has not been used under this mandate. `outside_categories`: `step_up.outside_categories` is set and a category is outside `categories_allow`. `first_order`: `step_up.first_order` is set and this is the first order under the mandate. `constraint_unresolved`: missing disclosures, drip pricing, a price that rose above the discovered price of an item shown with a `prior_price` (`discovery_price_changed`), a convenience fee that the mandate's [`convenience_fees`](#constraints) does not cover in HNP, an operator charge that the mandate's `operator_compensation` does not cover, the HNP `payment_mode_fee_inconsistent` warning ([Fees on the payer's `on_select` or `on_init` carries the `bacp` tag `seller_confirmation`, so the seller's request for the buyer's own confirmation reaches the principal as a template sentence ([Seller refusals and
