**Question.** Should gateway-signed webhooks carry a dedicated RFC 9421 signature tag, `bacp-webhook`, listed in the gateway's profile, so that a webhook signature can never be confused with any other signed message?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** Proposed: the tag is `bacp-webhook`. Fail-safe default until it is settled: an agent MUST verify every webhook against a key in the gateway profile's `keys` and MUST NOT act on a webhook that fails verification; it MUST NOT reject a webhook only because its signature has no `tag` or an unknown one. See [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#signature-tags) and [REST](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/index.md).

**Upstream issue UCP #659 (as of 18-10-2026).** BACP's webhook signature already covers `webhook-id` and `webhook-timestamp` ([REST](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/#webhooks)), so the header-coverage point of that issue (closed upstream on 31-07-2026) is met. Only the dedicated tag stays open.

### Q-62 Certification of assisted operators

**Question.** Who certifies the human assisted operators (village-level entrepreneurs at Common Service Centres, bank business correspondents, buyer-app agents) who complete sessions for principals on `channel: assisted`, and what identifier does that body issue, so that `Participant.ref` of an `assisted_operator` can be checked?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Working position.** An `assisted_operator` entry is REQUIRED on every assisted session and every Trusted Surface approval names it (`Presentation.assisted_by`), but its `ref` is asserted by the agent operator and not verified against a registry. The principal approves with the principal's own factor, never the operator's tap (BACP policy). Since 18-10-2026 the `ref` is namespaced `scheme:id` (`csc_vle`, `bank_bc`, `ondc_np_agent` or `other`) and the gateway sets `Participant.ref_verification`, which is `asserted` until a registry exists that the gateway can name and which an agent can never set to `verified`. `assisted_by` and `Participant.ref` are attribution, never authentication, and the Trusted Surface announces the operator before the factor without reading "unverified" aloud. See [Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#assisted).

### Q-63 Third-party render input on PSP surfaces

**Question.** Do NPCI's rules for PSP apps allow a payer PSP's app or IVR to render a step-up from a third-party, gateway-signed `ts_render`? Can an IVR or UPI 123PAY flow carry a confirm-only callback, and in which languages?\
**Owner.** NPCI, through a member bank.

**Working position.** The Trusted Surface renders only from `ts_render` and its own templates (TS-1). `StepUp.delivery: ivr_callback` is **Proposed** until this question is answered; a gateway offers it only where its PSP confirms the flow. The question also asks whether a UPI 123PAY or IVR flow can read and capture a challenge that the Trusted Surface draws (the [voice challenge](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#voice)), whether a PSP may publish the numbers it calls from (`ts_call_numbers[]`), and whether PSP apps already refuse to render or debit a link whose payer is not the logged-in VPA (which would make `payer_ref` a restatement). If the challenge cannot be captured, voice approvals are unavailable and feature-phone principals lose voice for non-money confirmations, while money is unaffected because voice never releases it. See [Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-render).

### Q-65 Agent-initiated draw on a Reserve Pay block

**Question.** NPCI UPI OC 228 describes a Reserve Pay debit as one "initiated by the customer action on merchant's platform", and the UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0, para 16.6, as one "initiated by the User action on Merchant's platform". Does a debit that an AI agent triggers for the principal, under a mandate, count as such a customer action?\
**Owner.** NPCI, with Legal counsel.

**Working position.** None of the rules depend on the answer. BACP counts every block as reserved spend at its full amount and binds it to one payee seller ([Usage ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#usage-ledger), [Per-leg rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule)) whichever way it is answered. A gateway uses an existing block for an HNP leg only under these rules. See [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md).

### Q-66 E-commerce entity status for sponsored listings and prior prices

**Question.** The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 789(E), 09-09-2026, in force from 01-01-2027) require sponsored listings to be "distinctly identified" (r.4(12)) and define a prior price as "the lowest price of a good or service thirty days prior to the announcement of price reduction" (r.4(13)). Rule 4(12) binds "every e-commerce entity", and r.4(13) binds "an e-commerce entity or the seller" that announces a reduction. Open points for counsel:

- Is an agent operator, or a BACP gateway, an "e-commerce entity" (2020 Rules r.3(1)(b): a person who "owns, operates or manages digital or electronic facility or platform")?
- Does r.4(12) attach in a human-not-present flow, where no human sees the list?
- Is a price shown beside a maximum retail price, an MRP strike-through, or a coupon, bank offer or cart-level minimum-value offer, an "announcement of price reduction"?
- Whose lowest price counts under r.4(13): this platform's, all platforms' or offline prices too?
- Do r.4(12) and r.4(13) bind for-resale (B2B) purchases (section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 excludes a person who buys for resale or for any commercial purpose from "consumer"; whether that exclusion applies to r.4(12) and r.4(13) is a question for counsel, as of 18-10-2026)?
- Does a gateway that alters or computes a prior price become the party that announces the reduction?
- Is brand-funded placement of an item a "sponsored listing" when the seller did not pay?
- Is a sponsored slot that is not targeted, shown to a minor, "targeted advertising" under DPDP s.9(3)?

**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position.** BACP carries the data and applies the stricter reading wherever counsel's answer would otherwise matter. Every item carries a per-item `sponsorship`; a prior price is only ever the seller's `lowest_30d` figure with its announcement date; an MRP is never a "was" price; and no reduction, strike-through or percentage is shown for an item without a `prior_price`, whatever produced the reduction. B2B profiles are not exempt. BACP states that its fields carry the data an e-commerce entity needs, and does not state that they satisfy a duty. See [Catalogue disclosures](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures).

### Q-67 Ranking parameters that a party can buy

**Question.** Should each entry of `ranking.main_parameters` become an object that carries its relative importance and a flag for whether a party can raise it by payment (a `purchasable` attribute), so that a buyer can see which ranking parameters are paid for?\
**Owner.** BACP WG, with Legal counsel (r.5(3)(f) as substituted requires main parameters "in descending order" with an "easily and publicly available description").

**Working position.** `main_parameters` stays a list of strings in descending order of importance, with an optional `description_url`. A parameter that a party can buy is covered by the definition of "sponsored": an item whose position was affected by it is `sponsored`. A self-declared `purchasable` flag would be set by the party it is meant to constrain, and changing the type breaks every producer and consumer, so it is not in this version.

### Q-68 Reviewed translations of fixed legal labels

**Question.** Is there a reviewed translation route for fixed legal labels (the [disclosure phrases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#disclosure-phrases)) in the Eighth Schedule languages other than Hindi?\
**Owner.** MeitY/DPDP, through Bhashini.

**Working position.** `en-IN` and `hi-IN` are defined, and are draft wording until the human-experience review seat and the owner sign them off. For any other language, an operator uses its own fixed, reviewed translation of the same sentence, never a translation made at run time. The same route is needed for the Trusted Surface's fixed sentences that [Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements) adds: the TS-6 refusal, the assisted announcement, "a matching code does not make a link safe", "your bank never asks for your PIN on a call it makes", the no-PIN-basis notice and the `seller_confirmation` and re-prompt sentences. The disclosure phrases `capability_absent`, `added_not_by_you`, `cart_estimate`, `loyalty_provisional` and `policy_not_stated`, and the marketing-consent sentences of the Trusted Surface, are drafts and need the same review.

### Q-69 ONDC catalogue tags for sponsored listings and prior price

**Question.** Will ONDC publish catalogue tags for a sponsored listing and for a prior price (and any vocabulary for its basis), so that BACP can map to them instead of its own `bacp.disclosure` tags?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Working position.** BACP maps its fields to its own `bacp.disclosure` TagGroup ([Catalogue disclosure mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#disclosure-mapping)). When ONDC publishes tags, only that mapping changes; the BACP field names stay.

### Q-70 Registry access and cached catalogues for verifying discovery sources

**Question.** An agent that verifies a discovery source needs the seller's key from the network registry ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results)). Can an agent operator that is not itself an ONDC subscriber query the registry, or must it subscribe or use a lookup service? And what should a gateway do when it answers from a cached catalogue, which cannot meet the search binding, or from a Beckn 2.0 signed catalogue index, which this version does not cover?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** An agent that cannot verify a source renders every item of it with no reduction claim and no MRP anchor, and renders its sponsorship as `undeclared` (or `sponsored`, if the result says so). A cached answer is unverified for the same reason. BACP adds no weaker freshness binding. A gateway that wants verified claims sends a targeted live `search` to the shortlisted sellers with the agent's `message_id`.

### Q-71 Agent-side verification of the `on_init` quote

**Question.** An agent can verify a discovery source with the seller's signature. It cannot yet verify, at run time, the `on_init` quote that the gateway relays, for example that a seller's automatic discount was not removed by the gateway when the buyer app collects the payment. Should the agent be able to fetch the seller-signed `on_init` body, using the same pattern as the discovery source?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** The evidence bundle's `bpp_signed_quote` catches such a change on dispute, after the fact. The mandate bounds the amount in a human-not-present flow. No run-time check exists in this version. A residual remains: `applied[].automatic` is derived by the gateway from the breakup tag `offer/auto`, so a gateway that submits an affiliate offer and labels it `automatic: true` escapes the [discount rule 2](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts) check at run time. It is caught only from `bpp_signed_quote` on dispute.

### Q-73 Trusted Surface repeat of catalogue disclosures

**Question.** The Trusted Surface repeats sponsorship and prior-price sentences before the total ([Catalogue disclosure on the Trusted Surface](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-catalogue-disclosure)). Three points are open:

- Should the item names in the repeat reach a payer PSP on a `rail_auth` render, which then learns what was bought?
- Should a long basket aggregate `sponsored` sentences the way it aggregates `undeclared` ones? Aggregation is acceptable on audio only if the visual render keeps a line for each item, and a `prior_price` sentence is never aggregated.
- Should a Mandate Manager or payer PSP fetch and verify the seller-signed sources itself, instead of trusting the gateway's signature on the render?

**Owner.** BACP WG, with the human-experience review.

**Working position.** Names are included. Only `undeclared` sentences aggregate, and only above three entries. The Trusted Surface trusts the gateway's signature on the render, and the agent checks the repeat at run time; a rogue gateway that shares an operator with the agent is caught only on dispute. A long basket puts many sentences before the PIN, which the human-experience review is asked to weigh.

### Q-74 Provisional and instrument-linked discounts on plain sessions

**Question.** The UCP Discount extension has provisional discounts (those that depend on eligibility, such as a bank or card offer, a loyalty tier or a buyer assertion) and an `eligibility` claim on each. Should a plain checkout session carry them, so that a UCP or ACP producer maps without loss?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** No. A discount that depends on the payment instrument or on a buyer assertion stays in TermSheet `scheme` mode, which carries an eligibility proof. The schema rejects `provisional` and `eligibility` on a plain session, so a producer that sends them fails loudly instead of being half-mapped. See [Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts).

### Q-75 Zero-payable orders

**Question.** A discount of 100% of the order makes the payable amount zero. Should BACP carry a zero-payable order, with no debit, through a mandate?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** No. Mandate evaluation step 0 refuses a payable amount that is not greater than zero (`amount_not_positive`), so a fully discounted order is refused.

### Q-76 Gateway-funded and buyer-app-funded discounts

**Question.** Should a discount that the gateway or the buyer app funds, and that is not in the seller's signed quote, be carried?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** No. Such a discount would break the rule that the closed mandates carry the amount of the seller-signed quote total, and it would make the payable depend on the gateway. The gateway never adds or keeps a discount the seller did not sign.

### Q-77 Explicit user action on UPI Circle

**Question.** NPCI OC 201B (NPCI/UPI/OC-201B/2025-26, 08-10-2025) extends UPI Circle to IoT devices and software and states that "debit transactions using IoT shall be only initiated by explicit user action." May a UPI Circle delegation back a human-not-present debit under a standing open mandate that an agent executes without the principal present? Is that "explicit user action", and does "IoT" there cover software profiles such as an AI agent?\
**Owner.** NPCI, Legal counsel. Linked from [Q-60](#q-60).

**Working position (fail-safe default).** `in.upi.circle` backs no open mandate, even when a conformance authority whose scope includes it is listed and the gateway's attestation lists it, until an NPCI member bank and counsel answer. A Mandate Manager refuses an open mandate request on `in.upi.circle` with `rail_binding_not_open_eligible`, and a gateway refuses every human-not-present `complete` under an open mandate on it. The registry marks the handler `open_eligible: false` for this reason. A human-present payment through Circle is unaffected. See [UPI Circle](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/#upi-circle-delegate).

**Blocking for settlement.** This question is marked Blocking so that settling it, or any other change that lets `in.upi.circle` back an open mandate, needs the approvals that GOVERNANCE.md requires for the resolution of a Blocking question (two maintainers and steering group sign-off), and for the interim period the further approval that GOVERNANCE.md (c) requires. The fail-safe default above means that it does not block the release.

### Q-78 Where a convenience fee is disclosed when an agent selects the payment mode

**Question.** NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 asks the Payee PSP to disclose a convenience fee "upfront to the User on the merchant payment page(s) prior to the selection of the payment mode", and to keep it consistent across the available debit payment modes (net banking, debit card, UPI and credit card). When an agent selects the mode, is a Trusted Surface reading, or the mandate notice with a `convenience_fees` constraint, disclosure "to the User" before that selection? Does "credit card" sit inside "debit payment modes", are PPI wallets debit payment modes, and does para 7.5 reach `in.cod.upi`?\
**Owner.** NPCI, Legal counsel.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** The gateway warns with `payment_mode_fee_inconsistent` and never refuses. In human-present checkouts the Trusted Surface shows the fee before the factor. In HNP the warning raises a `confirm` step-up, and a convenience fee that the mandate's `convenience_fees` does not cover raises one too. A warning that proves a false positive is narrowed by data, and no money moves on it. See [Fees on the payer's screen](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fee-lines).

### Q-79 Operator fees and commissions

**Question.** Must an agent acting for a buyer disclose a commission that a seller pays it? Does NPCI FAQ Q17 ("UPI App providers shall NOT charge Platform Fee or any other charge") reach an agent operator that is a UPI application provider? Is a per-order operator fee a "bundled fee" under rule 5(7) of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (from 01-01-2027), and is a BACP gateway or agent operator an "e-commerce entity" or "marketplace e-commerce entity" (rule 3(1)(b), (g))? What is the GST treatment of an operator fee line, and which BACP party is the "operator" for CGST s.52 TCS and Income-tax Act s.194-O TDS? Does the operator refund an operator charge when an order is cancelled for the seller's fault?\
**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position.** No Indian rule was found that requires an operator to disclose a seller-paid commission (not verified as of 18-10-2026). BACP requires the declaration in the mandate notice as its own policy ([Operator compensation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#operator-compensation)), and the `operator_charges[]` line discloses a fee without licensing one.

### Q-80 ONDC recipient on the breakup

**Question.** Does the ONDC breakup carry a recipient for a charge line? Is `misc` the carrier for convenience fees, and is the `np_fees` channel margin payer-borne? Who bears the collector's P2M MDR when the buyer app collects (`collected_by: BAP`), and does RSF carry it as a deduction line? Does a P2PM seller keep zero MDR on orders that a network participant collects?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** BACP publishes its own `title_type` to `recipient` mapping ([Charge recipient mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#recipient-mapping)). An unmapped type is kept with `recipient: other` and a warning, never a refusal. The mapping changes when ONDC answers; the field names stay.

### Q-81 Retained payment charges, MDR on refunds and on UPI mandates

**Question.** May a disclosed non-refundable payment charge (`convenience`, `payment_handling`, `platform`) be kept, including on a return for a defective, deficient, spurious or late item, and how does the symmetry of rule 4(8) of the Rules apply? Does netting MDR off a refund breach rule 6(3) or 7(4)? Is MDR reversed on refunds and on TAT reversals? Do Reserve Pay and OTM count as "UPI Mandates" under NPCI FAQ Q22 (no prescribed MDR)? Is splitting a payment below ₹2,000 permitted, and is the pricing circular behind FAQ Q17 and Q34 binding?\
**Owner.** Legal counsel, NPCI.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** A refund below the amount paid must match the lines in `charges_retained[]`, or the gateway returns `refund_short_of_terms` without blocking the refund. No conformance case passes a retained payment-related charge, or a retention on a return for a defect, until this is answered. A refund is never reduced by MDR or aggregator fees. See [Refunds](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#refunds).

### Q-83 Counsel flags from the plan, ledger and trade-act bindings

**Question.** Five points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the bindings:

1. Whether silence after a delivered notice of a ledger entry is acceptance or dispute (the `ack_window` default).
1. Whether attested seller delivery evidence fixes the MSMED acceptance date, and whether BACP may drop the requirement of a buyer-signed GRN for an acceptance-dated sale (with [Q-21](#q-21)).
1. Whether a `TCS` line (CGST Act s.52) may appear in a buyer-facing total.
1. Who bears the ₹100-per-day compensation of the RBI turnaround-time circular when a split-tender plan is unwound.
1. Whether the 90th-percentile limit on statement acknowledgements, a BACP design value, is enough to protect a principal.

**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** (1) An entry is `disputed` at `ack_window` only where a notice was delivered. (2) Seller-only evidence is recorded with `acceptance_basis: unattested` and no due date is derived from it. (3) A `TCS` line never enters a buyer-facing total or a projected UCP total. (4) The question is recorded and no allocation is made by BACP. (5) Statement acknowledgements are limited as above and a per-entry dispute stays possible.

### Q-84 Whether the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules reach machine timestamps

**Question.** The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 761(E)), Rule 7, say that "No entity shall use, display or record any time reference other than Indian Standard Time (IST) for all purposes". The Rules are notified and not in force as of 18-10-2026; they commence 180 days after publication, about 24-02-2027 (the exact day is not verified). From commencement, does Rule 7 prohibit (a) storing or transmitting RFC 3339 timestamps with `Z` or `+00:00` that denote the same instant as an IST time, (b) RFC 9421 `created` Unix-epoch integers, or (c) the `Z` timestamps that ONDC's validator requires on Beckn messages? Is the "standard format" of Rule 5 a mandatory format for machine records or only for display? Does Rule 7 reach entities outside the critical sectors of Rule 8(4)? Do Rules 5(2) and 6(1) bind times shown on a Trusted Surface render?\
**Owner.** Legal counsel, ONDC (for the `Z` on `context.timestamp`).

**Working position.** Every comparison is on instants. BACP-owned timestamps SHOULD carry `+05:30`; Beckn `context.timestamp` follows ONDC and keeps `Z`; every time shown or told to a person on a Trusted Surface is in IST; participants keep clocks traceable to NIC or NPL time. Under the committed-order rule the values that decide formation are integers, not time references. A schema pattern that required `+05:30` is not adopted now, because it would be breaking and cannot be met on Beckn. The SHOULD becomes a MUST, if counsel says Rule 7 reaches machine timestamps, in a release dated before 24-02-2027.

### Q-85 Counsel flags from the negotiation timing rules

**Question.** Points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

1. Whether a principal-signed `standing_accept` is the principal's own acceptance under ICA s.7.
1. Whether an agent may accept a bid for a farmer under eNAM or APMC rules.
1. Whether one Trusted-Surface-signed negotiation mandate is "explicit and affirmative action" under Rule 4(9) of the E-Commerce Rules for each later purchase.
1. Whether a gateway or agent operator is the principal's agent under ICA Chapter X (s.214).
1. Whether a buyer's signed declaration of commercial purpose can displace consumer status under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.2(7) for a sole proprietor's livelihood purchase.
1. Whether a Dutch tick acceptance is a bid under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, s.64(2), whether an instant award is the announcement, and whether s.62 can exclude retraction ([Q-35](#q-35)).

**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** (1) A standing accept exists only where the auctioneer enables it, and absent it only the base rule applies. (2) An `agri` seller gateway treats `accept_confirmation` as `ask`, so a farmer always taps their own acceptance. (3) `accept_confirmation` is never preselected and an absent key is `ask`. (4) The operator's role is recorded and no allocation is made by BACP. (5) A consumer marker always wins. (6) The text says that the bidder's tick message is legally a bid and that the award completes the sale.

### Q-86 Counsel flags from the Trusted Surface and human-participant rules

**Question.** Points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

1. Whether a voice or operator-relayed "yes" satisfies Rule 4(9) of the E-Commerce Rules for a non-money confirmation.
1. Whether an assisted operator's act can be attributed to the principal under IT Act s.11(b), and what proves "authority".
1. Whether a gateway or agent operator is a "platform" under para 3 of the Dark Patterns Guidelines.
1. Whether `device_signature` is an electronic authentication technique under IT Act s.3A.
1. Whether a UPI debit that the account holder authenticates with her own PIN, but that a third party's BACP step-up link induced, is an unauthorised electronic transaction for issuer liability under RBI/2025-26/79 para 9(b).
1. Whether a gateway that reads `support_operator` registry records is a fiduciary or a processor of the employees' personal data.

**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** (1) Voice confirms only what moves no money, and the question stays open for that. (2) `Participant.ref` is attribution, never authentication, and the principal's own factor is always required. (3) The Trusted Surface rules apply to the gateway and the operator whichever way it is answered. (4) `device_signature` is never called an electronic signature, and no verifier relies on it unless the mandate lists `principal.device_jkt[]`. (5) TS-6 is a MUST, so that the induced debit does not arise. (6) The record holds only a pairwise `person_ref` and the key, never Aadhaar.

### Q-87 Registry carriage of the Trusted Surface and support-operator fields, and the ONDC refusal codes

**Question.** Can the ONDC network registry carry `bacp_role`, `operator_id`, `person_ref`, `ts_origins`, `ts_notify_url`, and the legal `operator` (`entity_ids[]`, `assertion`), `regulatory_status[]` and `data_residency` ([`registry-record.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/registry-record.json))? Which ONDC error code maps to each `seller_reason.code` (the code 40002 is unlabelled in the ONDC build file)? Is there a seller code for "agent orders not accepted"? Who is the certifier of assisted operators ([Q-62](#q-62))?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Beckn's `Subscriber.type` is BAP, BPP or BG only. Until ONDC answers, a gateway that cannot read a signer's `ts_origins` from the registry mints no `trusted_surface_url` for it and answers `503 trusted_surface_unavailable`, and a side registry would be a second trust root that this version does not define. An unmapped refusal code gives `seller_reason.code: other`. Principals of an unregistered signer lose link-based step-ups until it registers. An operator that the registry does not assert is unknown and fails every separation check closed, so pilot handlers that need a conformance attestation stay unavailable for open mandates, as today, and a collector with no `verified` `regulatory_status` entry gets `403 collector_not_authorised`.

### Q-88 RBI treatment of a Reserve Pay block debit and an OTM execution

**Question.** Does RBI treat a debit under a single-block-multiple-debits (Reserve Pay) block, or an execution of a UPI one-time mandate, as exempt from two-factor authentication under the AFA Directions (RBI/2025-26/79), or as already authenticated when the block or mandate was created?\
**Owner.** RBI.

**Working position.** Neither appears in Annexure-1 of RBI/2025-26/79, so the registry sets no `afa.rbi_annex1_item` for `in.upi.reservepay`, `in.upi.otm` or `in.upi.circle`, and the schema forbids it for a handler that relies on authentication at block creation or registration. The basis of such a debit is cited to NPCI OC 200 item 3, para (d) (Reserve Pay) and to UPI Consolidated Circular v1.0 paras 15.2 and 15.4 (OTM). The answer decides whether a future `rbi_annex1_item` is ever set on these handlers. The registry grades only the NPCI layer of the basis (`afa.verification`), and notes that no RBI exemption basis for the later debits was found.

### Q-94 Review process for third-party extensions

**Question.** Who reviews and admits a third-party extension (a capability under a reverse-DNS id, declared with a `registry_ref` and a `schema_digest`) to the extension registry, on what criteria, and how is an entry published and revoked?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** No third-party declaration is active. A gateway ignores no third-party entry silently: it does not activate it, and every `ext` member of a request is refused with `400 capability_unsupported`. Only `in.bacp.*` declarations are valid. A third-party entry will be published in a dated release together with the registry release manifest (`source/handlers/release.json`), so that its digest is checked like a handler's. Principals lose nothing today except an option that a bank or a distributor would add: it waits for a BACP release. See [Capability declarations](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#capability-declarations).

### Q-95 A gateway-held cart

**Question.** Should BACP add a cart that the gateway holds between discovery and a session (UCP's `dev.ucp.shopping.cart`)? No ONDC primary source shows a server-held cart: the buyer builds the cart in the buyer application and sends `select`.\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** The capability is parked: a gateway does not list it, the UCP projection answers `404` for the cart operations, and a request that carries `cart_id` is refused with `400 capability_unsupported` at `$.cart_id` (UCPF-06). A cart lives with the agent operator, and a principal on a feature phone has no gateway-held list. Any future cart MUST meet these controls: each cart line carries `transaction_id` and `source_digest` and a gateway-assigned `added_by`, so that conversion still runs the `discovery_price_changed` check and the sponsorship copy; a cart total is an estimate (`estimate: true`, spoken with the `cart_estimate` sentence), is never a `Presentation` and is never approved by a step-up; a cart belongs to one (agent, principal) pair and anyone else gets `404`; a conversion re-quotes every line (a new `select`, a new `checkout_hash`) and never takes prices from the cart; and a replayed conversion with another presence, root mandate or `basket_id` gets `409`. The projection's alternative, to validate and re-quote, is open.

### Q-96 Linking a buyer's account at a seller

**Question.** Should an agent be able to link the principal's account at a seller (UCP's identity linking, which uses the OAuth authorization-code flow), so that the seller fills the buyer, address and instruments from its stored state?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Parked: no tool, DataPart or REST operation links an account. The negatives are normative now: no seller one-time password or password is requested or relayed by an agent, no seller-account token appears in a tool argument, a tool result, the InstructionLog, an evidence bundle or model context, and a link token is never a mandate ([MCP authentication](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/mcp-a2a/#mcp-auth)). Any future capability MUST meet these controls: the authorisation endpoint comes only from the seller's registry record; linking is a Trusted Surface consent event in every case and the seller's own origin is a second route only when the principal's modality is `visual`, never on voice or feature-phone channels; the token is bound to the agent key, the principal and the seller as audience; its scope is no wider than `data_scopes` and a ConsentReceipt covers it; and an address or instrument that the seller fills in never feeds `fulfilment` or `complete`, and any difference gives `requires_buyer_review`. Whether an account that a seller creates from a chained grant is consent is a question for counsel ([Q-101](#q-101)).

### Q-97 Ask: natural-language questions to a seller

**Question.** Should BACP carry UCP's Ask capability, a natural-language question to a business and its answer? Ask is in no UCP release as of 18-10-2026 (it is on UCP's `main` branch after `v2026-08-25`, [Q-82](#q-82)).\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Parked. If it is added, an answer is `untrusted_counterparty_text`: it is never an input of a human-not-present decision, never a binding disclosure and never evidence, and the agent MUST NOT execute anything it says.

### Q-98 Loyalty memberships and benefits

**Question.** Should BACP carry UCP's loyalty extension (memberships, tiers, benefits and earning forecasts on a checkout)?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Parked, and the controls that apply today are normative: a `provisional` loyalty benefit never enters `total` or `charge_lines[]`, a plain session carries no loyalty discount ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts)), and a paid membership that a seller adds is a line with `added_by`, read to the principal as a line she did not add. A loyalty claim on a plain session is refused (UCPF-06 on the projection). Points as a tender stay with [Q-59](#q-59), which is closed.

### Q-99 Catalogue lookup by id and product variants

**Question.** Should BACP add lookup of catalogue items by id and a variant model (options, selected options, product and variant ids) beyond today's `POST /discover` results?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position.** Not added: no panel evidence for either yet. An agent re-discovers an item by search, and an item is one `CatalogItem` with its own id.

### Q-100 Purchasable ranking parameters

**Question.** Should an agent be able to ask the gateway to rank by a purchasable parameter (a promoted placement, a sponsored rank) in the request?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Not added. If it is, the request field takes a value from a gateway-listed enum, is never a mandate constraint (an unknown constraint fails closed and this would be a new family), and the result is sponsored under [Catalogue disclosures](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures) and shown as such.

### Q-101 Counsel flags from the UCP capability parity rules

**Question.** Five points for legal counsel, none of which blocks the rules:

1. Whether a seller's business default (`source: "business"`, `granted: true`) can ever be consent under DPDP Act s.6(1).
1. Whether an account that a seller creates from a chained grant is consent.
1. How a BACP marketing receipt relates to the preferences under the Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018 (TCCCPR), and whether it satisfies DPDP s.6(1) with them.
1. Whether an upward weight adjustment after a human-not-present payment is a new supply that needs fresh consent, and whether the GST invoice must show the final weighed quantity.
1. What DPDP retention duty attaches to a list or cart that an agent holds.

**Owner.** Legal counsel.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** (1) and (3) A seller default is never consent, and with no marketing receipt every marketing purpose is `granted: false`; the receipt is Proposed ([Marketing consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#marketing-consent)). (2) No linking capability exists. (4) An adjustment can only reduce the amount unless the principal agreed an `adjustment_band` and a hold exists ([Weighed goods](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/post-order/#weight-adjustment)). (5) The agent operator's own retention rules apply, and BACP holds no cart.

### Q-102 ONDC and NPCI points of the UCP capability parity rules

**Question.** Four points for ONDC and one for a UPI member bank:

1. What ONDC buyer-app feature codes 011 and 013 mean.
1. Whether the ONDC B2B `buyer_id` is a GSTIN only.
1. Which Beckn paths carry a selectable fulfilment, a `unitized.measure` outside RET11 and a seller-view `added_by`, and whether any domain can carry a fractional ordered measure.
1. Whether a one-time UPI block can be captured in part, with the rest released, which an upward `adjustment_band` needs.

**Owner.** ONDC, NPCI (through a member bank).

**Working position (fail-safe default).** The gateway sends `quantity.count` only where the seller's pack measure equals the increment, and refuses otherwise ([Quantity and units](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#quantity-units)). The gateway projects `acting_for.gstin` into `buyer_id` and sends nothing else as a buyer identity. A band is accepted only where the rail holds the amount and the hold can be captured in part; otherwise adjustments are down only.

### Q-103 Annexure-1 treatment of a FASTag top-up and an NCMC top-up

**Question.** Does Annexure-1 of the RBI authentication directions (RBI/2025-26/79) exempt from two-factor authentication (1) a top-up of a FASTag, as an "NETC transaction" under row 4, and (2) a top-up of an NCMC card, which no row names?\
**Owner.** RBI, NPCI.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** Row 4 reads "NETC transactions" and the source circular (RBI/2019-20/126, 30-12-2019, para 4) exempts transactions in the NETC system; neither names a top-up. The registry keeps `rbi_annex1_item: 4` for `in.ppi.netc_topup` as a reading (as of 18-10-2026). No row names an NCMC top-up, so `in.ppi.ncmc_topup` carries no exemption and no `rbi_annex1_item`, and authentication applies under para 6(a) (`afa.model: per_txn_2fa`). The pre-debit notice exemption for both handlers is a separate rule from the e-mandate framework.

### Q-104 Wire form of the carried-exposure increment after a port

**Question.** When a `use` of a superseded root reaches the Mandate Manager after it has signed the successor, the Mandate Manager sends the successor's gateway a signed carried-exposure increment ([Porting](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#port)). Which event, endpoint or `TrustedSurfaceEvent` value carries it, and what does it contain (`period`, `window_start`, `amount` and the `seq` of the `use` it comes from)?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** BACP defines no wire form in this version. The rule is stated: the increment counts against the successor, and the gateway applies it inside the root's atomic section. Until a form is defined, the Mandate Manager does not sign the successor before it holds a `closed` event and every event up to its `last_seq`, or 60 seconds have passed without one. In that second case every window is `incomplete` and is pre-filled at `max`, so the carried exposure is treated as at the old `max`. The successor's gateway never receives the superseded root's events, so the rule binds the Mandate Manager and not that gateway. A `use` that arrives after signing makes the Mandate Manager revoke the successor and ask the principal to port again.

### Q-105 Payload schema of the notice render

**Question.** What is the payload of the gateway-signed notice render of an `agreed_by_agent` or `purchase_offered_by_agent` act ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/index.md))? No schema defines it, so the bytes that go into `notice_renders[]` cannot be tested with a valid and an invalid example. The members that the text names are `code`, `offer_hash`, `language`, `total`, `revoke_route`, `grievance_contact` and `expires_at`.\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** BACP defines no notice payload schema in this version. A notice is a gateway-signed compact JWS that is not a `TsRender` and not a step-up, and the specification names its content in prose. A verifier checks that each entry of `notice_renders[]` is a compact JWS signed by the gateway's registry key and does not parse its payload.

## Proposed design choices awaiting owner decision

No design choice is awaiting an owner decision. Design choices [(a)](#proposed-a), [(c)](#proposed-c) and [(d)](#proposed-d) are settled.

### Q-89 TAT row 4(b) and a payment that the rail completed

**Question.** Does row 4(b) of the Annex of RBI/2019-20/67 ("Account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location", auto-reversal within T+5, ₹100 a day beyond it) apply to a UPI P2M payment whose payee credit the rail confirmed, where only the seller's application-level order confirmation (the Beckn `on_confirm`) never arrives?\
**Owner.** Legal counsel, RBI.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** The message states the T+5 turnaround and the ₹100 a day only where the payer PSP reports the debit as pending or deemed (`reversal_basis: rbi_tat`). Where the PSP reports the credit as completed (`bacp_policy`) it states no RBI compensation, and where the response does not say (`unknown`) it names the refund, UDIR and Ombudsman routes and adds that RBI's rules apply if the bank shows the payment as failed or pending. If row 4(b) does apply, the bank pays on its own and the message adds nothing; if it does not, BACP promises no remedy that may not exist. Principals lose nothing they hold today except a promise that may be false. See [Debited but not confirmed](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#debited-not-confirmed).

### Q-90 What a payer PSP can sign about a refund credit and about a deemed or pending debit

**Question.** Can a payer PSP sign refund-credit evidence that cites `original_rrn` for a refund that the acquirer initiated through URCS (NPCI OC 165)? Do PSP response codes tell a deemed or pending debit from a completed one at the moment `on_confirm` goes missing? Does NPCI de-duplicate a debit on the gateway's PSP idempotency key?\
**Owner.** NPCI, through a member bank.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** The budget is released on evidence (a) from the bound payer PSP, or on evidence (b), a collector-PSP receipt plus the principal's confirmation on the Trusted Surface, so that a seller with an insider at its payment aggregator cannot restore the budget. If no payer PSP can sign the evidence, path (b) needs one confirmation for each refunded order, and without it the spend stays, as before. If the codes do not tell, every case reads `reversal_basis: unknown`. BACP asserts no de-duplication by the rail: the gateway allows at most one debit per `checkout_hash`.

### Q-91 Re-attestation of a Reserve Pay block under a successor root

**Question.** Will payer PSPs sign a fresh attestation for an existing Reserve Pay block, so that a successor root can re-bind it without revoking it?\
**Owner.** NPCI.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** A successor root MAY re-bind a block that its predecessor held when the payer PSP re-attests it. Where no PSP does, the old blocks are revoked and created again, the principal enters the UPI PIN once for each seller, and both blocks count as exposure while a revocation is unconfirmed ([Porting a mandate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#port)).

### Q-92 Deemed-debit scope after OC 228, and overdraft funding

**Question.** What is the scope of a deemed debit for UPI Reserve Pay after NPCI OC 228 (08-10-2025), given that OC 88/2020-21 and OC 128/2021-22, which OC 200 recites, are member-only? Should a payer PSP attest an overdraft account as `deposit` or as `credit`?\
**Owner.** NPCI.

**Working position (fail-safe default).** A credit-side timeout after a successful debit is read as deemed (OC 200 para (d); Consolidated Circular para 32.3), and a timeout on the debit side is a decline (OC 228). An overdraft account is credit unless the PSP attests deposit, and a missing funding is credit, so that a block on such an account needs `credit_funding_allowed: true`.

### Q-93 Gift PPI refund after expiry or closure, and to a non-reloadable instrument

**Question.** Where does a refund go when a gift PPI has expired or been closed? Does PPI Master Direction para 14.3(a) let a refund be credited to a non-reloadable gift PPI above the limits of para 10.1?\
**Owner.** RBI, Legal counsel.

**Working position.** The registry records refund to the same PPI immediately (para 14.3(a)), a transfer back to the source with the holder's consent (10.1(c)), and, for a balance left after expiry, a payment to the holder in a bank account on request for a non-bank issuer (13.3). The gap is not verified as of 18-10-2026.

## Settled

These questions are settled in BACP `2026-10-18`. Each answer is normative in this version; the linked pages state the rule. A settled answer changes only in a later dated release, under the [versioning policy](https://bacp.dev/versioning/).

### Q-28 Handler naming

Settled

Settled in `2026-10-18`.

**Question.** Who governs handler names (`in.*` or `bacp.*`), and how long is the alias deprecation window?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Handler ids under `in.*` (rails and instruments) and `bacp.*` (BACP constructs) are canonical; earlier names such as `upi.circle.delegate` are aliases. Registry changes, including new ids, aliases and status changes, are normative changes under [`GOVERNANCE.md`](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): a 14-day review and two maintainers' approval, one of them the payments editor, after the [proposal process](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/#proposing-a-new-handler). The deprecation window is set by the [versioning policy](https://bacp.dev/versioning/#deprecation): a deprecated alias stays supported for at least two dated releases after the release that deprecates it and at least 180 days after that release, whichever is later. Removing an alias is a breaking change and gets at least 90 days' notice. This also settles what was proposed design choice (b), canonical `in.*` handler ids.

### Q-41 Closing open mandates

Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in `2026-10-18`.

**Question.** What is the interoperable SD-JWT / KB-JWT encoding for closing open mandates, in place of the detached-JWS `cnf` closing?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** BACP `2026-10-18` has one interoperable encoding for a closed mandate: an attached compact JWS whose payload is the Mandate JSON, including an inner signature with `role: agent` made by the open mandate's `cnf` key, and whose header `kid` is the `cnf` key id. The optional `kb_jwt` on `complete` keeps its current rules. An SD-JWT / KB-JWT selective-disclosure encoding is not part of this version; a later release may add it as a new mandate `vct` without changing this one. The conformance suite will carry test vectors for the attached-JWS form. See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#closing).

### Q-42 Mandatory signature algorithm

Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in `2026-10-18`.

**Question.** ES256 is mandatory and EdDSA allowed, but no ES256 test vectors exist and the implementation exercised so far signs only with EdDSA. Should ES256 stay mandatory, should EdDSA become mandatory, or should both be required?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Both are mandatory to verify. Every verifier of a BACP signature (RFC 9421 requests and webhooks, JWS mandates, receipts, ConsentReceipts, attestations and InstructionLog entries) MUST support ES256 (ECDSA P-256) and EdDSA with Ed25519. Every signer MUST use one of the two; no other algorithm is allowed. The conformance suite will carry test vectors for both. See [Identity and Request Signing](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/identity-and-signing/#signature-algorithms).

### Q-43 Network-leg signing

Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in `2026-10-18`.

**Question.** Should Beckn messages be signed with a detached JWS over JCS, or with Beckn's Ed25519 + BLAKE2b `Authorization` header? Does BACP require Beckn 2.0 signed ACKs and the CounterSignature on which negotiation timing depends?\
**Owner.** ONDC.

**Answer.**

- On the Beckn leg the network's own signing profile is normative: on Beckn 1.x and ONDC, the Ed25519 + BLAKE2b-512 `Authorization` header. BACP adds no transport signature of its own.
- BACP does not require Beckn 2.0 signed ACKs. A gateway SHOULD use them, and the `request-signature` binding of callbacks, where the counterparty supports them.
- The CounterSignature that negotiation timing relies on is a BACP artefact, not a Beckn ACK: a JWS by the receiving participant's registry key over the request digest and message id, returned in the negotiation message's `counter_signature` (on Beckn, inside the `bacp` TagGroups), so it does not depend on the Beckn version.
- A counterparty that does not return valid CounterSignatures is treated as not supporting firm negotiation: the gateway MUST send it only non-firm offers (`firm: false`), so that formation follows the purchase-offer flow.
- Evidence of what a seller sent rests on the same header signature: the gateway keeps the raw `on_init` body and its `Authorization` header (`EvidenceBundle.checkout.bpp_signed_payment_terms`), which a verifier checks against the BPP's registry key. A per-object JWS over `payments[]` would be a convenience, not a requirement ([Sibling Payment Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#sibling-payment-mandates)).

Whether ONDC validators accept the `bacp` TagGroups at all is [Q-09](#q-09). See [Beckn / ONDC Binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/beckn/#signing) and [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md).

**Receipts in `Ack.tags` (18-10-2026).** Transport `Ack` signing is still not required. A `bacp.receipt` TagGroup in the `Ack` carries a CounterSignature that verifies on its own by the counterparty's registry key, so it does not borrow trust from the transport. See [Q-22](#q-22) for the ONDC dependency.

### Q-47 Purpose-code governance

Settled

Was Blocking. Settled in `2026-10-18`.

**Question.** Who governs the purpose-code registry and its bounds? The Sahamati Fair Use page that inspired it is marked "no longer relevant".\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** The BACP WG governs the purpose-code registry. The purpose-bounds table in [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#purpose-bounds) is the normative registry for `2026-10-18`. A change to a code or a bound is a normative change under [`GOVERNANCE.md`](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md) and ships only in a dated release; lowering a bound or removing a code is a breaking change. A `purpose_code` that is not in the table is refused with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch`.

### Q-53 DPDP commencement dates

Settled

The dates are fixed in the Gazette. Re-check only if an amending notification is published.

**Question.** What are the final DPDP commencement dates, given a reported MeitY consultation to shorten 18 months to 12 and a reported corrigendum G.S.R. 113(E)?\
**Owner.** MeitY/DPDP.

**Answer.** The DPDP Rules 2025 are G.S.R. 846(E) and the Act's commencement notification is G.S.R. 843(E), both dated 13-11-2025. Together they set three dates:

| From                  | Rules (G.S.R. 846(E), rule 1) | Act (G.S.R. 843(E))                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 13-11-2025 (in force) | Rules 1, 2 and 17–21          | ss.1(2), 2, 18–26, 35, 38–43, 44(1) and 44(3)                                                             |
| 13-11-2026            | Rule 4 (Consent Managers)     | s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d)                                                                                     |
| 13-05-2027            | Rules 3, 5–16, 22 and 23      | ss.3–5, 6(1)–(8) and 6(10), 7–17, 27 (except 27(1)(d)), the penalty provisions ss.28–34, 36, 37 and 44(2) |

The corrigendum G.S.R. 892(E) (10-12-2025) and the DPDP (Removal of Difficulties) Order, 2026 (S.O. 5458(E), Order dated 05-10-2026, Gazette issue 06-10-2026) change wording only and move no date. The reported consultation to shorten the eighteen-month period and the reported corrigendum G.S.R. 113(E) appear only in secondary sources; no amending notification had been found as of 17-10-2026. See [Security and Privacy](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#commencement).

### Q-60 Conformance attestation

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026, for the next dated release.

**Question.** Which registry role signs a conformance attestation, who may hold that role, and is the proposed payload (`iss`, `sub`, `levels[]`, `pilots[]`, `exp`, `status`) final, and which explicit JOSE `typ` does the attestation carry?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** The role is `conformance_authority` (`Signature.role`). Only a key of an entry in a public, dated, per-handler [conformance-authority list](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-authority-list) qualifies; an entry is an independent lab or a rail-sponsor bank, scoped to named handlers, and the list ships empty. A Mandate Manager may narrow the list by publishing an exclusion list and never add to it. The payload is [`conformance-attestation.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/conformance-attestation.json), with the JOSE `typ` `bacp-conformance+jwt`, `subject_role`, `scope`, `jti`, `registry_version`, `manifest_digest` and `report_digest`. The Mandate Manager verifies it at issuance and writes `rail_binding.conformance{iss, sub, jti}` into every pilot mandate; the gateway re-checks the bound `jti` at every `complete`. An attestation status list that is revoked, more than 24 hours old or unreachable fails closed, for issuance and for a new `complete` only. See [Conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation). Holders at release: none, so a Mandate Manager still refuses open mandates on every `pilot` handler. Adding an entry needs the approval in [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#interim-maintainer). Settling this question does not open the human-not-present path on `in.upi.circle`, which waits for [Q-77](#q-77).

### Q-72 Signed discovery results

Settled

Settled by owner decision of 18-10-2026, for the release dated 15-12-2026.

**Question.** The gateway verifies each seller's `on_search` signature, but nothing carried that signature to the agent, so a gateway could change a seller-asserted `prior_price`, `mrp` or sponsorship value between the seller and the agent. Should an agent be able to verify seller-asserted discovery values itself?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Yes. Each `results[]` entry carries a `source_digest`, the sha-256 of the raw seller-signed `on_search` body that every item of the entry came from. The gateway serves that body, with its Beckn `Authorization` header, at `GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}`. An agent that presents or relies on a seller-asserted value checks the digest, the binding of the callback to its search, and the Beckn signature against a registry key that it resolves itself, never from the gateway, and derives the values by the normative mapping. An unverified value is rendered with no claim, and sponsorship is rendered as `undeclared` at least. The gateway signs the discover response. Values that only the gateway asserts become non-repudiable through that signature. The seller's honesty is still not proved: verification shows that the seller said it. See [Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results); the open parts are [Q-70](#q-70) and [Q-71](#q-71).

### (a) Open mandates on class-O handlers

Settled

Was proposed design choice (a). Settled in `2026-10-18` by owner decision of 17-10-2026, in a narrowed form.

**Question.** May an open (human-not-present) payment mandate bind to any class-O handler, or only to the UPI standing authorities?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.**

- An open payment mandate may bind to any class-O handler, but only through a mandate primitive whose limits the rail or the issuer enforces (`limits_enforced_by` `rail` or `issuer`). Each descriptor lists these primitives in `binding.open_primitives`. The mandate names the primitive it uses in `rail_binding.primitive`, the PSP attestation covers it, and the Mandate Manager refuses issuance otherwise (`rail_binding_not_open_eligible`). For `in.ppi.wallet` only `ppi_emandate` is open-eligible, never the wallet balance.
- The descriptor's `status` must be `live`, or `pilot` only when the gateway's [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation) lists the pilot in `pilots[]`; the Mandate Manager verifies this before issuing. The attestation payload and its signer are settled ([Q-60](#q-60)).
- Eligibility is re-checked against the current registry at every `complete`. A registry downgrade pauses the affected mandates and cancels their open sessions.
- The atomic reservation is keyed on the root open checkout mandate, so sibling open payment mandates cannot together exceed its budgets.
- `in.store_credit`, `in.loyalty` and `bacp.credit_ledger`, whose limits the merchant or BACP enforces, are not open-eligible in this version ([Q-59](#q-59), [Q-46](#q-46)). `in.erupi` is `pilot` until [Q-38](#q-38) is answered. Agentic card tokens stay pilot-gated ([Q-39](#q-39)).

See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding) and [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md).

### (c) Acceptance revocation

Settled

Was proposed design choice (c), "acceptance revocation waived by default". Settled in `2026-10-18` by owner decision of 17-10-2026, amended the same day after review: `allowed_until_receipt` is refused everywhere, and the rules that would honour it are kept as sunset text.

**Question.** Should every firm offer waive, by default, the acceptor's right under Indian Contract Act s.5 to revoke an acceptance before it reaches the proposer, or should the waiver be opt-in per offer?\
**Owner.** BACP WG; the validity of any waiver stays with Legal counsel ([Q-19](#q-19)).

**Answer.**

- `acceptance_revocation` is REQUIRED on every firm offer, and there is no default. A gateway never inserts or normalises the value before hashing.
- In this version every receiver refuses `allowed_until_receipt` with `capabilities_incompatible`, on every binding. The value stays in the schemas. A matched-pair rule that would honour it on the REST, MCP and A2A bindings is kept as [sunset text](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation-sunset): the revoke names the acceptance and the offer and is dispatched no earlier than the acceptance; the proposer appends a revoke it receives first to its transcript and holds it until 5 seconds after the revoke's dispatch; and the receiver returns its CounterSignature, with `log_entry_hash`, in the synchronous response to each message, so that it commits to receipt order before it sees the next message. A later version lifts the refusal only when the sunset conditions hold.
- `accept_revoke` and `withdraw` are sent under `bacp-negotiate`. Every `accept_revoke` is countersigned, logged and refused (`accept_revoke_not_allowed`). Exposure release is idempotent, keyed on `offer_hash`.
- `waived` needs a signed `waiver_basis` (a contract, or the buyer's own RFQ) that the acceptor's gateway obtained from its own principal before the offer arrived, that names the counterparty (`np_id` or GSTIN) and that the principal marked as a waiver basis, and is refused in consumer sessions: sessions whose profile is a consumer profile, that declare none, or whose buyer side acts for an individual or sends no `acting_for`. The profile is fixed when the session opens.
- On Beckn legs, a `waived` offer with no basis, and in a consumer session any `waived` offer, may be accepted only by a human shown the consequence sentence; the only schema error excused is the missing basis. In a consumer session on REST, MCP or A2A no value is permitted, so only non-firm offers are possible there.
- A negotiation approval is posted as `negotiation.step_up.approved` with `Presentation.offer_hash`, never with `checkout_hash`.
- The Trusted Surface shows the value only as a fixed consequence sentence followed by the cancellation terms, never as "cannot cancel". BACP does not yet say which value an offer SHOULD use.
- RFQ awards have no fixed value. The comparison set is frozen at close (for `rfq_iterated`, the close of the final shortlist round); a revoked award, possible only under the sunset text, cancels the RFQ or auction (`NEG_COLLUSION_SCREEN`), and it cannot be awarded again (`NEG_AWARD_RULE`). `accept_revoke` never governs `bid_retract`.

See [Acceptance revocation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation), [Award](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/rfq-and-auctions/#award) and [Trade Profiles](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/trade-profiles/#profile-table).

### (d) Multi-seller hands-free shopping

Settled

Was proposed design choice (d). Settled in `2026-10-18` by owner decision of 17-10-2026.

**Question.** Given that a Reserve Pay block pays one seller, in what order does an agent fall back when it buys from several sellers with no human present, and what does each fallback mean for the principal?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.**

- A multi-seller purchase is a basket of sessions, one per seller, grouped by a gateway-local `basket_id`. No payment spans sellers, and there is no atomicity across sellers.
- **Per leg**, the gateway plans the payment in this order: the principal's designated preference; then the seller's existing payee-bound instrument, such as a block already held for that seller (3a); then a gift PPI the principal designated; then one planned human-present step, raised for the whole basket before any debit. UPI Circle and agentic card tokens back no open mandate while they are `pilot` and no listed conformance authority has attested the gateway for them ([Q-60](#q-60)); UPI Circle also waits for [Q-77](#q-77). No rung ranks above the principal's preference.
- A **new** per-seller block (3b) is offered only beside a one-time human-present payment to the same seller, with equal weight, never after a failed payment and never on an IVR callback. A block set up outside a checkout is exempt.
- Every sibling Payment Mandate sits under one root open Checkout Mandate; a block names its payee (`payee{vpa, bpp_id}`), bound to the seller's signed payment terms; the blocks under a root sum to no more than its smallest budget; each block counts as reserved spend at its full amount; revoking the root revokes each block.
- A change of a leg's funding class (own deposit, prepaid or borrowed), fee-bearer, payee or collector raises a `rail_fallback` step-up; an `in_doubt` leg is never re-routed.

See [Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#per-leg-rule) and [Sessions and Checkout](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#multi-seller-basket). Whether an agent draw on a block counts as a customer action is open ([Q-65](#q-65)).

### Q-44 Binding for plans, ledgers and documents

Settled

Was Blocking. Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4).

**Question.** What are the REST, MCP and A2A bindings for split-tender payment plans, credit ledgers and trade documents (GRN, CRAC, invoices)?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** All three are bound, each behind a capability id that a gateway lists in its profile, so that a gateway that lists none keeps the earlier behaviour:

- `in.bacp.payment_plan`: `payment.plan_options[]` on a session and `complete.payment_plan`. Plans are offered by the gateway or confirmed on the Trusted Surface, never composed by the agent. See [Wire binding of plans](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#plan-wire).
- `in.bacp.ledger`: paginated reads and an agent `payment` posting under a payee match, a `pending_ack` fall-back and a head compare-and-swap. See [On the wire: in.bacp.ledger](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#ledger-wire).
- `in.bacp.trade_document`: `POST /trade-acts` for GRN, CRAC, MSMED objection and ledger acknowledgement, with `subject_hash` on every act, and `GET /orders/{order_id}/documents`. See [Seller-side and trade acts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#trade-acts).

A gateway that does not list `in.bacp.payment_plan` still refuses a `complete` that carries `payment_plan` (conformance case T1-31). Tranches are accepted in the fail-safe form: a tranche carries no debit authority at `complete`. The carriage of a buyer-issued GRN or CRAC on Beckn stays with [Q-33](#q-33), so a trade act on a document is `delivery: recorded` until then. Counsel's points are in [Q-83](#q-83).

### Q-45 Intersection for plain sessions

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4).

**Question.** Should `POST /payment-handlers/intersect` support plain checkout sessions that have no TermSheet?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Yes, on a gateway that lists `in.bacp.payment_plan`: the request may carry a `session_id` alone. The answer covers only the session's own sellers, uses a closed reason enum with no amounts and no counterparty text, gives a `resolution` per reason and a `bpp_id` per seller, is rate-limited per agent before the lookup, is never forwarded to a seller and is never authority (`complete` re-evaluates). A gateway that does not list the capability keeps the `negotiation_id` requirement. See [Handler intersection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-intersection-and-preference).

### Q-64 Support-operator keys in the registry

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T6).

**Question.** How does a registry enrol and revoke keys of role `support_operator`, the keys with which a human support operator of an agent operator accepts and releases a handoff under tag `bacp-handoff`? What does the registry record hold (the agent operator the person works for, one key per person), who vets the person, and how fast does a revocation reach gateways?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** The registry record of a `support_operator` key is [`registry-record.json`](https://bacp.dev/latest/schemas/registry-record.json) with `bacp_role: support_operator`, `operator_id` (the agent operator the person works for), `person_ref` (a pairwise reference to one person, never an Aadhaar number), `keys` (exactly one key), `valid_from`, `valid_until` and `status`. There is one key per person and no shared desk keys. A revocation takes effect at the next registry refresh, as for other keys. A key of another agent operator has no standing and gets `404 not_found`; a key whose role is not `support_operator` gets `401 signature_invalid`; and a key of the same agent operator that is not `accepted_by` gets `409 session_state_conflict` ([Human handoff](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#handoff)). Support staff without a per-person key cannot accept a handoff, so a principal who asks for a human waits until the operator enrols them. Who vets the person is the agent operator's duty under its own HR process; counsel's question on whether a gateway that reads these records is a fiduciary or a processor of the employees' personal data is open with counsel ([Q-86](#q-86)). Whether the ONDC network registry can carry `operator_id` and `person_ref` is a question for ONDC.

### Q-61 Gateway-to-MM mandate events

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

**Question.** Should a gateway tell the Mandate Manager that issued a mandate when it pauses that mandate because its rail binding is no longer eligible (`binding_ineligible`, `reissue_required`) or lifts such a pause, so that the Trusted Surface can show the principal why the agent cannot pay and can offer re-issue? If so, through which signed event and endpoint? `POST /trusted-surface/events` runs from the MM or PSP to the gateway, and every webhook runs from the gateway to the agent, so BACP `2026-10-18` has no channel in this direction.\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Yes, on the `audit_uri` that the mandate already carries, with no new Mandate Manager endpoint. The gateway reports a use, a relinquishment and every addition or removal of a gateway-originated pause reason as a `MandateEvent` (`use`, `relinquished`, `pause_changed`), numbered per mandate by `seq` and chained by `prev_hash`, signed under RFC 9421 by the registry key of its BAP with the tag `bacp-mm-event`, and delivered within 60 seconds and retried with the same `event_id`. The Mandate Manager accepts an event only from the BAP of the mandate's `agent.bap_id`, and records `event_gap` on a missing `seq`. A delivery failure never blocks a refund, a reversal or a post-order write, and no money moves on the event: every gateway still re-derives eligibility at step 1 of evaluation. The Mandate Manager derives the change of registry status and its own issuance record itself, and learns an attestation swap and `unmatched_rail_debit` (which needs a block-debit feed, [Q-10](#q-10)) only from the event. A relinquishment of a root with blocks is not complete for the principal until the Mandate Manager reports `rail_revocation`, and the agent delivers the Trusted Surface revoke route until then. A `MandateEvent` carries no text for the principal, so it is not a notice: BACP still defines no gateway-to-Trusted-Surface notice event, and a `process.notice_route` of `tel` or `sms` remains the way to meet the condition for `autonomous` ([Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md)). See [Mandate events](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#mandate-events) and [Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding).

### Q-36 Atomicity across gateways

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

**Question.** How are budgets and negotiation exposure kept atomic across gateways (a principal with two buyer apps) and across replicas of one gateway? Should the Mandate Manager hold the authoritative reservation ledger?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Budgets are atomic per root inside one gateway, and each open mandate belongs to one gateway: the mandate carries `agent.bap_id`, copied by the Mandate Manager from the verified AgentCredential, and any other gateway refuses it with `403 mandate_scope_mismatch` at `$.agent.bap_id` (a mandate without `bap_id` is bound by `credential_hash`, which the gateway compares). A mandate moves to another gateway only by a principal-initiated successor root on the Trusted Surface, which carries the spend already made and revokes the old root first. The earlier working position, that the Mandate Manager publishes outstanding exposure, is replaced: nobody proposed a Mandate-Manager-held ledger, and a synchronous one would put every `complete` on the Mandate Manager's availability. Replicas of one gateway keep sharing a linearisable ledger. The gateway takes the principal-keyed section before the root's section, never the reverse, and a firm commitment of the negotiation guard is written into the root's ledger as a reservation keyed by `offer_hash`. See [Atomic reservation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#atomic-reservation) and [Porting a mandate](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#port).

### Q-50 Cross-seller split detection

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

**Question.** Should split-order detection add a cross-seller velocity signal keyed on (mandate, window) instead of the seller?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** Split-order detection is keyed on the root open Checkout Mandate and the seller, within 10 minutes, and counts completed and in-flight orders. The seller is identified by the tax id in the BPP-signed terms, else by the payee VPA, else by the pair `bpp_id` and `provider_id`. The `covers[]` legs of a summary-approved basket are exempt, because the principal has approved each of them. A cross-seller velocity signal is not added: velocity across different sellers is bounded by the budgets. See [Step-up](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#step-up) and [Atomic reservation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#atomic-reservation).

### Q-46 Exposure of credit-ledger deals

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7).

**Question.** Should the cross-session exposure check count B2B credit-ledger deals against the checkout mandate's budgets or against `credit_ledger.max_outstanding`?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** A credit-ledger sale counts against the checkout mandate's budgets and against `credit_ledger.max_outstanding` only when it is booked by a gateway `complete` under the buyer's mandate, inside the root's atomic section. A sale that the creditor posts never touches the budgets. A disputed entry keeps its count until it is resolved or credit-noted. A `payment` that settles a sale counts within the sale, never on top of it, and releases `max_outstanding` only; a `credit_note` releases both. See [Booking and settling](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#booking-and-settling).

### Q-59 Merchant- and BACP-enforced handlers

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T7), as closed: not open-eligible in this release.

**Question.** May an open payment mandate bind to `in.store_credit`, `in.loyalty` or `bacp.credit_ledger`, whose limits are enforced by the merchant or by BACP rather than by a rail or an issuer? If so, who may sign their attestations and receipts when the payee is also the party that acts, and how does a credit-ledger sale, which has no payment receipt, resolve its budget reservation?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** `in.store_credit`, `in.loyalty` and `bacp.credit_ledger` are not open-eligible in this release, and their descriptors have `presence.hnp: none`, because the limits of each are enforced by the merchant or by BACP and not by a rail or an issuer. A principal who wants to pay human-not-present from store credit, loyalty or a khata ledger cannot yet; human-present payment is unaffected. The conditions for opening them are written down now, so that opening later is a registry change plus an owner decision:

Proposed

A handler whose limits a merchant or BACP enforces MAY back an open mandate only when all of these hold, each tested by a conformance case (T7-40 and the cases of the [handler-binding cases](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#handler-binding-cases)):

1. Attestations and receipts are never signed by a key of the payee's operator.
1. A failure receipt signed by the payee keeps the reservation counted as spent until the principal confirms on the Trusted Surface.
1. A credit-ledger acknowledgement comes from the principal's or the Mandate Manager's key, never the agent's `cnf` key.
1. A store-credit debit carries the merchant-signed `balance_before` and `balance_after`.
1. A loyalty redemption carries a programme-signed `conversion_value`.

Whether a gateway that funds a ledger needs RBI registration under the RBI Act, 1934, s.45-IA is a question for counsel (not verified as of 18-10-2026). See [Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding) and [Booking and settling](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#booking-and-settling).

### Q-82 Pinned UCP release for the UCP checkout projection

Settled

Settled on 18-10-2026 (owner decision, panel round R2, topic T4 with the T8 apply).

**Question.** Should the `in.bacp.ucp_checkout` projection pin a tagged release of the Universal Commerce Protocol or a commit?\
**Owner.** BACP WG.

**Answer.** The projection pins UCP's tagged release `v2026-08-25` (25-08-2026, commit `cd78fb3`), the latest of UCP's four releases as of 18-10-2026. The pin was commit `a5e7cfe` (12-10-2026) on UCP's `main` branch, which upstream labels `draft` and which is 39 commits after the tag; four of the 41 pinned files differ, so the move changes the copies of `link.json`, `policy.json`, `warning_code.json` and `ucp.json`. Three changes that UCP made on `main` after the tag are not in the pinned release, and BACP does not depend on them: the Ask capability, the cart rule that `line_items` SHOULD be `[]`, and the registry of policy types (the tagged text lists `dev.ucp.shopping.policy.return` and `.warranty`). A gateway MUST NOT claim UCP compatibility on any other UCP version. A later re-pin to a newer tag re-runs the projection checks. The projection's handler keys are the UCP aliases `dev.bacp.<handler id>`, each with a schema at `https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/<handler id>.json` (decided 18-10-2026, after the owner confirmed that BACP holds `bacp.dev`); the old keys stay accepted for the dated release that introduces the alias. See [UCP checkout projection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/ucp-checkout/#namespaces).

### Other settled points

| Question                                                                                   | Answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
