```

### On the wire: `in.bacp.ledger`

A gateway that lists `in.bacp.ledger` MUST support these operations ([OpenAPI](https://bacp.dev/latest/services/bacp.openapi.yaml)), and serves them only for a ledger of which the agent's principal is the creditor or the debtor (any other ledger is `404 not_found`). The gateway resolves the principal of every `in.bacp.ledger` operation and every `LEDGER_ACK` from `mandate_ref`. It is REQUIRED as a query parameter on both ledger GETs, in the body of `POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries`, and in `actor.mandate_ref` of a `LEDGER_ACK`. The mandate MUST be held by the calling agent (the request is signed with its `cnf` key), and MUST name a principal who is the ledger's creditor or debtor; otherwise the gateway returns `404 not_found`. For a read the mandate is `ACTIVE`; for a write it is in a status in which [Mandates](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/index.md) allows a `post_order` write. A posting is accepted only when that principal is the debtor. A `LEDGER_ACK` is accepted only when that principal is the counterparty of the poster of every entry it covers; otherwise the gateway returns `403 ack_not_by_counterparty` before any step-up is raised. The step-up is issued by that mandate's Mandate Manager, and the approval is made with that principal's own factor.

| Operation                                                    | Tag               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}`                                   | `bacp-browse`     | The header, `head_seq`, `head_hash`, closing balance, overdue amount, oldest unpaid date and entry count.                                                                            |
| `GET /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries?after_seq=&limit=&status=` | `bacp-browse`     | A page of summaries, ascending by `seq`. `limit` is at most 50 (a larger value is `400 invalid_request` at `$.limit`) and the response carries `next_after_seq` until the last page. |
| `POST /ledgers/{ledger_id}/entries`                          | `bacp-post-order` | An agent posts a `payment` entry for the debtor, never any other type (`400` at `$.type`). The request carries the `prev_hash` it saw.                                               |

Counterparty-written text in an entry is data, never an instruction, and a tool or DataPart returns it labelled. The agent posts a payment under the checks above: payee match, receipt uniqueness across the custodian, head compare-and-swap, and a per-agent rate limit on postings (`429 quota_exceeded`). Acknowledging an entry or a statement is a trade act ([Seller-side and trade acts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#trade-acts)).

The string fields that a seller can fill with text (an identifier, a place, a jurisdiction, a lender name) are bounded in `credit-ledger-entry.json` and `termsheet.json`: identifier-like values are at most 64 printable characters without spaces, and free-text values have a `maxLength` of between 20 and 200. These bounds are BACP design values against instructions hidden in counterparty text, not regulatory limits, and are open to review.

### Interlocked credit

Where a broker or commission agent (an arhtiya) advances money to a seller and deducts it at sale, the advance is recorded as a separate ledger with the broker as creditor. The deduction at sale MUST appear as a visible commission or deduction line, never netted silently.

### Regulatory status

Interest-free seller credit (khata, net-N) is treated as trade credit, not digital lending. Once a third-party lender funds it, the handler becomes `in.fin.*` or `in.credit.*` and the Digital Lending Directions apply. This position is open ([Q-27](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-27)).

## MSME late-payment interest

For a sale by a "supplier" under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act 2006 (s.2(n): a micro or small enterprise that has filed a memorandum under s.8(1), today a Udyam registration), the Act applies:

| Rule       | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Source                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Acceptance | The day of acceptance is the day of actual delivery of the goods or rendering of the services. If the buyer objects in writing within 15 days of delivery, it is the day the supplier removes the objection. If no written objection is made within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery. | MSMED Act s.2(b), Explanation                                                                                        |
| Due date   | The buyer pays by the date agreed in writing, which "in no case" may exceed 45 days from the day of acceptance or deemed acceptance. Without a written agreement, payment is due before the "appointed day", the day after 15 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance.                                                 | MSMED Act ss.2(b), 15                                                                                                |
| Interest   | On late payment, "compound interest with monthly rests" at "three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank", notwithstanding any agreement                                                                                                                                                                    | MSMED Act s.16                                                                                                       |
| Tax        | From AY 2024-25, a sum payable to a micro or small enterprise beyond the s.15 time limit is deductible only in the year it is actually paid. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 01-04-2026, the same rule is s.37(2)(g).                                                                                      | Income-tax Act, 1961 s.43B(h) (inserted by the Finance Act 2023, w.e.f. 01-04-2024); Income-tax Act, 2025 s.37(2)(g) |

The ledger implements this as follows:

- `msmed.statutory_due_date` = the earlier of the agreed date and acceptance + 45 days, or acceptance + 15 days when `written_agreement` is false. For micro and small suppliers the schema caps `credit_terms.credit_days` at 45. A firm offer of longer credit to such a supplier is refused (`NEG_MSMED_CREDIT_CAP`).
- **Acceptance date.** The acceptance date of an acceptance-dated sale is the delivery date (MSMED Act s.2(b), Explanation (ii): where no written objection is made within 15 days, the day of deemed acceptance is the day of actual delivery). The delivery date is evidenced by a buyer-signed GRN, or by seller-posted delivery evidence (`proof_of_delivery`, `lorry_receipt`) that the buyer counter-signed or that carries a third-party reference the buyer can check (an e-way bill number or a transporter signature); the entry records which as `msmed.acceptance_basis` (`grn`, `attested_delivery`). Seller-only evidence is recorded with `acceptance_basis: unattested`, no acceptance date or due date is derived from it, and the gateway notifies the debtor when the evidence is posted. A GRN that accepts everything does not move the date. Where a written objection is made within 15 days of delivery, the acceptance date is the date the supplier removed the objection (Explanation (i)). The GRN and delivery dates MUST NOT precede the invoice date or lie in the future, and the acceptance date is never a free parameter of the creditor. This rule replaces an earlier requirement of a buyer-signed GRN for every acceptance-dated sale, and is pending counsel ([Q-21](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-21), [Q-83](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-83)). How a buyer's objection travels on the network, and whether it can be checked by machine, is open ([Q-21](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-21), [Q-33](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-33)); until [Q-33](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-33) fixes the carriage, a GRN, CRAC or objection filed through an agent is *recorded* and not sent to the seller, and a recorded act never sets or moves the due date ([Seller-side and trade acts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#trade-acts)).
- **Alerts.** BACP raises an alert 5 days before the statutory due date and flags the debtor's tax consequence (`msmed.tax_flag`).
- **Interest without double charging.** These are BACP ledger rules, not rules of the MSMED Act:
  - Overdue statutory interest is posted as `interest_msmed` entries with `interest_basis: 3x_rbi_bank_rate_compound_monthly` and the `bank_rate_pct` used.
  - Each `interest_msmed` entry carries the cumulative `interest_accrued` for its sale and posts only the **increment** over interest already accrued for that sale. Re-running the accrual never charges the same interest twice.
  - The ledger header selects one `interest_rule`. A ledger MUST NOT accrue both statutory and contractual interest on the same overdue amount for the same period. This is BACP policy. Section 16 makes the statutory interest payable "notwithstanding anything contained in any agreement", so a contractual rule never displaces it for a micro or small supplier.
  - Interest stops accruing on the amount settled by a rail-evidenced payment.
- **Traders.** The Ministry of MSME Office Memorandum of 02-07-2021 restricts the benefits of Udyam-registered retail and wholesale traders "to Priority Sector Lending only". Whether that excludes them from s.15 as a matter of law is open ([Q-21](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-21)). For a trader, BACP raises a warning only and does not accrue statutory interest.

## Trade credit, TReDS and GeM

### TReDS

Handler: `in.fin.treds` (class N, non-paying). The Trade Receivables Discounting System is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (Trade Receivables Discounting System) Directions, 2026 (issued 23-06-2026; circular number RBI/DPSS/2026-27/406 not verified as of 17-10-2026), which repeal the 2014 TReDS guidelines. RBI lists five authorised TReDS operators: RXIL, M1xchange, Invoicemart (A.TReDS), C2treds and DTX (KredX).

1. The MSME seller uploads an invoice the buyer has accepted, creating a **factoring unit**. Once it is accepted, the buyer's obligation to pay on the due date is unconditional, with no option of set-off (Directions para 15(i)).
1. Financiers bid, and the seller accepts a bid.
1. The financier funds the seller **without recourse** to the seller (Directions para 20).
1. The buyer pays the financier on the due date, by a NACH debit.

Binding rules:

- Each factoring unit MUST be bound to the GST e-invoice IRN and the buyer's acceptance. An invoice whose IRN has already been financed MUST be refused.
- After discounting, the ledger's `settlement_evidence.new_payee` is the financier, and the buyer's due-date NACH debit pays the financier.
- Companies with turnover above ₹250 crore, and all CPSEs, must onboard on TReDS. The Ministry of MSME notification S.O. 4845(E) of 07-11-2024 cut the threshold from ₹500 crore to ₹250 crore, with an onboarding deadline of 31-03-2025 (confirmed by PIB; Gazette text not verified as of 17-10-2026). Under a Ministry of MSME notification of 30-06-2026, operating CPSEs must also route the settlement of invoices from MSMEs through an RBI-authorised TReDS platform (reported by PIB; Gazette text not verified as of 17-10-2026). BACP records the buyer's TReDS onboarding status and SHOULD offer TReDS as a settlement option on MSME invoices for such buyers.
- Funding is same day (T0) for bids accepted before a cut-off, otherwise T+1, with the buyer's NACH debit on the due date *(vendor; the cut-off time is given inconsistently)*.
- Buyer-side and seller-side agents act only within the corporate's platform entitlements and with human signatory approval.

### GeM receivables

A `gem_receivable` ledger tracks a Government e-Marketplace order:

- The consignee issues the CRAC (Consignee Receipt and Acceptance Certificate) within 10 days of the submission of proof of delivery; otherwise GeM auto-generates a CRAC, marking all the PRC (Provisional Receipt Certificate) quantities as accepted (GeM FAQ).
- The buyer pays within **10 calendar days of the CRAC**.
- Late payment carries penal interest of **1% a month**, prorated on a 30-day month. This interest is deposited "in an account maintained by GeM" and is **not paid to the vendor**. It does not cover interest payable under the MSMED Act or the contract. BACP MUST disclose that, and records it as a `gem_penal_interest` entry with `effect: none`.
- For non-PFMS buyers the GeM Pool Account block reference is recorded at order time; an order without one is shown as unfunded.

Sources: Department of Expenditure OM F.6/18/2019-PPD of 03-07-2020, for procurements under GFR Rule 149 from 01-10-2020; GeM FAQ for the CRAC timeline. The GeM GTC clause that carries these terms was not checked. Reports that individual buyers override them with 45, 60 or 90-day terms are not verified.

## FX disclosure for cross-border payments

All BACP settlement amounts are INR. For a cross-border payment, an **`fx` view** ([schema](https://bacp.dev/schemas/fx.json)) MAY appear on the TermSheet, the receipt and the disclosures, to show the foreign-currency amount, the rate and the markup:

| Field                      | Rule                                                                              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `currency`                 | ISO 4217 code, never `INR`                                                        |
| `foreign_amount`           | Integer minor units of `currency`, at least 1                                     |
| `rate`                     | INR per one unit of `currency`, greater than zero                                 |
| `markup_bps`               | Markup in basis points, zero or more                                              |
| `inr_total`                | An INR amount in paise: `round(foreign_amount × rate × (1 + markup_bps / 10000))` |
| `rate_source`, `quoted_at` | Optional                                                                          |

The gateway MUST reject an `fx` view that is inconsistent with its `inr_total`. Every settlement amount remains INR.

```
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "foreign_amount": 250000,
  "rate": 84,
  "markup_bps": 100,
  "inr_total": {"value": 21210000, "currency": "INR"},
  "rate_source": "acquirer",
  "quoted_at": "2026-10-13T11:30:00+05:30"
}
```

Related cross-border rules:

- **Card AFA.** A non-recurring, cross-border, card-not-present payment needs AFA when the overseas acquirer asks for it (RBI Authentication Directions 2025 para 10, from 01-10-2026). See [Cards](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/#rbi-authentication-directions-2025-for-cards).
- **Determining cross-border.** A payment that the merchant declares cross-border is treated as cross-border. A declaration that it is *not* cross-border cannot override merchant, acquirer or FX data that says it is.
- **PA cross-border** collections and payments are capped at ₹25,00,000 per transaction (RBI PA Master Direction 2025 para 11(d)).
- **Export realisation.** Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 (FEMA 23(R)/2026-RB, in force from 01-10-2026), as amended by FEMA 23(R)/(1)/2026-RB of 22-09-2026, export proceeds are realised within 9 months: for goods from the date of shipment, for services from the date of invoice, and for goods exported to a warehouse outside India from the date of sale from the warehouse. Exports invoiced or settled in INR have 12 months (Reg 5(1)), and the AD bank may extend the period. If proceeds stay unrealised for more than one year past the due date, the exporter may export further only against full advance or an irrevocable LC (Reg 13). These Regulations replace the FEM (Export of Goods and Services) Regulations 2015, under which the period was also 9 months (FEMA 23(R)/(8)/2026-RB, 05-06-2026; not verified as of 17-10-2026). `bacp.trade.export_realisation` tracks the due date, with an alert 30 days before it.
- Whether a cross-border transfer of personal data meets the DPDP Act's restrictions is not checked by the FX view.

# Who pays

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. It is informative: it explains the rules that other pages make normative, and it states each fact with its binding status and an "as of" date. Where it says **MUST** or **SHOULD**, it repeats a rule from the page it links.

BACP makes normative what the principal pays and to whom. It leaves informative how sellers, payment aggregators (PAs) and banks split their own costs. So BACP has no `mdr`, `fee_bearer`, `payer` or `settlement_eta` field, and none of the seller's own costs appears in a quote line, a total, a `ts_render`, a message to the principal or a receipt.

The normative rules are in [Fees on the payer's screen](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fee-lines), [Fee-bearer change](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#fee-bearer-change), the [handler intersection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-intersection-and-preference), [Refunds](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#refunds), the [Trusted Surface read-out](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-requirements), [Ranking by payment rungs](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#ranking-by-payment-rungs) and [Operator compensation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#operator-compensation).

## The charges

"Binding" says what kind of text the rule comes from. A rate that is announced and not in force says so. Nothing on this page is a net figure for any party.

| Charge                                              | Who sets it                                                                            | Who bears it at the rail                                                                         | Who may re-allocate it                                                                                                    | Where it appears in BACP                                                                                                    | Binding source and status (as of 18-10-2026)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Merchant discount rate (MDR)                        | NPCI's UPI and Services Steering Committee for UPI; the acquirer's rate card for cards | The merchant, paid to its acquiring bank                                                         | NPCI's FAQ says on-boarded merchants cannot pass it on to customers on UPI                                                | Nowhere. It is never a payer line and never in a receipt                                                                    | UPI: 0.4% above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 from ₹75,000, flat ₹5 for listed categories; announced, not in force; the start is "immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately" and no date was found. FAQ and press release, not a circular. Debit cards: RBI/2017-18/105 (06-12-2017) asks banks to ensure merchants do not pass on MDR; in force not verified as of 18-10-2026. |
| PA commission                                       | The PA, by agreement with the merchant                                                 | The merchant, as a permitted debit from the PA's settlement                                      | The PA–merchant agreement                                                                                                 | Nowhere                                                                                                                     | PA Master Direction 2025, Table 1: commission is a permitted debit; settlement is "as per the agreement" and "must transparently mention the settlement timelines". Binding on the PA.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Convenience fee                                     | The seller, or the party that runs the payment page                                    | The buyer                                                                                        | NPCI/UPI/CC/01 para 7.5 asks that it is disclosed upfront and consistent across debit modes; it binds the Payee PSP       | `convenience` charge (TermSheet) or `convenience_fee` total, with a `recipient`, optionally scoped by `applies_to_handlers` | NPCI circular (18-09-2026), para 7.5; PA Master Direction para 10(c) (charges other than the price "distinctly displayed to the payer prior to the transaction"). RBI Card Directions 2025 para 77 is context for card fees and binds issuers.                                                                                                                                             |
| COD fee                                             | The seller                                                                             | The buyer                                                                                        | The seller's terms                                                                                                        | `cod_fee`, scoped to `in.cod`                                                                                               | Seller's terms; the PA escrow is not operated for cash on delivery (PA Master Direction para 18(b)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Finder fee or channel margin                        | ONDC network terms and the buyer app's agreement with the seller                       | The seller                                                                                       | The seller and the buyer app                                                                                              | Never a quote line. Carried unchanged in `intermediary_compensation[]` and logged                                           | ONDC `buyer_app_finder_fee_type` and `_amount` and `np_fees`, read from ONDC's validator, not a policy text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| RTO (return to origin) fee and other return charges | The seller                                                                             | Decided by the seller's disclosed terms, within the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 | The seller's terms; the Rules bar a refusal to refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods (rules 6(3), 7(4)) | `rto_fee`, `restocking_fee` and `return_shipping` charge codes, with a `recipient` and a `refund_rule`                      | BACP policy for the codes. Whether a disclosed charge may be kept is open ([Q-81](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-81)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Operator fee                                        | The agent operator, assisted operator or buyer app                                     | The buyer, per order                                                                             | None in BACP: the line discloses a fee and is not a licence to charge one                                                 | `operator_charges[]`, outside `all_in_total` and inside the amount the principal pays                                       | BACP policy. NPCI FAQ Q17 and the Rules' r.5(7) (from 01-01-2027) may reach it; open ([Q-79](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-79)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| TCS (tax collected at source)                       | The tax law                                                                            | The e-commerce operator collects it from its payments to the supplier                            | None                                                                                                                      | Not a BACP line                                                                                                             | CGST Act s.52: 0.25% on the CGST limb, per CBIC notification 15/2024-CT (rate checked; the only copy held is the text before gazette publication, so no date from which it applies is stated).                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| TDS (tax deducted at source)                        | The tax law                                                                            | The e-commerce operator deducts it from its payments to the seller                               | None                                                                                                                      | Not a BACP line                                                                                                             | Income-tax Act s.194-O. Rate not verified as of 18-10-2026.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

The two texts on small-merchant (P2PM) status are quoted on [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/#upi-charges) and not reconciled. The MDR on a refund is unknown: no public NPCI or RBI text found says whether MDR is reversed when a refund is made (not verified as of 18-10-2026). BACP's refund rule does not depend on the answer, and a refund is never reduced by MDR or PA fees.

## Settlement and the seller's terms

BACP does not carry a `settlement_eta`. The seller's settlement terms are ONDC's `settlement_basis`, `settlement_window` and `withholding_amount`, carried unchanged. The PA marketplace limits (PA Master Direction paras 10(b) and 13(f)) stay open with RBI ([Q-51](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-51)).

## Money maps

These maps show who receives money from the payer's money, with no net figure.

**A kirana counter, paid by UPI at the shop.** The payer pays the shop's VPA. The merchant's acquiring bank and the PA, if any, take their costs from the merchant's side under their own agreements. BACP sees only the order total and the receipt's `rrn` and `utr`.

**An ONDC prepaid order.** The buyer app or the seller app collects (`collected_by`). The payer pays one amount. Settlement between the collector, the seller and any logistics provider follows ONDC's settlement terms. Who bears the collector's P2M MDR when the buyer app collects is open with ONDC ([Q-80](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-80)); this reading is an analysis, not a published rule.

**A direct-to-consumer order with a return.** The payer pays the total, including any disclosed charge lines. On a return the refund goes back to the original method. It equals the amount paid less only the lines that the terms disclosed as retained and that the Rules permit; a short refund gets `refund_short_of_terms`, and the money is not blocked.

**A B2B order on NEFT with net-30 terms.** The payer pays on the due date by NEFT, outside any quote line. MDR does not apply. A credit-ledger entry or a term sheet states the terms ([Credit and Split Tender](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/index.md)).

## How a seller or an operator can game the lines

These are the patterns the rules are written to catch.

- **Steering to MDR-free primitives.** A seller or a gateway ranks sellers by whether they carry a rail with no MDR. The default ranking must not use rungs, MDR or the finder fee ([Ranking by payment rungs](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#ranking-by-payment-rungs)).
- **Splitting.** An agent splits one order into payments under ₹2,000 to change the fee a seller bears. An agent SHOULD NOT do it, and the suspected-split-order check applies.
- **Uniform-fee recovery after para 7.5.** A seller that may not surcharge UPI charges the same convenience fee on every debit mode. That is lawful under para 7.5 when it is disclosed upfront; BACP does not warn on it, and the fee is in the total from round 1. A fee that first appears in a later round is drip pricing.
- **Mode-specific discounts.** A discount for one mode is the mirror of a surcharge on the others. Whether it is a negative surcharge under para 7.5 is open with counsel.
- **Discount for lock.** A discount offered only if the principal sets up a block or a mandate can nudge her to a rung that costs the seller less. BACP shows an offer with its condition ([Discounts](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#discounts)) and does not rule on whether such an offer is lawful.
- **Collector incidence.** On a buyer-app-collected order, the party that collects may be the P2M merchant. Which party bears the MDR is open ([Q-80](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-80)).
- **Operator incentives.** A recommender that is paid by the recommended seller is the main gaming risk. The operator discloses how it is paid in the mandate notice before the principal approves, an item whose selection is paid for is `sponsored` with `by: agent`, and the finder fee is never a quote line.

## What each human sees

- **A principal at a screen.** The total, each fee line with who receives it, and the remaining figure as one amount, before the factor.
- **A principal on voice, IVR or UPI 123PAY.** The same, read in her language from the Trusted Surface's own templates. A feature-phone or IVR principal never sees a payment page and cannot follow a hash, so each fee line is read one at a time. An order with no fee line adds no audio.
- **A principal whose agent pays on its own (HNP).** She agreed to the operator's compensation at mandate approval and, if she set `convenience_fees`, to a convenience fee up to her cap. Anything else raises a `confirm` step-up first.
- **A seller.** A seller's quote has no operator line: the operator's fee sits outside the BPP quote.

## Informative and normative

Every statement above about an NPCI FAQ is about an FAQ, which is not a circular. A statement about a rate in the future says "announced, not in force" until a date is notified. This page is re-checked at each release against the sources, and its dated facts (the MDR start, RBI/2017-18/105, the passage of Bill No. 150 of 2026) are re-verified then.

# Handler Registry

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

The handler registry lists every Indian payment mode BACP can bind to: 57 handlers across UPI, cards, net banking, account-to-account transfers, NACH, PPIs, credit, COD, BBPS, e-RUPI, e₹, AePS, transit, trade finance, cross-border, GeM, PA settlement, cheques and the BACP credit ledger. Each entry is a **handler descriptor**: a JSON document that validates against [`handler-descriptor.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/handler-descriptor.json).

Descriptors are **data**. Limits, AFA models, refund routes and notice rules are configuration that a gateway loads, not code. When a regulator changes a limit, the descriptor changes and the gateway's behaviour follows without a code release.

How handlers are used at payment time is defined in the [Payments Overview](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md). The rail-by-rail rules are in [Rail Bindings](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/rails/index.md).

## Descriptor format

A descriptor has the fields below. Required fields are marked **R**.

| Field                        | R   | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `handler_id`                 | R   | The canonical id: `in.<family>.<variant>` for an Indian rail or instrument, `bacp.<construct>` for a BACP-native construct. Pattern `common.json#/$defs/HandlerId`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `aliases[]`                  |     | Legacy ids that resolve to this handler during the deprecation window. A trailing `.*` makes a glob alias. See [alias resolution](#alias-resolution).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `name`                       | R   | Display name as language-tagged text, e.g. `{"en-IN": "UPI AutoPay (recurring e-mandate)"}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `family`                     | R   | Rail family: `upi`, `card`, `netbanking`, `a2a`, `nach`, `ppi`, `credit`, `cod`, `bbps`, `voucher`, `cbdc`, `aeps`, `transit`, `trade_finance`, `cross_border`, `government`, `pa`, `cheque`, `ledger`, `loyalty`, `store_credit`, `pos`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `kind`                       | R   | `payment`, `mandate_registration`, `financing`, `security_verification`, `tracker` or `ledger`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `status`                     | R   | `live`, `pilot`, `reserved` or `deprecated`. See [governance](#registry-governance).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `rail`                       | R   | `operator` (required), `network`, and `params` such as `qr_type`, `network`, `kyc`, `funding`, `direction`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `regulator[]`                | R   | One or more `{body, instrument, ref}`, e.g. `{"body": "RBI", "instrument": "E-mandate Framework 2026"}`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `presence`                   | R   | `human_presence` (`required`, `mandate` or `none`), `hp` (may run with a human present), `hnp` (`none`, `rail_enforced` or `order_only`), `device_bound`, `assisted_only`. `rail_enforced` means a standing authority whose limits the rail or issuer enforces. `order_only` means the order may be placed HNP but payment happens later with a human (COD).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `binding`                    | R   | `class` (`O`, `C`, `A`, `D` or `N`; see [handler classes](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#handler-classes)), `open_eligible`, `open_primitives[]` (the `mandate_primitives[].type` values that may back an open mandate; only primitives whose `limits_enforced_by` is `rail` or `issuer`, and at least one when `open_eligible` is `true`), `open_requires` (a condition in words, e.g. "only with an AFA-registered PPI e-mandate"), and `closed_auth[]`: the per-transaction authorisations a closed HP payment may use (`upi.pin`, `upi.biometric`, `card.3ds`, `card.otp`, `card.passkey`, `netbanking.login_otp`, `maker_checker`, `aadhaar_biometric`, `voucher_code`, `wallet_pin`, `kfs_esign`, `dsc`, `cash_at_door`, `parent_rail_binding`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `mandate_primitives[]`       | R   | The rail object that carries the standing authority: `type` (e.g. `sbmd_block`, `otm_block`, `circle_delegation`, `upi_autopay_umn`, `card_emandate`, `agentic_token_intent`, `nach_umrn`, `ppi_emandate`, `balance_cap`, `voucher`, `programmability_rules`, `upms_registration`, `topup_mandate`, `loan_sanction`, `payee_binding`, `approval_policy`, `assisted_session`, `credit_limit`, `factoring_unit`, `gpa_block`, `pps_registration`), `ref_name` (what `rail_binding.rail_ref` holds, e.g. UMN, UMRN, SBMD block id), `limits_enforced_by` (`rail`, `issuer`, `merchant`, `lender`, `bacp`, `none`), `payee_scope` (`single_merchant`, `single_biller`, `single_creditor`, `any_merchant`, `purpose_locked`, `issuer_contracted`, `lender`, `n_a`) and `multi_capture`. `issuer_contracted` means that a seller accepts the instrument only through a contract with its issuer, as for a gift PPI (RBI Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, paras 2.6 and 11.4.3), so that a gateway checks the seller's acceptance before it ranks the rung. |
| `limits[]`                   | R   | Each limit has a `name` (`per_txn`, `per_txn_min`, `per_day`, `per_month`, `per_year`, `first_24h`, `balance`, `block_amount`, `mandate_max`, `voucher_max`, `no_afa_debit`, `no_afa_debit_special_categories`, `validity`, `devices`, `pps_threshold`, `cash_threshold`), one of `amount` (integer paise), `duration` (ISO 8601) or `count`, an `applies_to` note, a `source` citation, a `verification` grade (`verified`, `secondary`, `vendor`, `unverified`, `conflict`), a `conflict_note` where sources disagree, `configurable`, and an optional `bound` (`min` or `max`) that says whether the value is a floor or a ceiling, for example the one-year minimum validity of a gift PPI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `afa`                        | R   | `model` (`per_txn_2fa`, `at_registration_and_first_debit`, `at_registration_only`, `at_block_creation`, `at_provisioning`, `exempt`, `exempt_below_threshold`, `biometric_assisted`, `maker_checker`, `loan_acceptance`, `voucher_code`, `none_cash`, `n_a`), `threshold` and `threshold_special` (amounts above which AFA is needed), `pre_debit_notice` (`required_24h`, `bacp_policy_24h`, `exempt`, `unknown`, `not_applicable`) `verification` (optional; how well the `source` citation was checked, on the scale of `limits[].verification`, so that an NPCI-layer citation is graded separately from the RBI layer), and `rbi_annex1_item` (the row of Annexure-1 of RBI/2025-26/79 that exempts the handler: REQUIRED when `model` is `exempt` or `exempt_below_threshold`, FORBIDDEN when it is `at_block_creation` or `at_registration_only`, so that Reserve Pay or UPI Circle is never labelled an RBI exemption; the upper bound is kept by the registry, because Annexure-1 says that later additions also apply).                                    |
| `refund`                     | R   | `route` (`source`, `source_with_card_credit_consent`, `same_ppi`, `release_block_or_source`, `lender`, `user_elected_account`, `same_balance`, `issuer_or_sponsor`, `new_credit_push`, `ledger_credit_note`, `n_a`, `unverified`), `failed_txn_tat` (ISO 8601 duration), `compensation_per_day`, `notes`. See [refunds](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/#refunds).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `dispute`                    | R   | `channels[]` (e.g. UDIR, issuer billing dispute, RBI Integrated Ombudsman, Bharat Connect complaints, GeM incident management) and `window`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `settlement`                 | R   | `mechanism` (free text), `evidence_refs[]` (the keys a receipt may carry: `rrn`, `utr`, `umn`, `umrn`, `arn`, `auth_code`, `bconnect_txn_id`, `voucher_id`, `cbdc_txn_id`, `factoring_unit_id`, `loan_id`, `lc_no`, `ebg_no`, `gem_order_no`, `crac_no`, `pfms_payment_id`, `pa_order_id`, `cheque_no`, `uetr`, `ledger_entry_id`, `awb`, `none`), `escrow` (`pa_escrow`, `none`, `gem_pool_account`, `platform`, `n_a`) and `timeline_source`. The PA-to-merchant timeline follows the PA–merchant agreement; there is no RBI T+N.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `data_minimisation`          | R   | `payment_leg_fields` (by default `payee`, `amount`, `mandate_ref`, `checkout_hash`), `never_collect` (always includes `pin`, `otp`, `card_pan`, `cvv`, `card_expiry`, `netbanking_credentials`, `aadhaar_number`, `biometric` and `basket`; vouchers add `voucher_code_plaintext`), `retain_only` (cards: last four digits and issuer) and `basket_blind`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `funding`                    | R   | `debit`, `credit`, `prepaid`, `cash`, `voucher`, `loan`, `cbdc`, `trade_credit` or `n_a`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `funding_sources[]`          |     | Every source of funds a payer can bring to the handler, when it is more than `funding`. It MUST contain `funding`. UPI Reserve Pay lists `debit` and `credit`, because a block can sit on a savings, current or overdraft account or on a RuPay credit card or a pre-sanctioned credit line (NPCI Consolidated Circular para 16.1). The source of a given mandate is the one its payer PSP attests, never the list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `credit_disclosure_required` |     | MUST be `true` when `funding` is `credit` or `loan`: the agent discloses that the payment is credit and holds the user's prior consent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `segments[]`                 |     | `b2c`, `b2b`, `g2b`, `c2c`, `assisted`, `cross_border`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `requirements[]`             |     | Identifiers of the requirements the descriptor implements (see [Regulatory Mapping](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/regulatory-mapping/index.md)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `sources[]`                  | R   | Citations for the descriptor's content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `notes`                      |     | Free text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The schema enforces these cross-field rules:

1. `binding.open_eligible: true` requires `presence.hnp: rail_enforced`.
1. `binding.open_eligible: true` requires a non-empty `binding.open_primitives`.
1. `presence.device_bound: true` requires `binding.open_eligible: false`.
1. `funding` of `credit` or `loan` requires `credit_disclosure_required: true`.
1. `presence.hnp: rail_enforced` requires at least one entry of `mandate_primitives` whose `limits_enforced_by` is `rail` or `issuer`. A descriptor whose limits only a merchant or BACP enforces is `hnp: none`.
1. `funding_sources`, when present, contains `funding`, and `binding.open_primitives` never lists `none`.

That every `binding.open_primitives` entry is one of the descriptor's own `mandate_primitives[].type` values with `limits_enforced_by` `rail` or `issuer` cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. `scripts/validate.py` checks it for the registry, and registry review MUST check it for a proposed descriptor.

An abridged descriptor (the `in.upi.autopay` entry, with optional fields and the per-field citations shortened) looks like this:

```
{
  "handler_id": "in.upi.autopay",
  "aliases": ["upi.autopay"],
  "name": {"en-IN": "UPI AutoPay (recurring e-mandate)"},
  "family": "upi",
  "kind": "payment",
  "status": "live",
  "rail": {"operator": "NPCI"},
  "regulator": [{"body": "RBI", "instrument": "E-mandate Framework 2026"}],
  "presence": {"human_presence": "mandate", "hp": true, "hnp": "rail_enforced"},
  "binding": {"class": "O", "open_eligible": true, "open_primitives": ["upi_autopay_umn"], "closed_auth": ["upi.pin"]},
  "mandate_primitives": [{"type": "upi_autopay_umn", "ref_name": "UMN", "limits_enforced_by": "rail", "payee_scope": "single_merchant", "multi_capture": true}],
  "limits": [
    {"name": "no_afa_debit", "amount": {"value": 1500000, "currency": "INR"},
     "source": {"file": "RBI E-mandate Framework 2026", "section": "8", "label": "RBI"}, "verification": "verified", "configurable": false}
  ],
  "afa": {"model": "at_registration_and_first_debit",
          "threshold": {"value": 1500000, "currency": "INR"},
          "threshold_special": {"value": 10000000, "currency": "INR"},
          "pre_debit_notice": "required_24h"},
  "refund": {"route": "source", "failed_txn_tat": "P5D", "compensation_per_day": {"value": 10000, "currency": "INR"}},
  "dispute": {"channels": ["UDIR in payer app", "MyUPI automated chargeback", "RBI Integrated Ombudsman"]},
  "settlement": {"mechanism": "NPCI UPI settlement cycles", "evidence_refs": ["rrn", "utr"], "escrow": "pa_escrow"},
  "data_minimisation": {"payment_leg_fields": ["payee", "amount", "mandate_ref", "checkout_hash"],
                        "never_collect": ["pin", "otp", "card_pan", "cvv", "card_expiry", "netbanking_credentials", "aadhaar_number", "biometric", "basket"],

  "sources": [{"file": "RBI E-mandate Framework 2026", "section": "8", "label": "RBI"}]

## Registry governance

The registry is maintained in the specification repository as `source/handlers/registry.json` and is versioned with the specification. Each descriptor has a `status`:

| Status       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | May back a payment                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `live`       | The rail or instrument is generally available, and its rules are documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Yes, subject to its class                                                                                                                                        |
| `pilot`      | The rail runs as a pilot or closed user group, or has no general availability (e.g. UPI Circle software delegates, network agentic card tokens, retail and programmable e₹, OCEN), or BACP has not verified how agents may use it (e-RUPI, until [Q-38](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-38) is answered). | Only when the gateway's [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation) lists that pilot in `pilots[]` |
| `reserved`   | The id is held for a rail that is not yet published or not open to agents (`in.upi.uap`, `in.cbdc.wholesale`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | No                                                                                                                                                               |
| `deprecated` | The handler is being withdrawn.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | No                                                                                                                                                               |

Rules for registry content:

- Every limit MUST cite its source and carry a `verification` grade. A limit graded `conflict` MUST carry a `conflict_note`. Where sources conflict, a gateway SHOULD enforce the stricter value unless the deployment documents a different choice.
- A limit whose regulator may change it SHOULD be `configurable: true`.
- A registry in which an exact alias maps to two descriptors, or a canonical id is also declared as an alias, MUST be rejected at load.
- Every descriptor MUST validate against [`handler-descriptor.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/handler-descriptor.json).
- Status changes (`pilot` to `live`, `reserved` to `pilot`) are registry changes and follow the [proposal process](#proposing-a-new-handler).
- Eligibility is evaluated against the current registry at every `complete`, not when a mandate was issued. A change that makes an active mandate's binding ineligible (a downgrade from `live` to `pilot`, `reserved` or `deprecated`, or a primitive removed from `binding.open_primitives`) pauses the affected mandates ([Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding)). Mandate Managers and gateways take the registry from the dated release, never from a gateway's `GET /payment-handlers`, and a gateway adopts a downgrade within 24 hours of the `published_at` of the publication that makes it. There is no registry-signed snapshot: no party holds a registry key.

### Release manifest

Each publication of the registry files has a release manifest, `source/handlers/release.json`, valid against [`registry-release.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/registry-release.json). It names the `registry_version`, a strictly increasing `registry_serial` (backports included), the `published_at` instant in IST and the `sha-256` digest, over the JCS form, of `registry.json` and of the conformance-authority list. A copy is newer than another when its serial is greater. `scripts/validate.py` recomputes the digests, and `scripts/registry_release.py --write` refreshes them after a registry change. The rules that use the serial and `published_at` are in [Handler binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#handler-binding) and the [versioning policy](https://bacp.dev/versioning/#registry-release-manifest).

### Conformance authorities

Who may sign the attestation that admits a `pilot` handler is data, like the handler status: the public, dated [conformance-authority list](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-authority-list), published as `source/registry/conformance-authorities.json` beside `source/handlers/registry.json` and valid against [`conformance-authority-list.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/conformance-authority-list.json).

- Each entry is scoped to named handlers (`scope.pilots`, at least one). An attestation that lists a pilot outside the signing entry's scope is refused.
- The list is the floor and the ceiling: a Mandate Manager MAY narrow it by publishing an exclusion list and MUST NOT add a signer to it.
- The list ships empty in `2026-10-18`. Until an entry is added, no pilot handler can back an open mandate.
- Adding an entry, and moving any handler from `pilot` to `live`, needs the approvals in [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#interim-maintainer).

### Reference patterns and receipt echo

A descriptor's `mandate_primitives[].ref_pattern` is an OPTIONAL regular expression that a `rail_binding.rail_ref` of that primitive has to match, so that a Mandate Manager can check the reference's shape. It is set only from a public source that states the format; no descriptor sets one in this version, and putting one on a `live` descriptor later is a breaking change. A payer-PSP-signed receipt SHOULD echo the mandate `primitive` and `rail.rail_ref` ([`receipt.json`](https://bacp.dev/schemas/receipt.json)), so that the gateway can reconcile it against the mandate's binding.

## Alias resolution

Settled

The `in.*` canonical ids, the alias rules below, the governance of handler names and the length of the deprecation window are settled in [Q-28](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-28).

A **handler reference** (`HandlerRef`) is a canonical id, an exact alias, or a string matched by a glob alias. It resolves as follows:

1. **Order.** First an exact canonical `handler_id`, then an exact alias, then a glob alias (`prefix.*`), longest prefix first.
1. **Exact beats glob.** An exact alias always wins over a glob alias. So `upi.uap.pin` resolves to `in.upi.intent`, not to `in.upi.uap`, whose glob alias is `upi.uap.*`.
1. **Globs never cover canonical ids.** A glob alias MUST NOT match any canonical id. It MUST NOT match an exact alias of another descriptor, except the deprecation-window aliases listed below, which MUST be removed when the window closes.
1. **One target.** An exact alias MUST map to exactly one canonical id.
1. **Emit canonical.** Producers MUST emit canonical ids in new artefacts: receipts, payment state, profiles, intersection results. Consumers MUST accept any handler reference and MUST compare handlers only after resolution, for example a session's handler against its mandate's `rail_binding.type`.
1. **Unknown fails closed.** A reference that does not resolve is not eligible: the intersection excludes it with `not_in_registry`, and at PUT or `complete` it gets 403 `mandate_scope_mismatch`.
1. **Resolution is not eligibility.** After resolution, the binding rules still apply: a `reserved` or `deprecated` descriptor MUST NOT back a payment, a `pilot` descriptor only when attested, and an open mandate only through a primitive in `binding.open_primitives`.
1. **Deprecation window.** Legacy aliases are accepted for one deprecation window: at least two dated releases after the release that deprecates them, and at least 180 days after that release, whichever is later ([versioning policy](https://bacp.dev/versioning/#deprecation)). Removing an alias is a breaking change and gets at least 90 days' notice. The registry SHOULD publish each alias's end date (a proposed descriptor field `aliases_deprecated_after`, not yet in the schema).

The registry declares two exact aliases of `in.upi.intent` for the deprecation window: `upi.pin` and `upi.uap.pin` (listed after the [registry table](#registry-table)). They identify a human-present one-off UPI payment authorised by UPI PIN. `auth_binding.type` stays `upi.pin`.

## Proposing a new handler

A new handler, or a change to an existing one (a new limit, a status change, a new alias), is proposed as a change to the registry:

1. **Open an issue** in the BACP repository titled `handler: <proposed id>`, with the rail, its operator and regulator, and the primary sources (circulars, master directions, operator product pages).
1. **Choose the id.** Use `in.<family>.<variant>` for an Indian rail or instrument and `bacp.<construct>` for a BACP-native construct. The id MUST match `HandlerId`, MUST NOT collide with an existing id or alias, and MUST NOT be matched by an existing glob alias.
1. **Write the descriptor** with every required field. Grade each limit honestly. A limit that comes only from a vendor or the press is `vendor` or `secondary`; one with no source is `unverified`.
1. **Classify it.** State the class and justify it against the RBI Authentication Directions 2025: a handler is class O only if a standing authority exists that the rail, issuer or both parties enforce, and the descriptor then has `hnp: rail_enforced`. An open-eligible descriptor lists in `binding.open_primitives` only primitives whose `limits_enforced_by` is `rail` or `issuer`. A device-bound handler is never open-eligible.
1. **Start at `pilot` or `reserved`** unless the rail is generally available with published rules.
1. **Add conformance cases.** A handler that a gateway claims under a conformance level needs cases for its binding, limits, AFA and refund route. See [Conformance](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/index.md).
1. **Validate.** The pull request MUST pass schema validation of the whole registry and the alias rules above.

The BACP working group reviews the proposal. A registry change is a normative change under [`GOVERNANCE.md`](https://github.com/bacp-dev/bacp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): it needs a 14-day review and the approval of two maintainers, one of them the payments editor, and ships in a dated release or an approved backport (settled in [Q-28](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-28)).

## Registry table

The table below is generated from `source/handlers/registry.json`. "Presence allowed" summarises `presence`: HP means a human-present payment, "HNP (rail-enforced)" means the handler may run with no human present under a standing authority, "HNP order only" means the order may be placed HNP with payment later. "Mandate binding" lists the `mandate_primitives` types. The full limits, AFA models, dispute channels and settlement evidence are in the JSON.

| #   | Handler id                      | Name                                                                    | Class | Presence allowed            | Mandate binding                    | Refund route                      | Status   |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------- |
| 1   | `in.upi.intent`                 | UPI intent                                                              | C     | HP                          | —                                  | `source`                          | live     |

# Rail Bindings

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

This page binds the [payment model](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/index.md) to each Indian rail family. For every family it gives the handlers, the limits with the regulation or operator text they come from, the authentication model, how a mandate binds, and the refund and dispute path. The descriptors in the [Handler Registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md) carry the same values as data, together with a verification grade for each limit.

**How to read the limits.**

- A limit taken from an RBI direction or an NPCI publication that was checked against the primary text is stated plainly.
