| Source       | NPCI IMPS page; RBI/2019-20/67                                                                                                                                                                                       | RBI NEFT FAQ                                                                                                                                        | RBI RTGS FAQ; RBI press release 2020-2021/748                                                                             |

**Payee binding.** Before any credit to a new payee, BACP MUST perform a beneficiary name look-up and store a `PayeeBinding` record: account, IFSC, returned name, timestamp and look-up reference. RTGS and NEFT members must offer Beneficiary Account Name Look-up, free of charge, from 01-04-2025 (RBI/2024-25/99, 30-12-2024). The user sees only the bank-returned name, never a merchant-supplied display name, and the agent cannot edit it. A payment to an account whose looked-up name does not match the invoiced seller is held for human confirmation.

**Rail selection.** The gateway MUST refuse RTGS below ₹2,00,000 and IMPS above ₹5,00,000 (configurable), and defaults to NEFT otherwise.

**Authentication.** Retail transfers need the remitter bank's 2FA every time, so they are human-present. For a business, the agent MAY act as **maker**, preparing a validated payment instruction, while a human **checker** approves it under the corporate's bank entitlement. The payment stays in state `pending_approval` until the checker event is logged, and the agent MUST NOT release it. Whether corporate host-to-host flows are exempt from the 2025 AFA rule is not verified.

**Evidence and refunds.** Every settled transfer records its UTR. There is no payer-initiated refund: the payee pushes a new credit. An unconfirmed IMPS credit enters reversal tracking (T+1, ₹100 per day). The refund-settlement signal for IMPS is open ([Q-49](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-49)).

## BBPS (Bharat Connect)

Handlers: `in.bbps.bill` (alias `bbps`), `in.bbps.b2b_invoice`, `in.bbps.upms`. The Bharat Bill Payment System is governed by the RBI BBPS Directions 2024 (29-02-2024, effective 01-04-2024) and operated as Bharat Connect by NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited (NBBL).

| Item       | Rule                                                                                                                      | Source                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Limits     | None at network level; the payment instrument's limits apply                                                              | NBBL *(not verified as of 17-10-2026)*                    |
| Settlement | 8 cycles a day to billers                                                                                                 | NBBL *(not verified as of 17-10-2026)*                    |
| Complaints | NBBL must run a centralised, end-to-end complaint management system; TATs per NBBL procedural guidelines *(not verified)* | RBI BBPS Directions 2024 (RBI/DPSS/2023-24/111) para 8(i) |
| B2B        | Bharat Connect for Business: over 20 lakh invoice-based transactions in Q3 FY26                                           | NBBL press release, 26-02-2026                            |
| Recurring  | UPMS presents bills and auto-pays them; its mandate types are not verified                                                | NBBL                                                      |

Binding rules:

- A bill payment runs bill fetch, validation and payment through a customer operating unit, and MUST store the Biller ID, the bill reference and the Bharat Connect transaction reference (`bconnect_txn_id`). Bill fetch is a consented read that an agent may do on its own; a one-off payment is human-present.
- `in.bbps.b2b_invoice` payments MUST carry the seller's GST IRN and the buyer's GSTIN, and MUST be refused if the amount differs from the fetched invoice. They run under a maker-checker approval policy.
- `in.bbps.upms` (class O) binds a UPMS registration to an underlying instrument mandate (a UPI AutoPay UMN, a card standing instruction or a NACH UMRN) and inherits that instrument's limits and notice rule. For example, a ₹15,001 bill debit under UPI AutoPay needs AFA.

## e-RUPI

Handler: `in.erupi` (alias `erupi`). Class O, status `pilot` until [Q-38](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-38) is answered.

e-RUPI is a purpose-bound prepaid voucher on UPI rails, launched in August 2021 with a cap of ₹10,000 per voucher, redeemable once (RBI, 10-02-2022).

| Item                | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Source                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Government vouchers | ₹1,00,000 per voucher, redeemable several times until exhausted. RBI "proposed" this and said instructions to NPCI would follow; the NPCI instruction was not verified as of 17-10-2026.                                                  | RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies, 10-02-2022 (Press Release 2021-2022/1694), item 6 |
| Wider issuance      | RBI proposed issuance by non-bank PPI issuers and on behalf of individuals, and changes to reloading, authentication and issuance limits, with "separate instructions" to follow. Whether those instructions were issued is not verified. | RBI press release 2023-2024/365, 08-06-2023, item 6                                                       |
| Authentication      | The beneficiary presents the voucher code (QR or SMS) and confirms with a verification code.                                                                                                                                              | NPCI                                                                                                      |
| Refund              | Unredeemed value returns to the issuer or sponsor on expiry. Merchant refunds after redemption are not verified.                                                                                                                          | NPCI                                                                                                      |

Binding rules:

- The voucher is the mandate: purpose, eligible merchant or merchant category, remaining balance and expiry are mirrored into the BACP mandate. The handler MUST enforce them before redemption, and MUST support partial multi-use redemption for multi-use vouchers.
- Issuer-type caps (government, corporate, individual; bank or non-bank) are configuration, pending confirmation of the 2023 changes.
- Voucher codes are never shown to the agent.
- e-RUPI is open-eligible only where redemption without the beneficiary present is supported ([Q-38](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-38)). Until Q-38 is answered the descriptor's status is `pilot`, so an open mandate may bind to it only at a gateway whose [conformance attestation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/conformance/#conformance-attestation) lists `in.erupi` in `pilots[]`.

## e₹ (CBDC)

Handlers: `in.cbdc.retail` (alias `erupee`; class C, pilot), `in.cbdc.programmed` (class O, pilot), `in.cbdc.wholesale` (class N, reserved).

| Item            | Rule                                                                                                                                                                              | Source              |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Retail e₹       | Pilot since 01-12-2022: bank-distributed tokens, wallet-to-wallet P2P and P2M, UPI-QR interoperability. Still a pilot as of 17-10-2026 (reported, not verified as of 17-10-2026). | RBI CBDC FAQ; press |
| Programmability | Rules on expiry, geography, merchant category and merchant VPA; used for DBT, subvention, lending and allowances                                                                  | RBI CBDC FAQ        |
| Offline e₹      | Unveiled at GFF in October 2025                                                                                                                                                   | *(press)*           |
| Wholesale e₹    | Launched 01-11-2022 for G-sec settlement; deposit-tokenisation pilot from 08-10-2025                                                                                              | *(press)*           |
| Limits          | Wallet holding and transaction caps are set per pilot bank                                                                                                                        | *(not verified)*    |

Binding rules:

- When settling in e₹, BACP MUST compile the mandate constraints (expiry, geography, merchant category, merchant VPA, amount) into a programmability rule set, and MUST refuse settlement where the token's rules conflict with the mandate.
- Offline e₹ payments MUST be marked `offline=true` with a deferred-sync state, and MUST NOT be initiated autonomously by an agent.
- Refunds are a push back from the merchant. Programmed tokens that expire revert to the sponsor (mechanics not verified).
- `in.cbdc.wholesale` is reserved and institutional only. It never backs a payment.

## AePS and Aadhaar Pay

Handler: `in.aeps.assisted`. Class A, assisted only.

| Item               | Rule                                                                                                                                            | Source                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Operator duties    | Acquiring banks run customer due diligence on every AePS touchpoint operator (ATO) before onboarding and apply risk controls                    | RBI AePS ATO Due Diligence Directions 2025 (RBI/2025-26/63, 27-06-2025, effective 01-01-2026) para 2.1   |
| Inactive operators | An ATO that has performed no transaction for a customer for 3 continuous months must be re-KYCed by the acquiring bank before transacting again | RBI/2025-26/63 para 2.2                                                                                  |
| Cash withdrawal    | Up to ₹10,000 in a single transaction                                                                                                           | NPCI/2021-22/AEPS/002 (18-08-2021), citing AePS Circular 3 of 25-01-2016 (not verified as of 17-10-2026) |
| Authentication     | Aadhaar number plus the account holder's biometric, in person at a business correspondent or micro-ATM                                          | NPCI; RBI Authentication Directions 2025                                                                 |
| TAT                | AePS or Aadhaar Pay debited without merchant confirmation: credit adjustment within T+5, ₹100 per day after that                                | RBI/2019-20/67, Annex row 5a                                                                             |

Binding rules:

- AePS and Aadhaar Pay MUST be human-present at an assisted touchpoint. The binding is an `AssistedSession`: ATO id, terminal id, the RRN, and an order hash.
- The order summary and amount MUST be shown, and spoken in the user's language, before biometric capture. The AI agent MUST NOT trigger the capture and is never the authenticator.
- BACP MUST reject a session from an ATO flagged inactive for 3 months or more without re-KYC, where the acquirer exposes that flag.
- BACP never collects the Aadhaar number or the biometric.

## FASTag, NCMC and transit

Handlers: `in.ppi.netc_topup`, `in.ppi.ncmc_topup` (class O) and `in.ppi.transit` (class C).

| Item                  | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Source                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FASTag                | NETC FASTags are bank-issued PPIs; KYC at issue. NETC transactions are exempt from AFA (Annexure-1 row 4). BACP reads a FASTag top-up made inside NETC as an NETC transaction, because neither Annexure-1 nor the RBI circular of 30-12-2019 names a top-up (as of 18-10-2026; [Q-103](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-103)).                                                                          | NPCI NETC *(not verified as of 17-10-2026)*; RBI Authentication Directions 2025, Annexure-1 item 4; RBI/2019-20/126, 30-12-2019, para 4 |
| Auto top-up notice    | E-mandates that auto-replenish FASTag and NCMC balances need no pre-transaction notification. A post-transaction notification is still required. This notice rule is separate from authentication: no Annexure-1 row names an NCMC top-up, so an NCMC top-up claims no authentication exemption and is authenticated under para 6(a) of the Directions ([Q-103](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-103)). | E-mandate Framework 2026 paras 6(d), 7                                                                                                  |
| FASTag Annual Pass    | ₹3,000 for one year or 200 trips at NH and NE fee plazas from 15-08-2025, bought only through the Rajmargyatra app or the NHAI site                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | *(press; NPCI and NHAI text not verified as of 17-10-2026)*                                                                             |
| NCMC offline wallet   | ₹500 per offline transaction and ₹2,000 in total per instrument at any time (the 2024 uplift to ₹1,000 and ₹5,000 is for UPI Lite only)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | RBI/2023-24/57, 24-08-2023, para 2; RBI/2024-25/93 para 1                                                                               |
| PPI-MTS (transit PPI) | Outstanding balance ≤ ₹3,000, no KYC, no AFA, reloadable, perpetual validity; no cash-out, refund or transfer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | PPI MD para 10.2                                                                                                                        |

Binding rules:

- A FASTag, NCMC or transit top-up by an agent MUST run under an AFA-registered top-up mandate with threshold and amount fields. BACP MUST NOT require or send a pre-debit notice where the e-mandate framework exempts it, but MUST send a post-debit notice. An NCMC top-up carries no `rbi_annex1_item` and takes authentication under the descriptor's `per_txn_2fa` model.
- Transit and NCMC offline caps are configurable, defaulting to the values above. A ₹3,001 PPI-MTS load and a ₹501 NCMC offline debit are refused.
- The toll or transit spend itself is tag- or card-present and involves no agent. Buying the FASTag Annual Pass is a human-present payment on the official channels.

## Other B2B and cross-border rails

These handlers mostly track or verify rather than pay. They are listed here for completeness; the financing ones are in [Credit and Split Tender](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/index.md).

| Handler                   | Class | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Source                                  |
| ------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `in.xb.pacb`              | C     | PA cross-border collection or payment, capped at ₹25,00,000 per transaction; carries the export invoice or EDF reference. Outbound card payments need cross-border AFA.                                                                    | RBI PA MD 2025 para 11(d)               |
| `in.pa.settlement`        | N     | Read-only PA settlement status. The settlement timeline comes from the PA–merchant agreement.                                                                                                                                              | RBI PA MD 2025 para 16(a)               |
| `in.cheque.positive_pay`  | C     | Record and track cheques. Banks must enable Positive Pay for cheques of ₹50,000 and above and may make it mandatory from ₹5,00,000. BACP requires a Positive Pay reference before marking a cheque payment of ₹5,00,000 or more as issued. | RBI/2020-21/41, 25-09-2020              |
| `in.gov.gem`              | N     | GeM order and payment tracking: payment within 10 days of CRAC, 1% a month delay interest retained by GeM. See [trade credit](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#gem-receivables).                | DoE OM of 03-07-2020; GeM GTC clause 12 |
| `in.fin.lc`, `in.fin.ebg` | N     | Verify and track letters of credit and e-bank guarantees (NeSL e-BG platform) before treating them as payment security.                                                                                                                    | ICC UCP 600; NeSL                       |

# Beckn / ONDC Binding

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

BACP is an agent layer over Beckn and ONDC, not a fork. The BACP gateway speaks ordinary Beckn on the network leg, adds agent semantics in a namespaced extension that network participants who do not speak BACP can ignore, and hardens the transport for machine clients (mandatory idempotency, callback binding, replay protection). This page defines that binding. The agent-facing side is the [REST binding](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/index.md).

## Roles

- **The BACP gateway is the BAP.** It runs inside, or on behalf of, a registered buyer app (BAP). The agent operator either is that BAP or contracts with one. The BAP subscriber (`bap_id`, registry key `subscriber_id|ukid`) is the network-visible party; the agent never talks to the network directly.
- **Seller apps (BPPs)** are ordinary Beckn providers. A BACP-aware BPP additionally reads `context.bacp`, verifies the closed checkout mandate's key-binding JWT and enforces the negotiation rules. A BPP that is not BACP-aware still interoperates, because the gateway verifies on its behalf and the evidence binds through the BPP-signed quote.
- **The Beckn gateway (BG)** routes `search` on `context` only and MUST NOT see personal data or mandate content beyond `context.bacp`.
- **The registry** (the ONDC registry or a Beckn 2.0 DeDi record) holds subscriber keys and, by default, issues AgentCredentials ([Q-02](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-02)).

Money does not move on Beckn. Beckn carries payment *terms*; the gateway moves money through the payer PSP and reports it in `confirm` with `payment.status: PAID` and the rail reference.

## Action mapping

### Commerce operations

| BACP operation (REST)                                    | Beckn / ONDC request → callback                                                                                                                                   | Mandate `action_scope` | Signature tag     |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| `POST /discover`                                         | `search` → `on_search` via the BG and registry lookup (Beckn 2.0 also exposes `/discover` over signed catalogue indexes)                                          | DISCOVER (optional)    | `bacp-browse`     |
| `GET /discover/{transaction_id}/sources/{source_digest}` | none; serves the `on_search` callback the gateway kept ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results))    | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `POST /sessions`                                         | `select` → `on_select` (quote with TTL)                                                                                                                           | QUOTE                  | `bacp-browse`     |
| `PUT /sessions/{session_id}`                             | `select` (items changed) or `init` → `on_init` (billing, fulfilment, payment terms, seller-signed quote, disclosures)                                             | ORDER, SHARE_DATA      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `POST /sessions/{session_id}/complete`                   | Rail debit through the payer PSP, then `confirm` → `on_confirm` with `payment.status=PAID` and the rail reference                                                 | ORDER + PAY            | `bacp-pay`        |
| `POST /sessions/{session_id}/cancel`                     | none (no order exists yet)                                                                                                                                        | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `GET /orders/{order_id}`                                 | `status` → `on_status`; unsolicited `on_status` updates the order                                                                                                 | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `POST /orders/{order_id}/cancel`                         | `get_cancellation_reasons`, then `cancel` → `on_cancel`; a seller-side cancel arrives as an unsolicited `on_cancel`                                               | CANCEL                 | `bacp-post-order` |
| `POST /orders/{order_id}/returns`                        | `get_return_reasons`, then `update` with `update_target=item` → `on_update` (Return_Initiated → Return_Approved → Return_Picked → Return_Delivered or Liquidated) | RETURN                 | `bacp-post-order` |
| `GET /orders/{order_id}/returns/{return_id}`             | read model over `on_update` / `on_cancel` refund state                                                                                                            | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `POST /issues`, `POST /issues/{issue_id}/actions`        | IGM `issue` → `on_issue`                                                                                                                                          | RAISE_ISSUE            | `bacp-post-order` |
| `GET /issues/{issue_id}`                                 | none; the gateway's issue snapshot, kept current from IGM `on_issue` callbacks (IGM 2.0 has no `issue_status`)                                                    | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `GET /evidence/{transaction_id}`                         | none; referenced from the IGM issue, joined to the payment dispute channel by the rail reference                                                                  | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| `POST /mandates` and the other mandate operations        | none (off-network: Mandate Manager and payer PSP)                                                                                                                 | —                      | `bacp-browse`     |
| (Trusted Surface) revoke, pause, resume, step-up result  | none (signed Mandate Manager or PSP event to `/trusted-surface/events`)                                                                                           | —                      | `bacp-ts`         |

Proposed, with no REST operation yet: order tracking (`track` → `on_track`), rating (`rating` → `on_rating`, or Beckn 2.0 `/rate`) and human handoff (`support` → `on_support`).

**Post-order rules.** Cancel policy errors 50001 and 50002 map to `cancel_not_allowed`. A return refund MUST be issued exactly once, on the first of `Liquidated` or `Return_Delivered`, to the original payment method. The order state remains Beckn's authoritative machine (`Created → Accepted → In-progress → Completed | Cancelled`).

### Negotiation operations

| BACP                                                                                                  | Beckn 1.x / ONDC carrier                                                                                                                                      | Beckn 2.0                                    | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Capability advert                                                                                     | `on_search` provider tag `bacp.negotiation`                                                                                                                   | provider attributes, `Offer.offerAttributes` |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| RFQ (`POST /rfqs`)                                                                                    | `select` with a `bacp.neg.rfq` TagGroup and `context.ttl` P1D; one `select` per BPP under one `rfq_id`                                                        | `select` with contract DRAFT                 | ONDC B2B treats `select` as the RFQ                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Seller offer, quotation or counter                                                                    | `on_select` with `quote` (= `all_in_total`), `quote.ttl` derived from `expires_at`, plus a `bacp.neg.offer` TagGroup                                          | `on_select` with `Offer.validity`            | `quote.price` ≠ `all_in_total` is drip pricing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Buyer counter (`POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/offers`)                                          | `select` again, same `transaction_id`, next round                                                                                                             | `select` / `update`                          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Seller-paced message (auction tick, counter after silence, WITHDRAW)                                  | Unsolicited `on_select` within the transaction; fallback: the buyer polls with `select`                                                                       | `on_select`                                  | [Q-26](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-26)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Per-issue status                                                                                      | ONDC `*_status` Assert / Agree / Disagree / Terminate, generalised to every TermSheet issue                                                                   | `SettlementTerm.committed`                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ACCEPT (`POST /negotiations/{negotiation_id}/accept`)                                                 | `init` carrying `bacp.neg.accept` plus billing                                                                                                                | `init`                                       | An `init` without `bacp.neg.accept` in a BACP negotiation is not an acceptance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| BOUND                                                                                                 | `on_init` echoing the identical term-sheet hash in the seller-signed quote                                                                                    | `on_init`                                    | Any difference is `NEG_TERMS_DRIFT`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Purchase order                                                                                        | `confirm` with `offer_hash` and `BAP_TERMS.ACCEPT_BPP_TERMS`                                                                                                  | `confirm`                                    | The PO MUST NOT alter terms                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| PO acceptance                                                                                         | `on_confirm` → CONTRACTED                                                                                                                                     | `on_confirm`, contract ACTIVE                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| REJECT                                                                                                | `on_select` / `on_init` error (for example 50005) or `bacp.neg.reject`                                                                                        | same                                         | Typed reasons                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ACCEPT_REVOKE                                                                                         | Not carried in this version                                                                                                                                   | —                                            | A firm offer with `acceptance_revocation: allowed_until_receipt` is refused with `capabilities_incompatible`, on every leg in this version and on a Beckn leg until a carrier exists ([Q-22](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-22))                                                                                                                   |
| Firm offer with `waived` and no `waiver_basis`, or in a consumer session any `waived` offer (interim) | `on_select` or `select` with the `bacp.neg.offer` TagGroup                                                                                                    | same                                         | The only schema error excused is the missing `waiver_basis`. Never accepted by an agent. The buyer accepts only through a Trusted Surface step-up (`requires_buyer_review`); a human seller only in the BPP app with the consequence sentence shown ([Acceptance revocation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation))                     |
| Buyer withdrawal of a purchase offer (`withdraw` with `accept_msg_hash`), and a buyer `terminate`     | Not carried in this version: a carrier would be an `init` withdrawn before `on_init`, which is not defined                                                    | —                                            | Until ONDC defines one, the `purchase_offered_by_agent` notice on a Beckn leg shows no stop control, and the principal's only exit is the decline of an `AGREED` or `BOUND` deal under the terms ([Decline](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#decline-of-an-agreed-or-bound-deal)); [Q-22](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-22) |
| Auction                                                                                               | AuctionSpec in `on_search` from the auctioneer's endpoint; bids are `select` to the auctioneer; award by `on_select`, then `init` / `confirm` with the winner | `Offer` + `availableTo`                      | [Q-25](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-25)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

**Receipts on a Beckn leg.** A Beckn message is **ordered** for the [committed-order rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#contested-crossings) only when a `bacp.receipt` TagGroup in the `Ack` of the same exchange carries a CounterSignature (the compact JWS whose payload is a `CounterSignaturePayload`).

- The CounterSignature MUST verify on its own as a JWS by the counterparty's registry key. Transport `Ack` signing is not required ([Q-43](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-43)), so the tag cannot borrow trust from the transport.
- An `Ack` with no receipt, an unverifiable receipt or a NACK leaves that message **unordered**, and every crossing that depends on it is contested.
- On re-delivery with the same `message_id` and `msg_hash` the receiver returns the identical receipt (same `log_seq`). A second receipt with another `log_seq` is `evidence_unverifiable`.
- Beckn 1.1.1 `Ack` carries `tags: TagGroup[]` and ONDC RET 1.2.5 `Ack` does too; ONDC's core v0 `Ack` has `status` only. Whether ONDC validators and live participants accept a `bacp.receipt` TagGroup is not verified as of 18-10-2026 ([Q-22](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-22)). The rule is the same either way. If ONDC refuses it, every Beckn crossing is contested, both principals review it, and it closes `crossing_unconfirmed` if they do not answer; Beckn deals with no crossing are unaffected.
- `context.timestamp` stays `…Z` as the ONDC validator requires. BACP-owned times follow the [IST rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#signed-seller-acceptance-and-clock-skew).

`context.bacp.mandate_ref` always points to the **checkout** mandate. The negotiation mandate never travels; only the `within_bounds` attestation does. See [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/index.md).

## The `context.bacp` extension

Schema: <https://bacp.dev/schemas/beckn-context-bacp.json>.

The gateway MUST add `context.bacp` to the `context` of every BACP-originated Beckn message, including IGM messages. The key is `bacp`, not `agent`, because "agent" in Beckn means a fulfilment agent.

| Field                                         | Required                                                                                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent.id`                                    | yes                                                                                         | The agent's id from its AgentCredential (`sub`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `agent.credential_hash`                       | yes                                                                                         | Hash of the presented AgentCredential                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `agent.operator`                              | yes                                                                                         | The operator's legal entity id as `<type>:<value>`, where the type is `CIN`, `LLPIN`, `GSTIN` or `PAN`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `agent.class`, `agent.uap_agent_id`           | no                                                                                          | Agent class; slot reserved for an NPCI UAP id                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `presence`                                    | yes                                                                                         | `HP` (human present) or `HNP` (human not present)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `idempotency_key`                             | yes                                                                                         | The agent's `Idempotency-Key`, carried end to end (22–64 characters)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `mandate_ref`                                 | on `init`, `confirm`, `update`, `cancel` and IGM `issue`; optional on `search` and `select` | `{id, hash}` of the open checkout mandate, plus `kb_jwt`: the agent's key-binding JWT with `aud` = `bpp_id` and `nonce` = the `confirm` `message_id`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `log_head`                                    | on every committing message                                                                 | The current InstructionLog head, which anchors the log to network-signed traffic                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `ai_disclosure`                               | yes                                                                                         | Constant `true`: an AI agent originated the message. Also mirrored in the `bacp` tag group ([Mirroring](#mirroring))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `acting_for`                                  | no                                                                                          | `{kind, gstin, display_name}`: whom the agent acts for, `kind` being `individual` or `business`. `gstin` and `display_name` are sent only when the mandate's `data_scopes` include `ACTING_FOR`, and otherwise omitted; a sole proprietor's GSTIN or name is personal data                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `operator_name`, `operator_grievance_contact` | no                                                                                          | The agent operator's legal name and its grievance officer's contact                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `profile`                                     | no                                                                                          | The one [trade profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/trade-profiles/#profile-table) the session declares, fixed when the session opens; a later message with another profile is refused with `capabilities_incompatible`. With none, or when the buyer side's `acting_for.kind` is `individual` or it sends no `acting_for`, the session is a consumer session for [acceptance revocation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#acceptance-revocation) |
| `channel`, `language`                         | no                                                                                          | For example `voice`, `hi-IN`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `version`                                     | no                                                                                          | Extension version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

No other keys are allowed (`additionalProperties: false`).

```
{
  "agent": {
    "id": "did:web:agents.vaani.example.in:sakhi",
    "credential_hash": "sha-256:n4bQgYhMfWWaL-qgxVrQFaO_TxsrC4Is0V1sFbDwCgg",
    "operator": "CIN:U72900KA2025PTC000000",
    "class": "voice_shopping",
    "uap_agent_id": null
  },
  "presence": "HNP",
  "mandate_ref": {
    "id": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3",
    "hash": "sha-256:47DEQpj8HBSa-_TImW-5JCeuQeRkm5NMpJWZG3hSuFU",
    "kb_jwt": "eyJhbGciOiJFZERTQSIsInR5cCI6ImtiK2p3dCJ9.eyJhdWQiOiJicHAua2lyYW5hLmV4YW1wbGUuaW4ifQ.c2lnbmF0dXJl"
  },
  "idempotency_key": "01HZX8W3T6Q9M2R7C4B1N8K5D0",
  "channel": "voice",
  "language": "hi-IN",
  "ai_disclosure": true,
  "log_head": "sha-256:LCa0a2j_xo_5m0U8HTBBNBNCLXBkg7-g-YpeiGJm564",
  "version": "2026-10-18"
}
```

### Message ids

The gateway MUST derive the Beckn `message_id` as `UUIDv5(ns, agent_id | idempotency_key | action)`, so that a retried agent call re-sends an identical message. The name that UUIDv5 hashes is the UTF-8 bytes of the string `agent_id + "|" + idempotency_key + "|" + action`, joined by the literal character `|` with no spaces. `agent_id` is the `sub` of the AgentCredential that signed the request, `idempotency_key` is the value of the `Idempotency-Key` header exactly as sent, and `action` is the Beckn `context.action` of the message (for example `search` or `confirm`). The gateway MUST publish the namespace `ns` in its profile as `message_id_namespace`, so that a BACP-aware BPP can check the key-binding JWT's `nonce`.

Worked example: for the namespace `55884fda-3b41-58be-87a9-2be7b3b43b7f`, `agent_id` `did:web:agents.vaani.example.in:sakhi`, `Idempotency-Key` `idem_7Q2W9X4K1M3` and action `search`, the name is `did:web:agents.vaani.example.in:sakhi|idem_7Q2W9X4K1M3|search` and the `message_id` is `7d225f10-d430-5b7b-9826-0c7621e7fdd5`.

### Mirroring into tags

ONDC 1.x validators may reject unknown `context` keys, because the ONDC core context schema is fixed. Until ONDC accepts `context.bacp` ([Q-09](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-09)), the gateway MUST also mirror it into `message.order.tags[]` as a TagGroup with `descriptor.code = "bacp"` (FQDN-namespaced tag keys are allowed), and into the IGM issue's description tags. The mirror MUST carry at least `presence`, `mandate_ref` (the mandate id), `log_head` and `ai_disclosure` (`"true"`), so that a seller learns that an AI agent is ordering even when a validator strips `context.bacp`. It MAY also carry `acting_for` (as `acting_for.kind`, `acting_for.gstin` and `acting_for.display_name`), `operator_name` and `operator_grievance_contact`. `acting_for` names whom the agent acts for. The gateway sends `acting_for.gstin` and `acting_for.display_name`, in `context.bacp` and in the mirror, only when the mandate's `data_scopes` include `ACTING_FOR` and a per-seller ConsentReceipt of that seller lists `ACTING_FOR` in its `data_items[]`; without both it omits both tags. A sole proprietor's GSTIN or name is personal data ([Human participants](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ai-disclosure)).

```
{
  "descriptor": {"code": "bacp"},
  "list": [
    {"descriptor": {"code": "ai_disclosure"}, "value": "true"},
    {"descriptor": {"code": "operator_name"}, "value": "Vaani Voice Commerce Pvt Ltd"},
    {"descriptor": {"code": "presence"}, "value": "HNP"},
    {"descriptor": {"code": "mandate_ref"}, "value": "mdt_CHK7Q2W9X4K1M3"},
    {"descriptor": {"code": "log_head"}, "value": "sha-256:LCa0a2j_xo_5m0U8HTBBNBNCLXBkg7-g-YpeiGJm564"}
  ]
}
```

Every `bacp.neg.*` object is likewise carried as a namespaced TagGroup.

### Catalogue disclosure mapping

A seller app sends the disclosure fields of a [discover item](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#catalogue-disclosures) in the signed `on_search`. The gateway and an agent that checks a result against its signed source MUST derive the same values from the same body, so the mapping below is normative.

| BACP field                                      | Beckn / ONDC source in the signed `on_search`                                                                                                             | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unit_price`                                    | item `price.value`                                                                                                                                        | Decimal rupees string, converted to integer paise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `mrp`                                           | item `price.maximum_value`                                                                                                                                | As above                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tax_inclusive`                                 | item TagGroup `bacp.disclosure`, tag `tax_inclusive` (`"true"` or `"false"`)                                                                              | An absent tag means an absent field                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `prior_price.amount`, `.basis`, `.announced_on` | `bacp.disclosure` tags `prior_price`, `prior_price_basis`, `prior_price_announced_on`                                                                     | `basis` MUST be `lowest_30d`; the date is an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `sponsorship`, party `bpp`                      | `bacp.disclosure` tags `sponsored` (`"true"`) and `sponsored_by` (`bpp`)                                                                                  | Combined with the gateway's own statements by the monotone OR rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `requires_principal_confirmation`               | provider TagGroup `bacp.confirmation`, tags `reason` (`made_to_order`, `age_restricted` or `high_value_cod`) and `above_amount` (a decimal rupees string) | `above_amount` is REQUIRED for `high_value_cod` and absent otherwise; it follows the decimal rule below. The same tags in an `on_init` order that the seller did not declare at discovery are an undeclared confirmation ([Seller confirmation profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#principal-confirmation)) |

`price.listed_value` and `price.offered_value` never map to `prior_price`, and the gateway MUST NOT derive a `prior_price` from any Beckn `Price` field. Until ONDC publishes catalogue tags for sponsored listings and prior prices ([Q-69](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-69)), the tag names above are BACP's. The field names in BACP stay when ONDC's tags arrive; only this mapping changes.

An agent that checks a result against its signed source ([Verifying discovery results](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#verifying-results)) derives the values by this mapping, exactly as the gateway does.

**Locating an item.** The provider list is `message.catalog["bpp/providers"]` (ONDC) or `message.catalog.providers` (Beckn core). If both are present, or the provider whose `id` equals the result's provider id occurs other than exactly once, nothing can be derived from the body. Within that provider, the item whose `id` equals the result's item `id` MUST occur exactly once; otherwise nothing can be derived for it. Ids compare as decoded code-point sequences, without Unicode normalisation.

**Decimal rule.** A price field MUST be a JSON string that matches `^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,11})(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$`. The value in paise is the integer part times 100 plus the fractional part right-padded to two digits, computed on the string and never in floating point. Any other form (a JSON number, a sign, an exponent, a leading zero, more than two decimals) makes the field absent, and the gateway reports `prior_price_invalid` when the field was `prior_price`.

### Seller refusals, requests for confirmation and substitution

A seller can say why it refuses, and can ask for the buyer's own confirmation, only in a BPP-signed message. The gateway reads each reason from the signed message and from nowhere else, and seller prose reaches the principal only in the labelled `counterparty_text` slot.

**The seller asks for confirmation.** A BPP MAY send the tag `seller_confirmation` in the `bacp` tag group of a BPP-signed `on_select` or `on_init`, with a value of `first_cod_order`, `above_seller_threshold`, `new_credit_line`, `credit_limit_exceeded` or `other`.

- The gateway, never the agent, turns it into a `confirm` step-up with reason `seller_confirmation` and a Trusted Surface template sentence for the value (draft wording under review, with a fixed translation for other languages):

  | Value                    | `en-IN`                                                                                                         | `hi-IN`                                                                                        |
  | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `first_cod_order`        | "The seller asks you to confirm this order: it is your first cash-on-delivery order with this seller."          | "विक्रेता चाहता है कि आप इस ऑर्डर की पुष्टि करें: यह इस विक्रेता के साथ आपका पहला कैश-ऑन-डिलीवरी ऑर्डर है।"   |
  | `above_seller_threshold` | "The seller asks you to confirm this order: it is above the amount above which the seller asks you to confirm." | "विक्रेता चाहता है कि आप इस ऑर्डर की पुष्टि करें: यह उस रक़म से ज़्यादा है जिसके ऊपर विक्रेता आपकी पुष्टि माँगता है।" |
  | `new_credit_line`        | "The seller asks you to confirm this order: it opens a new credit line with this seller."                       | "विक्रेता चाहता है कि आप इस ऑर्डर की पुष्टि करें: इससे इस विक्रेता के यहाँ आपका नया उधार खाता शुरू होता है।"    |
  | `credit_limit_exceeded`  | "The seller asks you to confirm this order: it is above your credit limit with this seller."                    | "विक्रेता चाहता है कि आप इस ऑर्डर की पुष्टि करें: यह इस विक्रेता के यहाँ आपकी उधार सीमा से ज़्यादा है।"          |
  | `other`                  | "The seller asks you to confirm this order."                                                                    | "विक्रेता चाहता है कि आप इस ऑर्डर की पुष्टि करें।"                                                      |

The `hi-IN` sentences say, in English, what the `en-IN` sentences say.

- At most one such step-up is raised per `checkout_hash`. It is not counted against the agent, and it is counted in the per-principal step-up cap of [Negotiation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/negotiation/#step-up-to-the-trusted-surface).
- Its resolution is `requires_buyer_review`, the same word as UCP's message resolution ([UCP checkout projection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/ucp-checkout/index.md)).
- A confirmation that the seller asks for at `on_init` through the `bacp.confirmation` group without having declared it at discovery stays a `constraint_unresolved` step-up ([Seller confirmation profile](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#principal-confirmation)).

**The seller refuses.** `bpp_nack` carries an optional `seller_reason{code, beckn_code}` that the gateway sets only from the BPP-signed NACK ([Errors](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/#error-object)). `code` is `item_unavailable`, `quantity_reduced`, `price_changed`, `not_serviceable`, `store_closed`, `agent_orders_not_accepted`, `terms_mismatch` or `other`, and a Beckn code that the gateway cannot map gives `other`. Which ONDC code maps to which value is for ONDC to answer: the code 40002 is unlabelled in the ONDC build file (not verified as of 18-10-2026).

**Substitution.** `bpp_nack` is `recoverable` only for a retry of the same item at a total no higher than the one that the principal was shown.

- In a human-present session, a substitute item or seller at a higher total than the quote that the principal saw needs a new `confirm` step-up, with its own `ts_render`.
- In a human-not-present session the same rule applies: a substitute item or seller at a higher total than the last BPP-signed quote of the session needs a `confirm` step-up (reason `constraint_unresolved`), and no money moves until the principal decides. A substitute at or below that quote, within the mandate's constraints, is what the principal authorised. The `seller_reason` appears in the order notice and in the receipt, in the principal's language. A higher-priced substitution is exactly where a principal who is not present needs protection.
- The basis is the dark-pattern guidance on bait and switch (Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023, Annexure 1 (7), illustration (b): "out of stock", then a higher-priced product).

**After the order.** A seller's `RETURN_REJECTED` and an unsolicited `on_cancel` produce the messages `return_refused` and `seller_cancelled`, each with resolution `requires_buyer_review` and the `grievance_contact`. Neither is ever terminal ([Errors](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/errors/#registry-session)).

### Charge recipient mapping

A BACP quote line that is not goods carries a `recipient`. ONDC's breakup has no recipient: the `@ondc/org/title_type` enum is `item`, `delivery`, `packing`, `tax`, `misc` and `discount`; the build file's examples also use `offer`, which is not in the enum (read from ONDC's build file, not a policy text; as of 18-10-2026). BACP therefore publishes its own mapping, and the gateway applies it. The mapping is a published rule, not an inference from the charge's code. It is BACP's and is open with ONDC ([Q-80](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-80)).

| `title_type`                | BACP line                            | `recipient`                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `item`, `discount`, `offer` | Goods or discount; not a charge line | none                                                  |
| `delivery`                  | Total type `delivery`                | `seller`                                              |
| `packing`                   | Total type `packing`                 | `seller`                                              |
| `tax`                       | Total type `tax`                     | `government`                                          |
| `misc`, or any other value  | Total type `other_charge`            | `other`, with the warning `charge_recipient_unmapped` |

- `delivery` and `packing` map to `seller` because the quote is the seller's, and it does not say whether a logistics provider is paid on from the delivery charge. A seller that wants a different recipient states it in the breakup item TagGroup `bacp.charge`, tag `recipient` (a value of the `ChargeRecipient` enum). A stated value takes precedence over the table, and the gateway never rewrites it.
- An unmapped type is a **warning, never a refusal**: the line is kept with `recipient: other`, and the gateway adds the message `charge_recipient_unmapped` (`warning`, `recoverable`) at the line. The warning on its own is not a price change. An `other_charge` line that first appears after the round that the handler intersection consumed is drip pricing, like any other fee line.
- Until ONDC answers whether `misc` carries convenience fees ([Q-80](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-80)), a line of type `other_charge` is a fee line. The Trusted Surface reads it on its own as "other charge", with its recipient, and never inside the remainder figure. In a human-not-present checkout it is counted with the order's `convenience` lines against the mandate's `convenience_fees`, and an uncovered line raises the `confirm` step-up with reason `constraint_unresolved`. That step-up is never a refusal.
- A stated `bacp.charge` recipient that breaches the [type-to-recipient rule](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#fee-lines) is ignored: the gateway applies the table and adds the warning `charge_recipient_invalid` (`recoverable`). A line that named the agent operator or the assisted operator is also treated as an operator charge that the notice does not cover.

### Offers and discount codes

| BACP                  | ONDC retail 1.2.5                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `discounts.codes[n]`  | `select` and `init`: `message.order.offers[]` with `id` = the code and the tag `selection` / `apply` = `"yes"`                                                                                                                                              |
| `applied[]` (by code) | `on_select` and `on_init` `quote.breakup[]` line with `@ondc/org/title_type: "offer"`; `offer_id` = `@ondc/org/item_id`; `amount` = the absolute value of `price.value`, in integer paise                                                                   |
| `applied[].automatic` | the breakup item tag `offer` / `auto` = `"yes"`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `results[].offers[]`  | provider `offers[]`: `id`; `descriptor.code` as `kind`; `item_ids`; `time.range` as `valid_from` and `valid_until`; `qualifier.min_value` as `min_order_value`; `benefit.value_type`, `value` and `value_cap` as `benefit`; `meta.additive` and `meta.auto` |
| a rejected code       | no matching breakup line gives `discount_code_invalid`, unless the seller's error says expired or not combinable (the ONDC error codes for these are not verified as of 18-10-2026)                                                                         |

Codes travel in `message.order`, not in `context.bacp`. The decimal rule of the [catalogue disclosure mapping](#disclosure-mapping) applies to every price and benefit figure. For a percentage (`benefit.value_type` `percent`), the value is a string of the same form with at most two decimals, and `percent_bps` is the value times 100 by the same rule; a value of 0, or above 100, makes the benefit of the offer absent. A negative `benefit.value` is read as its magnitude only where ONDC defines the sign, and otherwise the benefit is absent. The gateway validates every offer against `CatalogOffer` itself, and does not rely on the network's validation of offers.

### Quantity and units

A BACP `ItemRef.quantity` is a whole number of steps of the item's `measure` ([Units, quantity and weighed goods](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/checkout/#units)). ONDC Retail, as checked in ONDC's log-validation utility (domain RET11, as of 18-10-2026; not verified for other domains), carries the ordered quantity in `select` as an integer `quantity.count`, and the item's pack measure in the catalogue as `quantity.unitized.measure{unit, value}`, with `unit` one of `unit`, `dozen`, `gram`, `kilogram`, `tonne`, `litre` and `millilitre`. The gateway maps between them as follows.

1. **Count rule.** The gateway sends `quantity.count = quantity / increment`, and only where the seller's `unitized.measure` equals the increment in the same unit (a `measure` of `{unit: KGM, scale: 3, increment: 250}` against a seller's `{unit: gram, value: 250}`). Then a BACP quantity of `1500` is `count: 6`. Where the seller's measure is anything else (a seller that lists only 1 kg packs, for an increment of 250 g), the gateway refuses the line with `400 invalid_request` at `$.items[n].quantity`, sends no `select`, and never converts or rounds.
1. **The unit table.** The ONDC unit enum maps to UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 codes as below. The codes are to be checked against the Recommendation 20 list at the next review (not verified as of 18-10-2026).

| ONDC `unitized.measure.unit` | Recommendation 20 code |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `unit`                       | `C62`                  |
| `dozen`                      | `DZN`                  |
| `gram`                       | `GRM`                  |
| `kilogram`                   | `KGM`                  |
| `tonne`                      | `TNE`                  |
| `litre`                      | `LTR`                  |
| `millilitre`                 | `MLT`                  |

1. **Fulfilment, policies and minimum order.** The gateway projects `fulfilment_options[]` from the fulfilments of `on_select` and `on_init`, the typed policies from the tags `returnable`, `return_window`, `cancellable` and `available_on_cod`, the `tat` of an option from `time_to_ship`, and `min_order` from the seller's minimum order value and minimum item quantity ([Typed policies](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#typed-policies)). The Beckn paths for a selectable fulfilment and for a `unitized.measure` outside RET11 are not verified ([Q-102](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-102)).
1. **Business buyer.** On an ONDC B2B order the gateway projects `acting_for.gstin`, which it sends only under the `ACTING_FOR` scope and a per-seller ConsentReceipt that lists it, into the order's `buyer_id` ([Mandates and Consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#consent)). Whether `buyer_id` is GSTIN-only is not verified ([Q-102](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-102)).

### Registry record mapping

A gateway that reads a Beckn registry lookup response builds the BACP [registry record](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/discovery/#registry-lookup) from it as follows. The Beckn field names are informative and are not verified as of 18-10-2026 against ONDC's registry specification (a question for ONDC, [Q-87](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-87)).

| Beckn lookup field                          | BACP `registry-record.json`                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `subscriber_id`                             | `subscriber_id`                                                                                                                         |
| `ukid`, with the signing algorithm          | the `kid` of a `keys[]` entry, `{subscriber_id}\|{ukid}\|ed25519`                                                                       |
| `signing_public_key`                        | the `jwk` of that `keys[]` entry                                                                                                        |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until`                 | `valid_from`, `valid_until`                                                                                                             |
| `type` of `BAP` or `BPP`                    | `bacp_role` of `bap` or `bpp`. A Beckn `type` has no value for a Mandate Manager, a PSP, a support operator or a conformance authority. |
| `status` of `SUBSCRIBED`                    | `status: active`                                                                                                                        |
| `status` of `UNSUBSCRIBED` or `INVALID_SSL` | `status: revoked`                                                                                                                       |
| `status` of `EXPIRED`                       | no BACP record: the reader produces none, because the Beckn record is past its `valid_until`, and MUST NOT use it                       |

The legal `operator`, `regulatory_status[]` and `data_residency` have no Beckn field. Whether the ONDC network registry can carry them is not settled. Where it cannot, an operator is unknown, which fails every separation check closed, and a collecting party has no `verified` `rbi_pa` or `bank` entry, so `complete` returns `403 collector_not_authorised`.

## Signing

The signing profile on the Beckn leg is settled in [Q-43](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-43):

- The gateway signs every Beckn message with the BAP's registry key, using the network's own signing profile. On Beckn 1.x and ONDC this is the `Authorization` header: Ed25519 over `(created)`, `(expires)` and a BLAKE2b-512 digest of the body, with `keyId="{subscriber_id}|{unique_key_id}|ed25519"`.
- The gateway MUST verify every callback against the BPP's registry key, and the signer MUST equal the `bpp_id` in the callback's `context`. A key of the wrong registry role MUST be refused.
- The gateway MUST NOT hold or use an agent key. Negotiation messages carry the sending network participant's registry signature; the agent's own act is evidenced by its RFC 9421 request signature to the gateway under tag `bacp-negotiate`.
- BACP does not require Beckn 2.0 signed ACKs. Where the counterparty supports Beckn 2.0, the gateway SHOULD use signed ACKs and the `request-signature` binding of callbacks.
- Negotiation timing uses the receiver's CounterSignature timestamp as the time of receipt. The CounterSignature is a BACP artefact, a JWS by the receiver's registry key carried on a Beckn leg in a `bacp.receipt` TagGroup in the synchronous `Ack` of the same exchange (see "Receipts on a Beckn leg" above) and recorded on the message as `counter_signature`, so it does not depend on the Beckn version.
- A counterparty that does not return valid CounterSignatures is treated as not supporting firm negotiation: the gateway MUST send it only non-firm offers (`firm: false`).

## Callback correlation

1. **Bound callbacks.** A response to a request MUST match it on `(transaction_id, message_id)` and its action MUST be `on_` plus the request's action. Only the first matching callback is accepted; duplicates are logged.
1. **Addressee.** A callback whose `context.bap_id` is not this gateway's BAP MUST be ignored and logged.
1. **Unsolicited callbacks.** A seller-initiated `on_status`, `on_update` or `on_cancel` is applied only to a known order, keyed by `(bpp_id, order id)`, because a seller's order id is unique only within that seller. An `on_issue` is applied only to a known issue whose order belongs to the same `bpp_id`. An unsolicited `on_select` carrying a negotiation message is applied only to a known negotiation.
