| POST   | `/checkout-sessions`                                                    | ucp-checkout     | `bacp-browse`                                                                        | required        | Create a checkout in UCP shape (`in.bacp.ucp_checkout`; [projection](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/ucp-checkout/index.md))            |
| GET    | `/checkout-sessions/{id}`                                               | ucp-checkout     | `bacp-browse`                                                                        | —               | Get a checkout in UCP shape                                                                                                                                  |
| PUT    | `/checkout-sessions/{id}`                                               | ucp-checkout     | `bacp-browse`                                                                        | required        | Update a checkout in UCP shape                                                                                                                               |
| POST   | `/checkout-sessions/{id}/complete`                                      | ucp-checkout     | `bacp-pay`                                                                           | required        | Complete a checkout in UCP shape: one UCP instrument for each tender, each carrying a BACP closed payment mandate                                            |
| POST   | `/checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel`                                        | ucp-checkout     | `bacp-browse`                                                                        | required        | Cancel a checkout in UCP shape                                                                                                                               |

The status codes each operation can return are documented in the OpenAPI document. Every operation documents every status it can return, including 401, 404, 409, 413, 422, 429, 502, 503 and 504 where they apply.

## Lost-response recovery

```
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Agent
    participant G as BACP Gateway
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (Idempotency-Key K1)
    G--xA: response lost
    A->>G: GET /sessions/ses_01HZXD
    G-->>A: 200 status complete_in_progress, payment in_doubt
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (same key K1)
    G-->>A: 409 idempotency_in_flight, Retry-After 2
    A->>G: POST /sessions/ses_01HZXD/complete (same key K1)
    G-->>A: 200 status completed, Idempotent-Replayed true
```

# UCP checkout projection

Version 2026-10-18

This page is part of BACP version `2026-10-18`. Rules marked **Proposed** depend on an open question and may change in a later dated release.

BACP is not wire-compatible with the checkout of the [Universal Commerce Protocol](https://ucp.dev) (UCP); the differences are listed in [BACP and other protocols](https://bacp.dev/latest/documentation/other-protocols/#ucp). A gateway that wants a UCP-built agent to reuse its UCP response parser, status machine and totals renderer can list the optional capability **`in.bacp.ucp_checkout`**, which adds five operations that answer in the shape of the UCP checkout. This page defines that **projection**. A gateway that does not list the capability serves no `/checkout-sessions` path: a UCP client gets `404`, as it did before this release.

Pinned to UCP release v2026-08-25

The projection is tested against unmodified copies of the UCP JSON Schemas of UCP's tagged release `v2026-08-25` (25-08-2026, commit `cd78fb3`), kept under `source/ucp/` ([provenance and licence](https://bacp.dev/latest/ucp/PINNED.txt)). The other UCP releases are `v2026-04-08`, `v2026-01-23` and `v2026-01-11` (as of 18-10-2026). Text that UCP added to its `main` branch after the tag (the Ask capability, a cart rule that `line_items` SHOULD be empty, and a registry of policy types) is not in the pinned release, and the projection does not depend on it ([Q-82](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-82)). A gateway MUST NOT claim UCP compatibility on any other UCP version.

## Whole or absent

A gateway MUST NOT list `in.bacp.ucp_checkout`, or claim UCP compatibility in any form, unless it passes **all** the entry criteria below. A partial projection is worse than none, because a UCP client would trust the parts that look right.

| Criterion | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Cases                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| UCPF-01   | A key used on `/sessions/{id}/complete` is replayed on `/checkout-sessions/{id}/complete` (and the reverse) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: the projection has the same canonical operation, so the same key space ([Idempotency](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/transports/rest/#idempotency)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | BND-UCPF-01            |
| UCPF-02   | A request signed with UCP's default signature, without `nonce`, `created` or `tag`, is refused with `401 signature_invalid`. The BACP signature profile applies unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | BND-UCPF-02            |
| UCPF-03   | An instrument whose credential is not of type `in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate` is refused with `400 invalid_request` at `$.payment.instruments[i].credential`, with no rail call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | BND-UCPF-03            |
| UCPF-04   | `continue_url` is only `step_up.trusted_surface_url` and otherwise absent, and `links[]` carries only typed policy links with titles from the gateway's own templates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | BND-UCPF-04            |
| UCPF-05   | A `complete` that carries `ap2.checkout_mandate` is refused with `400 invalid_request` at `$.ap2.checkout_mandate`, with no rail call.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | BND-UCPF-05            |
| UCPF-06   | A request that carries a UCP member of a capability that BACP does not define is refused with `400 capability_unsupported` at that member, with `capability` set to the UCP capability id named (`dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent`, `dev.ucp.common.loyalty` or `dev.ucp.shopping.cart`), and no session is created or changed: a buyer-consent member (`$.buyer.consent`, UCP `dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent`), a loyalty member (`$.loyalty`, UCP `dev.ucp.common.loyalty`) or a cart reference (`$.cart_id`, UCP `dev.ucp.shopping.cart`). The paths are those of the pinned UCP schemas. The projection never declares these capabilities in its `ucp` envelope. | BND-UCPF-06            |
| Shape     | A projected checkout validates against the pinned UCP `shopping/checkout.json`, and a discount line is a negative integer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | BND-UCP-01, BND-UCP-02 |

## Operations

Each operation is the same BACP operation as its `/sessions` twin, with the same signature tag, the same mandate checks and the same state machine; only the request and response shape differ. The UCP MCP tool names are used.

| UCP operation and MCP tool | REST                                    | BACP operation    | Signature tag |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
| `create_checkout`          | `POST /checkout-sessions`               | `createSession`   | `bacp-browse` |
| `get_checkout`             | `GET /checkout-sessions/{id}`           | `getSession`      | `bacp-browse` |
| `update_checkout`          | `PUT /checkout-sessions/{id}`           | `updateSession`   | `bacp-browse` |
| `complete_checkout`        | `POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete` | `completeSession` | `bacp-pay`    |
| `cancel_checkout`          | `POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/cancel`   | `cancelSession`   | `bacp-browse` |

- The `id` is the BACP session id. A request carries `UCP-Agent: profile="..."` as UCP requires. The gateway does not use it to authenticate or authorise: the agent is identified by its AgentCredential and its RFC 9421 signature. A gateway SHOULD NOT fetch the profile that the header names at all. A gateway that does MUST follow [URL fetch hygiene](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/security-and-privacy/#url-fetch-hygiene), and takes nothing from the fetched profile that affects a version, an amount, a payee, a handler or a mandate.
- A request body is the UCP body, plus a top-level `bacp` member that carries what BACP needs and UCP has no place for: on `create_checkout`, the seller (`bpp_id`, `provider_id`), `transaction_id`, `presence` and `mandate_ref`; on `complete_checkout`, the checkout mandate, `checkout_hash` and `presence` ([below](#complete)).
- A response is the UCP checkout. BACP-only state is under the top-level `bacp` member (UCP's checkout schema allows additional members): the BACP `status`, `checkout_hash`, `all_in_total`, every language of every message, the `step_up`, `plan_options` and `payment_plan`. A UCP client ignores it.
- The `ucp` envelope declares `dev.ucp.shopping.checkout` at version `2026-08-25` (the UCP version of the pinned release) and the session's BACP handlers as `payment_handlers`, each keyed by its UCP alias `dev.bacp.<handler id>` and carrying the BACP handler id as `id` and the BACP release id (for example `2026-10-18`) as `version`, not the UCP version ([Namespaces and the handler keys](#namespaces)). It never declares `dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate` ([No AP2](#no-ap2)).

**Namespaces and the handler keys.** The projection never declares an `in.*` id together with a `schema` in the profile or envelope that a UCP platform reads, and a BACP gateway MUST NOT accept or fetch a schema for an `in.*` id from a UCP business profile or from any other source: it logs `extension_not_registered` and does not activate the handler or capability. The BACP handler ids are not DNS-bound ([Extensibility](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/overview/#extensibility)), whereas UCP requires the `schema` URL of a handler or capability to be served from the namespace authority in its name (UCP overview, Authority Binding, at release `v2026-08-25`). BACP holds the domain `bacp.dev` (owner confirmation of 18-10-2026), whose reverse-DNS authority is `dev.bacp`. The projection therefore applies UCP's own rule and adds no grammar to it:

- **Handler keys.** The key of each entry of `ucp.payment_handlers` is `dev.bacp.<handler id>`, where `<handler id>` is the canonical id of the [registry](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/handler-registry/index.md) descriptor (`dev.bacp.in.upi.circle`, `dev.bacp.bacp.credit_ledger`). The doubled label in `dev.bacp.bacp.<name>` is intended: the alias is the authority `dev.bacp` followed by the unchanged handler id, so a reader recovers the handler id by removing the prefix `dev.bacp.`. UCP treats the labels after the authority as opaque, and the full handler id keeps the mapping one to one. The entry carries the BACP handler id as `id` and a `schema` of `https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/<handler id>.json`, whose host reversed (`dev.bacp`) is a label-aligned prefix of the key. Each schema is published in the specification repository under `source/schemas/ucp/`, with an unversioned `$id` that the build rewrites per version like every BACP schema. Each schema is self-describing as UCP asks (UCP `schema-authoring`, release `v2026-08-25`): it carries a top-level `name`, `dev.bacp.<handler id>`, and a `version`, the BACP release id, and an entry in the envelope carries that `version`. The key suffix after `dev.bacp.`, the entry's `id` and the schema file name MUST be equal, otherwise the envelope is invalid; a `complete` that names a key which is not in the session's envelope is `400 invalid_request`. A schema describes a handler entry with no `config`: the limits and rules of the handler are registry data, not UCP handler configuration (loss-table row 7).
- **Extension keys.** The projection declares no extension today (its `ucp.capabilities` holds `dev.ucp.shopping.checkout` only). A key that BACP adds later is `dev.bacp.<service>.<capability>`, the shape of UCP's naming convention for capabilities, with its `schema` under `https://bacp.dev/schemas/ucp/`.
- **Old keys.** A BACP handler id used as a key, as in a profile that was written before the alias, is accepted as an alias of its `dev.bacp.` key for the dated release that introduces the alias, and a later dated release MAY stop accepting it ([versioning policy](https://bacp.dev/versioning/#deprecation)). The `handler_id` of a `complete` instrument is the BACP handler id, and the alias key is accepted there as well. The projection emits only the alias keys.
- A gateway does not need to fetch these schemas: they are for a UCP platform that validates the envelope. The `in.bacp.*` capability ids do not change.

**Parked UCP operations.** The projection answers `404` for the UCP cart operations and for every other UCP operation that this page does not list; the cart ([Q-95](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-95)), account linking ([Q-96](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-96)), Ask ([Q-97](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-97)), loyalty ([Q-98](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-98)), catalogue lookup and variants ([Q-99](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-99)) and ranking parameters ([Q-100](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-100)) are parked, each with its controls. If the projection ever declares UCP buyer consent, it confirms `granted: false, source: "platform"` for every purpose unless an active marketing ConsentReceipt of the seller exists ([Marketing consent](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#marketing-consent)); until it does, UCPF-06 refuses a buyer-consent member.

## Complete

`complete_checkout` pays with one UCP payment instrument for each BACP tender:

ucp-complete-request.gift-upi.json

```
{
  "payment": {
    "instruments": [
      {
        "id": "tdr_gift001",
        "handler_id": "in.ppi.gift",
        "type": "in.bacp.tender",
        "amount": 100000,
        "selected": true,
        "credential": {
          "type": "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate",
          "token": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln"
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "tdr_upi001",
        "handler_id": "in.upi.circle",
        "type": "in.bacp.tender",
        "amount": 116000,
        "selected": true,
        "credential": {
          "type": "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate",
          "token": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "bacp": {
    "checkout_mandate": "eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9.eyJ2Y3QiOiJpbi5iYWNwLm1hbmRhdGUucGF5bWVudC4xIn0.c2ln",
    "checkout_hash": "sha-256:MdzPb6o2QprB1t01MqITDlt_3VlU_4O8efFu8026Jpo",
    "presence": "HNP",
    "plan_id": "plan_GIFTUPI0001"
  }
}
```

- Each instrument is `{id, handler_id, type: "in.bacp.tender", amount, credential}`. `id` is the `tender_id` of the BACP plan, `handler_id` the BACP handler id, `amount` an integer in paise (**required**: an open-amount instrument is refused), and `credential` is `{type: "in.bacp.closed_payment_mandate", token}` with the BACP closed payment mandate as an attached compact JWS.
- One instrument is a single-tender `complete` and equals a BACP `payment_mandate`. Several instruments are a BACP `payment_plan`, so the capability `in.bacp.payment_plan` is required, `bacp.plan_id` names an offered plan, and every rule of [Wire binding of plans](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/payments/credit-and-split-tender/#plan-wire) applies (the tenders MUST hash to an offered or Trusted-Surface-confirmed plan, one closed mandate per tender).
- The closed checkout mandate travels in `bacp.checkout_mandate`, with `bacp.checkout_hash` and `bacp.presence` (and `accepted_disclosures_hash`, `step_up_id` and `kb_jwt` where BACP's `complete` takes them).
- An instrument whose credential is of any other type is refused (UCPF-03).

**Failure at `complete`, with a clear error.** A UCP platform that does not know BACP's mandates cannot be stopped at `create_checkout`, because UCP has no way to make an extension mandatory at negotiation: capabilities are intersected by name, and a requirement is enforced only when `complete` arrives. So the projection serves `create_checkout`, `get_checkout` and `update_checkout` to such a platform and fails at `complete`: a `complete` that carries no BACP closed payment mandate gets `400 invalid_request` at `$.payment.instruments` with the message code `bacp_mandate_required` (`unrecoverable`), and no rail call.

## No AP2

The projection MUST NOT advertise `dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate` in the `ucp` envelope. BACP's closed mandate is an attached compact JWS, which is the only interoperable encoding in this version ([Q-41](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-41)); UCP's AP2 extension carries an SD-JWT with key binding. A later BACP release may add an SD-JWT mandate `vct` and only then may the projection advertise the extension. A `complete` that carries `ap2.checkout_mandate` is refused (UCPF-05).

## Escalation and links

UCP requires a `continue_url` on `requires_escalation`, set by the business. The projection sets it only when the session has a `step_up` with a `trusted_surface_url`, and then it is exactly that URL, which the gateway mints only on an origin of the step-up's signer ([Origins and delivery](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/human-participants/#ts-origins)); with no step-up it is absent. A step-up with `delivery: app_push` has no link, so the projection sets no `continue_url` for it and the detail is in `bacp.status`. A seller's URL, even one a quote carries in its tags, never becomes a `continue_url` (UCPF-04). `links[]` carries only typed policy links (`terms_of_service`, `refund_policy`, `privacy_policy`, ...) whose `title` comes from the gateway's own templates, never from the seller.

## Differences that the projection keeps (normative)

The projection loses information. This table is normative: a gateway MUST project exactly as the second column says, and an agent that reads a projected checkout MUST read the `bacp` member where the third column says the UCP shape loses something. The rows are in the order in which a UCP client fails.

| #   | BACP                                                                        | In the UCP projection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | What the UCP shape loses                                                                                                          |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Discount sign.** A discount is a non-negative `Amount` of type `discount` | A negative integer in paise: BACP `discount` of ₹30 is `-3000`. The UCP `total` line is `all_in_total` plus the operator charges, and each operator charge is a UCP `totals[]` line of type `fee` with `display_text` from the gateway's templates; `bacp.all_in_total` keeps the quote figure     | Nothing, if the sign is flipped; a projection with a positive discount fails the pinned schema and adds the discount to the total |
| 2   | A declined payment makes the session `cancelled`                            | UCP's own rule would be `incomplete` with a recoverable `payment_failed`, but the projection reports the BACP outcome: `canceled`, with `bacp.status: cancelled`                                                                                                                                   | The retry that UCP offers after a decline                                                                                         |
| 3   | `cancelled`                                                                 | `canceled`. A UCP platform treats a checkout as canceled only when the business reports `canceled`, so the projection reports it                                                                                                                                                                   | The spelling                                                                                                                      |
| 4   | `complete` takes mandates (JWS)                                             | `payment.instruments[]` with a BACP closed payment mandate as the credential, and the checkout mandate in `bacp`                                                                                                                                                                                   | UCP's own payment instruments and AP2                                                                                             |
| 5   | `step_up.trusted_surface_url`                                               | `continue_url`, only that URL, else absent                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Any seller-supplied handoff URL                                                                                                   |
| 6   | `human_handoff`                                                             | `requires_escalation`, with the detail in `bacp.status`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The distinct status                                                                                                               |
| 7   | Handlers are in the gateway profile                                         | `ucp.payment_handlers`, keyed by the alias `dev.bacp.<handler id>` with the BACP handler id as `id`, with no UCP `config`                                                                                                                                                                          | UCP handler configuration                                                                                                         |
| 8   | `Amount` is `{value, currency}`                                             | An integer in paise, with `currency` at the root (`INR`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Nothing                                                                                                                           |
| 9   | `/sessions`                                                                 | `/checkout-sessions`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Nothing                                                                                                                           |
| 10  | MCP tools take the body's properties, path parameters and `idempotency_key` | UCP's tool names, with the same arguments plus UCP's `id`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `meta` is not used                                                                                                                |
| 11  | Messages carry a `LangText` map, and counterparty text is labelled          | One string in the negotiated language in UCP `content`, every language in `bacp.messages`. Counterparty text never goes in UCP `content`, and a UCP `line_items[].item.title` is seller text in a UCP field, marked as counterparty text in `bacp`. `ai_disclosure.notice` becomes a UCP `warning` | The other languages, and the labelling of counterparty text                                                                       |
| 12  | `links` come from the gateway                                               | Typed policy links with gateway-template titles                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Seller links                                                                                                                      |
| 13  | GST heads and `TCS`                                                         | The GST heads sum to the UCP `tax` line, with the split in the sub-lines of that line or in namespaced total types; a `TCS` line never enters a buyer-facing total (whether it may is flagged to counsel, [Q-83](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/open-questions/#q-83))                  | The split of GST in a client that ignores sub-lines                                                                               |
| 14  | `prior_price` and `mrp`                                                     | UCP's catalogue `variant.json` carries a `list_price` ("List price before discounts"), which is not among the pinned checkout schemas. Wherever the projection states a price before discount, it takes `prior_price.amount` and never `mrp`                                                       | The MRP                                                                                                                           |

UCP `buyer` fields on `create_checkout` are held by the gateway and are not sent to the seller before the ConsentReceipt ([Data minimisation](https://spec.bacp.dev/draft/specification/mandates/#consent)). A payment instrument that carries a member that UCP allows and BACP does not define, for example a display or billing field, gets `400 invalid_request` rather than being ignored: the projection fails closed, and this is a known delta from UCP.

## Pinned schemas and checks

`scripts/validate.py` checks the examples named `ucp-checkout.*.json` (a projected checkout) and `ucp-complete-request.*.json` (the body of `complete_checkout`) against the pinned UCP schemas and against the OpenAPI components `UcpCheckout` and `UcpCompleteRequest`, and requires every `*.invalid.json` to fail.

```
          "hi-IN": "आप एक AI सहायक से बात कर रहे हैं।",
          "en-IN": "You are talking to an AI assistant."
        },
        "param": "$.ai_disclosure",
        "resolution": "recoverable"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
